No game can deliver a punchline better that Tales from the Borderlands.
I've never played a Borderlands game and still found myself enjoying and understanding the story.
So if you're wondering if you should play the borderlands games before this, theres no need (unless you really want to)
Graphics: Trying to look like a comic, but failing.. miserably..
Ok, graphics here arent that good. The art style isnt really anything special here. But it gets the job done, informing the players what things are, how theyre placed, and what you can interact with. Although, I need to point out that the physics in this game are very very cumbersome. Moments where force needs to be the equivalent of a slap from a woman you've cheated with is portrayed as if a baby was giving you a high five. The object physics are just... Odd to look at.
Audio: "Where can I download these tracks"
Ok, the tracks in this game really suit the overall tone of the game. The music here, I wanted to download right off the bat after playing each episode. It was fantastic on all sides. Althoughhh~ Sound layering isnt all that good, nor is it particularly bad. It's just mediocre. The sound effects, they didnt bother to give emphasis on. The sound of metal clanking to each other, sound like metal clanking to each other. Yet the layering isnt really there. Probably also because there isnt much sound effects on each of the scenes to begin with. And to touch on it a bit, The voice acting was superb. I could feel their sarcasm radiating from the screen because of their performances. It was amazing. Props to the voice actors.
Gameplay: Really? -.-"
Its a telltale game......
Story: Can't get enough of the dialogue
To clear things up, the story here is very very simple. But its the dialogue of the individual characters that make it very interesting. Jokes here are moment-reliant and extremely funny. And its elevated with such awesome voice actors. Making each of the little simple moments in-game engaging and entertaining. I would buy this game full price for the story alone. The writing here is clever and immature in all the right places, which is hard to do to begin with. Add to the fact that the developers have to mesh it with some gameplay elements, It makes their jobs a whole lot more difficult. Story gets an A++++ in my book because of that.
TL;DR:
A Buy at full price. It's probably the best Telltale game to come out after The Walking dead (Season 1 of course) series.
Its got a LOT of laughs. And suprisingly a bit of the feels.
Its the most underrated Telltale game in my opinion.

Steins;Gate is one of the greatest if not the best visual novels I have had the pleasure to experience.
The story had ensnared me within it's universe within the first hour. Which is quite the feat considering my attention span. A story focused on time travel is one very easy to mess up and can easily become a convoluted mess. But Steins Gate managed to accomplish this feat seemingly effortlessly. The way that the rules that are set within it's universe are shown to the readers and the show manages to make sense within it's own rules. The dialog and conversation between the characters never leave any dull moments, no matter the situation the characters manage to set the scene emotional or comedic. My only gripe is the slow first half but I wouldn't change it as it serves to make the second half even more powerful.
Hououin Kyouma shown to us as a wannabe mad scientist with his ability to retain memories of other timelines "READING STEINER" (later explained in game). Erratic in nature but always fun later turned melancholic, pessimistic Okabe Rintaro in the latter half of the novel has easily become my most favourite character in this novel. The way that he talked in the first half with his cocky and delusional alter ego put me off at first but I later came to enjoy this personality. This served to make things more dramatic and deliver a strong emotion when we see this alter ego of his die out. This change made the later revival of Hououin Kyouma a much more impactful moment.
The way that the all the labmems responded to Okabe was amazing and served to glue together this masterpiece of storytelling. The chemistry between all of them was absolutely amazing, especially Kurisu and him (ps. Kurisu best girl). It wasn't like other visual novels where I found myself mindlessly clicking waiting for the stories climax, this had me actively paying attention with my eyes glued to the screen lost in the story.
The art in this game is absolutely mesmerizing to say the least. I was unsure at first as it was a new style that I had not seen before but not long after I found it growing on me. It is one of the most colourful, vibrant visual novels I've ever seen.
I say that Steins;Gate is worth every cent that it costs. It was one hell of a ride and a unforgettable experience it and I guarantee you that you will hold it as one of your favourites for many years to come. Do not dismiss it if you are a new reader although it may seem daunting, stick till the end. Also play with the committee of zero patch as it fixes various formatting issues and makes for a even more enjoyable experience.
Overall:
I'd give it a solid 10/10

2. Backing up the truck to hook onto a trailer at the warehouse can be a nightmare unless you are lucky (see comment one above). You need to back up over a bump and whamo, you're into the trailer and it moves to an impossible angle.
Save before you try to hook up any trailer.

If it starts to go back in reverse lots of luck stoping it on a slope. Don't even try pushing paydirt to your plant, its not designed for that. On level ground the blade won't even dig in.
4. The keyboard controls can be very frustrating. I don't know how many times I've popped out of the excavator when I accidently touch the "e" key when I'm pushing the "w" key. How a about a key that disables automatic exit from the excavator, something like a seat belt to undo before exiting (just don't do it for all vehicles) or disable the "e" key in the digging mode? It seems to have the same modeling as the pickup truck (so does the excavator in driving mode). All vehicle seem to have the same poor driving model and all get hung up in the same places. Comon guys, a real bulldoze can go almost anywhere!!! Lets beef the model up a lot!
5. Graphics are good at times, but objects tend to "meld" together. I lost a bucket never to be seen again after it was sticking part way through my first plant. Other objects "pop" through other solid objects. This is a basic gaming graphic no no.
Also it has to load /pause too frequently when going into town, also furstrating.

The slope world is the twist on this version of the game that salvaged the review, as the main continent was simply three bridge designs in different lengths, depending on what supplies you were granted.  Slope you have to think about it, and deal with the crazy physics.
Bought in a bundle for about 75c US.  Played for about 18 hours, with 4 of that on just a couple of bridges (see my guide on the worst one IMHO).  NOT worth full retail of US$10, but if you can get it for 2.50 or less I think you will find it to be a pretty decent game.

First, I had issues starting the game because of ASN_App_pcDx9_Final. It seems others have the same issue, here is how I fixed it. Go to the games local files folder (right click game in steam library-preferences-local files-browse local files) the copy the ASN_App_pcDx9_Final file, paste it into the same folder (you will now have a file named ASN_App_pcDx9_Final - copy) rename the ASN_App_pcDx9_Final - copy to ASN_App_pcDx9_Final.EXE then start the game again and it should work!

I've put a ton of time into the Windows 10/Xbox One version of the game so excuse the low playtime. Also, I'm not a pro player by any stretch but I'm pretty decent-ish at this game.
This game is really lovely. I personally didn't think much of the original games at all and was skeptical when this was announced but since then it has probably become one of my favorite in the genre.
The cast of characters is bananas in every way and covers a lot of playstyles. Want to zone? You got that. Want to be a grappler? Sure! Want to rush down but also zone and how you play that character is determined entirely by RNG? Absolutely! It can seem overwhelming because you effectively have to learn how to fight all of this but it's a lot of fun figuring that out, at least for me.
One thing about this game also is everything is governed by the combo system which is very unique. Don't think of it as combos and more like mixups. Every combo in this game can be broken as long as you guess correctly and nothing is guaranteed. However, if you try to break a combo and the opponent guesses that you are going to break, they can effectively extend their combo if they guess right. If they're wrong they have a huge cooldown window for you to punish. It's largely all mindgames and execution isn't really a barrier here. Quarter circles, tapping back to forward (or down to up), and the standard dragon punch is all you'll get here. In a way it gives people who may lack execution a chance. Obviously there is more to this game than the combo system but it's hard to cover all of that in a review. See the bottom for a link to a guide.
On a pure visual level it has some pretty great art. Characters are modeled well, stages look really good, and everything seems to pop. It's usually pretty consistent across the board. In terms of audio, the soundtrack is amazing. Mick Gordon started getting his name out with this game and it shows. Later music by Celldweller and Atlas Plug is also generally pretty good but I prefer Mick's music for the most part.
Anyway I really like this game and everyone should give it a shot, especially if you like fighting games and want to try something a little different. If you're having any trouble, a KI player named Infilament made a great guide that explains the ins and outs of how the game works.

Ignore my current playtime, I have 200+ hours on the Windows Store version.
Reasons Killer Instinct is legit as ♥♥♥♥:
- Insanely fun combo system
- Offensive/Defensive options for absolutely any scenario
- Easy-input option for players wanting to get their feet wet and experiment
- C-C-C-COMBO BREAKER and ULTRAAAA COMBOOOO never fail to fill me with utter glee
- The best tutorial in fighting games to date, which teaches you how to play fighting games in general, right down to frame data and mindgames
- Wide range of characters with totally unique playstyles
- Plenty of modes to tackle, even if you don't want to go online
- One of those modes is basically X-COM
- Visual character customization, for those of you who also buy costume/color pack DLCs in other games
- Bangin' soundtrack
- Runs buttery smooth, even on under-performing systems
- Online cross-play with the Windows Store and Xbox One versions
Reasons why Killer Instinct might not be for you:
- Fighting games are hard (thank goodness for that fantastic tutorial, right?)
- Combo system can be really daunting at first (Openers, Autos, Linkers, oh my!)
- Doesn't support DInput fight-sticks (yet)
- I sat here for at least 2 minutes trying to think of other reasons and I can't
Honestly, if you're not already interested in fighting games as a whole, download the Windows Store version (I feel sick typing that) and give it a go. It's a free trial with Jago and a weekly rotating character so you can get a feel for things without taking the plunge. On the other hand, if you're already a fan of fighting games, there's no reason why you shouldn't be checking this out. Shadow Lords (the X-COM mode) almost carries it alone. Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is a mix of Mario Kart-like randomness and chaos, and Trackmania-like skill-based precision racing, and then some more.
So it is a game with several very different game-modes and race types, in singleplayer you'll go through all of them, wether you like them all or not. How much fun you will have depends on what kind of preferences of racing game types you have, and I'll try to point out those things in this review.
First off, if you're a completionist, going for 100% achievements or as close to that as possible, this game is quite ok into the 70-80% region, and then it becomes difficult, even frustrating, and a game of chance much more than a game of skill. That's a very clear thumbs down from this perspective. Most people don't care about that but I wanted to mention it for those who do.
If you're a fan of fun racers with random weapon pickups, this game has alot of that, in singleplayer aswell as multiplayer.
The randomness is really really prominent in singleplayer races against AI. No matter how good you are, winning in the hardest ("expert", unlockable) and second-to-hardest difficulty modes is very difficult mostly, and when you win, you don't have the feeling that you did that, but you just got lucky with the pickups and the enemy AI's rubberband mechanism. Someone might be out there who does enjoy that kind of racing, but I didn't. As mentioned, it's the central part of the game.
If you're a fan of driving skill based racing with no element of randomness, this game has some of that, too, and I happen to like those parts. The higher difficulties are a challenge, but it's how well you race that makes the difference, and there's a clear sense of progress and improvement with each retry. You memorize the courses, you spot shortcuts, get a feel for the physics model (unrealistic but that's ok) and the different unlockable drivers that handle differently, and most importantly you learn how to get "boosts" by performing slides around corners and stunts during jumps. So you have to keep an eye out for opportunities to do that, and pull it off with some skill and precision. I enjoyed these kinds of races the most. They come in different variations and make up about 1/3rd of the singleplayer game. Those variations are racing against the clock/against a pre-recorded non-random ghost, racing against AI but without weapons, drift challenges, boost challenges, and ring races in air levels.
There are sections in the levels (with varying extent per level) of air and boat racing, that handle quite a bit differently. The air controls are a disaster, imho. The slower you are, the faster you turn, which is ok on paper, but it makes handling steep curves extremely imprecise and frustrating, especially when the curve is not only left/right, but at the same time upwards/downwards. They should have looked at the 15 year old Pilotwings 64 to get an idea of how to design good, uncomplicated but precise controls for such a game mode.
The great downside to the game as a whole is, that, unless you happen to like all of these different kinds of racing, you'll hate some parts of the game. Due to how the singleplayer progression is designed, you can't really ignore those parts, if you want to progress through the game.

I force myself to stare into my friend’s eyes. It’s painful. I feel like a villain. Do I really want to send this life-altering email? If I do this, they’ll lose someone important in their life. But If I don’t, I’ll lose someone important in my life. It’s an agonizing decision, but it’s not the first gut-wrenching call I’ve made today, and it won’t be my last. I silently beg my friend’s forgiveness and press the send button on my phone. The past and present change instantaneously. I hope I did the right thing...
This kind of tough choice is the basis of Steins;Gate, a visual novel for the PS4/Vita that does a lot of neat storytelling acrobatics but doesn’t quite stick the landing. While I really enjoyed the emphasis on science and friendship in the first act, much of it gets torpedoed by intrusive dating elements that detract from the second act’s darker, more serious tone.
Steins;Gate gets off to a great start. As the goofy, self-proclaimed “mad scientist” Rintarou Okabe (AKA Okarin), I loved  experiencing the thrill of time travel while learning about real-world science. Terms like Kerr black holes and “lifters” were easy to understand, thanks to humorous use of pop culture to explain abstract phenomenon. (Okarin cites RPGs and erotic manga to explain bits of quantum theory at one point - you have my full attention.) I also appreciated the underlying story of friendship between Okarin and his fellow lab members. Whether Okarin was verbally sparring with the brilliant and sarcastic Kurisu, babbling silly nonsense at his childhood friend Mayuri, or praising his best bud Daru for his hacking skills, I felt a real bond of friendship between Okarin and his peers - which is why I was fully invested in trying to save them when his time-traveling experiments start to go terribly wrong.
My attachment to my friends made tough decisions like the one above incredibly difficult. More than once I spilled tears as I pushed the “send” button on my phone, which activated a mini time machine in Okarin’s makeshift lab and changed the course of history. Some of the changes I made in the beginning  were intended to make my friends happy, but ended up making things miserable for someone else, causing me to try and undo what I thought were good deeds, which meant possibly depriving my friends of happiness, and leaving me feeling like a big jerk.
Steins;Gate offers multiple endings based on crucial decisions you make during your playthrough, most of which are bittersweet. I actually like that, because not only does it ground the story in reality (mess with history’s weave and everything gets tangled), it also motivated me to try for the “true ending,” the only real happy ending you can achieve. Plus, by exploring all the different endings.
In large part, I enjoyed Steins;Gate. Its first half is smartly told, its characters are genuinely likable, and I enjoyed learning about science in humorous ways. I just wish that the dating elements had been more smoothly incorporated into the established narrative and not forced (gruesomely at times) on the player. Sometimes, it’s enough to just be friends.

This review is sort of a mixed bag, unfocused and harshly critical, and for that I apologize. I want to get it out there very early that I recommend you experience this visual novel, but also that not much would have changed my review to something far more negative. If you do like it, that's fine, but me not sort of not liking but kinda? has to be fine too.
This visual novel is probably one of the most fluctuating things I have ever played in terms of quality. I have considered it to be boring, interesting, good, laughable, terrible, all kinds of things over the course of several hours, sometimes it changes in just minutes, and in one brief moment I found it to be outright amazing.
But, overall, I just sort of felt it to have been bad, but bad in a good way. I  mocked it beyond belief, pointed out every single bit of poor or laughable writing. My biggest issue isn't with the story, the story is fine, the problem for me is undoubtedly the characters.
So let's begin there: I did not care what happened to these people for far too long. I would have praised this visual novel had I just liked them, but in the end there was only really one exception, maybe one and a half.
The main character is also, from this day forward, my most hated protagonist yet. This guy is just unbearable. Obnoxious, self-centered, idiotic, and with reasoning and memory worse than a dead goldfish. I understand that might very well be the point, that it could be a way to create a contrast with the character he was (supposed) to grow into later, but if that's the case we spend far too much time with him in his unlikable state. But when one considers the journey he went through, you realize that he started as a self-centered obnoxious manchild, and ends it as a self-centered obnoxious manchild that has attempted to commit first-degree murder. I'm not even mentioning some things that are so despicable I don't want to spoil them. Our protagonist, ladies and gentlemen!
The other characters are more likable on paper, but just like paper I find them to be as two-dimensional as possible. For long stretches of time these are not characters, but walking quirks, repeating annoying traits to the point I would not have endured if I hadn't mocked them relentlessly. There was this moment that was clearly written to be a shocking! To make me gasp! A character we knew died suddenly, and all I can do was to sarcastically go 'yaaaay', because at least that meant I didn't need to listen to them anymore. Unlike the main character they were merely annoying, instead of outright hatable, with some exceptions.
The story, as  I said, is fine, and I followed it through to the end because I was legitimately interested to see what would happen next. Credit where credit is due, but it's very slow to pick up speed.  The last third or so is by far the best, and actually managed to keep me intruiged, it was just such a shame that on top of the characters mentioned above, the first half was also very slowly written. Characters refused to connect the dots, made wild assumptions, had no reasonable communication, repeated themselves and their traits over and over beyond any necessity. It felt like padding, and entire scenes could have been cut entirely. "Yes, this character is quirky, we get it." "Yes, these two bicker a lot, we get it."
As I said, the last third was the best. I wondered why, and then it hit me, because it actually moves at a decent pace, and more importantly it moves so fast that the characters don't have enough time to say anything irrelevant. They suddenly seem to have motivation, and aren't around long enough for me to consider punching my screen. Thank goodness!
Speaking of goodness. There was a geniune moment of humanity that, as I mentioned, I found amazing and had I been more invested would have brought me to actual tears, rivaling some of the best moments in games I've played. It certainly helped that one of the few characters I liked was part of it. There were similar moments across the visual novel, but since those involved characters I either felt indifferent about or outright despised, it fell flat.
While the music can be a bit too peppy at times considering the larger concept and themes, it was actually quite good and did give it more of an identity. I would elaborate, but I don't know nearly enough about music to do so.
Something else I did like, at least the concept, was the inclusion of a cellphone as part of the experience. While it only really served as a specialized menu,  a very context-sensitive menu, the idea is quite good and I would love to see it expanded upon. It could have been much better if taking out a cellphone during conversations had gotten some sort of reaction from the characters, but baby steps. I know that could add a lot of complexity in terms of development, but I would have loved to see the complexity it could have brought to interactions.
And, the best part, the part that ultimately keeps this review a positive one, was that it was so easy to laugh at. I did not laugh with the game as much as I laughed at it. In fact, the only joke I found to be legitimately fun and clever the visual novel immediately shot down. When the experience was awful, it was very easy for me to almost mimic Mystery Science Theatre 3000 of old, and while it did intrigue me at times, that feeling of having fun at the expense of the game never really went away.
If you have likeminded friends, get them together, brings snacks and drinks, mock, point and laugh together, you might have a good time.
And if you play it or have played it, and you find yourself liking it on its own merits, we may never be friends, but I'm jealous because I suspect you might have enjoyed it immensly.
While I can't say I had a great time with this, this was still something I won't forget any time soon and while it wasn't in the way the makers intended, I still had fun. Besides, I got it on sale. At the end of the day, what do I have to complain about?
Yes, I recommend it.

To be fair, you have to have a very high IQ to understand Steins;Gate. The humour is extremely subtle, and without a solid grasp of theoretical physics most of the jokes will go over a typical viewer’s head. There’s also Kyouma’s nihilistic outlook, which is deftly woven into his characterisation- his personal philosophy draws heavily from Narodnaya Volya literature, for instance. The fans understand this stuff; they have the intellectual capacity to truly appreciate the depths of these jokes, to realise that they’re not just funny- they say something deep about LIFE. As a consequence people who dislike Steins;Gate truly ARE idiots- of course they wouldn’t appreciate, for instance, the humour in Kyouma’s existential catchphrase “El Psy Congroo,” which itself is a cryptic reference to Turgenev’s Russian epic Fathers and Sons. I’m smirking right now just imagining one of those addlepated simpletons scratching their heads in confusion as Dan Harmon’s genius wit unfolds itself on their computer screens. What fools.. how I pity them.

If you happen to see this game on sale with the DLC pretty cheap, pick it up.
First, addressing all the Non-recommended reviews:
The community is small but pleasant most of the time, and the developers are working and responding to how the community wants to shape the game.Yes they try new things, and yes they mess it up sometimes. But if the community doesn't like it then it gets revoked and they take a step back. Mana System is not bad at all despite what people make it out to be. There are bugs that people happen to lose their relics and then come write a negative review instead of troubleshoot the problem with developers. You should also note the date of most of the (Helpful Reviews) are from more than two months ago (with exception).
The game itself (As of February 5th 2016)
PROS -------------------
- Latest update has smoothed gameplay a lot
- If you are in the U.S. they just added dedicated servers so multiplayer is a lot more playable with other people. (Other dedicated servers are in Germany, sorry Asia dwellers)
- Community is small and you'll make friends fast
- Gameplay is pretty fun, loot system lets you pick up gear and there is a decent (albiet small and not too variable) skill    system.

CONS ----------------------
- Siege Mode doesn't let you skip waves at the moment.

I'll update with more as the game progresses, but it is very much playable in it's current state and quite fun despite what others think. If you got more than a full day in game time, I'd say you have gotten your money's worth.

The number of relics that you acquire used to be limited by how many bosses you could fight, how many shops you could find, and how many dungeons you could complete. Now that you can replay bosses as often as you'd like, they had to put a cap on the number of relics, and there is no longer a point to risking your life in the dungeons. This makes one of the most interesting and exciting parts of the game pointless. In many different ways, the changes have turned the game from a challenge into a grind.

One of my favourite games. I bought the spearhead edition three times (me, my sis and a third copy that's just lying around unclaimed) because I wanted to support the devs.
This game is still in a pre-alpha state (i.e. there's still a lot coming) but it's already tons of fun!
-Very dynamic maps (moving platforms, day/night cycles, lights that can be destroyed, doors that open/close) + they are beautiful
-Basic implementation of the important stuff: crouch, jump, scope, laser, flashlight, shooting, etc.
-The devs are really nice (you can sometimes meet them in-game, and shoot them!)
-Updates are regular (every month or so) and of great quality (rather than quantity)
-When near death part of the UI will go offline
-Very tactical. This is totally
like COD or CS. Winning depends on every member of the team working together rather than a bunch of hyperactive cellar-kids punching their keyboard and mouse to death. Respawn rates are slow, and the only reliable way to get team members to respawn is by capturing points (or killing enemy players if you're the last man standing) this makes games very tense (unless the teams are unbalanced, ↓see below↓)
-Only 2 guns (but more are coming!)
-No melee.
-No team balancing (has to be done by the players)
-No way to kick people (but the players are nice, the only people I've wanted to kick so far were afkers)
-No teamchat, voicechat or map/mode voting (it's rumoured these will be added in the next version)
-Only multiplayer (so far, co-op and campaign are in the make) EDIT: one co-op scenario has been added a few days ago, although I like it, it's still the most buggy part of the game, I suggest you only play it if you don't mind losing because of invincible bots, random deaths, falling through floors and not knowing what to do. If you do mind, wait until the next update!
-Only use your flashlight occasionaly, enemies can see it
-Only use your laser when you're gonna use it, enemies can see it
-Don't camp, you need to capture points to revive teammates. If you camp (for too long) you're letting your team down.
-Keep together. Cover all entrances with your team. Try to flank enemies, force them into corners, etc.
-If on your own, watch your back. You're never safe.
-Use the SMG for close quarters and the rifle for medium to long shots.
-Always. ALWAYS.
use cover. There's a lot of it, and it will save your life.
-Keep to the dark. When a point/doorway you need is in light, shoot the light. If you don't need to cross a light, don't shoot it. It can help you spot enemies or force them to take another path.
-You can't disable alarm lights (red lights) by shooting at them.
-Use night/dark to go offensive. As long as you keep to the dark snipers/campers can't spot you.
-Don't shoot teammates. When your UI is down (because of damage) try to keep out of combat because it will be very hard to distinguish enemies/friends.
It doesn't feel or look like a pre-alpha to me, so I wonder what the game will look like when it's finished.
Apparently the next update is going to be a big one. So I'm really looking forward to that, I think it might be co-op. We'll see.

Red Alert 3 Uprising is one of those games you either love or hate. I for one love it, and let me tell you exactly why.
Let's get this out of the way first; this stand alone expansion has no multiplayer component. None. Not even coop. There are some unit in this game that upset the balance to such a degree that it would be unethical to let anyone play against one another. If you can get over this, then you'll like the game. If you really need this mulitplayer thing, then you might want to pass.
With that out of the way, let me describe Uprising for you. Uprising is an exercise in scenario building. It tries to create the coolest kinds of single player levels seen in RTS ever with ridiculous units and abilities that make a game of Warcraft seem tame. Image transforming tanks, ice beams, rockets everywhere, robots, tanks that eat buildings and giant floating heads with death rays that make any unit or building completely worthless. It does not end there. Each civ gets a few new units. The allies get to parade their new giant gunship and otherworldly tanks, as well as freeze troopers. The soviets have to do with a complete hack of an infantry killer, and some fast mechs. No, for the really cool stuff you need to check with the empire, who come rolling onto the scene with laser archers, robots with swords and the aforementioned flying death ray. Plenty of cool stuff to go around and no stupid balance that is holding any of it back.
The game features three gamemodes. The campaigns, that come with some really impressive production value. General skirmishes. Finally, the commanders challenge. Where you have to overcome extremely strong AI opponents with limited units. Each victory gives you access to new units to use in your conquest. It is extremely hard, and fiendishly challenging, but funny and rewarding.
I can reccomend this expansion. It's a blast while it lasts, and it provides some of that cartoonish fun that you don't get in any of the newer RTS games. If this is on sale, just shell those two bucks and indulge in some robot vs tank tomfoolery. You know you want to.

"It's like Fallout mixed with a toned-down Grand Theft Auto."
That statement is both true and false. This is definitely a wonderful and timeless game in my opinion. Advancing on the whole "RPGs can be more than swords and dragons" concept, Borderlands comes in with serious foolishness and it seems to happen wonderfully with a charm.
Built rather comic-looking, the graphics, for sure, aren't gonna be the selling point, however, it has a likeness to it, whether its the bright displays of weaponry, wicked monster-creatures or even how disproportionately perfect the midgets are, the game does what it needs to in the visual department and keeps it at that.
Built low-key, plays smoothly. I like the control and feel of the game. The way the weapon system works, the shooting, aiming (this is big for me and I honestly think that 2K nailed it nicely) even the grenade-throwing which is definitely remiscent of Halo 3/Reach with it's absolute Hail Mary'ness. Moving is wonderful although there's some moments in the game where the enviornment seems to be out to get you, but, I digress; love the infinite sprint, by the way.
The games seriously has a replay factor to it, in my opinion. It's long enough of a game that you can play it 2, 3, maybe even 4 times before you really catch and take in everything. Not to mention the fact that every single time you play it, you end up with a different set of guns which really does keep it fun. However, I think the addition that could've gone wonderfully with this game would've been an enemy AI that's constantly changing a la Left for Dead. But, I do think the idea of constantly going somewhere and there being the same enemy is rather helping to those that grind, which you won't HAVE to do but it IS fun, which returns me to my point, PLAYABILITY. It's fun enough to grind when you don't really need to. That says something to me.
In the end, Borderlands is fantastic. Good enough to spawn a franchise off. However I think the storyline of "Finding a vault" can get stale after a while, but if you're feeling gung-ho, love RPGs, FPSs and even some good old fashioned shameful humor (Midget Shotgunners that blow themselves back when they shoot, shooting Rakk crap off of turbines, Nine Toes Three Testicles, etc.).
Visuals: 7 out of 10
Handling: 8 out of 10
Replay Factor: 7 out of 10
Overall: 8 out of 10

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

RimWorld is a self-proclaimed "A sci-fi colony sim driven by an intelligent AI storyteller".
It is a god-game in which you take care of a group of colonists, give them orders and ensure their well-being.
Throughout the game, the storyteller will trigger random events - some good, some bad - to keep you on your toes.
Similar to other god-games, RimWorld is a rather indirect experience. Most of the time, you will plan strategies, issue orders and check up on everyone to see if they have any needs.
Progress manifests through a larger base, more technologies and better weaponry. Depending on your scenario, you will begin with bow and arrow or simple bolt-action rifles, and end up with power-armor and rocket launchers.
In the default setting, the goal is for you to repair a spaceship found somewhere on the planet, repair it and flee said planet.
To be honest, this goal is more of a pro-forma goal, as I personally believe the goal is just to build a base and enjoy yourself.
The description of the game mentions "an intelligent AI storyteller". What this means is you can choose between three different storytellers as of version A17.
These storytellers have varying "personalities", which events trigger how often. The "classical" storyteller is designed to provide a steadily increasing challenge, the "relaxed" storyteller is aimed to provide a more laid-back experience (my personal favourite), while "random" storyteller is - you guessed it - more random.
In addition to choosing which storyteller you like, you can also set a difficulty, which affects how much of a curveball they are going to throw you. If you're unlucky, one of your colonists might have a heart attack while a generator explodes, igniting your warehouse in which you store your highly volatile chemical fuel, all while a group of heavily armed raiders land in rocket pods and promptly begin murdering everyone in sight. But hey, at least sometimes a squirrel tames itself.
I personally did not have a problem with understanding the game's core mechanics. The in-game tutorial does a great job at explaining the gameplay basics and the controls and after an hour or two of playing around, you'll get the hang of it. I should mention that the game does have a very active subreddit (/r/RimWorld) and a somewhat extensive wiki, which are great sources for additional knowledge.
All in all, I consider this game to be easy to pick up, if you do not go overboard in the beginning and settle in the middle of an ice desert on extreme difficulty on your first run.
Even though the game is in early access, the game has excellent modding support. After several hours of playthrough, I did install a few mods, which just extended the game in a way I enjoyed it. One mod, for instance, allowed me to create prosthetics myself (in the vanilla game, anything more complex than a peg leg needs to be purchased from exotic goods vendors, if they have them available). Another allowed me to set up a temporary camp instead of a permanent settlement, which I enjoyed.
If you can have fun with a game that does not provide explosions and action 100% of the time, then you can have fun with RimWorld. The game is easy to pick up, yet has a surprizing amount of depth and complexity once you get into it, that you can easily sink whole days into it. I mean, in which other game do you hear questions like "Is it feasable to create an organ farm or should I sell my slaves directly?" or "How can I stop my drug-addicted cook from killing his wife?"?

For my Red Alert 3 review: go
. Highly recommended to read it in order to understand what I'm talking in this review.
To start it off, the campaign is shorter than Red Alert 3's, not featuring as many missions as the original game, but there are 4 campaigns now; aside from the normal Allies/Soviets/Empire you also get to play the story of Yuriko Omega, a story which plays pretty much like a MOBA match. For each mini-campaign there are only 3 missions, but make no mistake, missions are not easy, even with difficulty toned down.
Most of the new units added are an interesting and useful addition, but there are a few which seemed pretty broken, as in pretty overpowered:
Harbinger Gunship (Allies): These are the Mammoth Tanks of GDI from C&C 3, with two twin-engines strapped to them. They are able to switch between twin Collider cannons (same but smaller cannon as the Proton Collider superweapon) and an infantry-shredding auto-gun. What ticks me off about this airborne tank is that it has a huge HP pool (oh, it also self-repairs), it shatters everything on the ground, and you'd need quite a bit of anti-air to take them down. If you let your opponent make more than 3 of these and are not aware he's rushing to build them, you can just surrender immediately before you get roflstomped. It is indeed the most expensive unit of the Allies, but it's also very cost-efficient, and can go 1v1 against a sea-landed Giga Fortress.
Grinder (Soviets): Although they fit the character of the faction, any ground forces facing these head-on is going to have a really bad time, because they are borderline impossible to beat without swarming them, and never from the front where the main melee weapon is. This is particularly an issue if you play as Allies because they're hard to escape from and are hard to retaliate against (as Allies you either swarm or use attacks from air). If you play Empire and don't field expensive ground units like King Onis, you're in the clear since you should always have Chopper VX's in your arsenal against these battleship-armor menaces. Oh yeah, these are also amphibious, but thankfully they can't grind your packed MCVs in water.
Reaper (Soviets): These are the big bad older brothers of the Sickle. What is most annoying about them is that they are a carbon-copy of Empire's flexibility when placing defensive turrets, except these can shoot back at your units constantly. Their special ability permanently entrenches them and gives them a defensive bonus, not to mention they're both anti-surface and anti-air.
Giga Fortress (Empire): Oh yeah, saved the best for the last. This sonofa♥♥♥♥♥♥ is THE most expensive unit in the entire game, but if you give the Empire player to make one or two of these, you're done for, might as well surrender before getting absolutely smashed. This unit dubs as a mobile sea fortress and a giant airborne head whose attack is also VERY long and pretty wide, doing two series of damage: when  it touches the unit and when the attack explodes a short while after. In its sea form it has 8 guns, faster-firing and more but shorter ranged version of the ones from the Shogun battleship, as well as an array of anti-air/anti-ground rockets. Be extremely wary of this if you play on a map with mini-lakes against a Empire player, because the airborne form has no anti-air capability, but once you give it the chance to get over water, the situation changes dramatically, firing back at your airborne attackers. Here is where those unit disablers (Hydrofoil with the ray gun, Rocket Angel with the para ray) are a must, and you must dish out the Harbinger Gunships/Kirvos against this, preferably when it's on the sea because in air you obviously can't hit it.
Skirmish and multiplayer are covered in my Red Alert 3 review.

An impressive needle in a haystack of crappy Sonic games, Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is truly worthy of competing with other iconic racing games for the title of "The Best One." This game will make you laugh, this game will make you cry, this game will make you rage until there is no tomorrow, but most of all, this game is addicting!
Screw all the jazzy intro speech, lets make a pros and cons list:
*I didn't bother with Online play, so I can't give an honest review of that feature.
Pros:
-Graphics are pretty darn good! crisp and clear, water is fluid and reflective, and the sun is even blinding! This is a game that will blow you away visually if you just finished a Mario Kart 64 nostalgia run.
-The music is wonderful. There isn't a single track that doesn't make me feel strange, and they all fit very well with the environment. Sound quality for SFX is great too.
-Plenty of challenges, and the game kind of evolves with you! Several different modes that will test different skills you didn't think were required to do well in each map, like drifting and boosting, and even knowing when to use a boost in the right moment. It also keeps the gameplay fresh, and you have to option of having a game with or without computers.
-Competitive AF. Coms really give you a run for your money in this game. There is no "Easy" way to beat the hardest parts of the game, and that keeps things... interesting to say the least! It also helps you to hone your skills, and learn from your mistakes.
-Downloading ghosts allows you to compete with people worldwide without ever needing to battle them directly! This also helps to learn from their driving skills, and improve your skill pool.
-Mods allow you to switch things up so you can use your favorite character on more than one track away from their standard stats. They also provide incentive for continued gameplay.
-Achievements and stickers give OCD Completionists something to do, increasing gameplay time for much longer.
-Stickers and License allow you to show off your achievements online, and can be a testament to your skill.
-Plenty of unlockable characters, many whose names echo down the halls of SEGA, and some who are just plain "WTF?" (I'm looking at you Ralph... I still don't understand why you're in this game... not that it matters. I love you.)
-Multiplayer option for local fun, just like mario kart seshes.
Cons:
-Content may seem redundant after a while, mainly I am thinking "Complete the same task on a different course" or "OKAY now beat everything all over again but we'll just increase the difficulty," (this is after you unlock expert mode)
-NO TUTORIAL!!! NO DESCRIPTION!!! REEEEEEEEE
I had to Google what I couldn't figure out by fiddling with my controller, and there's no clear direction to help you understand the basics. The game literally just throws you in and you learn through experience. I'm still not entirely sure what the All-Star stat does, but my hunch is it determines just how amazing your All-Star ability is.
-Hitboxes are irritatingly inconsistent, or just way too large. And this can work for or against you, but for someone like me who likes to drift as close to walls and around corners as I can, it sucks. Item boxes will sometimes be magnetized toward you, and sometimes you have to drive RIGHT down the MIDDLE of it to get the item. Sometimes, you will shoot a rocket or ice and think "I really shouldn't have hit them..." and sometimes Coms will hit you and you will rage "THEY SHOULDN'T HAVE ♥♥♥♥ING HIT ME!!" I have also squeezed my way through various narrows passages in plane mode, and other times I will hit what seems to be an invisible wall. Nothing makes me rage more than invisible walls... just kidding, the next thing is actually worse.
-Coms are extremely OP in Expert mode. They have a handicap for all stats, so they will move faster than you, boost faster, they will get all-stars more often, and they seldom mess up on the map.
-Coms will almost ALWAYS target you and only you, and in Gran Prix/Battle Race, it will very often feel more like 9vs.1 rather than a free for all. On expert mode, this becomes incredibly frustrating, because it is almost impossible to advance with people hitting you constantly. It forces you to play smart, and sometimes conservatively, or even recklessly... anything to win.
-In this game, you ALWAYS start in last place, even in Gran Prix mode, which is kind of a slap in the face for traditional racing games. You ALWAYS have to fight your way to the top, and in no way can you earn a 1st place start.
-All of the cons on Coms above lead into the next one: A lot of the time in expert mode, you need to rely on good luck to win, which is kind of a slap in the face to skilled players who truly know what they are doing, but are set up to lose. Even getting an All-Star is not a guaranteed win, and you will have to remain vigilant to hit those stripes first.
-Some of the voice acting for this game is just... terrible... I haven't played as every character yet, but Shadow sounds like child with a pitch filter to make him sound lower and more "evil" I suppose.
There may be more, but I can't think of anything right now.
All in all, this game is like Mario Kart, Diddy Kong Racing, and Sonic Riders all mixed and refined into an amazing and diverse product. I may have listed a lot of cons, which may be intimidating, but I am also very critical, and maybe snotty. I am still having a lot of fun playing this game, as I have a LOT of stickers to earn still, and a lot of Time Trial ghosts to beat, and A LOT of mods to unlock. (Note to others, don't choose to be a completionist... it really sucks.)
I'd give this game 8.3 out of 10. It's truly a wonderful experience, and it has it's flaws, but definitely worth the time.

Truly a masterpiece for the Ages, this gem of a game conveys the true meaning of life. I cannot recommend this beautiful work of art enough, as it has changed my life in so many ways. In the future, when historians look to study the old world, this game will not only serve as a model for history, containing an immensely detailed account of the Age of Kings itself, but also as a model of gaming for the 21st century and beyond. Gaming developers should definitely look to this game for inspiration and to know "what to do right."
In addition to the marvelous game design, the cultural elements are very accurately represented in the game, such as the English having the most broken range on their longbowmen, or the Italians and the smell of their spaghetti. In addition, the team behind the music design clearly had Mozart and Beethoven within their employ, as the soundtrack is truly astounding to witness and enjoy.
The voice acting is also beautiful, bringing to mind the marvels of the cinema age in terms of line delivery. Lines such as "I need wood," "Builden," "Gadurer," and "Get out" evoke emotions within me that I never even knew I had. "Start the game already" put me into an emotional spin. The characters themselves will embed themselves in your heart as well. When I was playing, I had the great joy of playing with none other than King Henry himself, and he personally destroyed 2,000 of the enemy's units. Truly a sight to behold.
All in all, Age of Empires II is not a game you should pass on, and ultimately, it will be the only game that ever truly mattered in the future. Seriously though, stop reading and start playing!

I just finished the game today, what a thrilling ride! So I decided to write down some of my Opinions:
- I love this story. It has an incredible writing. I must say that I watched some episodes of the Anime, but I'm quite disappointed. They are so "plain". This Novel is waaay more detailed, and more fun. That because of the "tips" which explain what's going on through the story and decode some difficult scientific definitions or weeaboo stuffs (Japanese pop culture memes). The Authors offer some serious skills, tell a complicated story about some time-travel nonsenses, but actually about friendship, love, betrayal, kindness and hopes about a better future. They also described the atmosphere of modern Japan and the lives of young Japanese people, although sometimes they mockingly criticize the lifestyle and the (weebs) "pop culture" of Jp, too.
- First 4 or 5 hours are quite boring and...dumb. Be prepared! If It's the end of Chapter 2 and you are not interested enough, maybe the game is not for you. But once you want to continue, you're going to say: "totally worth it!" in the end.
- The characters are OK. They are some typical individuals in a "Japanese Squad": A chuunibyou main guy, a genius sidekick girl, a fat Otaku guy, an innocent girl, and so on...I'm a Japanese Speaker (although I suck) and I'm quite interested in Japanese culture, but I don't find this kind of "squad" interesting. The main Heroine (Kurisu) is very popular in the Otaku Community. I think she's kind of a Mary Sue, but she's ok, loveable. Again, the characters are quite good, but not as significant as the plot.
- The game (novel) itself is well made. Although It's from 2009, but the graphic quality is quite elegant, the sounds and insert songs are top notch. It's well-dubbed and the translation is accurate. you can't play in the borderless window mode which is a down point, but there is a guide to fix that.
- In conclusion, for 40 hours of "reading", the price is totally acceptable and I really recommend it! 9/10 for the Plot and 8/10 for everything. I hope that we'll get Steins; Gate Zero soon...

It's good, but...
... it's weird. I didn't expect to play a Wolfenstein game largely for the world-building and story, but that's where you have it. It's particularly notable given my exhaustion with what I call "Nazi romanticism", where Nazi-era Germany is presented as literal sci-fi baddies, with wunderwaffen well beyond the dreams of even most ardent weiraboos... ignoring the fact that most Nazis were anti-science turds who just happened to take over during a time of a scientific boom. MachineGames takes Nazi romanticism and runs with it to all of its chilling implications - and yet undermines it, without going too far into the details. For once, I didn't mind the superNazi tropes. And shooting them. A lot.
Weirdly, though, the shooting itself is where things to start to fall a little flat even though this is probably the strongest Wolfstein gameplay to date. Though it tries to emulate the run 'n gun style of the original games, the truth is that our hero is vulnerable. So much so that the cover and optional stealth sections start to feel more mandatory, a necessity to narrow down the numbers before the guns start firing. And while I respect the stealth parts as a nod to the pre-3D Wolfenstein games, they're just too thin for the amount you're expected to do them - it's just not refined, with practically no stealth toys or tools to make it interesting. Granted, being able to dual-wield almost any gun is satisfying, and the gunfeel is solid. The problem is, it came after games like Bulletstorm and Shadow Warrior, which were much stronger nods to the run and gun playstyle with wilder options. And now that Doom is out, Wolfenstein feels a little too tame and safe. It's not exactly bad, but it doesn't stand out. The feel of a shotgun sending a Nazi flying is absolutely satisfying, but being cut down by the Nazi you didn't notice behind you in two seconds is not.
That being said, this game is the whole of its parts, and the parts work together well. The stealth may be weak, but the difficulty means mastering it can be really satisfying. The environments are beautiful and sharp, and things that may have been tiresome in other hands reinforce the story and setting. Grey concrete environments all over might be a lazy fallback in other games, but here it's a nod to the literal monolithic nature of the Nazi forces.
Overall, it's a game worth going back to if you're in the mood to gun down some particularly well-done baddies, and already have more innovative shooters like Doom, Bulletstorm, and Shadow Warrior under your belt. It reminds me to an extent of Hard Reset, a game I previously reviewed, but with a far more compelling premise and IP to work with. It's worth a lookand a play, particularly at the price point it often falls to during sales, but don't expect it to change your world; it's a very solid popcorn game that makes killing Nazis fun again.

To start: I used to add a much longer header to these reviews describing my reviewing ethos, but since it often made the review too long to submit, I've opted to leave it on my Backloggery.
Gameplay: Just to start out, I'd like to say that I'm not the greatest at platformers, but I do consider myself fairly competent  at them, considering that I got Golden God in Super Meat Boy after about 20 hours my first time through. As such, I wasn't too sure quite what to expect going into this game. I will say that this game is largely easier than what I expected, ranking in terms of difficulty around Light World Salt Factory to start and ending around Light Hell. There really wasn't too much of a difficulty curve, to be honest. However, I've also been one of those people who has been somewhat against the influx of "masochistic platformers," 'cuz they're usually not all that fun. Does this game manage to break the trend? ...kinda.
Platforming in ESJ is about as simple as it gets; you can move left and right and jump. There's no momentum to your run, and you can control the height of your jump. I will say that the game is much slower than what I expected (also maybe for a good reason, since the game doesn't handle fast scrolling all that well), which can throw you off for a bit. There's actually only three other gimmicks you get throughout the game: a slam attack that moves you straight down, allowing you to kill any enemies in your path, a double jump that you get for all of five levels and have arbitrarily taken away from you, and flight which you get for like the last three stages and that's it. There's also your standard fare of obstacles: lasers, portals, mid-air jumping arrows a-la Jumper, and a few others. The enemies are largely unimpressive and consist of enemies that either walk left to right, shoot a slow-moving projectile, or have a laser coming out of them. They're usually not a big deal at all to deal with, but the laser enemies do require a bit more precision to eliminate than they honestly should, considering that they're standard enemies. Boss fights are pretty much just about dodging projectiles and hitting the weak point.
This all sounds like pretty standard fare, right? Well... you're right. There really isn't much else to this game. There's no trial-and-error gameplay and all levels can be beaten first try if you're good enough, but there just isn't much substance to the level design. It just feels like it's going through the motions that other games went through, of which, the short length of the game certainly does not help. I got very close to completing all the stages but stopped on 4-4 because it took a design page from I Wanna Be the Boshy's design (one that I certainly do not approve of), and even then, this game only took me about three and a half hours to beat. Even as a "masochistic platformer," there really isn't much here. All the extra gameplay comes from either no-deathing or speedrunning the stages. Other than that, it's just... okay. $8 is about right as a price; it's about as long as an average movie and just as satisfying, which is to say as satisfying as peanut-flavored packing peanuts: maybe alright in your mouth for a few seconds, then you realize that it's just filler. 6/10.
Story: Ehh, the humor is take it or leave it. You could fit all the dialogue in-game onto one page of a single-spaced Word document, so I'm not gonna bother rating it.
Graphics: I'll just get the technical stuff out of the way; the game fullscreened to my native resolution of 1080p without any hassle. As far as graphics settings, you really shouldn't need them. If you do, you should probably think about updating your system. As for the graphical style, it's alright I guess? Again, this is something of a take it or leave it thing. Levels usually only have two or three colors to them (excluding black for the stage and your character), but there's a lot going on in the background. I'd again refer you to my peanut-flavored packing peanut analogy as far as my opinions go on that matter. As for the pixel art, it's fine. Nothing impressive, though. There were a few moments where the background/foreground elements hid some parts of the stage, which is always frustrating to die to something you can't see because the level designer put too much stuff in the way. Again, this is just okay at best. Passable. Average. 2/5.
Sound: Yes, they use porn star sound bytes for the checkpoints. Yes, it does get a bit annoying after a while, but I was able to drown it out. As for the music, it's loud screechy techno; if that's your thing, you'll like it. If you're like me, you'll get bored with the music and put on your own. There really isn't anything else to talk about here. 2/5.
Overall scores are: 6/0/2/2; cumulative score of 5.0/10. I've opted to lean on the side of recommendation just because there *is* some fun to be had here; it's just that it becomes so painfully mundane after a while. Not terrible, but definitely a one-and-done game, which for something as short as this, may not be good value for your money.

I really wanted to like this game.  Long review ahead.
Did I get my $10 worth?  Sure.
My PC is right in between the minimum specs and recommended specs, and so while the game itself ran okay, the achievements lagged, all the cinematics failed, and any chance to freeze was a chance taken.  So I rented a high end rig to play instead.
This is not a management game, and could hardly be called a game at all.  This is merely an idle game with a bit of interactivity requiring top of the line hardware to support useless, game interrupting, cheesy-as-hell cinematics.  The tutorial is 'hand-holdy' to the point of not showing the mechanics properly until full game, and even then the narrator comes off as condescending and infantalizing rather than seductive.
You do 3 things in this game: You walk around "fixing problems" by selecting from 2 choices on a very finite number of scenarios, which are good for a laugh the first time, but quickly become dull since there are only about 5 for each category (supposedly you get more as you unlock more, but I got most of the way unlocked and didn't see anything new).  You also purchase club upgrades which have no gameplay differences, only an annoying cinematic with each and every upgrade.  Each and every, that's right.
The last thing you do is complete "Events" which are tricky little mini-games where you click on the falling objects before they hit the bottom of the screen.  This is one of the redeeming factors in the game and the only bit of gameplay involved.  The mini-games are tough, but fair, and more than doable without cheating with a bit of practice and some top of the line hardware.
I hate to find myself disappointed in this 'game', but one of the things 'good' about it are the annoying-as-crap achievements for each and every little thing you do (which also lag the game if you aren't top-spec).  Instead of 1 achievement for "Hire 25 dancers" there are 25 achievements:  'hire 1 dancer', 'hire 2 dancers', 'hire 3 dancers'... all the way up to 25.  You did this, community.  You asked for more achievements, and you got them. *tuts*
Perhaps if this was an actual game with actual gameplay, instead of a shiny idler with boobs that's marketed as a game, it'd be really good.  I'd kill for a good strip club management/tycoon game.  Well, maybe not kill, but seriously maim.

Tales from the Borderlands is an episodic game (5 episodes), produced by Telltale Games, creators of the highly acclaimed The Walking Dead, The Wolf Among Us and many other point and click games. The complete season is already available since the last episode was released a month ago. As the name implies, the events of this game occur in the universe of the Borderlands series, being chronological situated after Borderlands 2 events. In it you take control of not one, but two highly charismatic characters - Rhys and Fiona - embarking in an adventure filled with humor, living up to this acclaimed series.
This game uses the same winning formula of the last games released by Telltale. As such, this is a game focused on the story, so there is not much to discuss gameplay-wise. The game mechanics are very identical to the rest of Telltale games, with several dialogue choices that influence the story. At first it will seem that the different choices will all have the same outcome, but at the end they will actually have a special meaning, something that I liked a lot. Quick-Time Events (QTEs) are once more present, working like a charm in the action sections, but it still feels like its little in terms of gameplay. Its also important to refer the addiction of two pretty interesting new mechanics. The first one is Fiona being able to loot money. With that money you can buy many customization items, as in the other games of this series. Playing as Rhys, you have a Cybernetic Eye which allows you to analyze several objects, providing lots of laughs since those objects have delicious descriptions. Obviously this is an extremely linear game, but it has some exploration sections once in a while, being extremely limited though.
In the games made by Telltale, the story its the most important aspect to me and in this game they really nailed it. When I first heard about this game I though it would be a simple cash-in using the name of the Borderlands series. However, it ended being a really good surprise. The characters are excellent and the chemistry between some of them almost achieves perfection. Besides the characters made by Telltale, there are some familiar faces from the previous games who fit like a charm in the story, like Zer0, Brick and Mordecai for example. The comedy in this game is another of its strong points. Few games will give you as many laughs as this one. Most of the dialogs are very well done and overall the story is very good, with some great twists and a pretty good ending too. Although focusing on comedy, the game has its share of dramatic sequences too, with an exceptional balance between comedy and drama.
In terms of visuals, this game has the distinctive cel-shading of the Borderlands series, which does the job like a charm in this game. The majority of the animations look good but some of the characters body movements still leave much to desire. The performance is also great since the graphical resources of this game are not "heavy" at all, so you will not have problems running this game.
Longevity wise, it is pretty good for a game like this. I took about 9 hours to complete, while being completety stuck to the screen every time I played because of how good this game is (lots of moments of pure action).
In the sound department, another win. The soundtrack is amazing! It complements this universe in a perfect way. Something that I liked a lot were the opening credits of each episode, all with different songs in it, being all absolutely awesome! The voice acting is also out of this world. An impressive cast that has great names like Troy Baker (Rhys), Laura Bailey (Fiona), Nolan North (August) and Ashley Johnson (Gortys). Patrick Warburton, best known for giving voice to Joe Swanson in the Tv Show "Family Guy" is also present in the game, giving voice to the character Hugo Vasquez.
9.0/10
Few games are funnier than this one! With frenetic action, awesome characters, exceptional soundtrack and voice acting and a great story, this game puts the standard for comedy games in a very high level. A must-have for those who want to laugh like a crazy man and recommended not only for those who played a game from the Borderlands series, as for those who never played.

I've only played about 45min but I'm impressed so far. I've never been a fan of CoD or Battlefield and this game isn't like them. If i had to pick a military shooter to compare it to i would probably say MAG. It is very spartan. You get a HUD that puts a marker on teammates and the locations of cap points, a rifle, and a flashlight.
Respawns in the mode that i was playing are every 2 min unless your team captures an objective or gets a kill. The lighting is very well done and the movement reminds me of doing combat glide drills. There is no insane death run sprinting, you actually have to look for targets, and from what I can tell the game doesn't screw new players by giving vets perks like increased run speed, recoil reduction, extra body armor, or a Javelin.
They mentioned a cover system, but I didn't seem to see it work (you can crouch though). However I didn't feel it was nessesary. You can hide behind cover then expose yourself fully. if you need to park and lean to get a kill stick to CoD. Camping doesn't seem to be an issue because there are 2 ways to everywhere and no gaps to be overly exploited. Also, if you park, the enemy team will capture all the points and win anyway.
Guns were basic. primary is an AR with 30 round mags, reflex sight, flashlight (optional), and laser sight (optional). I saw one gun in spec mode that had an actual scope (never found/used it though). You also have to manually reload, which I love. Didn't see any shotguns, pistols, or grenades and I'm relatively positive that there is no melee.
I didn't care for the ability to switch teams after each round without force balancing to equal numbers. I had rounds where I kicked-a** and rounds where I caught a bullet to the head right away, but it never felt one sided (save for team switching. had a 6v3 match).
Pros: Movement, lighting, weapon mechanics, basic HUD, only has 2 guns.
Cons: Team switching (to an extent), multiplayer only, only has 2 guns.
It definitely satisfies my inner need to build vehicles with guns, and then go blow up other people's vehicles with guns.
It's amazingly fun. Give it a try!

One day you find yourself marooned on a distant planet, a rimworld some would call it.
The literal butt end of ruled space that is akin to a pit stop in hell.
You are far from what you would call home, a nice glitterworld where all of your fantasies can come true.
Here your only friends are a giggling pyromaniac and some guy who thinks he is some sort of space knight.
All the other people you have meet have been drooling tribals who keep on looking at you with slightly hungry eyes.
Or space pirates who just want to maim, kill and burn everything, including you.
Also squirrels are also the most terrifying creatures imaginable, having seen a horde of them eat a man alive.
There are also very angry robots that keep on trying to blast you into atoms.
If this place has ticked any of the 'come here for a tourist visit' boxes then the people who did tick them should be rightfully sent to a 'corrective facility'.
However for some reason, somehow this place is home too you.
Heck you will be damned if someone is going to move you off of this rock.
Those that tried now have their bones scattered across your couger pen, but thats a story for another time.
While your new associates did take a while to get used too, they do seem to be pretty nice people.
You think.
Maybe.
Deep down inside they are.
At least you thought that until the day when you woke up too the sound of manical laughter as the pyro sets your bed on fire, with you still in it.
The space knight had also inconveniently decided to have a mental breakdown and start bingeing on all the potatoes you spent all summer growing.
To say you were angry was an understatement.
There was alot of repressed rage to be let loose at that moment.
Now all that remains of your 'Comrades' are being roasted on a small campfire in what now remains of your once glorious house fort thing.
The 'a mans gotta eat' saying feels a little corny thinking about it right now.
Did i also mention that you are a cannibal?

Just recently completed the game (Not going to spoil it for people who haven't played yet) I would rate this game as a 5/5.
Story Line: 5/5
The story line is fun and there are a lot of twists and turns, there is also a lot of stupidity in it as well (humurous stupidity). You will more than likely put several hours into beating the story line, because you have to level up, find weapons, complete side jobs, it's a good story and afterwards you can go back and do the other side stuff.
Content: 5/5
Along with the story, as I mentioned previously, there are a LOT of side jobs to do. Along with the DLC, you will probably spend several more hours completing all of the side jobs. You also have levels, you level up to use new weapons and advance on your skill tree (which makes you more money and helps in other things as well). There is contless hours of things to do in this game.
Character Interactions: 5/5 (Hilarious!)
It's nice to see in a game where everyone has some form of dialouge, even if you can't actually interact with some of the characters. The dialouge is funny, and the intro for some of the enemies and their dialouge can be funny as well. When I first began playing I had a good time laughing at what some of the guys would say to you.
Weapons: 5/5
You may not be able to customize the weapons, which some may see as a downside, this is made up for by having so many weapons. There are so many different weapons to choose from; including machine guns, smgs, snipers, rocket launchers, shot guns, grenades, the list just goes on. Not to mention all of the weapons have different damage rates, firing speeds, some even have elements to make them better.
This game may be a little bit of an older game now, it's still better than anything EA or Activision is making right now. As the Trailer says It's a RPFPS (Role Playing First Person Shooter). It's a wonderful game for anyone on most any PC, I can run it on a old 2009 macbook (bootcamp) that has DualCore 2.13ghz Processor, 9400m Nvidia Graphics, and 2GBs of ram, on low settings just fine! Definitely recommend this game.

This is Sega at their best. I was already a fan of the first one (played on the Xbox 360) and they made great additions in this "Transformed" version. I totally imagine this game being launched at the Dreamcast era.
This is as good as any kart game can get: good old arcade gameplay with weapons and over the top races, local multiplayer to up 4 players and colorful graphics. If you're playing alone, you can try to unlock tracks and racers to your next game party. The Death Egg + Metal Sonic DLC moved to this sequel and the package is solid: various racers, a lot of tracks and all the traditional modes. I got goosebumps with the After Burner and Golden Axe tracks. The good part of all this is the PC requirements: my laptop with the GTX 740m 2GB runs the game at 60fps (and the loads are minimal in my desktop).
Why there is no sequel to this is beyond me. I loved Sega at the 1980's and 1990's and there are still plenty of franchises to cover, like Altered Beast, Space Harrier, Fantasy Zone, Vectorman, Comix Zone and even OutRun. And they could ask to include characters from other franchises that made success at the Genesis era. Could you imagine Toejam & Earl as playable racers? You could take my money already, Sega.
Edit 11th July 2016: there is actually an OutRun Bay stage and Space Harrier is present in the Race of AGES stage in form of music and hologram reference. So, there you have it, a complete package for Sega fans.

Very repetitive. Unlike some of the Dynasty Warrior games, where you can combine light and heavy attacks to do a variety of different combos, this game has almost no variety in that regard.
The one interesting mechanic is the transformation. Transformations heal you and allow you to use your special moves, but you can only transform once per fight. It's an interesting little bit of resource management that I really liked.
Another positive point is the soundtrack. It has a bunch of rock remixes of classical music. I love it.
On the sexual nature of the game: I'm no prude, but it's a little excessive. I was very pleased to find that there were many different costumes to unlock, but I was a bit disappointed when I found out that ALL of it is geared towards various fetishes. Its very limitng, and makes the wide variety of costumes actually fairly boring. Very few of the costumes look nice outside of their sexual appeal. Even then, most of the costumes aren't really all that sexy, in my opinion. I'd be all for sexy girlfs fighting in sexy outfits. I just don't think this game does a very good job of it.
On the plus side, some of the girls default costumes look great. Yumi and Hikage's outfits are very sexy and cool, and I love Asuka's Strider-esque scarf.
Also, I don't think this is outright stated in the game, but the implication I get is that not all the girls are over the age of 18. I didn't know this until after I bought and played the game. It's a bit icky, and really unnecessary. Nothing about the story necessitates the girls being underaged. One of the younger characters is a masochist who begs other characters to beat her. Having a young teenager do something like that is a bit much, I think. I guess it's not HUGE deal, since they're just animated characters. But I know it would bother some people, so I thought it was worth bringing up.
If they refine the combat system and improve the costume options, then I could really enjoy this series. For now, though, there are better action games you could be playing, and better booby anime you could be watching.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a first person shooter Developed by Machine Games, who's internal staff have previously worked on "The Darkness" and "Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay" The game is a "soft reboot" of the series, meaning that story elements from previous games are mentioned, but it can be played standalone.
The game follows the ongoing adventure of captain William "BJ" Blazkowicz as he slaughters his way though the Nazi menace in an alternate reality 1960 where they won World War 2 and subsequently took over the world, following 1 of 2 very slightly different timelines in which BJ ether fights alongside an old war buddy or a young army private in an attempt to kill returning villain General Deathshead.
In the gameplay department, we have 16 stages of Nazis to fight through, with around 5 distinct enemy types and some VERY light puzzles. What the game lacks in enemies it more than makes up or in ways to dispatch them, featuring 8 weapons with alternating fire modes and duel wielding, including throwing knives, EMP devices, assault rifles with rocket launchers, silenced pistols, and laser weaponry. The game also offers gameplay reward perks to increase survivability, as well as health and armor boosting collectables.
All and all, I'd say The New Order is a solid above-average shooter, definitely worth looking at if you're a fan of first person shooters and/or war games.
