I would recommend being cautious about purchasing Dragon Ball Xenoverse at this moment.  While I enjoy this game greatly, it still has many issues and I'm not sure how serious they are about fixing them. I'll update my review if things change for the better.
The Negatives:
-No online play. I bought this game after being assured by an announcement that server issues were now fixed. Despite playing multiple times a day every day straight since then I have never been able to connect to their servers.
-Vague stat and power descriptions. This is a game in which you're going to spend time leveling up a character and learning techniques and acquiring gear. You'll spend a lot of time getting and trying things out which won't work for you because actual numbers and stats are usually never given to you.
-There are poor gamepad controls and poor customization options.
-AI issues. Your AI companions on PQ missions will be for the most part terrible and will just float around launching an occassional attack. AI enemies will be functional but because supposedly "hard" enemies will be easy for you to beat they'll sometimes give AI controlled fighters unlimited energy to fight with. Thus you're very likely to see someone "much more powerful" on your side getting knocked around by special power spam from a weaker version of their own self. If you have to face someone like Goku or Vegeta, keep in mind they can go super saiyan for apparently forever when they're not on your side and they will spam ultimate attacks even into their allies (no friendly fire).
-Annoying enemies. This relates to the past point. You're going to fight enemies who are supposed to be a fun and decent challenge to you. Except they won't be fun, and they will usually fail to be a challenge. The AI will instead use an emergency super block power that blows you away (you can't interrupt your attack to block), and they will use it far more often than you'd be able to (and your AI companions will never do it even if they're the same character or even a stronger character). The most difficult fights will be where you're facing multiple enemies. Unless they're completely trash they can suddenly create an explosion from themselves at any time and they can charge into you and work together to hit stun you. Even when you're significantly stronger than an enemy, you just want to enjoy beating them now that you can do so easily, and you get them in a combo, they can still use their explosive super block to interrupt and annoy you.
-Rather than go through an interesting training story to get moves, nor learn them as you see enemies use them, instead you get the worst of both worlds and the worst of random number loot drops. Bascially if you want to learn the Super Saiyan transformation technique you're going to have to grind certain missions and there's no telling when or if you'll get it as a random drop.
-Imbalanced PVP, supposedly. This is what I've seen in videos and stories and in guides. I haven't been able to do any online pvp and very limited local pvp.
-While variety in builds are good, this is Dragon Ball Z where all characters used hand to hand combat and energy blasts. The way your stats work the game encourages you to specialize into either melee or ranged.
-Limited customization and your character's aesthetics will effect your stats. The game doesn't tell you this but your hidden stats will change based on your character's weight and height. Clothing options in the game are not purely aesthetic and you may end up wanting to wear a clothing set that looks stupid just for the stat bonuses.
-The story has its issues. The new NPCs are fine but conflict with them isn't explored very well because they're all "mysterious" and the story quickly moves you from fight to fight on rails rather than have even Mass Effect dialogue options. If you like Dragon Ball Z you'll love going through all the big moments in the series, but if you're not familiar with it then the story may not mean anything to you. For example unless you've seen how Frieza acts arrogantly and seen his attrocities and sadism in the show or manga you won't enjoy getting to fight him as much as a fan of the series would. He'll just be another fight to you.
-Slow movement in town. Yes you can't fly or use your incredible super speed in town to get around and you'll be stuck walking. When grinding missions and they keep teleporting you away so you have to run around just to get back to start the mission again you're going to get annoyed.
The Postives:
-You get to play your own super powerful energy blast wielding martial artist in a fighting game version of a hack and slash RPG.
-You can do local PVP, and people have made videos showing that online pvp and cooperative missions exist. If online play cooperative and pvp can actually work that would be a big plus.
-There are lots of fun supers and ultimates to use. There's a decent enough variety of super techniques to try.
-The fighting system mostly does the job and is fairly fun even if it does have issues.

Reccommendation:
If you're a fan of RPG hack and slash mixed with fighting games and you're a fan of Dragon Ball Z, then I really recomend this game. You may not want to get the season pass yet as it's expensive and there isn't enough content to justify getting that yet.
Because of present issues with the game I'd recomend you get some other kind of action game like Borderlands or Diablo 3 unless fighting game action RPGs are your thing. The fighting game aspect is better then say DC Universe Online but it's not going to be anywhere as good as Lunia or many all out fighting games like Guilty Gear, Street Fighter, Mortal Kombat, Injustice and so forth. If present issues were fixed I'd heartly recomend this game, and I do enjoy this game, but I don't want to recommend it yet.

This game is, to say the least, a little controversial and odd. If you don't already know (which if you don't, then you were SERIOUSLY not paying attention), Senran Kagura is a game series that is highly well known for the rampent fanservice it is filled with, especially the PC and Playstation games. However, behind the naughty outfits, jiggling♥♥♥♥♥♥ and cute, slightly one note characters, this is a fun, sometimes rather complex game that is worth checking out for those who love games like Dynasty Warriors and Sengoku Basara.
Story: Pretty simple, you are in the world of shinobi, or ninja, at one of several different schools. The characters you play as are each students at these schools who are learning to be the best ninja they can be. You fight, you win, and you strip your opponents. Have fun. ;)
----------
Pros: For those who haven't already guessed, this game is very silly fun with a good fighting system and plenty of girls to choose from. The controls for handheld controllers are easy to pick up on and even helpfully explained in tutorials (if you decide to view them). The story is also pretty interesting from what I've seen so far (only played the story missions and individual missions for the characters of Hanzo Academy so far) and the characters are likeable...at least, for the most part.
But while all that is important, one of the biggest points to make about this game IS, of course, its fan service. There are MANY different outfits to choose for your voluptuous fighters, from their fighting outfits to their underwear (there's actually a Lingerie Lottery you can enter to get more) and even special accessories like glasses, animal accessories and animal paws. They can even come in a variety of colors if you're picky like that. Also, the animations in which characters have their clothes torn off can be fairly exaggerated, with most giving cries of shock while some others may actually enjoy it, with one girl being a full-blown masochist who squeals in delight as you rip away her clothes. This all helps to keep the "SEXAH" parts from feeling too weird and awkward which really does help.
----------
Cons: The big thing that will likely drive anyone away from this game is, of course, the very thing I was just talking about, the fan service. If you are very uncomfortable with that, or consider it too tasteless, then you probably won't enjoy playing this game. This can be exasterbated by the fact that, while it's not openly stated, the girls are basically high school girls, which makes it rather squicky that you can put them into thongs, or a "Naughty Apron" outfit, etc. Granted, it never goes so far as to let players actually SEE nipples, butts, or nethers, but it will undoubtedly feel weird for some.
Also, not all of the characters are enjoyable to play as, with some easy targets being Hibari and Minori, who are both immature and unfortunately short ranged, or the girls of Hebijo Academy if you prefer the more lighthearted storylines.
And finally, the controls for keyboard are very awkward and difficult to use. If you don't have a good USB controller or prefer to play using the keyboard exclusively, then you'll likely find this game difficult to handle.
----------
All in all, I find the game enjoyable and fun for anyone who likes third person hack n slash beat'em ups. The customization can be fun to play around with, the fighting is pretty good, and the story is fairly easy to understand while having slight complexities to it. But I would recommend you at least watch someone play the game first before you buy, such as Gaijin Gamers.

So this game has been getting a lot of negative feedback and I really have no idea why. I get that people are lazy or don't have the patience to get their♥♥♥♥♥kicked for a few hours of grinding before they get some of the big boy toys. I haven't seen a pay wall or any other such nonsense either. Yes you can drop a few bucks to accelerate the grind and you can drop a lot of money to buy toys that take a long time to create but, it will cost you. If you decide to do the grind it isn't bad at all you just have to understand that their is a learning curve and a skill gap on some matches.
This game is truly a piece of work and I can't wait to see what comes next from the devs. It is everything I wanted in this type of game and I find the challenge to be satisfying. The crafting is rewarding and the learning curve is difficult but, manageable. Some people think this game is too hard, well this game is not for those people. This game is hard and take skill, dedication, and some cunning to win. It takes good communication and planning to win the matches. All of this is very doable even if you are facing the "Wallet Warriors from Hell".  So I say to you that this game is freaking awesome and I would challenge you to stick it out and give it another go. Once you get your first blue crafting done it is extremely satisfying to continue. Yes there is a grind it's a free to play and that doesn't make it a bad game. The only things I would change in the current build of the game is the matchmaking timer, the AI being randomly good or terrible, and the Power Score gap in some matchmaking when the search takes to long broadens the range of people it selects.
So get in here and check this game out. I would give it a solid 4 stars out of 5.

Where to begin with this game?
From game ending Manhunter packs of Boomalopes to peaceful work days, RimWorld is a Rollercoaster of game. Many of my first colonies were doomed from the start, lasting only a few weeks or even days, mainly due to ignoring the Tutorial prompts.
RimWorld is like your Mother on drugs. You never quite know what mood she is in. One day, she might bombard you with mortar fire, other days she may send a care package full of raw yorkie meat. Or maybe both. But you make the most outta what she gives you, and push through. RimWorld is about making the most out of a really bad situation.
While the updates are slow,
, the content upon an update are impactful and meaningful. Rimworld also supports a wonderful and active modding community that adds to the replay value of the game.
On a side note, I enjoy playing RimWorld as much as I do listening to my friends play this over voice chat, and hearing the problems caused by a Pyromaniac setting everything ablaze or an Infestation occuring in their mountain base.

I'm going to be honest andsay that steam needs to have an undecided or "mixed" option for recommendations.
To be straight and to the point, this game has an extreme grind to get the things that you want. The only way to bypass this is to equip a fuel tank and farm fuel and sell that to other players for gold to buy what you want. Other than that you'll spend weeks trying to grind that one item for your vehicle all the while facing people that already have their things which is not okay.
To top that off this game has some serious balance issues. For example, this is a game about blowing [edited] up, yet, the easiest way to win is by capping and you can't reset the cap so instead of going by who destroyed the most vehicles if you have more cap points (there are 3 bars and once a bar is filled it cannot be reset and taking damage does not reset the current bar either) it goes by who threw in the towel and capped for the win. Stop this and fix it. It ruins the game.
Some weapons are just poorly balanced. Why use weapon A when weapon B does the same thing but better? More balance issues are with the cannons. If you get hit you might as well call it GG. Some shots are serious skill shots but if they're close enough you're probably not going to fair very well. Also I found the shotguns to be a waste of space the higher you go because of their stupidly high resource costs. They are already balanced by their low uptime, low damage output at long ranges, and high reload times they don't need to be restricted any further.
I could go on and on and on and on about a lot of the gripes that I have with the game because there are a lot and they haven't fixed these since beta and it makes me very unsatisfied with the product that had a lot of potential to be good.

EVE Online, so much to say about it, so much to do once you pass the steep learning curve. A sandbox space mmo, 13 years in the making, still evolving and very time demanding. But so rewarding in the end.
You will be amazed, you will fear, cry, be proud, be merciful and merciless, be an opportunist, be a savior, a destroyer, you will be something and feel so many emotions that games don't usualy put you through.
The hardest thing is maybe choosing a path, crafting your style. Create or join fleets and corporation, be a rivals, allies, just be and do what you please: raid and destroy/pillage others or follow the rules of your empire and corporations.
Explore, Trade, Fight anyone (factions, corporations, random players) and for anyone, Haul, Build, Mine or even spin your ship if you want to !
Do as you want and specialise in what you want, do something and excel in it, or do multiple things and be average in them, you will have to choose or you will have to invest time.
Time is the only way you gain experience and get skilled. You will play for years and still learn, you may think you know it all but you'll still be amazed at how much you still don't.
Talk, study, discover and learn the game, explore the game at your own pace.
Bigger is NOT Better in EVE Online, every ship and class has it's role and it's variations, any ship is useful in a way, the combat system is full of details, of counters, learning how to fight will take some time but when you grasp it it's probably the best tense pvp you will ever have, it's brutal, it's cunning, it's rewarding and punishing. Don't fly what you cannot afford to lose, keep that in mind.
I could talk about EVE for hours and hours without telling you everything there is to it.

I never bother with reviews but this game deserves a review for how garbage the checkpoint system is. The art style is easy on the eyes and while the mechanics were simplistic at first sight, they were made challenging by implementing them in a manner which limited you as well. Your only means of attack requires a heavy charge up which leaves you completely vulnerable and your dash helps you moveabout the arena to dodge around for the first few minutes to help you get a feel for what the boss is throwing at you.
The game drew me in with its well implemented mechanics but I have to say that I could barely get past half an hour into the game after the first three bosses (which weren't too challenging but were pretty interesting visually).
The game has this one anooying and what should be an easily fixable flaw which made me realize I won't be able to put up with it if I wanted to get through the entire game and I just quit early. The respawn mechanic.
It is by far the most, and probably the only, infuriating part of the game. Every time you die you have to go through these really sluggish load screens which send you back to the starting point and you have to make a trek towards the boss, which might I add is rage inducing when you spam roll to get there quicker and just bump into obstacles and knock yourself back. The Then loading up each boss takes up another few seconds and it just adds to the entire sluggish feel of retrying bosses. This might be fine for the first few bosses which do not require you to traverse great lengths, but I knew that once I trudge on and die trying to figure out what the later bosses do I would have to keep tracking back for some arbitrary indie artistic game design decision.
I love games when they are challenging and I like this game but the lack of an instant reload once you die absolutely kills the pacing. I mean would it be out of place if the game just put you outside the boss chamber entrance to not make me want to smash buttons in frustration before I even reach the boss?

This is for all of you who are lost and don't know which game to get and which game is what and how it all works.
This is kind of a comparison between this game and the new ones giving you an idea what each game offers.
I'd say this is the ultimate version of Trackmania. Has ALL content from previous games and MORE. Including stuff other than tracks. Does not include content from newer titles which means all of Trackmania 2 Enviroments and Trackmania Turbo.
(Trackmania Turbo and Trackmania 2 have same enviroments but Trackmania 2 sells them seperate and they have standard visuals while Trackmania Turbo has that arcady twist on visuals, worse track editor and no Dedimania)
It has dated graphics while Trackmania 2 and Turbo have amazing visuals for their time which look very good today and get updated. Trackmania United forever however does not recieve updates. TMUF also doesn't have the new Lagoon, Canyon and Valley enviroments which are in Tm2 and Tm Turbo. But it does have the Stadium one which all of Trackmania games on steam have.
TMUF enviroments: Stadium, Island, Coast, Bay, Rally, Desert & Snow
TMUF Stadium enviroment has normal tracks like other enviroments but also has all tracks from the free 2 play Trackmania Nations.
TMUF also had an update which added "Star" tracks for all enviroments which makes this game have the most content out of all TrackMania games by far.
Trackmania 2 and Turbo enviroments: Stadium, Canyon, Valley & Lagoon
These verions have completely new tracks excluding the ones from all previous titles and also have completely diffrent tracks from eachother.
Let me describe the TM2 & TM Turbo enviroments using enviroments from TMUF:
Stadium speaks for itself. It's the same exact thing with better graphics, slightly different visuals (example: boost now makes blue fire come out of your exhaust) and a few textures changed (other than being higher resolution obviously).
Canyon is a mixture of desert, island and coast.
It has a Desert-ish enviroment.
Cars can tip over sometims like in Desert even though they look like badass muscle cars.
It's mostly about precise drifting which makes it comparable to Coast but in this case it's at very high speeds, the drifting is very controllable and precise compared to Coast.
And last but not least it's comparable to Island because it can have very high speed tracks that make you go over huge distances in a short time, huge ramps, jumps, loops etc.
Valley is like a spiritual successor to rally but it's much more engaging, beautiful and harder.
Similar types of track but driving on the road has much more understeer, dirt makes you drift and oversteer. It also has mud/water roads which slow you down.
Lagoon is like Bay + Island.
High speeds, very controllable and grippy cars. Very similar enviroment to Bay but it also has magnetic tracks.
Hope this helped.

First thing of the bat to say is, that EVE is not for everyone. Yet for those who fall in love with it, it's a love for life. Most people will be repulsed by combat system which many call "simple" or "spreadsheets in space", but believe it or not it's one of the most complex and adrenaline fueled combat system in any MMO (talking about PvP), where when you loose, it has consequences much larger that having to run for your corpse from nearest graveyard.
In most MMO's you pick your class and all that stuff and then you grind yourself to top level along the path that everyone has to take, only to arrive at max. level, grind your gear and wait for next expansion, while meanwhile leveling your alts, in EVE you literally can take any path you want, from mining and production to running missions and incursions, from flying in a small gang pvp to large scale battles that gaming websites around the world then write about. And since all this is fueled by imagination and interaction between players, you have literally endless things to do without the need to wait for authors to release new content.
The other big factor that many have heard about, is the option to pay for your game time with ingame currency. It combines all the good stuff from classic subscription based models with the ability to play for free without the annoying stuff from F2P titles. At first the price for one month in the ingame currency might seem high, but give the game a few months and whatever path you choose you will be able to play for free without a lot of effort, or pay for multiple accounts.

Hold up, I didn't make a review for this yet? Well that's gotta change, even if it's just a quick two cents.
Have you ever liked a kart game in your LIFE? Yeah there's no bloody reason NOT to add this too your collection. Even if you've not been big on em and can catch it on one of the many low priced sales, you're gonna have some fun. Kart games like this are a fun romp weather you're a fast kinda guy, or even at least the roll through for some slower types who just might like the chance to get fast.
Every track is like a ride through a theme park attraction with some really nice views and imaginative design. It feels like how Sega use to feel and that's at no lacking to the grand theme part like approach to the tracks. Each track is themed to a Sega classic past and there's a lot of memories to dip into. Some of you may not remember a couple of them like 'Burning Rangers' yet if you do it's a warm fuzzy feeling. With that said, you might even get your mind jogged to say; hey, that sounds like a cool game idea, then go look up at the treasure past. In the case of 'Burning Rangers' it's not every day you see a game about sci fi fire fighters with propultion gear to quickly get around and extinguishing flames. It was a worthy ride that only ever got one installment back on the Saturn.
The controls are as good as I've ever seen in a cart game and a drifting system that you can actually carry over pent up boost from one direciton slide to the other and get really crafty with it. A game that's easy to pick up, a damn good time to Master, and yet the progress of that mastery feels so very continious. Take your rides online and you'll still feel it. You WILL get better and each track really helps keep it interesting along with the unlockable cars and their characters.
Items and power ups are also imaginative in the ways SEGA use to be, and hopefully some day will be again. A boost that finishes with a heat meter that you time for the best competitor slowing explosion, and making sure you vent that blast before you harm yourself pushing that engine attachment. All kinds of weapons, some good catch up toys to keep it tight but not nearly the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t levels we've seen in some Mario Kart games, though I still love em, and the boost chains, ground pads and otherwise, STACK! That's right the boosts actually chain together and stack in power as you use the drift boost, the boost pads, and anything else for a color coated rush of wonderment.
It's stunning, fairly resorce friendly for that gorgious look, it's fun for so many reasons by characters, tracks, remixed music, item ideals, and then we didn't even get to the big name sake yet, the transformed factor which can be a great point and one of the few considered down sides at times. Personally I love hammering some boat segments, it reminds me of Hydro Thunder. And in Land, sea, and air, you will also do more options to boost in some tricks and rings Tricks in the water off of jumps, off of waves and enough drops to fit them in, again you can get creative, the better you get, and fitting it in is done with a good flick of the right analog stick for those of you with microsoft controllers or others comparable.
Yes, seriously, play with a controller, it's an arcade racer for racing god's sakes.
So what's the real fault here? Well some of the menu design could be a lil better organized, and it's like the origional design for ease of joining your online friends doesn't quite work as intended. Thankfully however you'll figure this crap out pretty easy. You do it once, you're good for a long while, and racing with friends is a blast and it's done well for a kart game when you're actuallyon the track. last I recal the steam style of joining lobby games still works just fine anyhow. You WILL find your friends, trust me. Just don't let what looks like an obvious snafull in it's origional design make you think you're not going to get to your friends.
Well, I suppose that's most of it. Anything I missed is likely to be pleasent surprises. Even if you get beat a lot, it's still a marvel to look at, you'll have some fun, and if you keep at it, I promise you, you will get better, as said. Need a break from some of the online people? There are a LOT of fun things to unlock and level up. Levels you can unlock at the bare minimum and go back to further challenge yourself when you get better, to extend into farther reaches of unlocks later, the level trees work well like that. And there's also more than just racing there. Passing challenges, boost challenges, drifting chain challenges, there's a lot here to keep it diverse for a closed track racer.
So the bugs? Every once in a long while an online game locks up in the menu, something seems to go funnywith a server and one time I could almost swear the lobby was hacked to say something really silly that I got a laugh out of. But that's it. If there are hackers, it's certainly not on the regular and not malicious. Sometimes it's good to have an older great game that runs well thus and not in the lime light to be a hacker's concentration zone. There's just that one off in lobby play when something goes squirly but otherwise very well behaved. And I know every so often, I still come back to it. And this is coming from someone who also decimated pretty much all of the game on the Vita, then got it on STEAM, and come back to play some more.
Well I guess that was more words than just a little, but this was deffinately a game worth speaking about. There will always be a place in my heart for games that put fun factor on high and with good mechancis and theme to do it, and this  was one of those last Sega tittles to really do it right in an age where it seemed like SEGA just couldn't bring much else other than sonic tittles that were falling short time and time again. Even the PVP options available can be fun when you get a few playing and more imaginative with the pvp combat modes than Mario Kart has ever been able to push. It's not something a lot of people play a lot anymore, but I think you'll agree they did it better than Mario.
So pick this one up, we're going to see where old giant companies like SEGA and CAPCOM wind up sooner than later. Part of e wonders if Nintendo might sell off the Mariners baseball team ownership they still have for some reason and just either take majority control of Capcom, Sega, or Both. If my educated guess of curriosity comes true it's going to be worth a lot of kudos to me, and though I hate most monopolies, I think Nintendo could really make good ont he likes as they focus on their own IP's and give them love much of the time. They just need to stop forcing the movement controls thing down our throats too hard. It may have cost them on the recent StarFox tittle as of this writing, but that's a whole nother conversation.
Short version; This game is one of the best kart games since kart games of it's kind been a thing. It's a surreal great adventure theme part of what made SEGA great on every track and a good imagination and sound to back it up.
Get it when you can swing it. You just really can't go wrong here by now.

Some of the PROS and CONS of my Red Alert 3 Review are still applicable in the expansion. You can read it here:
Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3 Uprising is the stand-alone expansion to the RTS game 'Red Alert 3', which has been released by Electronic Arts in 2008. This expansion features new units, new campaign missions, new skirmish maps and new live action characters (most notably, professional wrestler Richard Morgan "Ric" Fliehr)
The story takes place where the events of Red Alert 3 resulted in a canonical Allied Victory. The Soviet campaign involves the Soviets attempting to stop the European Union President's plans to remove the Soviet Union from history with the help of an Allied Military Contractor called FutureTech. The Allied campaign focuses on pacifying remaining Imperial Commanders who still resist allied occupation of Japan. The Empire campaign is based on defeating Soviet Commanders who seeks to have a land grab of Imperial Territory while the Empire is vulnerable. A special campaign is also available where the player takes on the role of Imperial Commando Yuriko Omega and her origin story.
+ New Campaign Missions but...(See CON #1)
+ Yuriko Campaign is an interesting twist to the C&C formula although borrowing heavily from StarCraft's 'single unit' missions
+ New units that are both powerful and fun to use
+ Fun new game mode: 'Commander's Challange'
+ Stand-alone
- Short campaign with under developed plots
- Campaign coop (even the coop AI) was removed
- New units caused severe balance issues that resulted in...
- Removal of Multiplayer, both LAN and Online
- Removal of Skirmish live action cutscenes (which I found very entertaining in the base game)
- Live action cutscenes were lazily made
- Forces players to play the Soviet Campaign first before unlocking the 2 other campaigns (which was not the case with Red Alert 3)
- Expensive for an expansion with several features removed from the base game (like multiplayer)
NICE LITTLE EXPANSION but does not live up to the quality or scale of Red Alert 2's expansion; Yuri's Revenge. Red Alert 3 Uprising is not a bad game
. Despite having said that, the game feels as though it was rushed with many of its elements (particularly the Campaign), being half baked.
The removal of Multiplayer, caused by poorly balanced units, is one of the greatest sins anyone can do to an RTS game, even if its just an expansion. This prompts me to say that Red Alert 3 Uprising does not warrant its full price considering that it's currently priced the same as the Base game. BUY IT on a SALE or BUNDLE but NEVER at FULL PRICE.
Why do I still RECOMMEND this game? Well I particularly enjoyed the Commander's Challenge (more than the Campaign actually) It gave me several hours of fun. I DO NOT RECOMMENDED this game if you're looking to play Multiplayer.

I never bother with reviews but this game deserves a review for how garbage the checkpoint system is. The art style is easy on the eyes and while the mechanics were simplistic at first sight, they were made challenging by implementing them in a manner which limited you as well. Your only means of attack requires a heavy charge up which leaves you completely vulnerable and your dash helps you moveabout the arena to dodge around for the first few minutes to help you get a feel for what the boss is throwing at you.
The game drew me in with its well implemented mechanics but I have to say that I could barely get past half an hour into the game after the first three bosses (which weren't too challenging but were pretty interesting visually).
The game has this one anooying and what should be an easily fixable flaw which made me realize I won't be able to put up with it if I wanted to get through the entire game and I just quit early. The respawn mechanic.
It is by far the most, and probably the only, infuriating part of the game. Every time you die you have to go through these really sluggish load screens which send you back to the starting point and you have to make a trek towards the boss, which might I add is rage inducing when you spam roll to get there quicker and just bump into obstacles and knock yourself back. The Then loading up each boss takes up another few seconds and it just adds to the entire sluggish feel of retrying bosses. This might be fine for the first few bosses which do not require you to traverse great lengths, but I knew that once I trudge on and die trying to figure out what the later bosses do I would have to keep tracking back for some arbitrary indie artistic game design decision.
I love games when they are challenging and I like this game but the lack of an instant reload once you die absolutely kills the pacing. I mean would it be out of place if the game just put you outside the boss chamber entrance to not make me want to smash buttons in frustration before I even reach the boss?

Not sure why there are so many negative reviews recently. It's a gaijin game, and free to play at that. Of course there is going to be somewhat of a wall that would save you time if you spent money. I have maybe 70 hours of the game(played before steam release), haven't spent any money and at the moment have enough assets to be able to get almost any item, barring extremely expensive things or end-game weapons.
The game is pay to win? How? You can spend money in the game to get the regular currency, or a design for a vehicle with some tier 2 weapons to go along with it. I am not aware of anywhere where I am unable to get something another player has because I don't pay money.
People bringing in advanced items to lower powerscores? To that I say learn to play the game better. Do they bring a big cannon? Shoot the tires off their vehicle and avoid driving in front of it. Do they bring bigger machine guns? They can only bring one, at best two higher tier machine guns. These are also bigger targets, and you only have 2 guns to shoot off instead of 4-5. I will say the hurricane (TOW missile) is a little OP as it can one-shot low tier vehicles if they take a hit to the side, but once you are aware there is one it is easy to hide for the next one, then find the owner. Again, shoot off the gun first and it is no longer a threat.
I literally run all common items on my truck except for a blue gas tank which doesn't affect performance when exchanging fire, and I get mvp generally 1/3 games on my team. If the enemy team brings in higher tier weapons to the match, good. It honestly makes them easier to kill in most cases as they have fewer weapons to shoot off/avoid.
I can't speak for the balance at PS 3000 and up, but if you go above that I'm assuming you know the game somewhat and have better items, so it is your reponsibility to be smart with what you use. The only thing that you can't really counter is when a group of 3-4 runs drone builds, anything else there is almost always something you can do to beat it.
I will say it is a bit of a hurdle for a new player to get the money to rent a workbench, as it's quite expensive at first for starting out with basic things. Honestly though I've only rented a workbench once and gotten everything else I've ever wanted off of the market. Unless you want achievements, I honestly don't see the point of crafting items as generally you craft items at a loss anyways. Go play some brawls and sell some of the scrap you get though. It will set you up with enough money to buy a few Tier 2 items which you can use to complete missions for more items.
Just buy it on sale and play it.

The story of
is in no way new. There's treasure! Treasure so large and so old that there are stories about it. These stories attract treasure hunters. And then there's the uncountable number of enemies and inhabitants between the treasure hunters and the treasure. Do the treasure hunters give up? Naaah, they use guns. Lots and lots of guns. And one little annoying robot that somehow manages to survive and make it to the sequel. The characters of
manage to stay fun and interesting and very much unique which is actually surprising considering that at the end of the day they could all be using the exact same type of gun.
The main HUD is minimal and even blended in to the start of the story. The other menus aren't that fortunate though and until the user gets used them they will feel very clunky and unintuitive. This is to be expected with console ports but a menu overhaul or revamp would've been hugely appreciated. The feel of the controls is however very reliable and satisfying. Itemization focuses mainly around offense as there are no actual pieces of clothing or armor that can be found and worn. The amount of randomized weapons and the absolutely ridiculous number of enemies are what makes Borderlands feel like a hack-and-slash. The experience gain, skill trees, quest progression, open world and legendary items are what makes it feel like an action-role-playing-game. The fact that all those weapons are guns, that a lot of bosses have guns and that even the vehicles have guns are what make it a first-person-shooter. And all of these elements make it very fun.
The graphic style is one my favorites and as such, I can find no fault in it, although others might. The protagonists, the other characters, the world, the weapons are all very well made and blend in. There is no element that actually stands out. The music always fits the setting flawlessly, the sound effects are crystal clear and nothing users wouldn't expect and the voice acting is spot on as well. The protagonists do not really seem to interact that much with each other and that's a shame.
For a first-person-shooter all the controls are spot on as well and the integration with the protagonists' unique skills has no drawbacks. The options menus are not at all surprising considering that
is coming from a console port and the only main issue I found is the lack of an integrated Field of Vision option. There are a lot of Achievements but many of them will be reached by completionists without any issues. The others however, may take a little bit of work, depending on skill and luck.
Finally, all I can say is: join the Vault Hunters, visit exotic Pandora, meet strange psychos, then shoot them.

X-Wing is not a perfect game. It is the first in a series of four games and therefore had basically all of the growing pains; the worst game engine, a story much worse than its follow up (TIE Fighter), a less than intuitive menu UI (I personally don't think this was fixed until the third game; X-Wing vs TIE Fighter), but... it's still a very fun game. The story goes from just after the first death star was nocked out on until Hoth and it's an enjoyable ride.
My recommendation is to use the Collector's CD-ROM version which uses the game engine from TIE Fighter instead of the less than great original one; same as with TIE Fighter there is a MIDI based soundtrack that adjusts to recent events. Enemy reinforcements arrived? Scary music. Dogfight? Exciting music. Just took out a TIE Interceptor? Uplifting music that fades back to the exciting music because you're still in a damned dogfight. It's great, though it is graphically inferior to the Remastered edition that uses a version of the X-Wing vs Tie Fighter Engine and the accompanying increased graphical improvements. The Collector's CD-ROM version also has great voice overs though it suffers from the low bit rate it was obviously recorded at.
Long story short: Collector's CD-ROM is the best. Remastered is prettier but misses out on some neat features. Classic is bleh (it's basically a prototype to build up to making the TIE Fighter engine and game).
Technical Side notes:
There is an XWA wrapper required to get the Remastered version working 100% correctly and a launch option of -softwarecursor must be set as well.
just paste it in your remastered folder for X-Wing.
You may have to fiddle with some DOSbox settings for some of the versions to get the correct sized window or what have you but it isn't anything particularly complicated. A good 4:3 window size I like to use is 960x720.
If you have issues with the initial screen doing the joystick calibration on launch; alt+c during a mission or training will launch the in engine calibration and you can do it then.

There is one urk I found. These are the joysticks/gamepads I own:
Logitech Attack 3
XBOX 360 Wireless
Logitech Gamepad F310
I tried all of these controllers as my X-Wing was running into the proving ground platforms. It's not until I went into the Game Controller settings (in Windows) where I could configure my controller that I figured out what I could do. You have GOT to play this game!
It doesn't matter if you're a fan of adventure games or Borderlands, you should not miss this experience.
I'm not even sure where to start, but this is probably Telltale's best game yet. It is just so well written, it will grip you and never let you go.
The story starts out simple enough, but it will take you to unexpected places, with twists and turns. Some you will see coming, others are completely outlandish but you'll enjoy all of them. It has a lot of humour (it had me laughing out loud, literally), it's action-packed and also manages to be warm and relatable. Whatever cliches it may contain, they are rendered moot by the characters themselves pointing them out.
Which brings me to my next point: the characters. They are well fleshed out, very well written and feature excellent voice over. The delivery of the lines is perfect and helps draw you in, be it with jokes or simply the cool factor. There are several Borderlands characters being featured (some of them with very suprising developments) but you don't need to have played Borderlands to understand what is going on (although it definitely helps :) ). Also a big thumbs up for the soundtrack. Great music choices.
In terms of gameplay mechanics, the game is based mostly on QTEs but I guarantee that you will not get bored. There are several cool gimmicks inserted at various points into the game that make the QTEs extremely satisfying. There are all sorts of references to pop culture and other media, especially in Episode 5. I wish I could tell you, but the spoiler would be too great, that stuff needs to be experienced first hand :D
Although I clocked in about the same amount of time as with previous Telltale games, Tales from the Borderlands seemed a lot longer and definitely more satisfying. There is just so much going on and so much fun, I was very sad to see it end. I'm definitely keeping my fingers crossed for a sequel.
So please, for the love of all that you hold dear, do yourself a favor, enrich your life and play this game :)

A great TellTale adventure game set in the Borderlands universe.
If you have played any of the recent TellTale games than you know their format, which more or less is a visual novel with a few puzzles, rooms, and choices.  This isn't to imply that they are bad, just that they have less interaction than most games.  So if that sounds of that throws you off, than you should avoid this game, since no amount of charm or production value is going to win you over.  With that said, Tales from the Borderlands is one of, if not the, best TellTale adventure games.
The reason for that is that the game has high production values (musical intros, good VO, and great recap sequences), good writing (funny dialogue, likeable characters, dramatic moments)  and nice visuals (art, animation, and cut scenes). The game has so many things going for it, and only a few going against it.
The only thing that I personally dislike about the game was that it was overly positive. There is some lose and pain, but for the most part, everything works out for everybody. And that kind of undercuts the serious moments and ideas from the game.
Overall if you like TellTale adventure games, or point and click adventure games in general, then I think you should pick up this game.  It has a few flaws, but nothing that ruin the experience.

This is my first Telltales game.  I am just conflicted enough that I am going to post a quick review.  I'm recommending this game with some reservations.
First off, this game feels less like a game than a pick your own adventure movie.  The biggest gameplay are dialog choices and quick time events ala Dragon's Lair or Braindead 13.  When I started the game I played through one episode and quit, wanting something more interactive at the time.
I came back after a few days though, because the story is great.  I'm not entirely sure the dialog and writing are perfectly in line with the Borderlands universe, but I enjoyed it immensely.  One thing I have to say is that the folks at Telltale Games are masters at the art of storytelling.  One of the things under the hood that took me a little while to notice is that your choices can dramatically affect the dialog and the scenes that you play through.   For a game that you can play through in eleven hours, there is a ridiculous quantity of content hidden away behind the choices you don't make.
One thing I found really amusing about the game, is that every episode is introduced by Marcus in his storytelling style, and about a third into each episode there is a musical interlude similar to what starts each Borderlands game.  Telltale really pulled out all of the stops in trying to make this feel like a Borderlands game without actually being in the same genre.
In short (why do people always put this at the end of a review?) this game is a great example of storytelling over gameplay.  If you are looking for more of the Borderlands universe and don’t necessarily want the gameplay I'd say you should pick it up without hesitation.  If you want more run and gun fun and don't really care about the story, take a pass.  If you are somewhere in the middle I get the impression that this is a good place for a Borderlands fan to get a taste of what Telltale games are like.  Regardless of whether you like this style of game or not, there is probably enough Pandora in here to make the game an overall positive experience.

I don't read a lot of Japanese visual novels. Apart from a few well known series like Danganronpa, Zero Escape, and Phoenix Wright, I can count the rest on one hand; and none of the previously mentioned are "pure" visual novels since they have a lot of gameplay elements mixed in to make them more engaging for a broader demographic.
Seeing STEINS;GATE during a Steam sale, I was skeptical at first since the last true VN I read was marginally disappointing and soured my expectations for anything similar, but I decided to give it a chance all the same, and I can wholeheartedly say that I'm very glad that I did.
The first few chapters are a bit slow to build momentum, but the bountiful tidbits of science and the over-the-top characters kept me interested. At times, it felt like not much was going on, and the things that did happen were completely random, but in hindsight, the lengthy buildup is understandable since the story has a lot of rules to establish thanks to the time travel theme, as well as how the characters interact and relate to each other, which varies depending on the current timeline.
That being said, once I hit chapter 5...my god, did STEINS;GATE get GOOD! The story does a complete tonal shift and I quite literally could not stop myself from speed reading all the way to the very end. I just HAD to know if everyone achieved their happy ending; their perfect world. Almost all of the endings are so emotionally charged, I couldn't help but tear up each and every time. I never thought I'd care so much for these characters, and the raw emotion from just the spoken dialogue alone is so beautiful. I can't imagine STEINS;GATE working as anything other than a visual novel.
It's been a long time since I've become so invested in a story, so drawn to so many charming and lovable characters. I won't spoil the endings of anything else, but if you're a casual reader or an anime fan who loves crazy Japanese characters, science and time travel, and emotional storytelling, then I give STEINS;GATE my most enthusiastic recommendation~

Trackmania's a game about repetition. You do a track, do it again, do it again, and do it again until you've mastered it. Then you move on to the next track. The crazy roller-coaster tracks you need to navigate keep this cycle of repetition more interesting than any other racing / time-attack game I can think of. There's also a lot of variety in the types of cars you race, which keep it fresh. One drives like a F1, another like a hotwheels on bath salts and meth with butter for wheels, and another that has more in common with a topheavy aardvark than a car. Not to mention the different modes of Race, Platform, and Stunt that operate on a different scoring system than each other, which just adds to the replayability.
There's a♥♥♥♥♥♥tonne of customization
and fan-made levels, which pretty much makes this game immortal; it'll never get old. And even 9 years later I'd say the graphics hold up pretty well, too.
There aren't a lot of things that ♥♥♥♥ with me in this game, save for the fact that the camera occasionally switches positions mid-race, which will no doubt ♥♥♥♥ you up. Usually it's not a very big problem and just adds to the challenge of memorizing a track's quirks and little traps, but sometimes it can result in some game-breaking situations like not being able to see where you're going right before a massive jump and you just end up plummeting into the sea or slamming into some rock-hard palm trees.
There's not a lot of up-to-date content on the in-game browser, so you're way better off just ignoring the in-game currency of 'coppers' and just download♥♥♥♥♥♥online.
This game's totally worth it, though. If you like racing / time attack games, buy it immediately.

The story of
is in no way new. There's treasure! Treasure so large and so old that there are stories about it. These stories attract treasure hunters. And then there's the uncountable number of enemies and inhabitants between the treasure hunters and the treasure. Do the treasure hunters give up? Naaah, they use guns. Lots and lots of guns. And one little annoying robot that somehow manages to survive and make it to the sequel. The characters of
manage to stay fun and interesting and very much unique which is actually surprising considering that at the end of the day they could all be using the exact same type of gun.
The main HUD is minimal and even blended in to the start of the story. The other menus aren't that fortunate though and until the user gets used them they will feel very clunky and unintuitive. This is to be expected with console ports but a menu overhaul or revamp would've been hugely appreciated. The feel of the controls is however very reliable and satisfying. Itemization focuses mainly around offense as there are no actual pieces of clothing or armor that can be found and worn. The amount of randomized weapons and the absolutely ridiculous number of enemies are what makes Borderlands feel like a hack-and-slash. The experience gain, skill trees, quest progression, open world and legendary items are what makes it feel like an action-role-playing-game. The fact that all those weapons are guns, that a lot of bosses have guns and that even the vehicles have guns are what make it a first-person-shooter. And all of these elements make it very fun.
The graphic style is one my favorites and as such, I can find no fault in it, although others might. The protagonists, the other characters, the world, the weapons are all very well made and blend in. There is no element that actually stands out. The music always fits the setting flawlessly, the sound effects are crystal clear and nothing users wouldn't expect and the voice acting is spot on as well. The protagonists do not really seem to interact that much with each other and that's a shame.
For a first-person-shooter all the controls are spot on as well and the integration with the protagonists' unique skills has no drawbacks. The options menus are not at all surprising considering that
is coming from a console port and the only main issue I found is the lack of an integrated Field of Vision option. There are a lot of Achievements but many of them will be reached by completionists without any issues. The others however, may take a little bit of work, depending on skill and luck.
Finally, all I can say is: join the Vault Hunters, visit exotic Pandora, meet strange psychos, then shoot them.

Titan Souls is a boss rush game that plays around its main gimmick heavily, that being the instagib life system: You one shot the enemies, yet you yourself are killed instantly as well if they land a hit on you. You play as a small boy thrust into a world with practically no backstory as to who you are or how you got there. You can sprint, roll, and have a magic bow as your only means of arming yourself.
The cycle of the game is fairly basic. You travel to a location where you'll find a bunch of bosses and your goal is to defeat them all. To give credit where credit is due, the pixel graphics are very pretty and are partially animated which adds to the visual charm of the game. Next, you will enter the boss room and die a couple of times  trying to figure out what their gimmick is and how to defeat them. However, it is a very repetitive process of "Finding Boss -> Learning their moves and finding their weakspot (While dying a considerable number of times) -> Hoping you get lucky and hit their weakspot during a fairly small yet _almost_ always fair timeframe."
Let me give you an example. One of the very first bosses you encounter will be a brain in an ice cube. The arena which you fight it in has four pressure plates which activate a fire in the middle. The "gimmick" of the fight is to land a shot wherein you set your arrow on fire and manage to hit the sentient ice cube. The ice will then melt and out comes the brain which will hop around until you kill it. The timing of the shot has to be precise and accurate, otherwise you have to reset and hope that the game will give you a better placement of the cube and fire the next time. The RNG of it is annoying yet bearable. Mostly. The satisfaction that you feel after killing a boss is amplified by the great audio work and the visuals associated with this victory.
Some bosses, however, have stupid patterns that are almost unfair to deduce or have way too small windows to be able to aim and land a hit. After all, it is quite difficult to aim with a controller and no reticle. An example of this, sadly, is the final boss who I won't spoil yet will give a fair word of warning about: He is quite possibly the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and poorly tested boss in the entire game. How this is possible is beyond me as he will be the final boss for most people.
So is this game worth it? On a sale, most definitely. It is a fun experience for three hours if you want a challenge, like good pixel art, immersive sound design, and are resilient towards dying to _some_ (not all!) poorly thought out boss mechanics. I don't find it to be worth full price at 15 euro or your regional equivalent as a playthrough will roughly take you the aforementioned amount of time. You can, of course, run through the game multiple times with various options such as "hard mode" or ironman (only one life), or even a "no roll / no run" mode where you are only restricted to walking.

Randomly hard; epitome of trail & error, but with a lot of downtime (no action: walking to the boss).
If you want a hard game, this isn't it.  You spend most of your time walking to the boss, nothing to do along the way, then when you fight the boss, you die almost instantly.  Each boss has several attacks that you need to keep track of, but learn as you go along, it takes several dozen attempts to kill 1 boss; you're better off reading a walkthrough on each boss, then executing it rather than wasting your time dying & walking back to each boss.  It's not like dying leaves you right outside the boss door, no you have to walk there; even worse when the zones are mazes.
So bascially the game is a spritual successor of Zelda A Link to the Past, but only the boss battle parts, but in Zelda you would die only 0 to 3 times before figuring out how to kill any boss, and that was fun.  Here you die several dozen times, quickly, there's no room for error, and it's not fun (it's like work).

First of all, I'd like to say I found the game very fun and pretty nice to have a chill afternoon, but if you are not interested in achievement hunting nor speedrunning, that's about it. Also, I will not talk about the story to not spoil anyone that would like to discover it themselves, but mostly because I don't believe it is a big point in the game.
I'll start by talking about the environment. It really is beatiful. The music is amazing, and the points I highlight are on the big moments on the story the "orchestras" really hype it up and in one boss fight (
) it just syncs together and just makes the game that much better. The pixel art throughout the world is amazing, and the sense of scale you get when fighting some bosses is amazing. The one thing that trashed it a little bit is that most bosses are 3D models instead of pixelart and while most look really good, there are some that really stick out and don't fit the world at all.
Besides that, you have a huge world full of secret passages with unique "zones" to explore. Some of these zones have some unique mechanics to play with (
).
The concept is really simple. You have one arrow only, so after you shoot it you must get it back (either pull it to you or run to it). Every boss has a specific weak point and you must hit it to win. You die in one hit and so does the boss if you get the weak spot.
Every Titan feels different with a few exceptions, wehn they feel like one "isn't even the other's final form" and they are almost the same with a minor difference.(
)
Now, the main thing that throws me off about this game. The aiming, for being the main part of the whole thing, don't not feel good and is pretty hard to aim because of it. It's really hard to know where your arrow is going to go if you are not looking directly up/down/right/left. This makes some bosses where you have little time and a tiny target midly enfuriating (
).
When playing the game I believe I only experienced one bug, and it was easy to reproduce and avoid.
I really enjoyed the game, although short. The only thing I would change has to be the Roll/Sprint controls. Since they are on the same button, if you are sprinting your next roll will have a delay, and I think that could be fixed if they were on different buttons.
I strongly recommend it, specially if you find it on sale, has it becomes dirt cheap while still being a great experience!

Titan Souls is a pretty-looking but hollow and frustrating boss fighting game. The game's story has extremely little substance, basically some visual cues and one short and vague monologue to bait players into speculation on forums, and nothing else at all. So there's not much of a reward to all your efforts except the challenge itself, but that part isn't fun in practice.
The game's often-glorified difficulty comes from all the wrong things, certainly not from any clever enemy design because their weak points are instantly obvious and they're simply designed to give the player a bad time with relentlessly fast one-hit-kill attacks that usually leave the player with only one way out, sometimes not even that.
The gameplay is hampered by artificial difficulty due to bad controls (even on gamepad, although the 8-direction keyboard-and-no-mouse control scheme is worthy of special reprimand) and unclear combat mechanics (what angle and elevation actually warrants a hit in a 3D enemy with a 2D arrow).
Having an aiming cursor for the gamepad and maybe also implementing mouse aiming would have eliminated the single biggest problem in the game. You can have absolutely perfect understanding how to beat an enemy, but aiming your bow is very much a dice roll, especially since you have to do it extremely fast and aiming is done with the same stick as the one you move with.
I know that the popular counterargument against better controls is that it would make this awesomely difficult game such a cakewalk. I don't subscribe to the school of thought where an inaccurate input system is fine as an obstacle in doing what you're meaning to do. Even if better controls made the game easier, then so what? At least the game would be enjoyable and it would have better flow. I find it unrewarding to suddenly beat a boss that I've already tried to beat numerous times in that exact way, only to fail because of unreliable aiming and hit detection or cheap enemy attacks that leave no margin of error (or improvisation).
I gitted gud and beat 100% of the bosses in 3 hours, in case someone's wondering whether I just can't play the game.
I do like the game's concept of a single shot ending a battle. There's a potentially great game here, but it has such massive yet annoyingly easy-to-fix flaws that I can't recommend it. Something tells me that the developers are too proud to recognize, let alone fix, any flaws.
Would be much better with a tutorial and story guide. I'd also prefer if there was an alternative way so you could use your mouse..

I would recommend this game to anybody who likes Dragon Ball Z, it's got a unique storyline which fits your character in. There is ALOT of both good and bad things about this game however... so check what people are saying before purchasing.
The Pros:
- Create your own character 5 Races, 3 of which have gender options (Humans, Saiyans, Majins) and 2 which do not (Namekians, Freiza Race)
- Good Online Play in co-operative and against other players
- RPG-style Levelling System (3 attribute points a level, Attributes are Health, Ki, Stamina, Basic Attack, Super Strikes and Ki Strikes)
- Custom Equipment and Special Abilities
- Simplestic but easy to understand gameplay
- Doesn't require a controller (Keyboard + Mouse default bindings are very sensible when in battle)
- Good Hub World
- Original Story which builds on the Story of Dragon Ball Z
Cons:
- Have to go go to hub-world after each parallel Quest, wasting 30 seconds each time to get back to the counter
- The Online System sucks... the Xenoverse server is rather pathetic and it attempts to login each time you play, this seems uncessary. It could have had online game/offline game options on the start menu!
- If you connect to the Xenoverse server, after you select your profile/character it will connect you to the xenoserver server even if you select single lobby, just to download other people's characters to populate the hub world with.
- The multi-lobby is entirely pointless, it lacks basic chat features and only allows you to use pre-selected text and pretty much all features are available in the single lobby that are in the multi-lobby which includes online games!
- There is a colour customization option for clothing but most clothing isn't enabled for colour customization
- You can't see how clothing looks when browsing the clothing store or accessory store
- Some crash to desktop bugs do exist
- Online Gameplay can be very buggy with NPCs or Players becoming static and taking no damage
- Ally NPCs can be near useless in quest and storyline battles, many do not block super moves and don't engage an enemy properly if they are focusing somebody else.
- Humans and Saiyans are near impossible to see the difference between
- Online Game Browser is slow for both parallels quest and battles , it is very unintuitive and if a room has filled before you get in it, you need to rebrowse ALL rooms again, it doesn't allow you to go back and check others, you also can not see what levels and races people are.
There is overall a lot of technical problems with this game, but the gameplay and character customization make up for that. Hoping they can fix these issues in patches and/or DLCs.

I played a little of the supposedly superior collector's edition, which is not included with this, and I actually found I preferred the special edition that comes in this steam version with its 3d graphics, joystick mapping support, and music (vs the midi music).
Now, as far as gameplay, my main complaint with this game is the difficulty spikes and ensuing frustration. I was going to give this a negative review after getting stuck on one of the stages, but I eventually figured out a trick to overcome it. The difficulty spikes wouldn't be a problem if there was some way to lower the difficulty while still enjoying the story, but there isn't. You can turn on cheats, but it won't let you progress in the game. In addition, some of the levels have moments where you're sitting around doing nothing. There's a lot less of these moments in the later X Wing series games. That can be particularly frustrating when the hard part of the stage is towards the end, meaning you have to sit there playing the same easy part over and over and spend a bunch of time waiting. Anyway, if you aren't willing to put up with some occasionally stupid levels, I would not recommend this.
It's not just that, though. Even if you have a joystick, you'll be lucky if you can get rolling to work. This is actually really important to be able to use in some of the later stages and I couldn't get it to work. I'm not sure how it's supposed to be mapped because there isn't an option for roll in the joystick settings. Overall, the joystick support is a real hassle but the game doesn't really work as well on a mouse or controller.
On the positive side, for being such an old game, it's highly immersive. I actually think this is the advantage of the 3d and the actual music as opposed to the midi soundtrack (and, overall, the updated engine). It reminds me of the level of immersion and attention to detail you can find in the other awesome star wars game, Republic Commando. It's satisfying to master using your laser to hit moving targets, and the visuals and sound help make it that much more gratifying when you successfully take out a ship.
So, if you're looking to only play one really fun game in the series, I would look at the other X wing games. However, if you are willing to put up with some frustration in the pursuit of experiencing the whole series, definitely don't be afraid of playing this one. I haven't played it with keyboard or 360 controller, I only played this with my joystick. I would probably not recommend this game if you don't have a decent joystick.
But, overall, I wouldn't recommend this due to the frustration, lack of options for easing up the difficulty, poor joystick configuration capability, and the fact that you can get the same game with the extra collector's edition on GOG for the same price.

Hands down, far and away the best Telltale game I've played yet. While Borderlands 2 improved over the first game significantly with at least making you take notice of what was happening in the world
, Tales from the Borderlands made you actually care. I'm actually invested in Borderlands canon now singlehandedly thanks to this game, as long as future Borderlands games don't ignore what happened here and make some of the big storyline developments have consequences in further games.
So what makes this so great? It's really the characters, fully embodied by the great voiceover work from the entire cast. The overly busy Troy Baker might've made his mark playing Joel from The Last of Us or Booker DeWitt from Bioshock Infinite, but I think he's just as good here as he was in those games. And you also get some great performances out of Laura Bailey, Patrick Warburton, and many, many others (even Chris "I used to host Singled Out!" Hardwick). And a special shout out should go out to Ashley Johnson, who absolutely killed it as GORTYS.
What also worked? Choice mattered. Maybe they weren't earth shattering, and maybe everyone still got to point A to point Z no matter what happened in between, but when I arrived at that critical episode 5, I realized that things I had done and forgotten about really did carry over.

Racing games have been a huge genre in the gaming industry, most racing games are really popular, like Mario Kart, Forza, etc., and there are really bad ones like Big Rigs Over the Road Racing. Sega's Sonic the Hedgehog in the late 90's made their own spinoff Sonic Racing games, but the first one's were Sonic R, and Sonic Drift, these two games were considered by many to be terrible. then during the time of the PS2, Sega released a new franchise called "Sega Superstars," this game was really mediocre because it was one of the few games on the system to use the Playstation Eye, but it registered poorly, so the game was not good. Sega decided to step back into racing in 2006, with Sonic Riders, released for Gamecube, Xbox, PS2, and PC, this game was much better than Sonic R and Drift, it was different because unlike most racing games, this racing game used hoverboards, and a sequel was released in 2008.
2 years after Sonic Riders Zero Gravity, Sega decided to revive Sega Superstars with a tennis game before 2010, and in 2010, we got Sonic and Sega All Stars Racing. This racing game released for Xbox 360, PS3, Wii, DS, and PC, recevied really positive reviews. So much that it could start comparing to Mario Kart.
2 short years after Sonic and Sega All Stars Racing, we got the game were talking about today... Sonic and All Stars Racing Transformed. Released for Xbox 360, PS3, Wii U, PC, 3DS, PSVita, and mobile devices. So, is this a good racing game? Yes. The graphics on PC are stunning, especially in Max Settings, running 60fps, the colors are bright and colorful, and the small blur affects make the game a bit more intense. The gameplay plays like its original, Steer, Accelerate, Drift to charge up a mini turbo, and do tricks in mid air, which is replaced by flicking the right control stick in a specific direction, (I'm assuming you have a controller) the trick system is a lot simpler and quicker than the original.
The main gimic of this game is the ability to transform your kart into a boat, or plane, in boat form, you can ride the waves and  perform tricks by jumping off waves, specifically big ones, and even ride on hot lava, literally. In plane form, you can fly around in the air, while doing barrel rolls to dodge mid air obstacles, such as giant dinosaurs, construction areas, magic bookshelves, and flying aircrafts.
The game has a wide variety of modes, race, grand prix, time attack, world tour, battle mode, and even online, and the game has 20 race tracks and a large selection of Sega characters, and I mean it. You can even level up your favorite character and unlock mods for your character to customize their stats! So you can use your favorite character and still have good stats! Also, there are a handfull of collectable stickers and badges to put on your ID card.
The soundtrack in this game is really good, with many remixes, but voice clips are resused from past Sega games. But it is still nice to listen to to say the least.
If I had to give a final verdict on the game, I would say if Sega's goal was to make a racing game that uses features from many other Sega franchises, and bundle it all into one epic racing game, than they accomplished that very well, the gameplay is good, the soundtrack is epic, the online is fun, the selection of characters is great, and the graphics are beautiful to look at on the PC, but not so much on the Console versions of the game. This is a fantastic racing game that will keep you playing for hours, and has really fun online, I can safely say that this is one of the best racing games out there. I score this game with a 9/10. $20 is a good price, but in the steam sales, $5 is ridiculous, you better buy this in the sales! I reccomend this to any racing fan out there!

I would recommend this game to anybody who likes Dragon Ball Z, it's got a unique storyline which fits your character in. There is ALOT of both good and bad things about this game however... so check what people are saying before purchasing.
The Pros:
- Create your own character 5 Races, 3 of which have gender options (Humans, Saiyans, Majins) and 2 which do not (Namekians, Freiza Race)
- Good Online Play in co-operative and against other players
- RPG-style Levelling System (3 attribute points a level, Attributes are Health, Ki, Stamina, Basic Attack, Super Strikes and Ki Strikes)
- Custom Equipment and Special Abilities
- Simplestic but easy to understand gameplay
- Doesn't require a controller (Keyboard + Mouse default bindings are very sensible when in battle)
- Good Hub World
- Original Story which builds on the Story of Dragon Ball Z
Cons:
- Have to go go to hub-world after each parallel Quest, wasting 30 seconds each time to get back to the counter
- The Online System sucks... the Xenoverse server is rather pathetic and it attempts to login each time you play, this seems uncessary. It could have had online game/offline game options on the start menu!
- If you connect to the Xenoverse server, after you select your profile/character it will connect you to the xenoserver server even if you select single lobby, just to download other people's characters to populate the hub world with.
- The multi-lobby is entirely pointless, it lacks basic chat features and only allows you to use pre-selected text and pretty much all features are available in the single lobby that are in the multi-lobby which includes online games!
- There is a colour customization option for clothing but most clothing isn't enabled for colour customization
- You can't see how clothing looks when browsing the clothing store or accessory store
- Some crash to desktop bugs do exist
- Online Gameplay can be very buggy with NPCs or Players becoming static and taking no damage

Back when I first tried it out, TrackMania wasn't a game I was expecting to get addicted to. My friend's cousin was playing a free demo of it and my friend thought I might enjoy it. I did, a bit too much.
So what is TrackMania? As you can probably tell, it's a racing game. However, it is much different from most other racing games. Let's start with what it doesn't do: it doesn't use real-life cars, it doesn't simulate accurate physics, it doesn't aim to bring real courses to life, and it doesn't even let you collide with other cars.
So it's an arcade racer, then? Yes, but not in the traditional sense. There's no items to speak of, most courses aren't lapped, multiplayer is generally asynchronous, and courses are 100% static.
That might not sound like a lot of fun, but that's the baseline for what fuels this racer to be all fun. In most cases, you won't be driving on bland tracks. No ovals here; you get twisting loops, skybound jumps, and even ridiculous wallrides. No collisions means that you just need to worry about taking the track as fast as possible. Remember those jumps I mentioned? You don't get a lot of room for error sometimes, so a slight tap could throw you hurdling off into no-man's land.
This also sets the stage for pure skill. In all courses, you are already given the car to drive. You just need to deliver it to the end as fast as you can. No items and no collisions means no meddling with others, so all you have to blame for a poor time is yourself. When thing's come down to split seconds, you'll be glad you just need to worry about hitting the drift at the right time and not if you'll ram into some poor sap trying to pass.
Speaking of cars, TrackMania United is split into 7 different environments (one of which is featured in the free demo I mentioned earlier). From the slow and slippery Coast car to the ludicrously fast Island car, that's 7 unique vehicles to master. They never feel like tweaked copies, either. The Desert car tilts when turning, the Snow car is great at keeping speed but terrible at accelerating, and the Stadium car has so many tricks you'll be hard pressed to find them yourself.
As if that wasn't enough, Nadeo decided "Hey, let's just let the players make whatever they want." With the already amazing gameplay you also get a bunch of editors to suit your needs; make your own courses to blast through, paint your cars in your own patterns, and shoot videos of your best runs (or fails). And if you have the know-how, you can even make your own car models (which don't affect driving) and reskin your courses to use completely different textures.
Honestly, the map editor is what keeps me coming back the the TrackMania titles. While the default maps (of which there are hundreds of) are certainly fun to play, the game really shines when you take a look at some of the creations players have made. Heck, there's even a
with its own
!
I know it shows its age, but I can promise you that this is some of the most fun you'll ever have in a racing game.

Running this on a single-core Pentium with Windows XP. The classic version runs flawlessly (I have the original disked version running under DOS Box on the same computer, and it lags with unresponsive controls), The Special Edition version brings up at Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime Error ( R6030 -CRT not initialized ), so no comment on the Special Edition until I find out how to resolve that issue.
The game holds up very well in regards to game play and user interface. New to the game players should have little problem involving themselves in the game. The inability to use a throttle slider is a bit annoying--but simply demands a bit more ability to multi-task. My old pilot files fit right in.
Graphics obviously stand as dated, using fairly blocky shapes: but for a game that is 20+ years old one shouldn't expect smooth CG that demands 2GB GPUs. The older graphics do not rob the game of its playability, and for the old-school gamer (or those lucky enough to cut their teeth on gaming in the early 1990s), it will remind them of the days when it was about the mission, and the need to think of how to play the game, instead of the flashy visuals that dominate today's games.
Enjoy it for what it is.
And for those who have played it through, and want something a bit different, get X-ED, Dos Box, and modify and create your own missions (because having three or four Star Destorys battle it out with the same number of Mon Cal cruisers is a beautiful thing to weave your X-Wing through).
