Immediately I was able to get comfortable with the gameplay, though I did have to refer to my control screen for things such as targeting or Shinobi Transformation. The game seems a bit more challenging to me then it's musou brethren, focused more on smaller, slightly stronger enemy packs and character 'boss' battles. Though this difference is only slight, as AI still seems much to be desired and MOST of the mook enemies are rather easy to take down.
Graphically the game seems to work fine on my slightly dated computer. It looks good and seems to run a full framerate. The 2D opening looked rather choppy (making me have to skip it) and there was only one graphical hiccup where a character's hair started blinking out of existance in the Dressing Room. I will say though that the game is incredibly loud upon startup, which with all of the Japanese shouting (mostly of the same 3 or 4) one-liners and death cries, can start to get really grating on the ears.
At the point of writing this I've only finished the Hanzo campaign, and the story itself was a lot better then I expected it to be, if only because those said expectations were as low as they could be. It was a cohesive whole, mixed with moments character backstory, development and sympathetic moments when it wants to. Then you remember what game this is, and tone immediately falls into unintentionally comical or just plain stupid. Supposedly intense dialogue is ruined because not only is my enemy's fat♥♥♥♥♥♥out in the open while she tries to insult, but the nipples are also sensored by adorable chibi faces. Not to mention, it's hard to take my enemies as a genuine threat during a cutscene, when I just wiped thier sorry asses through the pavement and all I can think is "girl, just put on damn pants."
Speaking of this game being this game, there are a variety of outfits, accessories and, yes, underwear that you can dress each individual girl in to your hearts content. This is such a prominent feature to the point where the store literally has a "Lingerie Lottery", where you gamble money for 'Climatic' (thier word, not mine) underwear. I tried some of the alternate outfits during my playthrough, but honestly found thier base outfits (and those similar to them) to be the best option and the least cringy. If you're into the dressing up thing though, nothing will stop you. To be fair, I did change most of the characters' underwear out, if only to justify the existance of the "Lingerie Lottery." Overall, the game is exactly what it sells itself as: busty ninja girls beating the♥♥♥♥♥♥(and clothing) out of each other. It's a cocktease in combat, dialogue and content and if you're buying this that's part of the reason why. That being said, it's still a functional and enjoyable game as far as the actual gameplay elements go and has more emotional moments and character development then a game like this honestly deserves. If you like the genre (and♥♥♥♥♥♥ then you're going to be fine with this game, though your milage and tolerance may vary. Gentlemen, from Righteous Boobage Producer, Kenichiro Takaki, comes an epic game of ninjas, and boobs: Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus.
I absolutely love this game. This is the main course to Tamsoft games that I was waiting for after Neptunia U, And it was absolutely worth it.
The characters are huge! (In that area obviously.) But aside from that, they're also incredibly well written and have great personalities and lots of hilarious quirks to them. A lot of their backstories are interesting too as well, and some of these backstories are pretty shocking too. They're also plentiful, 22 characters in this game. And they all have their own unique strengths and weaknesses. Some have faster dashing, others have heavier attacking, some can harvest a ton of combos (good luck getting 7,777 combos), not one character feels the same in gameplay.
The story is divided into three different schools each with five characters to play with. All these schools go through the same story, but made so that they all get to tie in with each other. The story may be simplistic, but thanks to these campaigns, they get bigger and easier to understand. The writing is excellent balancing comedy and drama. In addition, there's a hidden fourth campaign with an extra five more characters that you unlock later on. Plus... there's even a special surprise for clearing all campaigns. The story has a lot to offer.
Gameplay is easy to pick up and play, and it plays a lot like Neptunia U mashing Square/Triangle (I use a Dualshock 4 now), except you gain scrolls that let you transform into your Shinobi Form, or Go Frantic (strip down to your lingerie). You can then use the scrolls to unleash special skills that can tear hordes of enemies apart and also the clothes of all bosses. Boss fights make it feel like a fighting game of sorts where the AI, compared to the dumb AI of the hordes, is a lot smarter, especially on Hard mode (which I recommend playing all Story Missions on, Character Missions are fixed at Normal). Again, the main gameplay may be button mashy, but you know you're in it when you want to see the clothes get torn down, lingerie included when you use Specials and Ultimate. Aside from that, there's even a fun online mode with a variety of unique modes, including a free for all brawl, a ninja killing spree (the ones with Dumb AI Of course) and one where you search for panties.
This game obviously delivers heavy amounts of ecchi fanservice. Righteous Boobage Producer Kenichiro Takaki has openly admitted his love for boobs, and no doubt it shows. Loads of jiggle physics, cute and sexy lingerie to choose and play around with, the man delievers all the goods to you. Though if you're not the kind of guy who loves big melons, there are two characters that are fla-- *Ryobi transforms* NVM, one of them can transform into a bustier girl like Nepu. Only one remains flat no matter what happens. You can dress them in various clothes and swimsuits, and even play around with their body too! There's so much ecchi goods in it, the only thing you have to worry about is your mother or anyone in your family seeing the game you play. I confess, I keep skipping cutscenes as a result of my worry for my parents seeing.
This game is amazing. It may not be for everyone obviously, but this game will forever have a place in my heart. It's an excellent piece of work and I highly recommend playing this game. Even if you haven't played the 3DS Games, this game is kind enough to recap the events that happened making it a good starting point for fans who are interested in this series and that you won't be missing out too often. Pros: - Time travel is well-explained and consistent in its applications and effects.
- The science behind the time travel is mostly based on real-world principles, which are explained in detail yet also accessible to anyone with a moderate knowedge of physics.
- Characters aren't generic anime trash. Mostly.
- Story is consistently well-paced and wastes zero time on filler.
- No sex scenes. This is a story about time travel, and it never loses sight of that.
Cons: - The method for reaching the Good Ending is obtuse, and the cutoff point for reaching it is only about 1/3 of the way through the story. Use a guide.
- The UI is never properly explained, making it easy to accidentally hit a "bad" ending on your first go-round.
Neutral: - Not for first-time visual novel readers.
- 25-30 hours of story.
- Seriously, use a guide.
Verdict: 4 stars out of 5. A few minor annoyances, but sci-fi and time travel fans should definitely make room for this in their library.

My friend bought me this game because he enjoys co-op FPS games and heard good things. Here's my experience with it so far.
Joined a game and we created a squad, named it a certain word meaning "disabled" or "stunted growth". Had no idea what to do or where to go, but we managed to pick up and/or steal an APC near home spawn. After grabbing some hitchhiker's from another squad, we drove to the Forward Operating Base, dropped them off, then proceeded to get stuck on a low wall. Our APC immediately got hit by RPGs and we bailed. Insert one hour of him trying to figure out how to squad leader and me throwing out bandages and med kits to whoever got shot.
Then Squad 2 asked us to go take a hill. By now we've accumulated around 5-6 more "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" and we set out up Ambush Hill only to get shot at by almost everyone on the opposing team. Through the clever use of running away, our squad managed to get on the another side of the hill where we received more heavy fire from a squad across the river/road. It was our own Squad 3. After kindly requesting they not shoot us, we made our way to their side of the river/road and proceeded to crawl ever so slowly on the road to the next objective. You see, there was a 2-inch high wall along the road that was your only cover.
After eventually flushing out a few enemies and taking over the next town, we settled down, did ammo checks, looked for any untended wounds, cleaned out our pants, and rallied up with Squad 3. About 10 minutes later the match had ended, the enemy's ticket count reaching 0. Throughout the entire match I only saw one actual enemy running in front of me. All-in-all, it was an interesting yet stressful experience that I will most likely experience again.

Let me get this straight: this game will kick you down. It's though. Cute, but extremely though.
Don't let these simple yet beautiful pixelated graphics fool you, the game is challenging for sure. Here you don't fight against minions, you go diretly to the boss, because that's what the game is after all: a series of boss fights.
You will die, you'll need to die. "Why I'll need to die, Baron?" - You must be asking yourself, then I explain: to defeat the bosses you must figure out how they work, their mechanics, their movements, so you can come up with a plan to defeat them. You'll die but you'll keep going on because the game is challenging you to do so and you want to prove yourself capable.
You have one arrow, that's all the equipment avaible for the entire game. Other than shoot one arrow, what can you do? Roll and run. That's it. Simple enough. All you have to do is shoot one miserable arrow (you can use some sort of magic to retrieve it), but the path you go down to shoot that arrow will make you eventualy mad.
The game is incredible, the graphics are marvelous, the soundtrack is beautiful, the gameplay is very instinctive and the game is as simple as it can get, yet it is very challenging. I strongly recommend it and you guys will find yourselves entertained through a lot of time, I guarantee.

I first got this game in early 2015. It was a fun game, but as time went by it gets closer and closer to a Pay-to-Win game. The game is much more fun now than it was just over a year ago (that was a disaster), but the game is still not as fun as it once was 3 years ago or when it first came out, before all of the DLC and limitations. It also takes a while to get upgrades and get enough money to purchase parts you need for your craft.
This game also used to have both tiers and levels with tech trees, but now that's all gone and replaced with levels that mean nothing. The matchmaking is unbalanced, which wasn't a problem with the tiers. Back when tiers existed, you were put into a match with other players of the same tier (1-10), and tiers were based off of weapons and vehicle size. Levels went up as you played the game, and level ups let you increase vehicle size and get closer to unlocking new weapons.
Now, the matchmaker puts you in a match with players in a similar level (+-3). Levels are gained by just playing the game and have nothing to do with weapons or vehicle size. The tech tree is gone and replaced with random blocks from crates, and it's impossible to get into a fair match or gain enough money to do anything in the game. The only upside is clans, maybe.
The early version of the game had an incredible premium system, where you pay-to-skip (you could pay to gain research and progress in the game instead of playing more battles) to pay-to-win where you have to pay in order to unlock any decent blocks or blocks you want, pay to get enough blocks to do anything, and pay to get a temporary premium account to actually gain a usable quantity of money after a match.
I would pay for the old version of the game (I joined right after the Easy Anti-Cheat Update), but that's never happening. We're stuck with this crappy game now.
A lot of new players will say that the game is great and fun, but they didn't experience the game in its golden age. They don't know how the old premium system worked, how horrible the new matchmaking system is, how incredible the Tiers with Tiered Blocks and Level-Ups for more CPU to build better bots was. They will never experience what we veterans have. We all miss the old version (late 2014-early 2015), and we've all given the new version a chance numerous times, but we can't stand the new systems.
Unless Robocraft releases their old version or fixes their new version to be like the older version, go get MachineCraft. It's a lot smaller in file size, has no block limits or purchase system, and hasn't been corrupted yet. It's as close as you can get anymore to the original Robocraft (without tiers or CPU though, just blocks, weapons, and servers).
Project DE:Construct is trying to create a game similar to the original Robocraft, just obviously with the few flaws that existed back then fixed and made better. The project is still in fairly early development. I am not allowed to disclose any information about the project by request of the Project Manager and Admins.

A fun little time-waster at best.
As of 4/1/14, the game itself is missing quite a few core mechanics that in my opinion really define the term "First Person Shooter", which are included but not limited to: more weapons, more game modes, more team-oriented play, more use of an interface, etc.
There are currently two game modes, being multiplayer and training. The multiplayer leaves much more to be desired, and unfortunately limits the player to only one class, and one weapon being an SMG; which has to be your close-quarters weapon, sniper rifle, assualt rifle, and secondary weapon. The only way to "rank-up" and I use this term lightly here, is to kill openents by shooting them in the head (as body shots do not count towards the enemy being hit); which makes me much rather just want to play Halo's SWAT game mode. When I first found this game, I was instantly hooked. Nice visuals, and watching as every bullet chips up your enemy's bot was incredibly satisfying. Before I had even started multiplayer, I found myself playing this game for hours on end in the afternoons. At the time, I was playing on a rusty laptop, so multiplayer was a struggle, yet I still had spent half my recorded time on it, building all sorts of bots and playing with the lower-middle ranked players and the bare minimum. Eventually my struggling laptop was burdened too much so I waited playing this game until I got a new computer.
When I got a decent computer for smooth multiplayer gaming, this was the very first game I picked up, and I was pretty shocked. The old system where having a 500cpu bot put you in with other 500 cpu bots was thrown out, and I found my tiny speed-bot pit against massively built killing machines, or even once a bot that was literally two fast legs and a minigun head. My very first game with a bot I was excited to try out lag free was horrible and I had to sit out the rest of the game, watching helplessly as my team lost. This was the same for many of my other bots, all but the one I had spent a lot of my time and ig money on. I tried getting back into the game, but the fact that I was put against children with their parents credit cards, or even adults with free time and splerging money, and the new system where you're lucky to get anything decent beyond a few dozen building blocks and beginner weapons, made this very hard to do.
Eventually I gave up on the game and left, hoping one day they'd work on their game some more to please its one massive fan and playerbase. So I just now came back, after who knows how long, and read the overall reviews were mostly positive. I got excited thinking they've done something right, except when I actually read the reviews they were still all negative, with the exception of children's reviews saying "its bad but its ok" which really couldn't compare to the paragraphs other users made explaining why the game isn't good, anymore. And apparently the mostly positive reviews are due to the devs deleting negative reviews? I'd believe that as easily as a simple influx of positive children reviews, regardless it is still clear this game hasn't fixed its problems and seems to have moved an opposite direction, seeing that they've completed its release. There's more to say, but it's already been said countless times.
Just to be fair, I could've gotten passed the pay to win system, because that's what a lot of these free games have. It's nothing new, nor will ever be changed, and they do need the money to keep the game alive. I could've gotten passed the people who spend a ton of money to build up their bots, because I still found it possible to beat them despite not spending a cent on this game. The same goes for the new currency system and tech tree, or lack of rather. The only thing I couldn't get over is the removal of the cpu ranking system, making it harder for new players to get into the game without paying, or at least how I see it, and discouraged me from making new bots to test in multiplayer, seeing that I had very little money or reason to do so. I can only keep one actual bot stored, with a few dummies maybe, but otherwise have to keep upgrading my main bot for whenever I get those rounds where I'm horribly overwhelmed by the enemy.
Shortly put, I miss my speed bot.

REVIEW BASED ON SOLO PLAY ONLY.
Highly recommended. Purchased for Xmas 2015. For less than a dollar, and one of my better game purchases of the year.
For my 89 cents, I got like five different classes. I can unlock the other five or so if I buy the DLCs, and maybe I will. In the meantime, I've already had 20 hours of fun and I'm only halfway through.
Gameplay is how I imagine Diablo 1 would be as an arcade game. You level up your character type with goofy skills, like a pirate shoots huge cannonballs and her capstone skill is a stupid parrot that kills monsters. You level up by clearing maps using W, A, S, D for movement and arrow keys for attack direction, spam spam spamitty. There are (dangerous) side dungeons with monsters, traps, and puzzles of the "step here and here" or "slide these pillars" varities.
You keep skills and items on character death, but your relics, which can be insanely OP, are lost. When I say OP, I mean OP, too, like I had a crown relic that multiplied my damage by 100. So death does sting a bit, and if you're into being a true PC Masturacer, there's a hardcore mode on top of about 5 difficulty levels with names like "Agony" and "Nightmare". I wouldn't recommend it, though, as the difficulty spikes considerably and without warning. I've been one-shot or close to it many times.
To go with those spikes, there are other cons to Hero Siege. It's not stable, for one thing. It crashes each time I quit the game, for example, and crashed my computer once. The UI, while efficient enough, is clumsy for me and I didn't find the option to change the key layout when I went looking. And while the character design (including abilities/weapons as well as appearance) is cool, the maps get repetitive and dull-looking.
Overall, Hero Siege has a great game formula and I hope to get at least another 20 hours of amusement out of it, making  my expediture an hour 2.2 cents. I know I'm harping on the price, just seems like other reviewers are expecting too much for what this game costs.

Very bad at the moment. Game is far from finished and even further from what was promised. Loads of bugs and glitchy gameplay mechanics. Here is why:
*Every new fix or patch breaks something else in the game.
*New content comes out untested and glitchy.
*Be prepared to forget about your progress and start a new game when game gets patched. Had to do this 3 times already myself.
*Fixes roll out slower and slower as time passes. Zero patches for almost 2 weeks at the time of writing this, even though last fix broke a lot of things and rendered bucket loader useless.
*AMD CPU/GPU users beware - you might not get sound in this game. This bug is around since release and still not fixed.
*Performance issues since day 1 even for people with high end PCs. Not fixed till this day.
*Graphics is somewhere between low and medium by modern standards. Not that this is too important for that kind of games. Remember that performance issues might not let you use the highest settings.
*Bad communication. Remember NMS? it's like that.
Forum is a mess. Bug reports are frequently ignored and/or lost in waterfalls of negativity. Requests  - the same.
*Strange thing is that devs are already working on payed DLC when the main game is far from complete. Remember that this is a small team. I have my doubts about this decision. Especially after seeing how slow the progress is. A lot slower than promised.
Some of my personal dislikes:
*excavators bucket has no ability to push and deform soil while digging. It just fills up and that's it. It gets stuck.
*You can not overfill bot excavator and bucket loader. Their buckets fill up to a fixed amount right to the edge. Almost its like water you are trying to scoop. If u ever used or seen those kind of machines at work you will know that you can scoop a lot more than the bucket allows (make a hill on the bucket if u will).
*You can not tamp dirt to flatten it with back side of excavator bucket. To fit a bit more in the truck for example.
*You can not back scrape with front loader bucket. To flatten the area where u are working for example. (Have to buy and use the bulldozer)
*Impossible to make ramps out of dirt to aid u in your operation. bucket loader is totally useless at this and bulldozer is semi useless (very hard to do).
* 1 machine of each type per claim. Might have something to do with performance problems.
*Tracked machines get stuck too easy. Got less ridiculous after a patch but the problem is still there.
*Thousands of invisible walls that you get stuck in. Not too bad of an issue but still... invisible walls...
*Loads of small glitches that are not even worth mentioning :D
*Yes I did post all of this on to the forum - ignored or/and lost.
To wrap this up:
You may expect 5 - 10 hours of interesting gameplay. Pestered with bugs, but interesting non the less. After that there's not much else to do. You can buy a new claim and go do the same things there, but I wouldn't say that's not repetitive.
In the state this game is at it's a BIG NO NO. Not worth 20$. If you really want it so bad< I recommend waiting for a sale. Or even better - waiting till it gets patched (if that ever happens) and a sale.

Hero Siege is a good idea with really poor execution in so many areas that shows some fundamental lack of ability about what it takes to polish a game in 2015.
It has probably the worst UI I have ever seen in a game in recent memory.
- inconsistent behaviour, it pauses when stat upgrading but not when changing inventory? Some items auto-pick up but not others?
- no tool tips or tutorial behavoiur of any sort, nor is there any tutorial for even basic things like how to pick up items. There isn't even a controls screen so you can see what controls are available. And there are WAY too many. I'm pretty sure a PC flight sim in 1994 had fewer buttons to remember.
- lack of feedback on so many things. You can select any dialogue options you want and there is no confirmation that it does anything.
- double-randomness involving requring a random chance to get keys and to get chests. So you end up finding a bunch of chests you can't open, with no way to go back to them once you have a key. Who ever thought that was a great idea?
- keyboard controls are basically so busted the game is unplayable.
- mouse operates only some things, but is otherwise inconsistent.
- inventory select screen is about as bad as you can make one. Why even have 'inspect' as a seperate opion? So dumb, it makes you press buttons all over trying to figure out what your best inventory item is. On top of this, not pausing the game during this fullscreen dialogue means you can easily die if you ever try to change items in the game. Compared to diablo where you would just highlight to inspect and double-click something to equip it if it was better, this game you have to nagivate with the keyboard and F and G keys, then press R and G to inspect and leave the inspect screen.. for every item. It's just insane, how could they ever think this was ok when diablo 2, one of the clear inspirations for them, solved this so much better over 15 years ago.
- Finally know that it's basically a free-to-play game they charge up front for, the base game should really be free with how much content is behind a paywall.
On the plus side the art style is very appealing. It's just a shame it can't be enjoyed to it's full potential.

Dragonball Xenoverse is a love letter to Dragonball Fans. As an American, the first DBZ game I was able to play was Budokai for the PS2 (if you don't count NES emulators running Japanese ROMs simply as a way to feed my teenage DBZ addiction).
I've seen the series front-to-back more times than I can count. Nothing is going to surprise me in the storyline. Dragonball Xenoverse seems to address this, by refreshing the story in a way that makes everything seem new again.
The fighting gameplay is quite addicting, as you can make very choreographed interactions with the fighters that really get your adrenaline going.
I think, though, this is a game made for DBZ fans, as the MMO style in between the fighting really seems to be shoe-horned in. I barely notice, simply because this is the type of DBZ game I've waited 17 years for.
I've had some crashing issues, which have either been midly irritating, to infuriating, depending on if the crash occurs after a rather crucial fight. For new players, as of right now, the best method of playing is by disabling the Steam Overlay. I'm quite surprised these crashing bugs exist because of a conflict between the game and Steam, since the PC release was advertised here. It seems like poor planning to me.
The servers have constant issues with disconnecting, or crashing the game itself. The developers have not been very transparent in their solutions to these problems. I've seen other games bounce back quite quickly from similar problems.
Overall, I am very pleased with the game. It has immense replay value with their RPG system, character specializations, and endless combinations of gear, fighting moves, and accessories. I'll be coming back to this game frequently I predict.

So I sold a TON of trading Cards to get this game on sale for 0.89 Cents. No DLC, Just the base game. This is going to be pretty long, So feel free to skim through the review and find what you need
This game manages to give little to no help on how to play. It hopes you figure it out yourself. Fourtunatly, That's pretty easy. You start out (In SinglePlayer) Choosing a Save Slot then a Class. There are 7 classes you can choose from when you buy the BASE game and 5 more you can get through the DLC (Thats not the only thing you get in the DLC's btw.). The Classes all have their own Speacial Abbilities, Each with their own powers and stats. Nothing feels unbalanced. You then name your character and begin.
The game starts you out in a town. There are people to talk to, but when you begin the game they are pretty useless. They become more important later. Anyway, the main things in the town are the Portals and the Difficulty Changer. The Difficulty Changer allows you to
. The Portals are the Zones. You start off by going through the First Portal and unlocking more as you progress. The Enemies also get stronger as you progress. You find Chests in Zones that contain Coins, Items, and Keys. At random a Speacial object/area will appear in a ZOne. These can be Dungeons and Crypts with extra loot, or simply just a Statue that gives you Full Heals and Stat Boosts. You kill monsters to gain XP and level up to get skills. The rest of the game is Self Explanitory.
The Character Customization is pretty broad but still decent. You can give your Character Hats using chrystals. You can also change your Name's Colour and Buy Minions. Other than that, There is really nothing to that.
This game clearly has A LOT of DLC. But don't think of it as a DLC commonly sold where there is Little to No Content, because that is NOT what these are. The DLC you can buy for this game seems like an expansion pack. It gives you Name Colours, Classes, and Skins. Nothing like More Weapons or anything lame like that. While it is good to buy these, I don't think they are neccesary at all.

I have already 100% on PS3 long ago and I'm willing to do it all over again on PC. Here's why Steins;Gate is so freakin' amazing.
First off, I'd like to make it clear that this is the very original visual novel that released in 2009 for the Xbox 360 only in Japan, which then got its anime adaptation about a few years later. It was then ported to PC, PS Vita, PS3, finally Steam, and a pre-order bonus of its "sequel" that's only available through that on PS4.

This game isn't a racing game like all others. Trackmania has its own things that makes it a special racing game - the physics for time attacking.
You can ride with cars over nice maps build by Nadeo, or a community on 7 different environments. Collect medals by improving your time. Chase your friends to see who's better driver. Build your own maps and share your maps with others, for example on
. There's a lot of stuff you can do related to cars.
True, you can do all of this in Nations, but United is another big expirience of driving with different cars and enjoying their unique environments. Please don't waste your money on this game because of Coppers support, it's stupid.
Now my review:
Gameplay (6 points max):
There are no car collisions, which is the biggest thing that makes this a time attacking game.  Simple to understand, drive from start to finish in a fastest time, or drive multiple laps on multilap track. That's all you need to know. Car physics itself are REALLY good. 7 enviroments with different cars means 7 different car physics. The car react just as you press the key and it's possible to understand how the car works. Obviously you need to play for some time to be good at driving. Hard to tell if it's good idea to spend some months to skill yourself for such a dead game, because there are no competitions atm, but you can still rank up in official rankings of Solo tracks.
Because cars are sometimes buggy and time attack can result some unlucky moments, I'm rating it
.
Graphics (3 points max):
Graphics. They're old for sure, but quite good on it's release date. Anyways it isnt really close to today game's graphics. When you look at the game, it's a game where environment (not gameplay environment) really matters.
Hard to decide, but I'm rating it
.
Atmosphere (1 point max):
This game has it's own atmosphere, like most of the games. But this one brings memories of older games like 2004-2008 - their graphics bugs, simple design, gameplay. If you played older versions of Trackmania like Sunrise or Original, then you'll understand the feeling. :D Anyway I think it deserves clean
. It isn't messy game with all kinds of things that don't fit together.
I'll say it simply, this game is awesome. This rating comparing to today games is very very good on 2008 game.
Community is very VERY friendly. Trackmania has one of the friendliest communities ever. From my expirience, I have no doubt of that. :D United community is dying (actually it's pretty dead now), but you can still meet some players around the servers and things.
You want to decide if to buy this game for 30 bucks or stay at Nations. It's simple: Do you want to try something new in a game you know? For myself I really enjoyed playing all of these enviroments and I'm still enjoying that! But if you're not really into trying other 6 environments for this amount of money (I understand, it's a lot), then don't go for it.
Overall I of course recommend this game. Absolutely no doubts about that. If you're trying to find a solid multienvironmental racing game rather for singleplayer purposes, this can be a good choice for you. :)

There's something Star Wars and Command & Conquer: Red Alert have in common: I was never able to play as the good guys at first. My computer couldn't run X-Wing, and our Allied disc of C&C: Red Alert broke, so I was stuck playing as the bad guys (the Soviets, and TIE Fighter). Then, a wonderful thing happened, the Special Edition of X-Wing and TIE Fighter came out in a single box, and I had to get it, and I found X-Wing to be rather disappointing. Don't get me wrong, I'm proud to fly for the Rebel Alliance, but X-Wing lacks features that TIE Fighter and later games included:
-The in-flight map is only two-dimensional.
-The targeting display is just a diagram instead of a 3D model.
-There are no in-flight messages, save mission-critical stuff.
-The Q-Spacebar method of ending missions isn't here.
But the biggest surprise is that this game is HARD. In order to get a training patch, you must complete 8 levels to earn a Flight Badge, which is no small feat. In the Tours of Duty, dying will get you demoted to the bottom rank, and you can expect to die a lot. Even when it came time for the Death Star Trench Run, there's so much junk and turets in the trench that I was torn to shreds like wet tissue paper. The only strategy I found to work was to flight some 20 km away from the nav buoy (and hope it's the right direction) and fly straight down, hoping I hit the exhaust port.
However, the game doesn't end there, taking you through 2 more tours, ending with the founding of the Hoth base, which gives you the impression that it's a long time between A New Hope and Empire Strikes Back.
In the end, if you're up for a challenge, or really want to be a Rebel like I did, go for it. If not, play the better games in this series.

A great racing game for gamers with low performance computers/craptops
This game has a good few years already and it's still widely played by gamers to this day, clearly the game devs got something right.
If you have played any trackmania game before you know what to expect from this one.
The great thing in this game is the customization of cars that is supported online (meaning others can see your custom car whilst competing online) as well as the track editor.
As the name of the game sugests, "trackmania" is all about the tracks, and boy do they have a lot to offer.
From normal tracks to absolutely batshit insane off the wall tracks that will peel the skin off your face.
The controls are insanely simple, just the arrow keys, the backspace/enter to reset track. That's it, that's all you need to know to be able to play this game.
Each type of track is absolutely unique along with the cars that come with it, each car controls completely different so you will find that some are just for you whilst others might seem difficult to master.
Of course the game does have some issues, just like any other game.
The first issue (albeit not a big one) is the sheer amount of information given to you in the online menu screens... there is a TON of stuff and it takes a while to figure out what is what, there are at least 5 different rankings showing at one time then there's all the other stuff going on. It's confusing at first but eventually it starts to make sense, this was one game where I would have wanted an instruction manual to go with it.
Another issue is the online community.
No, they're not jerks, the issue here is that there are a lot of players online... but exclusively on the stadium tracks (the formula 1 tracks) and if you like playing with the f1 cars then that's great for you but if you like playing with other cars on other tracks you will find it very difficult to find a server with other people on it (there are a few but they have a minimum skill requirement so if you've just started the game then they're off-limits to you)
Overall, this game is great, simple to pick up and play on the go, it suppoerts local coop and it also has a system where you take turns doing a lap and the one with the shortest time wins, but if you prefer head to head racing you can always make a local lan game with your friends who have the game.
Your friends don't have the game? no problem, Trackmania nations is essentially a free demo of this game, it contains exclusively the stadium tracks (this explains why everyone is always on the stadium tracks online) and it supports online play, so fire up that game and the demos and have fun.
8/10 due to those few issues

"It's me. An opportunity shows itself. I can reveal to the world my greatness through a Review!
An Organization trap?! ...of course they would want me to spill the beans on my plans, crafty bast ards. HOWEVER! This Hououin Kyouma will not be so easily tempted and fooled! For I KNEW it was a trap, but I have the world in the palm of my hand! Fuahahahahahahahahaha!!"
Where do I even begin? Steins;Gate has to be one of the most captivating, tear-jerking, awe-inspiring stories of all time and the most amazing piece of media that exists today with one of the most interesting concepts of time-travel you've ever heard of. The best part? There's absolutely no plot-holes like in virtually every other time-travel story out there and everything wraps up neatly leaving you completely satisfied.
Steins;Gate is a time travel sci-fi set in the real world and uses real life laws of physics; meaning that science and scientific theories are used and explained for time travel: no magic or extraterrestrials present. Steins;Gate also uses real-life phenomena and conspiracies such as the forum posts from the time-traveling John Titor in the year 2000 and the CERN conspiracy surrounding their ability to create mini black holes and integrates these into it's plot to make it work seamlessly.
The story of Steins;Gate puts you in the mind of Hououin Kyouma, a self-proclaimed 'mad scientist' who develops future gadgets in his lab with the objective of bringing chaos to the world's ruling structure and to thwart "The Organization" who are behind major conspiracies. In reality, Okabe Rintarou (his real name) is just a college student who rents out an apartment and hangs out with his friends and constructs "future gadgets" with random items they can find (ex. a toy raygun that functions as a TV remote, or a landmine repurposed as a de-humidifier). His "Hououin Kyouma" persona is all in his head, and his friends just roll with his chuunibyou.
One day, the lab constructs a future gadget called the "PhoneWave (Name Subject to Change)" that combines a microwave and a cellphone. This device's unintended side-effect allows people to send messages into the past and change the future. Around the time of this device's creation, a supposed time traveler with the pseudonym 'John Titor' appears on internet forums talking about how the organization SERN (CERN) uses time machines in 2036 to create a dystopia, and he has been sent back to warn people. This prompts Okabe to look more into SERN, and after doing so he realizes there are sick, dangerous secrets hidden behind the research organization.
The writers of Steins;Gate had obviously put lots of research, thought, and planning when creating it, and that dedication and attention to detail really makes this story so... timeless.
The writers even go so far as to explain (in depth) all of the scientific theories behind time travel, black holes, advanced technology, and so-on. This VN will give you a lot to think about and reflect on.
The gameplay is, well... it's a visual novel. However, Steins;Gate is different from conventional VNs, where you have many choice prompts throughout the story that branch into different paths. Instead, all gameplay comes from interactions with Okabe's phone. The 'branching paths' come from texting people back or calling a certain person when prompted to. The VN is more story oriented and focuses itself on that, while doing an excellent job of solidifying your role as Okabe Rintarou through the way you control his phone.
The music is great and immersive. Many of the game's soundtracks are remixes of Steins;Gate's central theme: Gate of Steiner, that are composed differently to set a certain mood. The music does a great job of making you anxious or ripping your heart apart.
There is an anime adaptation of Steins;Gate made, and I would highly reccomend watching Steins;Gate and then playing it through. The anime has a lot of the story cut out of it, but has more than enough to make it an amazing journey. After watching it, you'll want to come and play it because it turns a 10/10 anime into a 100/10 game. Also, it will give you extra motivation to grind your way through the first half of this game. I LOVE Steins;Gate, and even I admit this game is excruciatingly long at first. But make your way through it and mountains of gold await you.
I CANNOT reccomend this game enough. Steins;Gate is completely captivating and because it holds itself to real life physics and science (apart from the whole time travel thing) it really convinces you of "this makes a lot of sense and seems like it could've actually happened". The characters are all lovable, and the transformation that Okabe Rintarou goes through during the course of the game is absolutely phenomenal.
Stop what you are doing and go watch Steins;Gate, give yourself a week or two to reflect on what you watched and let it sink in, and then come back and get all the juicy details and amazing extra story in this game.

One of telltale's classic story adventures, where you play it like a movie but direct most of a character's dialogue and decisions with a few point and click scenes and quicktime events in between. But like all of the telltale story games there is always a distinctive feature, this one's feature is that you play through the perspective of two main characters instead of one (filled with the borderland hurmor of course).
There are twists, there are laughs, there are times of great bravery and times of great sadness or anger, it might become silly, it might become serious, and most importantly (I think) times of great badassery, from headbutting a psycho to defeating a great villain with one arm and one eye. This game has all the action a story telling game in the borderlands universe needs.
I admit I have made some "questionable" choices in the game that I've regretted (not as much as mass effect) but that is the part of the fun in the game, creating choices that question your morals, decision making skills and ability to think laterally is what I love from this game. You might only play it once or twice (and you need some knowledge of borderlands), but it's worth it!

People have a missconception about "pay to win" when it comes to Crossout, which is surely an in-game economy based game. Most negative reviews will be about the "p2w" issue (which doesn't exist) and have to explain:
All items in the game are obtainble at some point without spending any money in it. The market allows players to sell any goods. Market prices are PLAYER CONTROLED, so you can expect some people selling stuff at prices that exceed the $100 (but considering the time invested to make such artifacts, it is resonable: it's not easy) and prices go up and down as demand and supply go on a roller coaster. Players usually cry/rant because they want all the good stuff the same day or week... this game (like any other) requires quite a time of gameplay to achieve such power. This is where real money comes in: peolpe get desperate and buy the in-game currency (coins) to get "competitive". Let me tell you that Captain America needs to teach a lesson to quite a lot of people: PATIENCE! The game is very grindy, but that's the point of a game: to play it quite a long time.
So the "p2w" issue being explained, it all points out to be, in fact, pay to progress (faster). If you want to play it for free, feel welcomed to a grind similar to ranking in Halo 2, Halo 3 and Halo Reach... because, like those games, its needed a lot of time to get the good stuff out of it. If you think you are better off putting cash into it, go ahead.
To make parts, you need to rent a workbench. "I gotta pay to make parts" no... you just have to play the market game, sell goods, get coins, rent, craft and enjoy! If you don't want to play the market stuff... good luck: this is how the game works, and it feels fun too.
So there it is: pay to win and pay to progress, not the same.

Following the Battle of Three Tribes, there was a brief period of peace and prosperity... but such fleeting luxuries are best never taken for granted. One fateful, dewy morning as Amanda's mother, Arlene, strolled out to the edge of the valley to gather some wild herbs, an enemy faction mounted their attack. Arlene was promptly knocked unconscious, and as one raider whisked her away, the rest continued their assault deeper into the valley.
At the mountainside entrance, Grim took cover behind a tall oak tree and sprung into action with his sniper rifle, disposing of one of the encroachers with deadly efficiency as they all came around the bend. It would be a perilous fight, but the odds would be in Grim's favor just as soon as -
Suddenly, Amanda raced in to join the conflict, not aware of her husband Grim's location. As Grim lined up his next shot and pulled the trigger, a larger blur filled his scope. Lowering the gun, he saw Amanda's falling body, dead before it hit the ground. Grim destroyed the remaining attackers in a fiery rage and then rushed to his wife's side. There was nothing left he could do. He dug a hole in the graveyard and buried her. Maddened by guilt and loss, Grim went completely berserk and assaulted another colonist, who then shot and killed Grim in self defence.
The colony had been reduced to three people once again, but still they prevailed, just as they had in the past. Just as they would continue to -
Then, a noise. A chattering, almost. Coming from deeper in the caves. What could make such a sound? As the colonists gathered around a dimly-lit corridor to investigate, their weapons drawn, a swift-moving shadow leaped out from the darkness. Blood spattered the walls and the remaining colonists dropped to the floor, all dead or dying.
The caves would be home to something else now.

This was a hard desicion to make, but here it goes.
Robocraft is a good game, but it has always had a tad too many issues.
I have played robocraft since the early days of 2014, and it has always been a love-hate relationship. Through the games development, it has changed alot, some for the better, and some for the not-so-better.
I have always enjoyed the creative aspect of the game, designing and testing ones craft, and it has always been nice to enter a game, to find mangled and/or bizarre creations on the field of battle. If you got utterly destroyed by a certain design, you would either slam your hands on the nearest flat surface, or you would study the enemy craft, gaining knowledge about the current meta and so on. I like the learning curve, as it's more engaging and fun to gain knowlegde, compared to FPS games, where you almost NEED to follow tutorials online if you want even a chance.
I also like the loot box system in favor of the tech-tree. It makes the game less repetitive, and offers other ways to play the game. I'm of course reffering to getting a new weapon type through onboxing.
But then again, this game is nowhere near perfect. Everything has its flaws, and robocraft sometimes just has too many of 'em.
The game does not always feel balanced, as all players are able to play with each other, regardless of weapons and CPU. This makes the early-game for most players really grindy, before they get a real chance to compete with the 3-year players.
And now we reach the final part, and the biggest reason why I would NOT reccomend Robocraft. It's for your own good
Random disconnects.
The servers, where robocraft hosts their games, are unstable. Based on my own experiences, there is an about 25-33 % risk of a random disconnect. The risk gets higher the longer you play, making ranked play nearly impossible, where deathmatch always will be the preffered gamemode, due to the 10 minute time limit.
Besides this, you will be hit with a penalty for 'leaving the game'. This can add up to 30-60 extra seconds in the lobby, before you are able to join the que. Que times are on average 1-2 minutes, but it's typically longer, about 3-4 minutes sometimes. I recommend extra patience.
The devs are well aware of this server instability, but i don't think they will fix it anytime soon, due to the complex workings of servers. It will probably be fixed, but we never know when, as robocraft has had disconnection problems since 2015.
so, as i said at the beginning, Robocraft is a fun game at its core, but it is ultimately ruined by one problem. I really like the game, but i always end up frustrated, when i end my plaing session. The disconnection error NEEDS to be fixed, before robocraft truly can be great again.
Until then, i will not recommend it, but it doesn't mean, you don't have to ignore it. See for yourself, because it really is on the edge between a fun, playable game, or a dissapointment over time.

So I sold a TON of trading Cards to get this game on sale for 0.89 Cents. No DLC, Just the base game. This is going to be pretty long, So feel free to skim through the review and find what you need
This game manages to give little to no help on how to play. It hopes you figure it out yourself. Fourtunatly, That's pretty easy. You start out (In SinglePlayer) Choosing a Save Slot then a Class. There are 7 classes you can choose from when you buy the BASE game and 5 more you can get through the DLC (Thats not the only thing you get in the DLC's btw.). The Classes all have their own Speacial Abbilities, Each with their own powers and stats. Nothing feels unbalanced. You then name your character and begin.
The game starts you out in a town. There are people to talk to, but when you begin the game they are pretty useless. They become more important later. Anyway, the main things in the town are the Portals and the Difficulty Changer. The Difficulty Changer allows you to
. The Portals are the Zones. You start off by going through the First Portal and unlocking more as you progress. The Enemies also get stronger as you progress. You find Chests in Zones that contain Coins, Items, and Keys. At random a Speacial object/area will appear in a ZOne. These can be Dungeons and Crypts with extra loot, or simply just a Statue that gives you Full Heals and Stat Boosts. You kill monsters to gain XP and level up to get skills. The rest of the game is Self Explanitory.
The Character Customization is pretty broad but still decent. You can give your Character Hats using chrystals. You can also change your Name's Colour and Buy Minions. Other than that, There is really nothing to that.
This game clearly has A LOT of DLC. But don't think of it as a DLC commonly sold where there is Little to No Content, because that is NOT what these are. The DLC you can buy for this game seems like an expansion pack. It gives you Name Colours, Classes, and Skins. Nothing like More Weapons or anything lame like that. While it is good to buy these, I don't think they are neccesary at all.
-1/5 Don't Buy it-

But it can be played with a mouse.  But, if you're a mouser, stop reading now.  Vintage X-wing players and those who use a stick will find a massive deadzone on both stick axes. The Game is fun, but it has many flaws. First of all, the combination of genres is really cool. It's basically a Beat'em Up + RPG + Rogue-Lite, it definitely has many inspirations from The Binding of Isaac (it even borrows ideas like the bible makes you fly", "Book of Belilal, gives you DMG", and others, plus the way you attack.).
Now, when it reaches a certain point, with a certain combination of items, i became a lawnmower with my Viking, destroying multiple waves of monsters in high difficulties alone, with ease.
Now, i'll let the flaws come in. Trying to play with friends is a nightmare. You can either port-foward or use Hamachl, but the game constantly crashes, bugs you back to the lobby, many funky stuff that annoys.
In a server, you can exit in you don't lose any of your items, so the game is kinda broken there.
The sound effects are nice, but most of the voice acting is really unprofessional and distracting, like that Stickman active item that is really weird and badly dubbed.
Bosses are ridiculous easy at the beginning, at the point of enemies having equal or more HP than them, and later on bosses have a weird difficulty spike. (Hp barely changes between Normal and Nightmare, there was another one that jumped to Hell where Anubis had like, 500k hp, then on Hell he had 2 or more Million hp.)
There is a ridiculously frustrating puzzle in a dungeon where you have to place many crates over buttons (including a line of buttons, it probably sparkles the memories of whoeved did it), where if you don't have any flight it will be a nightmare, the crates get stuck in corners, and any slight touch can move them, so you gotta restart it a lot and it bugged me a ton.
And one of the biggest problems are the DLCs. Pratically half of the game content is locked behind DLCs, which are more expensive than the game itself. So yeah, if you're not into grinding through the same levels over and over with increasing difficulty, ready your wallet.
Now, is the game worth it? Well, yeah! I had fun with it playing solo, it's satisfying to cut my way through enemies, it has cool mechanics and creative concepts, they only need to improve the game a bit to make it golden (looking at you, servers!).

Let me start off by saying that the Trackmania games were my childhood. Me and my cousin spent hours racing, building tracks, and competing for the quickest times across the original game. Then Trackmania Sunrise came out, and the magic seemed to happen all over again. Eventually we got older, began to hang out less (We lived a good distance away), and started to move on with our lives. A few years ago, we found Trackmania Nations. It didn't quite feel the same, but it was almost a return.
Just recently I purchased Trackmania United Forever Star Edition (TU), as I realized that it seemed to have the vehicles and environments from the original games! I eagerly downloaded it, watching as the percentage slowly inched up. When it finally finished, I quickly hit play, loaded into the game, and got myself into a race in the desert environment of the original Trackmania.
"Wow, I could have sworn it looked better when I was a kid." I told myself upon being greeted by incredibly bad graphics.  Whatever, my nostalgia for the game made me see it better than it was. That's my fault.
But wait. It wasn't my fault. The game's screenshots showed it looking a lot better! Even the Stadium environment looked much worse on United than on Nations!
"Trackmania United blurry textures" were the words I fed into Google. Well, I started to. The term was already one of the suggested search terms, along with several other versions of the phrase, reworded in various ways. This was a problem all across the community! I began to follow whatever guides I found, hoping I could fix my game and get back to my childhood. Nadeo held a place in my heart, so I was pretty forgiving.
None of them worked! I tried adjusting the Distro and installing a patch! I tried all the methods people suggested. But none of them worked.
I still can't find a solution. I've validated the files, deleted and reinstalled, tried every guide I could find.
Ultimately, this is why I'm leaving a negative review. This glitch has been around for years. I believe the earliest time someone asked about the glitch was 2010! Yet Nadeo has not fixed it, and eight years later, I doubt they will.
If you buy this game, make sure your computer is not on Windows 8.1 (That seems to be the OS installed on a lot of computers that have the issue and can't fix it). I can't even give a specific set of graphics cards that might trigger the glitch, because they were all over the place.
Or just be safe, dont buy it.

There's no upgrade system in Trackmania. There's no collision detection between you and other drivers, there's no difficulty levels, no physics settings, no slow motion crashes, no random hazards, none of that. There's you. There's the clock. And there's the never-ending pursuit of the perfect line. Trackmania United is, simply put, the definitive example of a racing game in it's purest form.
This is one of the only games I have ever played in recent history where the one and only factor that determines your success is your skill. You can't blame anything on other cars getting in your way, moving track pieces, or not having enough nitro to shoot you past the competition. Barring things beyond your control such as real-life distractions or equipment malfunction, whether you win or lose is entirely determinate on how skillful you are. That's
This alone makes Trackmania United an ideal game for those who can do without more conventional elements found in other racing games; the people who are satisfied with the honor and glory of simply being more skillful than somebody else.
Trackmania United is somewhat of a compilation of all the games that came before it, and when compared to the latter games in the series (the fractured release of Trackmania 2 and the console port of Trackmania Turbo) it arguably has the most content. TM2 has 3 enviornments (soon to be 4), TMT has the same 4 enviornments (reskinned as a spinoff), and TMU has 7. There's tons of tracks for each and they all have their own unique physics:
-Stadium: One of the best-feeling envoirnments in the game. Stadium cars are quick, grippy, and honestly feel more grounded in reality than any of the other enviornments in the game. Not to say that I'm looking for realism in an arcade racer, just sayin. Stadium tracks demand precision, and merely grazing a wall is almost always a guarantee that you'll get a silver medal or lower.
-Island: One of my personal favorites, Island cars are blazing fast and extremely drifty at high speeds. The tracks are wide with long turns to compensate, resulting in an enviornment that's a blast to drive in. Bonus, load up your favorite Ferrari skin and play Splash Wave or something in the background for some mock-OutRun fun.
-Bay: Another one of my favorites, Bay cars are like a compromise between Stadium and Island. They demand the automotive dexterity of Stadium while still being almost as fast as Island. Also a lot of fun.
-Snow: Snow cars are extremely grippy and can practically turn on a dime. These tracks tend to twist and snake around; don't expect a lot of straightaways, and always try to keep your eyes one corner ahead.
-Rally: With scenery inspired by old rural Europe (I guess?), Rally cars are a little on the slow side and very easy to handle, and are actually a little grippier than you'd think on dirt surfaces. This is fine; you're still gonna have to pay attention to your line in order to nab those gold medals.
-Desert: One of the less enjoyable enviornments in my opinion (but that's just me), Desert cars are a little awkward to get used to. You will get used to them, though, and they teach you to manage your speed as you corner, lest you lose traction and therefore valuable momentum.
-Coast: My least favorite enviornment at first, Coast eventually grew on me. They're the slowest cars in the game, yet some of the hardest to control. Take a corner too fast or try to turn too hard and you start sliding, which will most likely result in that gold medal ghost cruising right past you. Where other enviornments teach you how to respond at high speeds, Coast demands patience and subtlety.
Trackmania United's price tag can be a little steep when you consider it's age, but you ARE getting a ton of content. If you want to try it out first, the Stadium enviornment is available as a standalone game for free (Trackmania Nations), with a fully fleshed out singleplayer campaign, the powerful track editor, full mod support, and unlimited multiplayer. There's people out there that have logged hundreds and even thousands of hours in the free version of Stadium alone. Try that out, and if you want more, then buy United, which will give you full access to all of these features in the other 6 enviornments. United also features extra modes for a change of pace. There's the Platform mode that puts you on much more technical tracks where time isn't a factor; medals are awarded based on how many times you have to reset your car to get to the end. When was the last time you played a racing game as a platformer? It sounds gimmicky but it's actually really interesting. There's also Stunt mode, which gives you a time limit to do flips and spins to get as many points as you can, and Puzzle mode, where the game gives you an unfinished track and gives you a limited number of extra track pieces, and you have to figure out how to arange them to make the track doable. All of this, combined with the track editor, the thousands of player-created tracks to download and enjoy, and both local and online multiplayer modes makes Trackmania United one of the most expansive racing games you will ever play. You can play it how you want; turn off the opponent cars and casually try to make it to the end of a track, shoot for gold or even Nadeo medals, or even compete in asynchronous multiplayer on the singleplayer tracks by doing official races to submit your best time to the global leaderboards. You can treat United like you'd treat Nations by spending all of your time exploring the wealth of content in your favorite enviornment, or become a jack of all trades and master every car's unique driving style. There's something for everybody. I've had the game for 3 days and I've already logged over 10 hours. I know I'm gonna sink many more into this game.
Trackmania United is purely a time trial game at heart. When judged by those standards, in my opinion it is one of the only games I would ever award the title of "flawless" to. If you want a time trial game, or even if you're just looking for the best Trackmania game, look no further. Trackmania United is among the best of the best.

I have played both intensively and casually every DBZ game from the PS1 editions to the GBA sprite versions to the popular budokai 3. I will make things detailed for each section for everyone looking to buy this game and/or get the season pass.
8/10,
as others have mentioned the game has a lot of skills and abilities for you to use from basically the whole series to its own unique versions, the grind in the game is actually a positive part of the game as it adds things for you to do HOWEVER there are some things I don't agree with. For example, You
get Super Saiyan  early by beating a 3 star mission or you can spend those same hours grinding to just unlock it in the shop. It would be fine if it wasn't for the fact that it's really hard to get the skill and the time spent grinding for it could just be spent getting to the point in the story where you can simply buy it. None the less I still helped my friend grind for it as there is a sense of accomplishment but strategically it's better to wait it out. The game offers quite a few ways for you to play your character but there are certain moves that are just outright unfair and unblockable, it's not as big of an issue since it's a new game and balancing still needs to occur but it is significant enough in the story mode to lower the rating. Additionally another problem which made this a solid 8 rather than when I originally wanted to 10/10 gameplay is that auto attacks are very simplistic and lack depth which is apparent since there is only a single page for when you open up the combo list, teleporting behind/infront of characters costs way too much even though I find teleporting is a significant part of fighting in almost all games and it is showcased a lot in the anime series.
10/10
As a Dragon Ball Z fan, the story gets real old with every retelling and you basically know what to expect, they have done a great job making the story engaging and making your character feel like they are genuinely interacting with the story and making things better. This becomes even more apparent as when you beat missions the city populates with new faces which creates a sense of accomplishment. After I had finished the story, I wanted more as it was engaging and while I haven't finished the story 100% (at 90% currently), I am happy to see there is more to come in the DLC packs. What makes the story engaging is as the other users have mentioned, the creators did a great job of answering popular fan questions of "what if goku failed", it lacked depth at times beyond "time and history will fall apart" but it is a great idea and it was well executed, sometimes even featuring what happens because goku failed. While you can't expect a whole new rendition of the story line, the game does a great job of telling the original story as well as adding its own twists, coming out of the game I could explain most of the DBZ story to another user without actually seeing the anime. This game is better than it has any right to be. Sega hasn't made an interesting game in a decade or so and has made some of the worst games of last decade (e.g. Sonic '06).
There is nothing spectacular or innovative about this game, but it is a very solid mascot cart racer for PC, with a reasonably high skill ceiling and a reasonable amount of catch up mechanics (AKA random BS). The catchup mechanics are there to keep the game interesting for less skilled players and to always provide some hope even if you're slipping behind in single player. These catchup mechanics are a bit less infuriating and random than the blue shell and lighting mechanics of a Mario kart game.
Most levels have you switching between 2 or 3 vehicles (cart, boat, flyer) which you do automatically by going through rings. On many levels there are alternate paths.
The skill ceiling comes from the fact that there are always more options than just pushing the gas and steering.
There are several different mechanics that allow you to accumulate small speed boosts, which you are constantly doing: Slide long enough (hinders the ability to turn the opposite direction while sliding), do a trick jump, go over a speed boost arrow/through a speed boost ring. Ontop of this you have the usual environmental hazards, opponents and weapons; so you're always trying to juggle 2-3 different things which gives the game longevity and interest.
The game has well designed levels based on classic sega game franchises. It is rarely difficult and confusing to see where you're going. Transformation rings and speed bosts are well telegraphed; the game does not rely heavily on memorization.
This game has no native support for and does not work well with racing wheels; it is best played with a controller. It has local multiplayer.

Wolfenstein 3D was a revolutionary game but does it hold up today and would I advise buying and playing it? Well, it's a minimalistic game with limited weapons with each weapon essentially being a faster version of the one that came before it and limited enemy types. There are dogs, weak enemies with pistols, fast enemies with pistols, strong enemies with pistols, a man with a machinegun and armour and numerous functionally identical bosses with 2 or 4 chainguns, perhaps even with a rocket launcher. The AI of the enemies is poor and the battles will often feel cheap. The levels are very linear with very few landmarks, making it difficult to navigate. The graphics quality is also a problem - while pixels are not necessarily bad, it may be hard to differentiate some things and it is advisable to rest your eyes from time to time.
Nonetheless, the game is fun and simple. For anyone looking for a minimal escape from modern gameplay, this game is worth trying out. For anyone who wants to explore FPS history, this game is an obvious starting point. Modern sourceports such as ECWolf and NewWolf have even fixed many graphical problems and added an automap to make things easier. When it came out, it was cutting edge and expensive. Now, it has fallen behind but it's only $5 so why not give it a go? 60 levels and hours of fun. It's terrific value for money.

As someone who enjoys difficult games, I just can't give this my recommendation.
Titan Souls is very obviously a game that is trying to ride on the "Souls-like" train. A game that is made to be difficult. A boss battle simulator.
Filled with difficult and creative bosses, Titan souls does make for an interesting formula. Interesting combat with fluid and nice controls. Beautiful pixel art...
The problem is the execution. You walk into a boss battle. You start running around blindly, and die to an attack that you couldn't have predicted. You respawn. You try again. You're hit by a different attack you couldn't have predicted. You try again. You dodge the attacks flawlessly and prepare to attack. You have no idea what you're aiming for. You die. You come back again and dodge blindly till you work out what to do next. You discover that the boss has other non-damaging attacks that move you around and screw you up. You die. You go back again. You find out one of the attacks you thought damaged you actually didn't. You try using this to your advantage. You still have no idea what to do. Suddenly an attack stuns the boss. You try to capitalise only for the boss's attack pattern to shift and suddenly be based on luck whether you are able to capitalise, seemingly moving randomly now. You die. After several dozen attempts, you do it flawlessly and kill the boss. Then you get an achievement that says you did something unecessary.
It's so bloody obtuse. You have no idea where to go. You have no idea what to do. It's F*cking trial and error. This is not a hard game. This is an unfair game. A hard game is like Monster Hunter or Darksouls where it's your skill that determines how far you make it, not your ♥♥♥♥ing obtuse reasoning on unrelated aspects to draw a conclusion.
Again, nah... It's not a game you should buy unless you're an M-type or have run out of games to play or it's very cheap.

Like others have said: generally strong concept, if deflated slightly by borrowing too much from Shadow of the Colossus. Okay visuals, decent lore, nice music, generally strong boss design. Judged on artistic merits Titan Souls is a thumbs up, although the graphics are nowhere near the ballpark of Ori or Hollow Knight or Hyper Light Drifter, or even really old 2D games like A Link to the Past or Super Metroid.
Unfortunately, the gameplay is extremely hit and miss. One huge issue is that majority of game time is spent running back to each boss after dying, which feels bearable at first but quickly becomes a major pain. Even more damningly, memorized positioning and luck are rewarded far too heavily compared to reflexes or skill. There are several exceptions to this, and these handful of Titan battles are the highlight of the experience. Finally defeating Titans does feel rewarding, but only for a moment as the next bout of frustration comes almost instantly. Exploration is highly underwhelming (there is almost nothing to find), there are no other monsters to fight in the world for a self-esteem boost, and there are practically no puzzles to mix up gameplay. Overall, Titan Souls is a boss rush mode stuffed with mediocre 2D walking simulator filler.
It took me just over 5 hours to beat it using a keyboard, a huge chunk of which I was stuck on the final final boss and a handful of other insufferably annoying Titans. Being locked to firing in 8 cardinal directions feels really limiting and makes an already difficult game even more difficult. The game does recommend using a controller, but why were better KB+M controls not implemented (like aiming with a mouse)? It's possible that a controller would alleviate some frustration, although looking at other reviews maybe not.
Tough call to make - and several bosses really do have wonderful visual and gameplay designs that are fun to experience - but the game is definitely not worth $15. I got the game for 75% off and even then it often made me wonder if I was wasting my time, despite only being 5 hours long. A small bit of polish and more respect for the gamer could have gone a long way in turning this into a positive review.

Review for Interstellar Marines Update #10
LINK TO VIDEO REVIEW:
Zero Point Software has proven that nothing will stop them from finishing Interstellar Marines. With long list of development setbacks, managing to get Interstellar Marines to this point is a huge accomplishment. For the past month, Zero Point Software has been working extremely hard to release the latest update for their game, update #10. Is it any good? Well, it’s a step in the right direction.
Visuals: At first glance, you will notice some major changes to the visuals. The HUD has been completely reworked, the weapon model has been replaced with a new, modern looking assault rifle, and the overall realism of the environments and their effects all blend together to make a very polished feel. I’ve been killed quite a few times while stopping to watch the environment change its weather cycle because it just looked that good. But, as much as I like the new visuals, the option to turn off the bloom effects has been removed, and while this makes the game fairer for those who would keep these effects on and play with the disrupted vision, the bloom glow effects can sometimes feel overused and disrupt the vision to the point of frustration. It would be nice to see ZPS turn down these effects or balance them more to keep the visual impact, but not make any sacrifices on the game-play side. Also, when you are walking, the HUD moves and bobs so much that it’s almost impossible to see who is on your team or what their score is without completing ceasing all movement. I liked to check how my friends are doing in previous updates but now I feel more excluded.
Gameplay: There is no doubt that Zero Point has worked very hard on making the experience in Interstellar Marines as smooth and polished as possible, and it really shows here. With the addition of a crouching and basic cover system in update #10, the tactical element has never felt more important. I’ve never had so much fun hopping from cover to cover with my squad mates. And the excellent improvements to the sound design only add to the overall experience.
In one instance, I would be moving from cover to cover with my squad mates to reach the building across, zzwhile being sniped by the enemy team from across the map. It’s moments like these which make Interstellar Marines different and memorable than any other shooter. The more ZPS improves the features in the game, the more the game will feel alive. Sometimes, though, the cover system doesn’t always work. The camera’s height adjustments when popping in and out of cover can feel a bit clunky and switching from crouching to standing to quickly escape gun fire feels too difficult to achieve and ends up in a cheap death. This isn’t a game breaker, but since the cover system is a big deal, after a few matches, the errors start to really stand out and impact my overall experience. With the lack of support for any communication with your squad mates personally in game, players are still forced to communicate through and outside source, which isn’t bad, but just a bit tedious. I understand that this is still an early update for the game, and the developers have promised some sort of squad communication system in the future, so I am looking forward to seeing what they will do with this.
Summary: Update #10 is a welcome addition to Interstellar Marines. While it has a few flaws, it’s a step in the right direction. It doesn’t do anything to drastically change the core game-play, but the additional features being added each update is really making a huge difference in the game and the fan base. ZPS has done an amazing job with the game so far, and I can’t wait to see where they take this game.
Visuals: 9.3 FANTASTIC VISUALS BUT THE OVERUSE OF BLOOM AND GLOW DISRUPTS GAMEPLAY
Gameplay: 7.5 CROUCH IS A SOLID IMPROVEMENT, BUT IT DOESN’T ALWAYS WORK
Audio: 9 EXCELLENT SOUND DESIGN HELPS PULL YOU INTO THE GAME
Lasting Appeal: 7.4 VERY FUN, BUT AFTER A FEW MATCHES, THE PROBLEMS START TO SHOW
Final Score: 8.3

Realtime vehicular combat with extensive customization (build your vehicle from the ground up).
If you just want to play at the highest power level you have available you can have issues as a free player, though a lot of it depends on your vehicle design and chosen weapons. However the RMT currency is earnable ingame at a reasonable rate and you can absolutely have lots of fun without paying any money whatsoever.
Decent matchmaking, which means that your "power score" is very important. Let it get too high by piling on lots of things and you will be fighting others with a similar power score. Build a more minimalist vehicle and your allies & enemies will be in more basic (and weaker) vehicles too.
The PvP & PvE are both fun, but I have not joined a guild so cannot comment on any guild-related content.
No direct trading, but the aution house lets to buy & sell looted / crafted items for RMT currency.
Standard group functionality, players required to ready up before queuing, group members easy to identify in the match, etc.
The MMO tag may be misleading though as it's really more of a lobby-based team deathmatch (capture the flag / king of the hill) for PvP with a variety of co-op game modes for PvE.
