Its story is gripping, intelligent, emotional. I laughed, I cried, I was captivated.
I had already watched the anime before, but I would recommend playing the game first.
For a long time, I heard that this visual novel was much better than the anime. To be honest, I wasn’t convinced at first. People usually say that when the book comes before the movie, and, personally, I like anime but I’m not a fan of reading manga. So I played the game semi-reluctantly.
And at first, I wasn’t enjoying it as much as the anime. It has more text, and is much more fleshed out. Because of that, Steins;Gate is a game that starts slowly. For the first 3 or 4 chapters (out of 10), I was only mildly-interested. Things were slow to happen. I then thought the game was overrated.
I was wrong.
All that bla-bla was necessary to really get inside each character’s head and habits, and to really have a big effect when the action comes. After chapter 4, I couldn’t stop playing!
What the Visual Novel does that the anime does not is show the inner dialogue of the protagonist, Okabe. Throughout the story, we are really in his shoes, and feel his pain, his despair, his happiness, and all the emotions he goes through while he slowly understands what is happening.
The voice acting is incredible. So is the soundtrack.
Contrary to the anime, the visual novel features many different endings. Most of them are satisfactory, but I did not stop playing until I found the True Ending (the one in the anime). I was skipping from save file to save file modifying my choices, feeling like the time travelling protagonist in the process ^_~.
But those cons are minor - Steins;Gate is simply a beautiful game.
TL;DR - El. Psy. Kongroo.

This game is... alright, I suppose, but barely worth half the price they ask - the amount of actual content in the game is not very large, with half of what content there is consisting of walking back to the boss after it killed you in 2 seconds, and overall the game is often more frustrating than fun.
While superficially the difficulty, the emphasis on boss fights, and, well, the title may make it tempting to relate the game to Dark Souls, this is a poor comparison. The thing that made Dark Souls boss fights work even in spite of the difficulty was that even when you lost you learned a bit more about the fight, and when you finally did win it was because of the combined effort of all of the previous attempts, not just because that one time you got lucky. Unfortunately, in this game, thanks to the predictability and limited movesets of the bosses (most have only one or two different actions), most fights consist of a few attempts - which is to say about two minutes - where you actually learn the fight and decide on a strategy, followed by a significantly longer period of executing that exact same strategy and hoping that it works. Not all the the fights were this bad, but the ones that were are the ones that I most remember, and perhaps unsurprisingly also the ones which took the most time. This is not the way a boss fight should be.
If this sounds like a harsh assessment of the game - and perhaps it is - this is largely because the concept seems really good. The actual execution, however, is poor - and so I can only really describe this game as disappointing.

Pros:
Very promising for an Alpha, one of the most polished I've seen in a while. The development process is made in to a 'storyline' it would seem, where the marines are currently doing a number of training scenarios. Future updates propose team based PvE combat against an unknown enemy as of yet(?) I haven't done that much digging in to exactly what is planned, but apparently it is the basis for the game. The PvP is fantastic, smooth and responsive. The level design is incredibly innovative and it will keep you interested throughout the entire round. Some levels will have the physical properties changed during stages of the round (doors/ramps being blocked or parts of the map moving up and down), and simulation of fire drills/power outages putting you in complete darkness and forcing you to change tactics.
Cons:
Server hosting issues where all across NA you will ping around 100 to the server, personally I ping 125-150 to every NA server despite this not being an issue anywhere else. This leads to a 1/4-1/2 second bullet delay, requiring you to lead moving targets slightly regardless of distance from you. This is also combined with a very small hit detection issue. Overall, the problem is minor for an Alpha considering it is the only apparent problem I've seen yet, and loving every second of the game otherwise.
The game is worth $15.00, so it's absolutely worth it for you to grab it at 7.50 on one of the sales or even pick up the more expensive version and score a free copy for a friend + some exclusive titles for you being a founder.

There are objects in the world.  Some fall under the category 'Games'.  Some fall under the category 'Art'.  But is there a category for an object that falls under both?  There is.  That category is called 'Bridge Constructor'.
Perhaps you think, "No! Bridge Constructor is not an art game; it is an engineering game."  To which I say, "Non Monsieur/Madame/Mademoiselle, non!"  Then I finish my thought in English because that is all the French I know.  Remember, you are
(apologies if you thought that this game might let you do that).  You are creating simulations, models, dreams of your inner self.  What you create on screen is you; you are what you create on screen.  I repeat: once you play this game, there will be bridges inside of you.
It should also be known that this game tells the story of a world.  Do you wonder what drives the cars, the trucks, the tankers?  Wonder no more my friend: it is a race of little insect people.  Ants?  Bees?  Weevils?  I do not know: insects.  All I know is that they cannot fly.  If they could, they would not need bridges.
-------------- The Story of JD7QW --------------
Designate JD7QW buckled the seatbelt around his carapaced waist, its legs quivering as it did so.  It tried to hide its fright, but even from outside the tanker truck the Planner noticed.
"JD7QW," the Planner said, its mandibles clicking furiously, "this is no time for fear.  You are performing the function for which you were produced, as am I.  By testing this bridge we are expanding the reach of the Colony and celebrating the greatness of the Queen.  That is all we can do.  That is all we shall do."
Not daring to look at the Planner, JD7QW nodded while fixing its gaze straight ahead.  The bridge in front of it was very wooden and very straight.  It also appeared very fragile, like sunlight on water.  How could it hold the weight of the enormously flammable tanker?  "I imagine that there are supports underneath?" JD7QW asked, doing its best to hide its anxiety.  "Steel?  Perhaps concrete?"
"Such questions!" the Planner snapped.  "I will answer, but know that I will be filing a Protest when I return to the Colony."  It shook its engorged head.  "It appears that the Breeders are producing defective Designates."
Again JD7QW did not dare turn around.  Instead it looked up.  The sky was cloudless and blue, so clear that the ghost of the moon could be faintly seen even in the daytime.
, the Designate thought suddenly.
But of course it couldn't.  Only the Queen was allowed to have wings.
The Planner continued.  "There is no steel.  There is no concrete.  There is wood and only wood.  But -"  The Planner's voice softened.  Surprised, JD7QW peeked over.  The Planner's mandibles had slowed, its multi-faceted eyes had grown clouded and dreamy.  "- but oh, the design, the joins and triangles and descending supports, the interlocking wheels of pressure and release, the. . ."  Caught up in the Planner's vision, it allowed itself to think:
Then the Planner shook its head.  Its voice turned to jagged stone.  "No more!  You are impudent, JD7QW.  Drive now.  Go."
It stepped back.  Unwilling and unable to disobey, JD7QW depressed the gas pedal and the tanker truck rumbled forward.
A short segment of paved road lay between the truck and the bridge.  It took both an instant and an eternity to cross.  Then JD7QW felt the wheels beneath him
as it rattled onto the wooden bridge, and right away it knew that it would not survive that day.
The bridge was already beginning to sway, the surface to buckle.  A series of grand snapping noises echoed within the ravine, each one like the shattering of an enormous tree.  The truck began to
; frantic, JD7QW pressed the gas pedal with all its strength.  The truck jerked forward, and for a moment the Designate thought that the vehicle might simply plow through the air to the other side, an invincible and impossible metal beast.
Then the wooden surface below him imploded, and the truck fell in earnest.
JD7QW barely had time to squeeze its eyes shut, to gag at the vortex in its stomach, when the fuel tank exploded.  Free of its burden, the cab of the truck shot up into the air, and the sudden reverse in sensation caused JD7QW's eyes to fly open in surprise.  And what it saw through the broken windshield was blue, endless blue, with the ghost of the moon traced far above.
It knew there wasn't much time left.  With legs that were no longer trembling, it pressed the release on the seat buckle.
The Designate shot out of the vehicle immediately.  Below him, the truck cab had already slowed and was falling back to earth.
, JD7QW thought.
And it began to smile as it dreamed of what it might find there.
----------------------------------------
There is a JD7QW inside all of us.  If not for yourself, play this game for it.

My issues with the game are:

1. The transformation system is ridiculous, you should have the choice of which transformation you want to take on, which brings me to my next point.
2. Move sets should NOT be relevant to the costume you pick, why not just use a similar system to Raging Blast and make custom sets for the characters and pick whichever costume you like?
3. Some Supers, Ultimates and Z-Souls are extremely unbalanced and are just way to necessary for Online Battles, a good example is the "I'm neither Kami nor Piccolo now..." Z-Soul, It is ridiculously over powered and feels like a staple if you want the best character you can possibly make.
4. A lot of the parallel missions feel stupidly unfair, for example 'Super Saiyan Bargain Sale' or 'Super Super Ultimate Series of Battles', both ridiculously unfair since the first time you take them on you have to do it alone, not to mention that by the end of them its 3v1 and they're all Super saiyan and spamming their ultimates every 5 seconds, and for anyone who hasn't played it yet, that is seriously NOT an exaggeration ...
5. There are very few combos in the game that work or even feel viable, i've played fighting games all my life and let me tell you that this is one of the clunky and unresponsive ones.
6. Dialogue and subs are so sloppy it baffled me, how can you even miss that...

This game takes everything Mario Kart Wii U tried to do and get's it right!
It's a truely next-gen game. The tracks are awesome - I mean litterally awesome. Each one is really creative, unique and stays fresh and exciting for each lap.  Most maps also have a bunch of short-cuts to be discovered and multiple routs to take. It's something you really have to experience for yourself to get it. But once you race on these tracks, Mario Karts' tracks will just look really dull and boring by comparison.
The carreer mode offers a really honest progression system. Unlike Mario Kart where you play but don't really know what you'll get for playing. This game makes it clear. Each race can earn you up to 3 stars (easy, med, hard). New carrear paths, characters, and vehicle mods are spread out throughout carreer mode with a required star value to unlock. This really motivates me to beat the game on hard because I know exactly what I'll get for it, and it'll be worth it - not some lame new tire like in Mario Kart.
There is no vehicle customization. Probably the most notibale new feature of mario kart wii U was customizing your vehicle. But the feature hurts more than it helps because rather than customizing for asthetic fun, you try to mix and match character weight class to vehicle parts to get the best kart performence. So in Mario Kart it sucks if there's a combination you like but the stats for that combo are weak.
Instead this game has each character matched with a unique vehicle that reflects their personality. This makes more sense and in return gives the characters more personality. Also, vehicles are level set to start. Playing through career mode with each character unlocks performance mods for that character's car. The mods have names like Balanced, Handling, Boost etc.. Boost for example really ups the stats for boost but takes away from exceleration etc.. each mod is balanced and consistent with every other car. There are no secret power combination in this game. Best of all, carreer mode has events which make you want to try different mods. For example the drift challenges might make you want to use handling. While the boost challenges would obviously encourage you to use the boost mod. And in races you might want to use balanced although the mod you choose really depends on your racing style.
I haven't onlocked all of the characters yet but I'm pretty sure there's no Glitch. Which is really dissappointing - I mean, why have Wreck-it-Ralph and not Glitch?  Anyway, the characters and their maps are REALLY different.  At no point do you trully feel like all of these characters belong in the same universe. It's a bit uncanny but it in no way hurts the gameplay. In fact, I like that I can play as BD Joe and my wife can play as Amy - if that makes sense. Point is there's a better chance this game has a character you really like - even if your favorite character doesn't look like he/she belongs in the same universe as your friends favorite character.
TL:DR
I'm enjoying this game WAY more than Mario Kart Wii U, and I think you will too. :)

As the basic archetype of the first-person shooter genre, Wolfenstein 3D was the earliest of ways to immerse yourself into a videogame, bent on survival instincts and critical thinking. Obviously, though, it hasn't aged well. The game provided on Steam is packaged to run using an emulator called DOSBox, allowing you to run DOS games on any modern Operating System.
Controlling the game was primitive, either using only the keyboard or mouse or setting up a gamepad with a very limited amount of buttons to assign to. This limit can be removed if you decide to throw out DOSBox and use a source port.
The retro sounds of FM music and jagged digital sound effects and voice clips are memorable. The dark and gritty synthesizers set the eerie and industrial mood to remind you to tread slowly through the 90-degree corridors of Nazi Germany's fortresses. The loud and low-quality gunfire from your person encourages you to defend yourself while the noises and cries from the enemies remind you to be aware and resourceful, as guards, dogs, the SS, and even mutants are armed to the teeth, ready to kill for their leader.
The graphics for its time were nice and colorful, detailing the hand-drawn characters and blood that erupts from their corpse pretty well. The first time you ever see it might disturb you. But it's one of many, so take the first blood with a grain of salt, because you're gonna wanna get used to the fact that you'll be fighting against practically an army to get the to the end of each chapter.
Level design was limited to 90-degree angle corridors like a line maze. It helps to have a navigational memory as you're likely to get lost on the way to the end of each floor.
There are several secrets in this game to keep yourself afloat in the maze. Extra lives, treasure and different guns can help you keep your head in the game and fight back with your own fire. Wouldn't have been a much interesting game without some diversity.
For what it's worth, don't be afraid to get your feet wet with where the FPS genre originated from and the exaggerated history lesson it brings as both a game and a fantasized side-story of World War II. But the best experience you can get from this game nowadays is investing the time and resources to set up a more modernized installation with source ports and community mods made across the Internet.

Wolfenstein 3D is quite the old game. It's the FPS that started it all. While not as popular as doom, it will always have a place in history. How is it compared to games of today? As well as any 25 year old game would. However, I wouldn't dismiss it completely. Some ideas still work even when it's limited at times.
The graphics have aged somewhat well. Nothing sticks out as unappealing, however there isn't much variation with wall designs, leading to too many rooms looking the same. The strong points are the little touches, like skeletons and food plates in jail cells. It really stuck out to me as dark and horrifying for such an old game.
The sound works well. Every enemy has a death cry and doors have sounds when they open or close. The effect of picking up items make getting them kinda satisfying. And the soundtrack does it's job just fine. The controls can be an issue. It doesn't start with the typical w,a,s,d button layout with mouse movement games of today use, but you can change it to feel more modern.
The gameplay has it's biggest highlights and flaws. First off it's still fun to shoot nazis. Period. The gunplay uses a bit of auto aim but don't think that makes this easy. You will die a lot. You lose health quick, particularly on higher difficulty levels. One big issue is there isn't a map(that i'm aware of). This is fine for old rpgs, but this game is far too fast paced for that. The game also has problems with repetition. There's not much enemy variety and most floors really drag themselves out. The most break you get from shooting is simply looking for keys. It's hard to be too critical though. This game is part of history and I recommend it for that alone. This game lead to amazing titles like doom,quake, and kickstarted FPS's in general, so it should be respected. Besides it still has one of the most awesome final bosses ever. Hitler in a giant mech.
Your move call of duty...
Overall 6/10- Getting lost so much really drags it down but there are enough highlights to make it worth my time. Just remember this is a game over two decades old.

Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD)[note 1] is a mental disorder that can develop after a person is exposed to a traumatic event, such as sexual assault,
, traffic collisions, or other threats on a person's life.[1] Symptoms may include disturbing thoughts, feelings, or dreams related to the events, mental or physical distress to trauma-related cues, attempts to avoid trauma-related cues, alterations in how a person thinks and feels, and an increase in the fight-or-flight response.[1] These symptoms last for more than a month after the event.[1] Young children are less likely to show distress but instead may express their memories through play.[1] A person with PTSD is at a higher risk for suicide and intentional self-harm.[2]
Most people who have experienced a traumatic event will not develop PTSD.[2] People who experience interpersonal trauma (for example♥♥♥♥♥♥or child abuse) are more likely to develop PTSD, as compared to people who experience non-assault based trauma such as accidents and natural disasters.[5] About half of people develop PTSD following♥♥♥♥♥♥[2] Children are less likely than adults to develop PTSD after trauma, especially if they are under ten years of age.[6] Diagnosis is based on the presence of specific symptoms following a traumatic event.[2]
Prevention may be possible when therapy is targeted at those with early symptoms but is not effective when carried out among all people following trauma.[2] The main treatments for people with PTSD are counselling and medication.[3] A number of different types of therapy may be useful.[7] This may occur one-on-one or in a group.[3] Antidepressants of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor type are the first-line medications for PTSD and result in benefit in about half of people.[4] These benefits are less than those seen with therapy.[2] It is unclear if using medications and therapy together has greater benefit.[2][8] Other medications do not have enough evidence to support their use and in the case of benzodiazepines may worsen outcomes.[9][10]
In the United States about 3.5% of adults have PTSD in a given year, and 9% of people develop it at some point in their life.[1] In much of the rest of the world, rates during a given year are between 0.5% and 1%.[1] Higher rates may occur in regions of armed conflict.[2] It is more common in women than men.[3] Symptoms of trauma-related mental disorders have been documented since at least the time of the ancient Greeks.[11] During the World Wars study increased and it was known under various terms including "shell shock" and "combat neurosis".[12] The term "posttraumatic stress disorder" came into use in the 1970s in large part due to the diagnoses of U.S. military veterans of the Vietnam War.[13] It was officially recognized by the American Psychiatric Association in 1980 in the third edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-III).[14]

I just beat this game with a keyboard in about 4 hours with alittle over 300 deaths. Honestly I enjoyed myself a lot.
In this game you have a bow and a single arrow. You can recall this arrow after you fire it or pick it up, while firing or recalling you can't move. You also have a dodge roll. Its a boss rush game at its core, The main gimmick being that most bosses die in a single hit. You also die in a single hit.
In this game I felt like a hunter, I studied each boss I encountered. I learned what its weak spot was, when and how it could be revealed, when was the earliest I could hit it. Then I'd practice and experiment to set up the kill. This led to a few bosses being killed in under 10 seconds. After many deaths of course.
Do not buy this game unless you have decent will to overcome a challenge. A lot of the bad reviews are from players with little patience.
Other peoples biggest complaints I see are.......
1. This time to get back to a boss is too long: The run back to a boss after death is nothing on par with dark souls. Its 20-30 seconds at most. Usually its 10-15. There are checkpoints near every boss.
2.The controls are poor and bosses are too fast: The games controls aren't bad, people have been blaming poor controls when they should be blaming themselves. Every one of my 300+ deaths was my fault for rolling too soon, too late, or missing a shot. Every boss is predictable as they have a set attack pattern and base their movement around yours. Think of it as a puzzle, How can I manipulate this bosses movements to line up that perfect shot?
3.If your using a keyboard you can only fire your arrow in 8 directions: I beat the game this way. Its harder but perfectly doable. 8 directions limits what you can do bigtime but with planning and proper movement you can do it. I would advise to just play this on controller, but don't let weaker keyboard controls be a deal breaker.

One mayor problem I had with this game, though, was that after more than one hour of playing, I still didn't get one single choice to make.

But the story is very weird (and not in a good way ... usually I like weird ... but this was more a you-gotta-be-kidding-me-weird), and the main character is annoying as hell. The levels generally consist of a generic "beat em up" style linear walkthrough of a course, followed by a boss battle.
The biggest issue I have with the game, is that the 1 vs 1 fighting style is INCREDIBLY unbalanced. Its entirely possible to fight one boss without taking a single hit of damage, and then lose the next while landing almost no blows. There is no linear progression of difficulty because of how unbalanced it actually is.
Its also really common place to beat the 100+ enemies before the boss without taking a single point of damage, and then lose to the boss in under a minutes worth of fighting.
I would STRONGLY suggest that the developers of the game look at how the battle system actually works, and FIX it. Its impossible to break out of combos leading to the sort of button spamming style of win that most franchise had resolved in the 90's, making the losses incredibly frustrating and the wins worth almost nothing.
If you're playing the game purely for the CG boobs and expecting nothing else, than this game is a good fit. If you honestly want any sort of depth or balance in a game, you should probably look somewhere else.
On a side note, this is one of the most poorly optimized games I have ever played.  I can play GTA5 on ultra on my 3K monitor at 45fps, however attemtping to play this game on anything over 1080 causes the game to grind to a halt. The gameplay speed is also tied to the framerate, meaning that you WILL see large fluctuations in play speed from events as simple as NPCS spawning in the battle ground.
TLDR; I want to like this game, but I really cant. I want to finish the game, but honestly I dont think I will. I really wish I hadn't bothered with it.

Senran Kagura is a series known for its ever growing cast of cute characters and its hack & slash gameplay. For those unfamilair with the series and need a reference, think of it as a Dynasty Warriors game on a much smaller scale, with a cast of characters that consist of young female ninja's.
The story to the game takes place six months after the second game, Senran Kagura 2: Deep Crimson (SK2:DC). Every character that was included with the vanilla game of SK2:DC is now back, and with the roster that doubles in size, more fan service, and customizable outfits for your characters. You have the choice of choosing between three different school's with five playable characters each to progress on how the following events to SK2:DC take place. With a foruth school of six characters to be unlocked. Hanzo academy, Gessen academy, Heboji academy, and Homura Crimson Squad. The Story varies depending on which academy you pick, and gives you the option to switch between academies in between missions. However they do not all co-exist alongside each other. Each main story consists of five chapters with five missions to play in each. You can either play through as one of your favorite characters the entire way, or rotate between the characters you have for the sake of variety. Along side the main story, each individual character has there own side story of five levels to play through. These stories are seperate from the main plot of the game and are mostly there for achievment sake to give the player more to do. During these side stories, you can only experience them all by playing as each individual character. Completing them simply gives players more achievements, experience points for the characters, and more items to purchase from the in-game store.
Cutscene's in the game however are very low in both quantity & quality. Majority of your time in this game will be spent simply reading tons of dialouge and exposition over gameplay. In a variety of two different ways, cutscenes will play out like visual novels that alot of japanese games have. With a background image thats partly faded, then paragraphs of information that a mandatory for understanding the plot to the game. Then there's more anime traditional cutscene's were various character models will appear on screen and interact with each other over their dialouge que's. This form of story telling is fine, however the character models themselves will distract you from the tension. Not because of the fan service or appeal that the game provides, but perhaps the biggest visual glitch in the game occurs, the game doesn't seem to know what outfit the characters are wearing, even if you haven't changed anything, the character models from their navel region; downwards will be patchy in a bizzare mash-up of color's, random pixel's, and piece's of outfits you can just barely recognize, even if said item thats showing up hasn't been unlocked yet. It can even be seen through the bright blue dialouge boxes. There are very few moments in the game when this issue doesn't occur and somehow it doesn't appear in any moments other than the cutscene's themselves. Whats noteworthy is you'll find yourself mashing the A button constantly as most of the dialouge is irrelevant, not contributing to the overall plot. By simply reading every other sentence or two your able to make out whats happening in the story to continue, so there's no need at all to see through and read every individual box of dialouge that makes an appearence.
The combat system & level design: After cutscene's, battle's will begin to play, each mission will take you onto a number of different locations, the only difference being which character you fight at the end, and how much ground you'll actually cover. It doesn't matter which story mode, academy, or character you play as, each level will play out the same. You'll begin in a fixed position on the map with a horde of enemies in your path, elminate them all without losing and you can progress further onto the map. Go through about two or three waves of enemies at each stopping point and you'll be given a boss character to fight. Beat said boss character at the end and you win. This is how previous Senran Kagura games have played out.
Each character you play as has a health guage that gradually gets longer the more you play as them and level up, and a ninja scroll meter for transformation's, secret ninja art's, and entering "Frantic mode". this too, gets longer as you level up with each character and lets you hold more scrolls for longer combo's. The basic gameplay for combat set's you in 3D enviorments to fight the many hordes of enemies with hack and slash gameplay. Leveling up boosts the characters stats and lets you use even more attacks to make your combo's even longer, more effective, and more efficient. On top of that, each charcter has three more meter's that fill up and upgrade depending on how you play. those are: Yin, Yang, and Flash.
Yin is applied when a player enter's "Frantic mode".  When a character has enough ninja's scroll's at one time, guard, the press their heav attack button, the camera will zoom in on your characters chest. Either press the heavy attack button again or move the character to the left or right and their clothes will fly off of them, down to their undergarments. in this mode your attack increases a ton along with your overall speed. However your defense will be reduced greatly. so use this only if your looking to get the job done quickly. However chances are you won't notice since the frequency in which combo's go, you'll only be hit if you either stand around for too long or just stop attacking.
Yang is applied when you use one ninja scroll and transform into your charcters ninja outfit, your attacks and defense are greatly increased. but you become slightly slower. howver you won't even notice becuase you'll be attack the opponents so frequently that you'll rarely be hit.
Flash is applied when you choosing neither option and go all out as you see fit in your standard clothes. Unless your struggling for extra health or just want to see the transformation animation again, this is how you'll experience most the game.
Once a level is completed you'll be given a grade based on how quickly you completed it, how many times you were hit, how many enemies you killed, and how long of a combo you were able to deal. Alongside some in-game currency and EXP, thats it.
How long will each level take you, and how tough is the overall experience? very little. This is the game's BIGGEST PROBLEM. The combat, and level's sound nice on paper, but the way they play out are overlly tedious and repetitive at best. Levels will only get shorter and shorter as you learn the controls and get a few level ups. at the start of the game levels many take anywhere from 6 minutes, and onwards. After learning the controls (and even simple attack spamming) levels will last as little as 15 seconds to close to a minute. (Thats no exaggeration either.) There's no real risk to dying since you level up during the combat itself and rewarded with any you didn't receive outside of battle right at the end. So there's no overall challenge, levels will take you back to the same arena so you'll contstantly be running to where the enemies spawn, use one or two attacks and they'll all die immedeatly. Little to no skill is involved here. This where its said that most of your playtime will be spent on the cutscenes since no level will keep you still long enough to really enjoy. Grinding is easy and simplistic, levels are small and lacking variety, its so brain dead that you'll quit playing to look for something with actual challenge and balancing to it.
The fan service and design are where this game stands out, but from the level of overlly reptitive gameplay and bad storytelling (compared to previous games), its just not worth the 30 dollar investment. Play a different SK game if you care that much.

This review was relevant to when this game was initially new.
There's no reason in my opinion , to purchase this game now that's it's sequel - Xenoverse 2 is out.
Before I even review the game I want to point out something important.
This is the first Dragon ball Z game to be released on PC in years (About 10 years give or take)
That alone is enough of a reason for you to buy it.
Why you may ask? Because the second game developers and publishers understand that it's popular here as much as it is on console (they can make money from us PC gamers),then every new game will also be released on PC as well.
Think about the Naruto ninja storm games. They released 3 for PC, and it turned out to be a big success. They also released Revolution on PC alongside the console releases as well.
In short support this PC/Steam release DBZ game for future titles for the master race.
Now for the actual review.
As a person who has had the chance to play most of the modern Dragon ball Z games to date.
I'd say Xenoverse is AMAZING.
Granted it does have it's flaws, but it does try to be different in a good way, and it has succeeded.
Pros:
-Outstanding soundtracks! I've found myself listening to a couple when not the game.
-An actual GOOD character creation (Looking at you Ultimate tenkaichi)
-A lot of moves to choose from and since there aren't many "bad" ones you actually have a varity of choice, rather than everyone using the same ones.
-The different races are actually fairly balanced and have a simliar pick rate. At first i thought the game would be populated with super saiyans, but i was wrong everyone is creative and picks different looks and skills making players actually feel unique.
-Team battle done right. (Yeah looking at you "Battle of Z")
-An actual challanging experience.Unlike most DBZ games you don't slide through every quest and mission with one attempt. I've personally spent dozens of attempts on a couple of missions myself and i enjoyed the challenge.
-Very appealing visuals
-The most SMOOTH game play i have ever experienced in a DBZ game for a while.
-MMO Feel. Actual intercation with other players.
-Towa's model
-Steam release!
Cons:
-It's been quite a while and the server issues are still not fixed, so online may be a bit sluggish for now. (Ignore this once the servers are fixed)
-The voice acting isn't really great. Granted most of the original cast was present, but the script and the acting itself was average from past games preformance's.
-The subtitles are sometimes incorrect. Showing something that isn't relevant to the actual speech. I suppose that's a translation error.
-The rooster isn't that large. And while I am aware that I'm obviously not gonna play EVERY character that BT3 represented. I do feel the lack of specific things bothering, such as "Future Gohan",Not SSJ "Teen Gohan","Zarbon" ,"Dadoria","Friezas" 2nd and 3rd forms, and a few other metionables..
-RNG factor. As much as I'm aware that Grinding and lucky drops are part of any MMO atmosphere. Repeating a task over 20 times just to receive something that isn't worth it gets on your nerves eventually.
That being said that same RNG factor is present in AI battles.
When sometimes a specific "boss" battle the enemy spams ultimates on you non stop making it impossible for you to win. Or the complete opposite  can happen and they NEVER use the ultimate and you win without difficulty.

Before I get to the actual review, I want to say that I don't recommend this game as a must have. It is deeply flawed but I do enjoy the game despite its flaws so I do "recommend" it. However, $50 is too pricey for a game like his.
Some more details are at the end.
Pros:
-Dragon Ball that is not 1v1
- Lots of moves
-Not too simplified
Cons:
- Graphics
- 1 accessory slot
- Deadly Tokitoki city
- jerky controls
- only 4 super moves and 4 ultimate attacks can be equipped
- (no weaponry)
- voice acting
- no varied movesets
Graphics and Tokitoki City
The graphics are much too simple. Its not a problem with cel-shading. The city is much too big and too little detail. It resembles a game in its early stages. Some characters move around, most others just stand there. Its pretty much a dead city. Not lively, not full of much detail.
I understand some of the rationale behind making a static city but to me, it comes off as poor design and laziness.  If the cel-shading doesn't allow for intricate details, then make this more compact. Giving too much space to move in a matrix-like emptiness isn't fun or atmospheric.
1 Accessory Slot/equipment
I know this isn't tekken but still, one of the selling points of DB:Xenoverse was its character customization. Character creation was a little lackluster but I'm not complaining about that. The accessories however, is a different story.
Accessories include decoractive swords and caps. I haven't unlocked any other types but I imagine that there could and should be more accessory types.
Is it that difficult to have an accessory slot for different parts of the body? They already have 4 seperate equipment slots for the torso, legs, hands and feet so I don't see how an accessory slot for the head and back will make much of a difference.
One could argue that excess accessories could overpower the player (equipment have stat boosts and debuffs) but that can be easily solved by removing stat bonuses for the accessories.
Besides, I haven't had an accessory that boosted stats yet anyways.
Jerky/Irresponsive Controls (Keyboard user problems but some aren'tkeyboard only)
I'm writin this as a keyboard user. I've played many other combat/action games and one game that has a similar attack scheme was Dynasty Warriors. The attacks in Dynasty Warrior seemed to flow nicely but the normal attacks in DB seemed to be very stiff and rigid as if it were in early stages of programming.
Its hard to put it into words but trust me, the attack flow in DB:Xenoverse could use
of improvement.
I have two examples.
One is pulling out during an attack. Every animation in DB:X has to be completed in its full cycle unless interrupted by an enemy attack. This is reasonable for a few attacks like Double Sunday or Galick Gun but for normal attacks, this comes off as poor design.
Another one is some irresponsiveness in chaining normal attacks with supers. I'd try to use Meteor Crash (a super move) a few times and it just takes seconds before the game registers the ctrl key, leaving me vulnerable for those few seconds. Sometimes it would register the ctrl key but it won't register the mouse click. Do I click too fast? No. I click after the ctrl key registers and after the buttons say that I can use that super but nothing happens.
Only 4 super moves
Restricting 4 super moves is very restrictive. And it makes for a less interesting battle than it could be if more super moves could be equipped.
First off, normal attacks are all the same for any created character of the same race. There is no learning new normal attacks or new normal chain attacks which means that if you enter the a battle without using any ability, all the battles will have the same look.
I understand that the game was designed around a console controller but even with the console controller, they could have had 2 skill sets of 4 for skill swapping during battle. Not that difficult. I've seen other older games do it. A control scheme would not impede gameplay like some people think.
I'm a keyboard user and I still think that the game could use an extra button for swapping skill sets in the middle of battle.
The only thing that would hold this design back is whoever does the programming for this game. As I said earlier, key responsiveness is poor and whoever did the programming for that did a poor job.
Voice Acting
DBZ voice acting has always had poor acting in my opinion. But I feel like they use that as a selling point. They all sound like uneducated rednecks.
Hey, the voice acting is the same as the anime but they could have tried to move forward instead of keeping the same voices. Most of the viewers are no longer children. No need to entertain us usng poor voice acting.
No Weaponry/Extra movesets
The problem here isn't about not using weapons as much as learning moves from other characters
One of the features in this game is having a master who will occasionally offer missions to the character for new moves. But in DB:X, the only customizable moves are supers and ultimates.
Normal attacks do grow boring after a while since the order pan out the same way.
Not using a sword isn't a killer but I've always wanted to have a Trunks character who can use the sword or something. DBZ had only a few characters with weaponry but weaponry was still there. Its not like the weapons have to have stats or anything. Its about the movesets.
Again, I enjoyed the game but I feel that the game is deeply flawed. Buy it when it hits the bargain bin though since its definitely worth somwhere around $20-$40

Okay. this game is great, but it makes me want to gouge my eyes out.
Like, jesus, don't play on permadeath, it doesn't add any challenge to the game and merely punishes you for things you can't control permanently. You can basically lose the perfect team to fire and a bunch of alphabeavers.
I get that hardcore and rogue-like 'n all that♥♥♥♥♥♥is really popular right now, but jesus. I can't enjoy this damn game without dying in-game at least once a day in real life. It feels like there's no point in putting any effort into it because you're just going to die soon enough!
It's like if you had a toaster that could toast the best kind of toast, but then would spontaenously combust after you take the toast out. Now you have a toaster that exploded, and a singed piece of toast. It doesn't matter if the toast is made perfect, 'cause it still gets caught in the explosion anyway!
I could compare this game to something like Prison Architect. When you first start off you put an hour into planning out your prison and working out all of the schedules and the systems. There may be some bumps like a couple of riots, but you can still recover from those kinds of setbacks.
However, in Rimworld, when you first start off, you put an hour or less into planning out how to build this damn thing so that it doesn't explode from a stray boomrat, and then your team of pawns gets attacked by raiders with frickin' frag grenades within less than a year of in-game time. You can't recover from that♥♥♥♥♥♥ because you're doctor is down, you're outta medicine, and two of your guys have infections. I have basically quit from four different play sessions pre-emptively because I know that there is no way to turn the situation around.
If your characters get caught in a fight, they're going to get damaged, no matter what, While I appreciate the realism, it still is tarnished by the fact that you are not given the tools to recover from such fights, or you do have the tools, but don't have the effort to deal with it.
It's like your ship in FTL, usually when you start taking hits, your chances of survival dwindles faster, even if you have a high hull gauge. Except, in that game, you actually have the tools to fight back, and there's not that bad of a loss if you do die, because you can start right up again almost instantly.
When you die, or your crippled enough that you know death is inevitable, so you quit, you lose everything. You lose the team, the settlement, the equipment, and it takes so long to acquire that stuff that it feels like a huge pain to even try again. It also requires a lot of luck, because I don't know if there's going to be a good setup for me to build my settlement once again, or if I can find a team good enough to survive the bull that the game throws at you.
I mean, okay. I like a challenge, I like difficulty and "playing the game how it was meant to be played", but I don't want to when I keep losing my stuff that I put a lot of time into, so that I have to start all the way back to square one. I wouldn't mind having an imperfect team if I could still have some fun with it. I wouldn't mind having a lackluster setup for construction if I felt as though it could give me a fair challenge. But I can't recover from it. I can't! That's why the best team and the most calculated and planned out settlement is required, 'cause otherwise, you're done before you even press start game.
I mean, fine, I could just not play on permadeath, but then it just feels like the game is cheating me out of being much more fined tuned by just letting me have a sudden psychic ability to know that the boomrat is going to explode in my kitchen. I don't get why I should have to have saves when I should just be able to enjoy the damn game in "how it was meant to be played", which is on permadeath.
Maybe I'm just being pissy. Maybe I'm holding a grudge against something that I could fix by just leaving a red "X" next to permadeath, or choosing an easier difficulty, but what's the fun in no challenge, but as well with an unfair challenge.
I think what would make it a better experience for me is if I could actually feel like I had an effect on the game. 'Cause when all hope is gone, that's just it. All of your work just goes *blip* and that's it, game over, I have gained nothing outside of the couple of hours I put into a run.
TL;FU: Game is fun when you reach the peak of your settlement, death ruins it and doesn't add to the experience. The slow and calculated build-up to a somewhat working settlement doesn't help with the fact that it could all just shatter within minutes. Kinda feels like there isn't a point to even trying when I feel there is no chance of succeeding or I'll just die to RNG.
I still like the actual game tho. The realism is actually really flippin' cool and I feel like there is a lot of depth to how this game works, but I don't feel like seeing how far down it goes because I keep breaking my legs on the damn sides of the hole. I know I could try climbing back up, but I know I won't get far with a pair of broken legs.

I hated this game when I first played. I didn't like the tracks switching almost every lap. I didn't like the controls. I didn't like any aspect of it. Then my friend forced this game upon me by buying it and I'm glad he did. I really enjoy this game. The
is pretty rock solid. This game is also certified local co-op! It's as easy as pressing start!
"Another Super Mario Kart clone". Perhaps, but this game does it's best to make sure your paying attention at all times. There is always an opportunity to boost or get ahead but proper steps need to be taken in order to make it to first. The biggest difference in this game in regards to other race battle games is that drifting (to acquire boost) is essentially critical. You don't have to hit an arrow to receive a boost. Rather drifting for a certain amount of time will give you a basic turbo. Keep drifting though and notice the color of your thrusters changing colors. Going from red to blue, you'll notice a definite kick to your character upon doing a successful drift. This is a big feature in this game where now it doesn't seem really appealing, but upon playing it the game mechanics will pull you in. On top of that, don't forget you can do tricks with the right stick if you want more boost!
Is there weapons in this game? Of course! Some weapons (and defensive weapons) included are baseball glove (that catches and gives you the weapon fire at you), freeze-balls with the ability to freeze opponents, blowfish that sit like mines, wasp swarms that set up "roadblocks", a rocket that locks on to opponents, a firecracker that fires in a straight line, "going all-star" which is similar to Mario Kart's star except you can shoot specialized rockets that rebound and follow, boost and explosive hot rod engines. The beauty of firing weapons is that you have the OPTION of shooting them backwards or forwards. This is a neat feature as this adds another depth to the game.
The tracks themselves (to say the least) are unique. I imagine it wasn't easy designing one course that would transform throughout the race. I should mention that the "Transformed" actually means that your mode of transportation transforms. It can either be a car, a (hover)boat or an airplane. So combine that with the tracks and you can get some challenging races but some over the top scenery to dodge. "Drifting" around a dinosaur in an airplane while trying to go through a boost while trying to shoot at an enemy is no easy work. The levels definitely seem like a lot of attention has been given to them.
On top of all this, they've added different game modes. The main menu offers career mode, match making and custom game. What is really cool is (local) players can play online as well as play in career mode! Having a hard time with a time attack? Wouldn't hurt to have a buddy to help you out. Some of the varying game modes include boost challenges, evasion, time attack, single race and even attack simulations where you have to destroy a tank while dodging his attacks. Characters themselves have the ability to level up (depending on how much you play with them) and your buddies character can level up at the same time. Upon leveling up, you will unlock certain modifiers for your car (such as boost to acceleration, handling etc...).
The
are decent graphics but it seems they attempted to pay attention to every little detail. For example, in the main menu there aren't much options regarding maps (as they haven't been unlocked). Upon unlocking them, you'll see more of these maps on your main screen. The maps as I've said are really interesting and really neat to play through. The characters at times will seem to fall out of their vehicle while doing stunts or boosting.The
are actually very good as each individual character has different dialogue for different situations. Little diversity concerning the explosion sounds and it would have been complete. I should add that when the announcer is saying 3-2-1 go that the player should hit "accelerate" (or RT) every time he says a number. This will give you a boost at the start.
Overall, a really good game. It gives Mario Kart a run for it's money  but I wouldn't say it's better or worse. It's tough to compare the two but Sonic Racing is definitely fun.

, traffic collisions, or other threats on a person's life.[1] Symptoms may include disturbing thoughts, feelings, or dreams related to the events, mental or physical distress to trauma-related cues, attempts to avoid trauma-related cues, alterations in how a person thinks and feels, and an increase in the fight-or-flight response.[1] These symptoms last for more than a month after the event.[1] Young children are less likely to show distress but instead may express their memories through play.[1] A person with PTSD is at a higher risk for suicide and intentional self-harm.[2]
Most people who have experienced a traumatic event will not develop PTSD.[2] People who experience interpersonal trauma (for example♥♥♥♥♥♥or child abuse) are more likely to develop PTSD, as compared to people who experience non-assault based trauma such as accidents and natural disasters.[5] About half of people develop PTSD following♥♥♥♥♥♥[2] Children are less likely than adults to develop PTSD after trauma, especially if they are under ten years of age.[6] Diagnosis is based on the presence of specific symptoms following a traumatic event.[2]
Prevention may be possible when therapy is targeted at those with early symptoms but is not effective when carried out among all people following trauma.[2] The main treatments for people with PTSD are counselling and medication.[3] A number of different types of therapy may be useful.[7] This may occur one-on-one or in a group.[3] Antidepressants of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor type are the first-line medications for PTSD and result in benefit in about half of people.[4] These benefits are less than those seen with therapy.[2] It is unclear if using medications and therapy together has greater benefit.[2][8] Other medications do not have enough evidence to support their use and in the case of benzodiazepines may worsen outcomes.[9][10]
In the United States about 3.5% of adults have PTSD in a given year, and 9% of people develop it at some point in their life.[1] In much of the rest of the world, rates during a given year are between 0.5% and 1%.[1] Higher rates may occur in regions of armed conflict.[2] It is more common in women than men.[3] Symptoms of trauma-related mental disorders have been documented since at least the time of the ancient Greeks.[11] During the World Wars study increased and it was known under various terms including "shell shock" and "combat neurosis".[12] The term "posttraumatic stress disorder" came into use in the 1970s in large part due to the diagnoses of U.S. military veterans of the Vietnam War.[13] It was officially recognized by the American Psychiatric Association in 1980 in the third edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-III).[14]

30 hours. All EXPERT events cleared.
When it showed "Congratulations! You are an all-star player" in the end, I remembered the days I was playing SSAR years ago. I was a high school student then, but not before I became a sophomore did I play SART. And I have been a Sonic fan for about ten years.
K let's get into the game. While SSAR is too simple as a racing game, SART is much better. More complicated and hardcore controlling is needed if you want to play SART. Transforming into three different types and different tracks in different laps are also very enjoyable. Unlike SSAR, different characters and different mods are a lot more different in performance. I have to admit that I didn't believe it until at a boost challenge I had failed for hours with Shadow but cleared it only one time with Tails.
NPCs in HARD mode and EXPERT mode are cheating. They are usually quicker than us and can accurately hit back, which is very annoying. And other challenges like boost challenge give us very little time. In this game, not every character can finish every challenge. If you get stuck at one event, try changing for another character. I recommend Sonic(Genesis Mod) and Tails(Standard or Handle). The former is heavenly fast while boosting, and the latter is surprisingly flexible. Beginners may have a hard time going through the events, but when they practice for some time, they are sure to complete the EXPERTs. In a word, the challenges in SART are a bit easier than those in SSAR. I can still remember the time I struggling in a star-ring-collecting rank S challenge in SSAR - that was HELL.
Like SSAR, SART also has a strange sense of gravity. For example, if you are hit when running upside down, you will not fall off the road. However, it feels good to some extent, for example I enjoy the map Casino Park. Similar to SSAR, maps in SART are all originated from other SEGA games expect one map. But some maps in SART directly come from SSAR, only with a few fixes. Anyway, repetition is better than none.
There are few bugs in SART, although mysterious trick fails and turn-arounds happen sometimes.
Cars in SART, in my opinion, might be lack of characteristics. SSAR is good, where Tails's car is a plane like the Tornado and Shadow's is a motorcycle from GUN. However in SSAR, Tails's car is just a yellow racing car, and instead of the motorcycle, GUN gave Shadow... a dodgem? lol
In conclusion SART is a good game worth to play. But if you ask me to recommend a Sonic racing game, I would recommend Sonic Riders series. Why don't SEGA bring Sonic Riders on Steam? Never know.
P.S. I am not a native English speaker. Sorry for some errors in language.

Sega, a company who live mostly in our memories. When it comes to talking about our favorite Sega games, you'd be hard pressed to name one game that was released in the past decade.
As a test, i asked a few of my friends on Steam what their favorite Sega game of all time is.
My best friend said "Sonic 3", Streets Of Rage 2 was another game mentioned by a few of my Steam acquaintance as well as Shenmue, but nothing from the past 10 years.
Just to give some insight into my history as a gamer, i grew up as a Nintendo gamer. My first console was an NES which i got for Christmas 1991, so it's fair to say, i was a Mario fan from day one.
The playground debate over who is better out of Mario and Sonic was always a no brainer to me, because as much as i loved Sonic The Hedgehog (and i did), Super Mario 3 was the game that blew everything else away and completely obliterated the competition.
Yes...you couldn't go far wrong with Mario. From 8 bit to 16 bit, from 16 bit to 64 bit, from 64 bit to 128 bit, Nintnedo always seemed to know what direction push Mario in, but with the success of 3D Mario games came similar attempts at 3D adventure games from other companies trying to achieve the same levels of success.
Introducing Sonic Adventure, The Dreamcasts answer to Mario 64. The first thing i ever saw of Sonic Adventure was a screen shot in a games magazine, and it blew me away. The graphics looked phenominal and i remember thinking if Sega manages to transfer the same gameplay from 2D Sonic games into 3D, this might be a Mario 64 killer....but little did i know, it would be the start of Segas downfall.
In present day 2016, attempts at recreating the Sonic franchise have been many. 3 Sonic Adventure games, Shadow The Hedgehog, Sonic Riders, Sonic And The Secret Rings, Sonic Rivals, Sonic And The Black Knight, Sonic Colours, Sonic Generations......the list goes on, and only sequels to the megadrive series of Sonic games captured a majority of peoples imaginations.
With this in mind, I approach every Sonic game with an equal amount of skepticism and trepidation, but when i noticed Sonic & All Stars Racing Transformed in a Steam sale, my curiosity got the better of me...and i'm pleased to say, i'm glad it did.
You may be wondering "why begin a review of a Sonic game with a whole spiel about Nintnedo", and this is why.
Sonic & All Stars Racing Transformed is a Mario Kart killer!. Yes, despite the fact Mario Kart games are rated higher and have a wider fan base, i can't help but feel Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed fell victim to the sour taste left in peoples mouths whenever the name "Sonic" is mentioned.
According to my Steam account, i have put 22 hours into Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed. In which time i have 100 percented it, something i never feel an incentive to do when playing a racing game, however, this game is so fun, i didnt want to leave any of it unexplored.
Just to state a few reasons why i believe this game is a Mario Kart killer, firstly the track design. Where Mario Kart suffers from repetetive courses that stay the same, courses in Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed changed depending what lap you're on. The first lap might be land based on four wheels, 2nd lap on water and 3rd in the air. Your vehicle transforms to accomodate changes in terrain and is done automatically and with such fluidity that it dosnt distract from what is a consistently smooth exoerience throughout.
The power ups are far more balanced and you don't often find yourself dropping from 1st place position to 8th in the blink of an eye just because someone decided to pull a blue shell from their back side.
Those are just 2 points which i believe to be factually better than what Mario Kart offers. There are many more aspects of Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed which i prefer to Mario Kart, but these are all matters of preference that i don't feel the need to mention, mostly aesthetics and other opinion based aspects.
To end this review, i'd just like to say i have over 150 games in my Steam library ranging from RTS to RPGs, from First Person Shooters to Point and Clicks, from Racing games to beat em ups, and Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is the most fun iv'e had thus far.

You know... I always loved time travelling since I've played the Zero Escape series. It is the perfect mix out of emotionality and science. And Steins;Gate just captured every moment of it in a manner, where you would think that time just has been a concept which can be skipped by humanity. It feels like you are in it, you can change the world at your own will...
Still, there always has been the difference... the decisions, whether you want to save one person or destroy his/her life... I just couldn't get it over heart to destroy these people's lives just to save one person... Every time when I saw an ending, I was crying or nearly in front of it... The whole game just left me devastated, but on an amazing way...
And it goes on to so many ways: The whole time-travel paradigm is in itself just a gigantic way to go through the psychological horrors of life: Seeing death, losing someone you love, asking your own identity and choosing between two of the worst things which could happen in life... And in the end you have to give up everything just to see the ones happy you love the most...
It is heartbreaking to see these people in suffering, having so many memories of them, as they were happy, sad and peaceful...

Dragon Ball Xenoverse give us fans a fresh new take on the dragon ball universe, with a fun and intresting campaign, as well as fun missions to play with friends. Along with a great stroy mode their are missinos called parallel quests that have a range of difficulties and the can be chalanged alone or with up to two freinds. Completeing these quests can give you items, exp, and new special moves. Another awesome feature is the create a character option. You get to create a character to play the main role in the story mode, you can also use this character to do quests and battle people online. When creating your character you are given a choice between a few differnt races, such as Sayin, Human, Namikian, Majian, and Friesa Clan. You level up by doing story missions and parallel quests, while earining many new moves and you are able to customise your characters stats. The combat system is fantastic, it might take a bit of getting used to, but when you do is is outstanding. Combos feel great and can be shained in epic ways, and there are no longer cutscenes for each special move. Wehn your character fires a Kamehameha it will zoom in on your charcter and show him/her doing the blast, but the other player can move freely to dadge or atempt to counter. This adds a whole new level to playing. Sadly the game is not without its flaws, the online servers a a bit buggy and can't handle the amount of people online, so they crash a lot. Character customisation, while really cool, is lacking and could use more hair and body types, also ther is a lack of characters that sghould be in the game, for example all the forms of Friesa and Cell. There is so mush i couldn't cover, but here are the basics:
Pros:
-Story Mode
-Combat
-Create a Character
-Questing
-Online Battles/Quests
Cons:
-Bad Servers (For Now)
-Lack of Character Creatin Options
-Lack of Characters
In conclusion its a great game with a few flaws, that mostly could be fixed with a few patches and some DLC, and if your a Draggon Ball fan you have no excuse for not buying this already.

This is an excellent FPS with a great deal of promise--I just upgraded to the Spearhead edition to support their work.
The environments look good and are varied (from a paint-ball like warehouse/base with different levels, varied lighting conditions, and changing cover to a snow-covered base that reminds me of BF 2142.  The heads-up display is useful, showing live teammates and just-killed enemy/teammates, which allows you to keep track of where contact is taking place.   Floating team identifiers are usually clear enough to prevent killing teammates.  The closed environments help teammates cooperate if they want to in the sense that you can provide cover for others and vice versa if so moved because you are often moving around in the same environment.
Reloading your weapon is quick, and ammo seems unlimited (unrealistic, but one less thing to worry about--"power-ups" aren't any more realistic..).  The  aiming is not unrealistically rock-steady, but not not too jumpy to frustrate (me, anyway).  The contained evnvironment allows enough room to creep around, but not so much you have trouble finding where contact is happening.  Even in nighttime environments the lighting is adequate to spot enemies if you're careful.  Firepower with the single weapon you have (auto rifle, basically), doesn't seem under or over-powered to me--seems to take two carefully placed short bursts to kill someone from 20-30 feet away.  You can crouch but not go prone.  You can run and jump.  Accessories are limited: laser sights (I don't see the advantage, and it reveals your location) and a flashlight.
It lacks:
- Single player.  Fortunately, I haven't had any problems finding and playing online games to play.  The player numbers seem about right.
- Coherent backstory.  Identifying them as "intersteller" marines seems unnecessary, since they are  fighting on earth against seeming other marines, and their craft which show up as props (which cannot be entered and are non-operable) look suitable for space shuttle use, but not interplanetary travel, and as for "intersteller," that's kind of silly.  Also, why have interplanetary marines with no identified threats?  However, I'm happy if they concentrate on combat gameplay and features and add backstory later.
- Different weapons and weapon capabilities are missing.  No single-burst-full auto choice, although you can control your fire rate to mimic them.  Quick on-off flashlight on the weapon would be a good addition.  No heavy weapons (maybe this is better in the enclosed environments).
- No permanent wounding and no healing--not sure but it appears that you recover health if you get out of wounding fire for a brief while.  Good for quick gameplay, tho.  Also means no healing needed--some like a first aid feature and some don't.
- Nothing I could notice as a reason to try to advance in rank.  No upgrades of anything, no badges, etc.
- No team system yet, unless I'm missing something.
The "vision" goals sound good.  I wish them luck in this.

Borderlands titles are a bit one-sided when it comes their content and could easily be described by several people as "boring" or "grindy". But what TellTale did with the series, is rather great in my opinion and to add to that, actually fun.
Tales from the Borderlands is an episodic point-n-click adventure game...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
Aaaaaaand that's pretty much it on the mechanical side, it's the same thing that TellTale has done for years. I'm struggling to find points to talk about, there is reasonably only one talking point. That being the story and it's writing, which I'm happy to say is f*cking fantastic in this game.
Without making many spoilers, the story follows two unlikely allies and their friends. On their varied and humorous misadventures on the craziest planet ever, Pandora.
And there's your story abreviation. The story has some spots where the dialogue seemed to be missing some minor pieces, as it was expecting me to ask one question over the other during dialogue. Other than minor hiccups dialogue side and the still used archaic TellTale Engine, I'm pressed to find flaws with it. I'm not counting in the minor clipping issues with the craphics and the sometimes extremely stiff animations, because those have been in almost every TellTale game ever published.
But to hammer home the most important and the best part of the game, the writing is awesome. It is exactly how you'd think an adventure on the crazy wastes os Pandora would go, you meet friends, enemies, raiders and psychos and have great deal of fun interacting with them. Especially with one, you know who I'm talking about. ;D
Unfortunately I really cannot talk about anything more, this is the problem with story driven titles. I really cannot say anything without spoilers, however I will say only this..

Ahhh, TrackMania United, the perfect arcade-based racing game.
I really don't know where to start this. Off the bat, TM: United is an arcade racing game, where you build tracks, perform loop-de-loops, crazy stunts, jumps, and tricks. This game houses several environments to race in (with Stadium being the most popular), and different cars for each environment (some cars may have better handling than overs, however most often the cars are tuned to the environment's racing style). The game's racing action is fairly solid, so handling and steering shouldn't be an issue (except on Coast, if you aren't familiar with rally racing).
The track editor is also very intensive and detailed (if you click the Advanced editor anyway). The track pieces pretty much go together like lego bricks, so the only way you can mess up a track is if you happen to forget a track piece to add in, or perhaps overshoot/undershoot your car's speed for jumps or sideways tracks. Believe me though, if you spend enough time in that editor, you can pretty well make some very challenging maps.
In addition to making your own maps, you can even set times on them. You can race your own creations, and try to set the best time, so other people can try to beat your time on your track. You can also choose to share your maps either via TMX (a website that specializes in maps for all the TrackMania titles), or via a Manialink (an in-game, hub store where users can upload their creations and buy them with in-game currency called credits (you cannot buy credits by the way, you earn them through logging in daily or by winning bets on the servers).
The other thing about TrackMania is that there is a paint option, so you can pain your cars very extravagantly and make them unique. Optionally, there's also user-made skins on TrackMania Carpark and on several Manialinks you can download. So if you feel like that old Stadium car is looking boring, you can download a BMW Z4 or a Mario Kart, or even one of the vehicles from F-Zero and race that instead.
Finally, the community of the game. I will admit off hand, I have logged a good lot of time into this game (was even playing its freeware version TrackMania Nations before I bought United), and in that time, it's tough to find good people there. To sum it up, you might not be that happy if you are a North American player, since the North American community (which is VERY small), tends to rank up on the global leaderboards in the top 10,000-100,000 range. While this may seem intimidating, there's also the EU community (which is VERY large), which can be ranked anywhere from the top 100,000-12 million range. Due to the wider range in the EU community, you might have better odds at placing in events on the EU servers over the North American ones (since the NA servers are few and far inbetween). On the upside though, your car doesn't crash into other players, so the only way you'll end up crashing is by human error.
However, if you don't quite want to roll with the multiplayer crowd, there is still the singleplayer, time trial maps you can play to earn medals (which do boost your ranking to some degree). Some of them can get very hard to beat, but it's still a good challenge if you feel like doing those sorts of games.
All in all, the game can be praised for it's creative prowess in regards to track building and racing, as well as the graphics too (which are still incredibly good despite the game's age). The multiplayer community might leave you wanting to have competition that isn't so incredibly skilled so you can have a chance to place, but the content that the community still pushes out is still impressive nonetheless, and still keeps me coming back for more.
To summarize, I recommend this game if you are the type that likes a good arcade racer with solid controls, and the ability to create maps.

One of the games that I'll start up and often times just leave running to see what ends up happening.
This game is great - a well done god sim with so many quirks and world effects that can often be your boon or demise.
Lots of different ways to tailor your start leading to many different interactions with new settlers and nearby tribes or raiders.
Depending on how you start you end up on world with ranges of climate types and biomes with a wide range of animals that can be tamed, or harvested; along with crops to feed and provide for your colony.
This is all supported by skill setup that useability will vary from colonist to colonist providing many hours of replayability.
An additional benefit that I'm glad to see is an active modding community providing tons of extra content that can completely change the way you play and the difficulty you experience - definitely recommend checking them out after a few hours of play.
I've had multiple base colonies with massive sprawling mountain bases packed with power armored badasses waiting for the right time to begin their world conquest and destroying the raiders around them.
I've also had a Hannibal Lecter-like colony of canibals feasting on unsuspecting traders and luring the unsuspecting to their dooms.
Sometimes while letting the game run colonies will die off and new inhabitants will inherit the fly equipment left behind the from the last strugglers. The game's your enchilada.
TLDR: For an early access, my experience has been well worth the price and I'm looking forward to more from the developers.

Trackmania United is definitely one of the best arcade racing games that is on offer on Steam! It's literally the Counter-Strike of racing games - highly competitive, yet welcoming to casual players. In order to be good, you need to be very skilfull as the game basically revolves around time trials and replaying levels over and over in order to get the best time. But if the competitive side is not for you, don't worry, because you can still play this game at a casual level and have a blast!
The visuals hold up really well considering the game's age. It is partly a compilation of the original Trackmania, Trackmania Sunrise, and Nations Forever (which is free and brings Stadium into the mix). I would recommend playing with a controller as the controls can be a bit twitchy for some car types - of which there are seven: Rally, Snow, Desert, Bay, Coast, Island, and Stadium. The sounds are decent, and the music isn't terrible, but I personally prefer playing with the music off and my own music playing instead.
In terms of what there is to offer, you can go straight into the multiplayer or you can start out on the Singleplayer levels. These come in a variety of forms, such as races on any of the environments or stunt, platforming, and puzzle events in the Stadium (you can also race in Stadium). As I said, these are based around getting the best time possible, so there is a lot of replayability in these levels! Apart from that you have a bunch more Stadium tracks and also some "Star Edition" tracks to add to the already-considerably-large amount of tracks in the game. And if that doesn't top it off, there is an in-game track editor that allows for you to create your own tracks or even play other people's!! (You can also download custom skins for your cars off the web if you're interested...)
The multiplayer is great fun too as it can be very competitive or really entertaining to spectate others playing the game. Overall it's a fantastic game and one of the best racers on PC, so if that's what you're into then this is a must-buy for you!
Enjoy! :D
