Theres a difference between being "hard" and just being badly designed - this is the latter.
For example, the age-old Super Mario Bros. force scroll levels - in SMB, they pause for a moment when you spawn and when you reach the edge of the screen, they push you along. In Electronic Super Joy, they kill you instantly, which is somwhat annoying when even the first few levels requires significant backtracking with little leeway for error, meaning I found myself dying needlessly, as my character touched the edge of the screen before he (would have) touched the teleporter.
Add to that the lack of acceleration on the main character, levels which are monochrome and hide the platforms from you frequently, a inconsistent frame rate (I strongly suggest you go into the options and turn frame locking on) and no leeway when it comes to pixel-perfect jumps, it seems to be making a point of being difficult, when it could be a significantly more enjoyable platformer, in the vein of the Trials series.

After 30 hours, I can conclude that Dragon Ball Xenoverse is not an AWFUL game.
However, its fantastically solid core gameplay and character customization are steeped in such awful game design reminiscent of MMORPGs a decade ago. If grinding levels, key items hidden behind double RNG, and repetition are for you, then I can safely recommend the title.
Otherwise, Xenoverse is only for the most hardcore Dragon Ball Z fans blinded by sheer nostalgia. There's just too much BS you have to sift through to find the gold. If you are just a casual fan, either wait for a STEEP sale ($20 or less) or the inevitable Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, which ideally will correct and streamline many of this game's wrongs.
I'm not really sure why the game is getting such widespread positive reviews... it's NOT a good game.  Maybe people are really excited to make their "Original Character Do Not Steal" DBZ fan creations, so excited in fact that they overlook all the game design travesties committed in Xenoverse.
Go in knowing what kind of game this is.  This isn't as straight forward as the Budokai or Budokai Tenkaichi series, and there are frustrating game design elements at EVERY turn.
Ultimately it feels wrong to tell someone not to play this game.  My recommendation is less of a recommendation and more of a friendly warning towards Dragon Ball Xenoverse.
Buy it only if you know what you're getting yourself into.

Getting this out of the way: I don't like Mario Kart.
However, I "do" like Crash Team Racing. While the MK franchise seemed to be all about item usage, CTR was about control. You went pretty fast, and you had to really learn how to control yourself around the turns. Items still played a bit part of it, but properly getting hang-time turbos and the like took some getting used to.
SART is like CTR, but with weaker items. Sure, they will hurt, but there's usually a way to dodge them with a well-timed turbo. SART isn't F-Zero GX levels of fast, but it's still pretty blistering when you're chaining turbos. And the best part? It's FUN. Really, really fun. Track designs are varied, graphics are colorful, music is traditional SEGA quality; overall, it's just a blast to play. If you want to race, get this. It even has local split-screen! Now how many PC racing games can you say do that?

Warning , this is a visual novel , meaning that the gameplay consists of mostly reading and indulging in the story , if you don't like the sound of this , you have been warned.
I liked this game so much that I completed all achievments and endings , aswell as buying the LEVEL 5 badge.
This must be the choice of Steins Gate...
This game is great , if you have any interest in it at all then buy it.
I thoroughly enjoyed it even after watching the anime fully.
The Story is great , it follows 18-year old Okabe Rintarou as he delves into the secrets of time travel and the mysterious organization SERN , all by modifying a microwave and a phone. The story really starts to ramp up around chapter 4/5 , so it may seem dull at first. Don't let that put you off , if you stop playing you will miss out on so much.
The Art style is really neat. It looks like what you would expect a sci-fi visual novel to look like. Detailed. Kind of strange. Atmospheric. It's not unpleasant to look at. Pretty good.
The background music is very atmospheric and really contributed to the whole feel of the game. The voice acting was on point and really immersed you , no complaints there. For every line of dialogue there is a voice that acts it out. Nice.
The characters are nice , there's Okabe (a.k.a Hououin Kyouma the chuunibyou mad scientist who can leap through time)
Mayuuri (The nice person who is oblivious to most things in the game) , Daru (The hardcore otaku who is the only one doing any work most of the time) and Kurisu ( a.k.a Christina , a.k.a Assistant , a bashful tsundere which helps Okabe).
There are some others but i'll leave it to that as I might spoil it if I describe further.
All in all , if you have any interest in this game you should buy it. There are 6 endings you can reach aswell as a unique cell-phone system where you choose your choices by answering calls or leaving them and replying in different ways to texts you get.
I strongly reccomend this , and I think that you will also want to reccomend this after playing this all the way through. The first ending occurs around 15-16 hours into the game , which is quite early into the game , so I advise you try doing some more endings if you don't feel satisfied.
That's all from me. I hope you enjoy!

- Description: "Hack 'n' Slash game with roguelike- & RPG elements."

These problems are solvable, so if the game is updated, I would be happy to give it a really high rating because it has potential.

Early Access as hell, but what's here is enjoyable and has a lot of promise. Unlike some other Early Access games, Interstellar Marines has also been building on that promise, rather than tripping over itself constantly. It's got the best HUD in ages (A visor that actually reacts to the game world, with rain drops dripping down it, and damage eventually causing it to malfunction and no longer display friend or foe indicators. Hell, you can even open and close the visor if you want.), intense gunplay that Rainbow Six fans will instantly love, and, well, that's kind of it for now.
As much fun as being paranoid, scanning around dark rooms, flipping your flashlight on for a second before turning it off again so you don't give yourself away can be, it's not going to keep you coming back for more time and time again when all that is here is a few maps, a few modes, and two guns. A complete lack of the main focus, co-op play, is also rather jarring.
Still, if you need a Rainbow Six fix, this is already one of the best choices you can make. And while the updates aren't frequent, they've been consistently high quality. IM is a game to keep an eye on, if nothing else.

360 gamepad controls are jerky and over-sensitive. Even if you turn the deadzone up and sensitivity all the way down, it's still way too touchy. There's also no way to map the triggers to accel and brake, so there's no analogue speed control. There are no setup options, no manual shifting, it's just stop or go.
Most tracks are start here, finish there (A to B) rather than having laps like a normal racing game. The stunts are cool, but most races are over in less than 2 minutes so you don't really get to enjoy the driving that much, unless you're trying to get a gold medal, then you're just going to be repeating the same short run over and over. All opponents (AI or players) are ghost cars. To unlock the higher tier tracks require you to get at least Gold on the previous, but because the controls are so touchy and jerky, it can be a pretty tall order.
I don't get why this game is so popular. It's expensive for being so old and simplistic. It would be nice to have a good stunt car game on Steam. There really hasn't been one since Stunts or Stunt Driver, so I guess this (or the sequels) would be it. You can make your own tracks and paint your cars, so that's a plus.
It's a good game if you're looking for something simple and over the top. It's just racing - no cops, no boosts, no setups or car tuning, no cockpit view (just two chase and one bumper cam). Not all tracks have jumps and loops, but most do. It's a good game, but I can't recommend it at the current price point.

Okay, this game is a seriously mixed bag, and I suppose the only thing that'll help one to decide to buy it is being a non-purist Dragon Ball (Z) fan. If you're not a fan or you get easily annoyed by certain races suddenly being allies or the Saiyans suddenly not being such a extinct race... OR if you're anti-GT, steer clear of this game. Oh yeah, the servers are having lots of issues right now as I write this, connecting is also a hit and miss.
The game is one of the few Dragon Ball games to come out on PC, only consoles have been enjoying Dragon Ball titles for now, but now there is a release for PC, finally. The game still bleeds console port everywhere and is best played using a joypad. The fights themselves can be highly addicting, trying to find new powers through quests, progressing through the story, etc. Being able to create your own character, with choices in race, gender, hairstyles, customizable faces and character size is also a really nice addition.
It's not a good idea to play this when you are prone to anger issues and controller tossing. Expect to curse at connection failed messages, COM controlled characters ganging up on yours and you not being able to do anything as you see your character being tossed around the level and that one online quest where you were doing so well suddenly being disconnected. (The server issues may be fixed, but if the host quits, the quest seizes.)
Now, you're able to create a unique character, depending on the race, in my case a Saiyan because I can't help myself, you can change their race, gender, size, face, hair, hair and clothes colour.
Best solution if this bothers you is to pick hair that looks alright when in Super Saiyan state. The devs however may have been able to solve this by letting Saiyans pick a second hair model or to have each model have a stand-up version, but alas. I see a lot of people also just pick up standing-up hair and colour it yellow, yet their eyebrows remain black and their pupils aren't green... Don't be that guy, please? Oh, and expect to get your♥♥♥♥♥♥kicked by a Human not matter what level Saiyan you are.
You are summoned through Shenron by Trunks and his Time Agent organisation as some evil is messing around with time for reasons I'm not going to spoil. Putting you in the typical 'Hey, you are unique and The One even though bloody everyone is The One' kind of situation. So much for feeling special. You travel through time to correct changes in time in many places. You will relive events from the TV series with fair resemblance. (Even Hercule/Mr. Satan gets kicked out of the ring by Perfect Cell.) You'll fight in areas like the Lookout Point, Mountains, Wastelands, Namek, Earth's Cities and many more.
Again a mixed bag here, the character's expressions are nicely done, the eyes are not switching Textures like in Battle of Z. The Textures itself however show some less likable details like low resolution lines that cut off abrubtly. Also details like realistic water and other shaders can look unbalanced against the less realistic looking characters and world. Plus side is that this game will run smooth on a lot of systems.
I play the game with English language, but it seems the lip-syncing was done for the Japanese dub, as the lip movement don't match most of the time and in some scenes they don't move at all. Some voices are not the original voices from the TV series, the music however is pretty good although some classic songs from the TV series aren't used and replaced by normal songs sung by some random Japanese bloke.
I only played using a XBox controller, and it does help making sense of all the buttons, the targetting system makes short work of any possible camera aiming issues you might have during a fight so you will be kicking butt and not spend time being disorientated. Button placement is pretty well done and you can assign special moves and items to various buttons. Nothing wrong here.
Now this one was a thorn in my side, the game offers voice chat, though I switched that off for obvious reasons. The chat however is limited 39 pre-programmed lines you can say. ("Hello!", "I'm sleepy.", "Awesome!", etc.) I guess this might be either because, well, this is clearly a quick console port. Or because the devs feared people would just keep cursing at each other. The option to type however with perhaps a colourful language filter in the hub would've been nice, I myself, even though the Internet is full of people less skilled in the arts of proper language, am not a fan of this hand-holding chat system.
So, the game is fun, if it let's you have that fun. We can only hope the server issues will be fixed, though I can imagine many people will be like: "To Hell with this." If they read the server improvement announcement was done and things were worse afterwards than before it took place... You will not find things like a polished looking game, you will get good controls though. However, weighing the troubles versus the joy I'd say I do not recommend this game unless you have nothing to do and/or are dying to fight some super powered battles and have a metric ton of patience. Don't get me wrong, there is still reason enough to get it, but you're going to have to be tolarable about a few things, there's just only a Yes and No button for if one should buy this game, but no Maybe. So, most cases I wouldn't recommend it, otherwise I would. At least best to wait for any sales.

Positive:

This game is build on a somewhat MMORPG feeling with the whole quest, duel and arena system.
You are not playing one of the main serie character, but rather your very own custom character (either human, sayien, namek, boo or freeza race). Lot's of customization is possible.

- As an inveterate fan of Dragon ball, I can't help but to like this new way of presenting the story of this classic Shonen.
Yet, the game in itself is now half as story immesing as Naruto shippuden : ultimate ninga storm 3 is...
Negative :
- The soundtrack is sincerly annoying and I'm not even talking about the poor english dubbling.
OK, purists will tell me to play in the original version with subtitle, but hey! There are some people too lazy to read when they are playing...
In any cases, the soundtrack annoy me so bad that I'm turning the sound off when not playing the main campain.
- The cell shading is not bad, yet it is not extra-ordinary at all. The colors and the lights are rendered somehow a little bit weird...
Globally, the graphics is far below games like Naruto shippuden : ultimate ninga storm 3 for cell shading or final fantasy 13 for regular japanese graphics.
It's a shame when a brand new game can't compete with way older games...
- No matter at which time I play, it is always a challenge to connect to the server. If I ever manage to log in, I can't even play more than a single quest without being disconnected...
Why the h*** can't we play offline?
Conclusion :
This game what most definitly build on good intention. Yet, no matter how good or bad a game is, it cannot be anything but a bad game if you can't manage to play it.
I mean, with the season pass DLC, this game cost something like 83 canadian dollars. That's quite a lot of money!
I hate those new generation game that you absolutly new to connect on game server to play. That mean that you can't play them when there are under server maintenance, when your internet is down or, like in this case, the server is most  obviously not designed to support so much players.
Anyone would agree that never being able to play a game you paid good money for is unnacceptable. This is not a 5 dollars indy game, this is supposed to be a AAA game...
I would recommend to wait for them to fix all the server bug before ever considering buying this game.
In the meaning time, you should consider, if you don't already own it, Naruto shippuden : ultimate ninga storm 3 for a way better fighting shonen based game.

Pros
The game is remarkbly story rich. The main story is a long and complex one and there are several branches.
The music is good, perfectly fitting to the story.
The theory of worldlines and timetravel in the game is not absolute nonsense as I expected in this kind of games(or animes). This game has exceedingly satisfied my expectation in its scientific core.
The story plots are extremly emotional. Seeing characters struggling in the face of a merciless fate, only trying to save each other, seeing them surrendering to the dark part of their nature are more than heartbreaking.
Cons
Compared with the anime, the game has more galgame elements. Sometimes I feel female characters' behavior is quite strange...Maybe it's just me. And it has nothing to do with the main game line.
I sometimes feel that the charaters are all too perfect in morality to be real human beings. It seems impossible to make a decision when faced with those dilemmas if you want everyone happy, which yields far more tear-shedding but less true sadness if you know what I mean. Go buy this any time because it is definitely worth its price.

Where do I even begin with this game?
Well my introduction to the Steins;Gate universe started with the first couple of episodes of the anime. However as I discovered that a visual novel release would come to Steam shortly I decided to postpone it. A decision that I am really greatfull to myself for choosing. This story is amazing! It has some really interesting characters to follow and you can really feel the development throughout the story.
My biggest praise however has to go to "hououin kyouma"/Rintaro Okabe for being such an odd person that you somehow still can relate to. I was actually surprised by how his internal dialouge changes as things turn more sour.
Though everything can't be a praise of this game as I would seriously argue that the PC port is somewhat pourly made especially in the controls department. I would have really appreciated if they had taken the time to make a proper use for the keyboard and not keep the same weird controller system. Also the different manues feel rather sloppy in design and the fact that you can only have 60 saves is an odd thing for a PC game??
But back to the praise, music is another high as they seem to have picked the quality over quantity with only a few songs reused throughout the story. I believe there is about 6 songs total however the mesmerizing sound that is pulled by especially "Believe me" is what really takes it home.
Voiceacting is something that I am not entirely sure how to judge as I don't speak japanese which is the only option. But I will strech as far as to say that most sounds seem rather appropriate for the chracters they portray. Even though they really should fix the screaming for Daru as it sounds nothing like a scream. The english text is really well written however occasional spelling errors can be found.
But how could I forget about the endings!
This is the main reason I would argue that you should play this before watching the anime as it allows you to make your own decisions on the way. So when you at some point get to watch the anime you will be able to enjoy seing the differences in decisionmaking. Otherwise the different options allow for an even larger story based upon the chracters which simply works as a great excuse to spend more time with a universe like no other I have seen in anime.
To summarize:
Pros +
+Engaging story throughout which only turns better as you continue
+Realistic character portrayal
+Mesmerizing music
Cons -
-poorly formatted for PC
-some use of japanse puns combined with english fall flat when you can only understand english

Unepic for me is considered one of the best games I've ever played. While I play this game and I am writing notes in my book, I can describe that I feel a lot of fluency because I travel at least 20 years ago, where at 10 years I tried to unravel certain platform games like pc snes or megadrive. This for me is considered a good snes game but with a modern twist.
This is a game that is a little difficult to play, because it requires a lot of effort and sacrifice spirit to be able to enjoy this beautiful game. This game has some similarities to the Castelvania, a game created in 1987 for snes and that had a great success until 2010. To walk in a giant castle, from room to room with the lights out, without knowing the danger that awaits to us, does not seem to be An easy task, but when we light up all the torches and we come across a room filled with enemy goblins, orcs, skeletons, and other villains thirsting for revenge, then yes we have all the items to be a good game. This game is full of quests and side_quests where we can win several items that can be extremely valuable in another part of the game.
Eventually opening up the entire castle is a fun process, but combat with the respawning hordes of monsters exposes Unepic’s major fallacy: its freedom of character creation. A hulking warrior in full plate mail proficient in axes; a mage wielding powerful ice and fire spells; a spry thief equipped with a twisted dagger and powerful sleep magic; the character you become is entirely up to your distribution of skill points.
That sounds great in theory, but Unepic’s enemies are incredibly unbalanced, and it’s much easier to survive as a magic user than as a warrior. I played through most of it specializing in melee weapons and found that, if a group of enemies spotted me, I was almost always surrounded and killed. To survive, I had to exploit the enemy AI; I would get a single enemy's attention, climb down a ladder, then attack it as it tried to climb down after me, which would freeze it in place on the ladder.
This looks great in theory, but Unepic's enemies are incredibly unbalanced, and it's much easier to survive as a magical user than as a warrior, for like magic we can make ranged attacks and we have one more chance to escape and heal . I played most of it specializing in hand-to-hand weapons and found that if a group of enemies saw me, they were almost always surrounded and killed. To survive, I had to explore enemy AI; I would catch the attention of a single enemy, climb a ladder, then attack as I tried to pull away, which would freeze him instead of the ladder. Another thing we should be careful of is with the thieves of the game, because if we leave an item on the floor for a while, an unknown being teleports and robs the item, and the problem is that it steals us keys that are important for us to open Certain doors of the castle. And those keys are acquired when we kill the giant bosses. If you have stolen the keys you have to drop a less valuable item at the bottom of some stairs and hide yourself upstairs, when the thief appears and he will drop an item, to get your key you will have to do the same process 17 to 20 times to recover the object.
This was one of the games where I saw great diversity of final bosses. Some find it easier than others because everything hides if you choose magic or strength to defeat your enemies. For me the most difficult boss was the boss of the library (Neuron), because as he was surrounded by books had to be the smartest, this could get me to drop all my items or when I was almost to defeat this teleport me to another site in the Castle. So we have to be smarter than him trying to figure out what his next step was and this was much more fun.
While the unbalance is frustrating, I found reprieve in Unepic’s surprisingly charming writing. The main character, Daniel, is the victim of a botched possession by a spirit named Zeral in the early moments, and the two banter with each other throughout the story as they share the same body. The writing is overflowing with nerd references, including nods to the X-Men, StarCraft, Metal Gear Solid, Spaceballs, Star Wars, Futurama, Dragon Warrior, the Matrix; two shopkeepers are even named after Linux versions.
This is a game that will let you grab the chair from start to finish. But I advise this game to dedicated people who like to complete the whole game, for a couple of players who do not have patience and just want to spend a game to pass what is a boring game and that is not fun :( The last note I want Leave and for me one of the most important is, that this game for me was a 10-10, but the version translated into Portuguese has hundreds of bugs and errors in the Portuguese language.What sometimes left me a little sad and confused. Please fixe this error of the translation so that the Portuguese can love this game as I loved.
Final grade 9-10

One of the most vivid memories I have playing this game came from probably one of the most intense situations i've ever encountered:
We were fighting on Kohat Toi as the americans, our squad was pinned down by Russian fighters and we were running low on ammunition. We had been holding this position for about 20 minutes - unable to penentrate their defenses. Our squad leader told us reinforcements and mortars would be coming in soon. We waited for about another ten minutes before another two squads came to our aid. By this point I was out of magazines in my marksmans rifle so I only had my pistol left.
We began to hear the mortars overhead - and we were hoping that finally we would break the stalemate. But all I remember is one of our squad members simply going:
Before we knew it, the mortars landed on our position - it turned out someone had messed up the range and now we were being shelled by our own team. Our squad leader screamed for us to get to cover, only to be killed by a direct hit - for over three minutes these mortars hit us, and all we could do was hide under the very little cover we had - in some cases people were just lying prone in the ground hoping they were not hit.
The russians, having seen the colossal screwup had started storming our position and we were left to retreat back, fighting with only pistols and grenades in an attempt to regroup and try again. Of about thirty people that had been fighting on that hill, only about four of us managed to escape.
This game has everything. Great controls, great community, great developers. What sets this game apart is the true feeling of adrenaline, running through trees with rounds cracking over your head, hearing an RPG hitting your AFV and your squad leader screaming for you to get out.
If you're someone who loves flashy graphics and over the top combat, this game isn't for you. If you love realism and team work, I cannot recommend this game enough. This game gives you so much content for how much it costs - and the only DLC you need to buy is bumper packs of underwear.

TL;DR: The 2.0 update brought the game down to 1/3 speed due to lag in multiplayer, low-level enemies can one-shot you, and often, you won't have enough
mana to be able to use your abilities. I doubt they'll fix any of this, and I really can't recommend buying this game until they do.
It completely ruins the experience.
Detailed version:
A bunch of updates ago, I would have recommended it reluctantly. Now I can safely say that the game has gone to sheit. Here's why:
In this game you have a skill tree in which you can upgrade passive and active abilities, just like so many other games. However, your items can also upgrade your abilities for you. The already high mana cost of your abilities increases with each level you put into it, and this is a horrible mechanic. Even if you spend every single attribute point on max mana, with some good gear, a simple ability can easily take 75% of your max mana. If you don't do this, you might not even have enough max mana to use the ability.
And even more importantly:
I love playing as a "Glass cannon", as some would call it. Fragile, but tons of damage. However, Hero Siege takes glass cannon to the level of absurdity where some non-boss enemies can one-shot you easily. (And even do it so fast that you don't really get to even see exactly what happened.) Even on a level 30 character, a boss from chapter 1 act 1 can one-shot you with some unlucky positioning from your side.
Also, here's another, even bigger problem:
The game runs
after the update that has made the map much bigger. (I haven't tested this in singleplayer, only in multiplayer, as that's all I really play in this game. I have however tested both the official servers and peer to peer.) My PC can run Dota 2 on the highest graphic  settings available, so this pixel game really shouldn't bring much trouble. However, the game runs so slowly that everything is just reduced to 1/3 speed. When you go into a dungeon, everything runs at normal speed, and the game feels genuinely good to play again, aside from the absolutely horrendous balancing. However, you will only be spending a very small amount of time in dungeons compared to normal levels, so this is quite irrelevant. The game was pretty fun in some previous updates, but after 2.0, I'm giving this a
thumbs down.

TL:DR The game is pay to win dispite what the devs may think. It's fun up to level 10, but after that the game is frustrating to play because you get stuck against people who paid for better gear. I do Not recommend this agme in it's current state.
The more I play this game the more apparent it is to me that this game is pay to win. I really like this game too which is the saddest part for me. Pre level 10 the game feels pretty balanced and fair, but past 10 you get matched with people who have vastly better gear than you. This is where the game turns into a steep uphill grind. You can get better gear by chance when you open crates your grind for, but said gear only lasts 2 hours which doesn't make them anywhere near worth using since it takes a week of grinding to get some of them. You can craft a lot of the better gear to keep perminantly, but it takes so flippin long and takes so many resources it's ridiculous. Most of the gear you can craft uses gear you had to previously grind for to get in order to craft the items. and some of the components used in the crafting are so hard to come by. For example: one component used in most crafting is copper, and a single part normally uses about 50 (which is the lowest crafting amount i can think of). You can get copper from doing raids which is good, but you only get about 1 copper per raid, so you basically have to do 50 raids in order to craft said part, and that's only one of the components you need! you usually also need scrap which you can't get in raids. another material is wire. now the only parts I've seen that need it call for 1000 of this wire. I currently have yet to come accross this resource.  How do the devs expect me to compete with someone who has these parts already if I can't get the materials to craft them. (their answer is pay real money) Honestly I'd rather just pay for the game once on steam instead of it being free so I wouldn't have to deal with this utter bullsh*t. It's really frustrating when you go into a game and your team can't even kill a single enemy before the enemy destroys all of you.
Devs if you're reading this either make the matchmaking more fair or remove the stupid pay to win features (make us pay for the paint, or make the crafting times longer to incentivise people to pay to complete them instead. Don't put me with people who can buy better guns and what not, that makes people angry because it makes the game not fun to play.)
Honestly the community is pretty nice, and I really like most of the other things about the game like the vehicle building, maps, and faction system etc. But I cannot recommend the game in it's current state. Thank the heavens the game is free, cause if I would've had to actually pay for what this game is now I'd be truely angry.

However... there are a ton of bugs and issues that kill the magic after a bit. The dedicated servers simply do not work for any of my friends and do not give an error message. You have to do the port forwarding direct games for now.

From items not working right to stuff being invisible to the 'remember username' box not actually saving the user name etc. Several friends died to fire towers or poison goo that is simply not visible. Sliding block puzzles are typically seen as lowlights in videogames, and they're very rarely used creatively or to good effect. As for the dislikes, it has an odd difficulty curve that spikes and dips frequently. Also, some more camera controls would be a great addition.
Despite all that, the game is highly recommended. It's fun, challenging, doesn't hold your hand, and looks fantastic.

First impression: cute casual puzzle game
This is a sliding puzzle: there's a single hole on the hexagonally tiled board, and you can move pieces into it to move the hole and eventually get Little Red Riding Hood to grandma's house. Bonus if you can do it within the alotted number of moves, but it's not necessary. This gets challenging when you learn that you also have to pick flowers (and a berry bush for bonus), there are immovable obstacles, there are bears (who can be moved) that the girl needs to stay away from, fire that the bears can't come close to, and more -- you get the idea.
The game is quite well designed, and that applies both to the artwork, the interface, the available settings, and even the tutorial. It is simply enjoyable to play. I have logged 1 hour playing the first 16 of 60 levels, and it's fun shoving the bears hither and yonder to get the red girl to where she needs to go and not waste moves. I expect it would take beginners longer, especially if they want to catch all the stars, but you don't have to: I expect this game is quite accessible to kids (who are more likely to play it on a tablet, though).

To be honest, I haven't played some of the Telltale games before, even if games like The Walking Dead were all over the news as masterpieces. I was playing another game that was not from Telltale but had similarities, Life is Strange, which I loved and I read reviews calling it "Telltale rippoff". So I was like, what the heck, if I loved this, I might like the Telltale games ever better.
So, I tried this one first because I was fun of the original Borderlands. And I can't say, they depict the Borderlands lore preety well and the dialogues and characters are some of the wittiest ever, I even expect to see some of these characters appearing in Borderlands 3 if it's ever out. In terms of story, characters, dialogues, Telltale does a marvelous job (and I expect this from their other games I have yet to play).
But here is the thing, I know this is like an adventure game or not (depending on who you ask). Maybe an interactive movie? And I don't mind that, maybe it's not my taste of games. But it gives me this awful feeling of what the game industry is going to. Making games even more easier, even more casual, in ways that are like insulting your intelligence. I get it, it's supposed to be more like a movie, there are dialogues which go too fast because you have to answer else it wouldn't have the flow of a movie. And skip that, when you finally are given control of your character after 10 minutes of forced dialogues, it's pointing you directly to the solution of the most trivial puzzles ever. They didn't even need to put it, it's more like a chore to click on what is in front of me. They have a very restricted camera, intentionally so that the objects of interest are always in front of you and you won't miss them, you grab an item and there is an imaginary inventory, but you just need to click on the next object and it shows you the icon with the object to use. It really shows the solution in your face, for example I had to lift some heavy objects, and my character couldn't, and at that point I wanted to start thinking whether I should use a lever or ask someone to help me, but even before that it shows small cinematic where my character is looking at the side of the robot, like it tells you "Hey, just ask the robot!". It tells you the solution in your own face and it wasn't even hard at all!!! I am not gonna talk about QTEs, which I absolutely loath.
I don't like the approach of Telltale games. I know it will be the same in the acclaimed masterpieces like The Walking Dead or others. It's like saying, OMG adventures are dead, the problem is that games stuck in puzzles and quit, what are we gonna do? Make them as easy than ever, people don't have to think, they should not stuck in a puzzle not even for a second. Omg, this ridiculously easy puzzle can still confuse players. Let's focus their camera directly to the solution.
It makes me feel this game has no soul, it's rather like watching your favorite Anime but with M$ Clippy popping out all the time to ask you about choices. But the control of your character is totally restricted so that it leads you to the solution. These restrictions take away the feeling of exploration and figuring out things for yourself. What they do would work like some Anime miniseries but not as an interactive experience.
I am not saying this is a "no-game" game. I used to love adventure games. I also like even "non-game" games like Dear Esther and Gone Home. For the single reason, they let you wonder around the environment 360 degrees, and there were a lot of things to discover, even if there was no actual gameplay. You felt you were exploring the world. Not being forced through Pablovian button mashing and destroying the sense of freedom.
Unless you like the Telltale games style of gameplay, I don't recommend this.

I've played a lot of DW-styled games. A lot. And I tend to spend more than a reasonable amount of time playing them. As far as things go, this game is not revolutionary for it's genre, however it's is fun in it's own right.
I'd like to preface the rest of this review by saying this is a tentative recommendation. The game definitely has it's fair share of flaws, but for what it does, it does it competently enough for the game to be enjoyable to the niche market the devs are aiming for.
Pros:
-The story is marginally better than Burst. The writing feels a fair bit less stilted and most characters have a few good moments. The different academies have a variance in the tone of the story, which helps the whole thing feel less repetitive.
-The gameplay is not cream of the crop, don't expect a Dynasty Warriors or Pirate Warriors level of polish here, but it is satisfying and enjoyable in it's own right. There are enough complexities that you won't get bored as some games.
-The soundtrack is actually an improvement - there are a number of memorable and catchy tracks that you'll probably want to go back and listen to them again.
-There is a good amount of content here. Even if you avoid replaying anything, and ignore the collectables and achievements you can rack up 25-30 hours of playtime broken up neatly between four academies.
-Lots of cute anime girls (Hikage is best girl).
Cons:
-The game seems to struggle with difficulty. The AI seems to switch on the fly from utterly mindbogglingly stupid to aggressive infinite combo beatdown. It's very jarring to see an AI than was giving you a hard time suddenly drop everything to taunt several times in a row. It's also entirely possible you'll do the DLC characters (Daidouji and Rin) side stories without realising how the final fights are one of the hardest in the game because they aren't really labelled as much more difficult (isn't this the point of having the difficulty meter?) than the main girls.
-They need to calm the hell down with the status effects. With how liberally they are applied, they seem to last too long. In particular the loss of control ones like freeze and paralysis aren't very fun to play against given you have no input for around 5 seconds at a time. These rarely result in you dying, but it doesn't feel very fun to be stuck doing nothing for an uncomfortable amount of time.
-The camera is just bad. There's no other way to say it. Half of the difficulty in this game is trying to get the camera to cooperate. With long range characters like Mirai who still need to use their lock on, the distance at which it breaks is just annoying. In addition, you'll often find yourself staring at a wall while your view of the characters on screen is completely blocked by it.
-All girls were not created equal and there are a few who just aren't very fun to play (Minori). This problem is further bogged down by the fact that when you first play a character, the vast majority simply do not have the tools unlocked to make them function as they should. This means that the first few levels are deeply painful until you start unlocking more moves.
-There's a decent amount of information that isn't made immediately obvious when you first play, but greatly impacts how you play a character. For example, Minori can throw stuff in her bucket. Over time and as you gain more hits, it changes color and grants you an attack power buff. The only place that you can learn about character specific quirks like this is the loading screens. However, if you're not a fast reader, it's very difficult to get all the information you need without having to look it up.
In summary, the game has it's fair share of flaws. But the pros are big enough that for people interested in this niche, they'll generally outweight the negatives. It's not as good as some of Koei's best, but it's not nearly as bad as some other games like Nep U.
If I wanted to play Shadow of the Colossus, I would. I would also have a much better time.

Tutorial to how to make RA3 - Uprising. Step 1: finish developing RA3, one of the most ambitious RTSes of 2008. Step 2: take all your assets, ideas that couldn't fit in the original game or haven't made the deadline and put them together. Step 3: craft a really lame and superficial campaign for each fraction as a wrap-around. Step 4: add Yuriko to the mix. Thus, Command & Conquer Red Alert 3 - Uprising has been born.
Uprising isn't a bad game. However, it wants to do so many thing at once that it can't achieve a single one of them (well, except one: Yuriko). All three factions got a new mini-campaign which takes place after the original game with the Allies winning the war over the Soviets and the Empire. None of the stories are overlapping this time like they were in the original game. There are 10 levels for the three factions combined and all of them are hard as hell. Even on medium difficulty you will be constantly attacked by the enemy on land, water and in the air. Sometimes the game gets so difficult that it will be annoyingly frustrating. Some levels may require over 1-2 hours to complete on medium and not because they are so long, but because you have to retry constantly.
The basic gameplay structure hasn't changed, but some new units were introduced on all 3 sides. Some of them are really unconventional and they can upset your good ol' strategies. The building system remained the same, but less than half of the stages start with base building. On most of them you start off with a smaller group and you have to complete some tasks before HQ can send you an MCV. These commando missions are fresh at first but they very quickly became annoying...for all the players crying out loud: just give us a base and let us build an army! We don't want to play commando with conscripts and attack dogs against tanks and robots! This and the annoying difficulty will make you believe that the creators used these cheap tricks to make the game last longer. Even though it will last longer, they will remain cheap tricks.
On the visual side the game looks great. Water movement is excellent, explosions are beautiful and devastating. You just can't get enough of a dozen Apocalypse Tank annihilating the enemy base. Splendid! Anyone who has seen a Red Alert game knows that its' cutscenes are performed by flesh and blood human actors and actresses. Also anyone can tell that these cutscenes are missing one thing only and that is good acting. The actors are still unconvincing and disbelieving, not that the words that were put into their mouths are any better. Sometimes you just wish the next cut-scene will be a lot shorter and without any speech at all. The debrief ladies look hot though and the short skirt of that Gemma Atkinson's won't disappoint you.
When you finish the campaigns you can try the most innovative and fun part of the game. Yuriko's mini-campaign. She is a psyche with mental powers capable of devastating armies. You have access to 4 powers at one time. After using a power you have to wait for the cooldown time. You can brainwash enemies to fight on your side, create black holes that suck everything inside or simply heal yourself with her powers. This game mode is really interesting, intriguing and its the greatest fun you can find in this game.
When you are done with the mini-campaigns you can play Skirmish, where nothing has changed from the original or play Challenge missions which are actually a lot like Skirmish maps only with cutscenes and a limited arsenal. When you beat a challenge new ones will appear and by beating them you can unlock new units to fight with. Before starting a map you can always select your fraction. It's nothing groundbreaking but thanks to the limited arsenal and gameplay tweaks this game mode can engage lots of players. And finally, there is the multiplayer...oh...wait...there aren't any MP or Co-op modes in this game! No MP in an RTS game. Well played EA, just well played!
Rating: 57/100; Replay Value: 3/5; To Beat: 10-12 hours; Played on: medium/easy.

Where do I even begin with this game?
Well my introduction to the Steins;Gate universe started with the first couple of episodes of the anime. However as I discovered that a visual novel release would come to Steam shortly I decided to postpone it. A decision that I am really greatfull to myself for choosing. This story is amazing! It has some really interesting characters to follow and you can really feel the development throughout the story.
My biggest praise however has to go to "hououin kyouma"/Rintaro Okabe for being such an odd person that you somehow still can relate to. I was actually surprised by how his internal dialouge changes as things turn more sour.
Though everything can't be a praise of this game as I would seriously argue that the PC port is somewhat pourly made especially in the controls department. I would have really appreciated if they had taken the time to make a proper use for the keyboard and not keep the same weird controller system. Also the different manues feel rather sloppy in design and the fact that you can only have 60 saves is an odd thing for a PC game??
But back to the praise, music is another high as they seem to have picked the quality over quantity with only a few songs reused throughout the story. I believe there is about 6 songs total however the mesmerizing sound that is pulled by especially "Believe me" is what really takes it home.
Voiceacting is something that I am not entirely sure how to judge as I don't speak japanese which is the only option. But I will strech as far as to say that most sounds seem rather appropriate for the chracters they portray. Even though they really should fix the screaming for Daru as it sounds nothing like a scream. The english text is really well written however occasional spelling errors can be found.
But how could I forget about the endings!
This is the main reason I would argue that you should play this before watching the anime as it allows you to make your own decisions on the way. So when you at some point get to watch the anime you will be able to enjoy seing the differences in decisionmaking. Otherwise the different options allow for an even larger story based upon the chracters which simply works as a great excuse to spend more time with a universe like no other I have seen in anime.
To summarize:
Pros +
+Engaging story throughout which only turns better as you continue
+Realistic character portrayal
+Mesmerizing music
Cons -
-poorly formatted for PC
-some use of japanse puns combined with english fall flat when you can only understand english

This is a fun game with many flaws. On one hand, it directly targets and massages the nostalgia glands of anyone who grew up watching this show. On the other hand, the AI is simplistic and the way the game chooses to ramp up the difficulty on you is absurd and encourages you to use tactics that are not at all effective against real, living people.
The game has been out for more than a week as of this review, and the servers are *still* unable to handle the volume of players that want to play. The game has semi-always online features, which can result in you being disconnected and losing progress, even if you only wanted to play offline, by yourself. There are workarounds, but both of them are tedious and should not be required to play in single player mode. Local play options are limited, and they force both players to awkwardly share a screen in a game where the desired viewpoint is directly behind the shoulders of your character.
Many aspects of this game could be overlooked and even a lot of fun if only you could reliably bring friends along for the ride, but thanks to technical issues that plague this game, (including bugs that go beyond the server issues) that in and of itself is quite difficult. I am actually mildly insulted that this game not only had pre-order bonus DLC, but launched with crappy, broken servers and day one DLC. I honestly cannot see myself recommending this game to anyone else in its current state.

Honestly it's disappointing that I can't recommend this, because I should be able to. This game does quite a few things right. The controls are pretty great and the player mechanics work wonderfully. There's a lot of interesting platformer-y elements that can come together to make interesting levels.
The problem lies in that the actual level designs... fall flat, far too often. See, this game has missiles. And the level designer liked these missiles a lot. To the point where they are spammed, far far too much. It feels like the design process went as such: "Hmm, this level's okay, but it's a bit too easy. Let me just place a missile launcher or two in a random spot. There, much better!"
Because, frankly, a lot of these levels would be pretty good with less or no missiles! It's amazing how this one gameplay element has completely overshadowed everything else about the game for me. I'm insane and masochistic so I still aimed for 100% anyways, but I'm not really sure why.
Infinite Love Mode is also a pretty neat idea but could be a bit better implemented; some of the submaps become literally impossible at 20+ portals, and a few of the submaps are far, far harder than the rest. Also, empty rooms that automatically end your run aren't very appreciated. I kind of want to see this mode tweaked a little because it's a lot more fun than the main game.
Also the soundtrack exists. I spent about 75% of my playtime with it muted since I kind of can't stand the soundtrack at all. So no real comment on it. Graphic style is also alright, nothing amazing but, it works. The trail of light behind the player character is pretty neat.
I don't think it's the worst platfomer I've ever played (or even close to it) but it's not solid enough for me to recommend, unfortunately.

This game is a lot of fun. So why am I not recommending it? Read on...
It started when I opened what was the last in a series of 20-25 loot crates (you get these as login rewards, quest rewards etc) over a period of about 3 weeks.
Not one single time was I lucky enough to get anything better than a basic 'white' (common) quality item.
When you open a loot crate, a prize 'wheel' flicks past showing pics of the prizes with what seems like a 50/50 split between white items and blue items and every. single. time it lands on a white item. The only way that I was able to get a blue quality item from one of these is to spend scrap (in game 'currency') to reroll and even then it took several rerolls (each one costing increasingly higer amounts of scrap) and then finally, when I did get a blue item - it was TEMPORARY (ie only lasts 2 hours) FFS what a joke.
The feeling of disappointment when I realised the item I'd 'won' was only going to last 2 hours made me realise that this game has stopped being fun and is just pushing me in the direction of spending money to get access to better gear.
You can craft your own, better quality gear, but the amount of resources of various types needed to craft even the first tier of blue items vs the rate at which those resources can be accumulated makes this game one of the grindiest games I've played in a very long time .. this system has _clearly_ been tweaked this way to encourage people to spend real money to advance. Trying to advance without spending real money has started to become fairly repetitive and not fun.
This is a real shame, as this game has all the right elements to be a good, fun, online game with a long lifespan. I've spent quite a decent amount of money in other online f2p games when I was enjoying the game and didn't feel pressured to spend money in order to advance (eg GW2 is a good example). When you are having fun with a game where you feel like you're making progress at a reasonable and fair pace, you're quite ok with willingly spending real money as you are enjoying the experience the game delivers. Crossout could have been a game like that, but it feels like the devs have lost sight of the long term benefits of a large, loyal playerbase, but instead have opted to gouge now for a quick buck at the expense of creating that large and loyal community of players who play (and spend) because the game is still engaging and fun.
tl;dr - this game is fun, but the advancement system is tweaked to strongly encourage players to spend real money in order to avoid very lengthy, boring grinds for even moderate improvements in gear etc.

If you have to be critical, and it's pretty hard to be so, then there are two cons and they are simply this:

2) I'm on PC with a mouse and a keyboard, this could be me or it could be something that's been improved by the devs over time, but initally I found using the mouse to be really clunky compared to when I've used a PS3 controller with the walking dead (also by Telltale Games). This was frustrating at times because I found I couldn't select the dialogue options I wanted or would sometimes miss quick time events that I otherwise shouldn't have. Although this didn't annoy for more than two episodes, it did initally leave me thinking I might have been better off purchasing it on console.
Neither of those things should really put people off though, it's more something to be aware of, the pro's of this game absolutely crush the cons.

TL:DR, discovered near the end of the game that I don’t have a stone heart after all while cringing at Zer0’s voice acting in episode 5 9/10 would cry-cringe teeth again with different choices.
As of this review I just finished the game so I decided to make the review instantly after I beat the game instead of a 6 month interval like with my axiom verge review.  And a small note that before Tales From the Borderlands I haven’t played a single Telltales game that is like Tales From the Borderlands or The Walking Dead(which I will review somewhere in the future).
You view the story perspective from 2 characters the middle manager from the biggest space company in the galaxy: Hyperion’s own Rhys and the Pandoran con-artist from hollow point: Fiona.
the whole game consists of 5 episodes in which the story will develop in its own way as you make critical choices that actual choices but it all starts with this: Rhys is looking for Fiona to talk out what happened during the story (in which you decide what happens there) and Rhys gets captured by a stranger with a Hyperion shotgun, and while Rhys is getting dragged through the wastelands of the Borderlands of Pandora Rhys tells the stranger (and the player) how it all started.
The presentation is as borderlands as it can be, the presentation in the same way as Borderlands 2 and The Pre-Sequel has been made in terms of art style, the voice-acting is for the most part perfect making the characters feel like they are more than just video game characters, the only issue I have with it is Zer0’s voice-acting. In the first episode Zer0 sum he has the same voice actor as he had back in borderlands 2 (Mike Turner) but in episode 5 he has a noticeable different  less husky, more formal-sounding voice.
The Music soundtracks are a blessing to the ears with Jungle – Busy Earnin’ as my personal favorite(I was listening to this song on repeat while making this review) .
In my final conclusion this game is a must play for every borderlands fan just for its fair share of humor, emotional moments and badass moments of complete awesomeness. You most NOT watch this game on YouTube since you most likely will disagree with the choices the Let’s Player will make, so you should rather play this game yourself than watch it.
Have fun with the game and see you all next time

So what can I say. As with all Dragon Ball games this one is best reserved for fans of the series. It's less of a traditional fighting game and more of a brawler with fighting game inspired themes. The gameplay regardless is solid and responsive. The A.I. does seem to have a few advantages over the player in single combat, being able to react and counter more quickly than human players are able even with the best of reflexes, but it forces the difficulty factor up a notch.
There is a learning curb to this game, and no luxury of a difficulty mode to chose from. Getting stronger will help with those super tough fights, which is paramount to the Dragon Ball theme. Some seem to have it better than others. I was able to plow through the story and mission modes with relative ease, encountering few road blocks on the way, whereas my friend spent a good 2 hours trying to kill Saibamen and failing... miserably.
Most everyone you'd care to see in a Dragon Ball Z game is in the roster, with few overlaps in "Form based" characters. The custom characters hold well to Akira Toriama's style and overall the game looks well polished. Add in the expansive and engaging gameplay with the story it's a great game. There are some notable bugs, but nothing that can't be patched in the future.
At present the games servers are marred with connectivity issues. The most negative thing I can say about the game is the programers made a huge error in the way the game format is meant to run as an MMO. To even log in you have to make an initial connection to the "Xenoverse server" which is glitchy to the max. If you're lucky you'll make it to the character select screen. From there you're lucky if you can make it into the actual game to play a mission or two before losing connection to the server and rolling the dice to see if you can get back in again. Namco games has made it public they're aware of this issue but one week since release we've yet to see any fixes yet.
For now you're best off stowing your money towards something until they fix the connection issues and make the game more stable. There is a way I discovered to get an uninterupted session but it requires a lot of luck, and doesnt persist through changing characters. Definatly keep an eye out for the fixes though and be ready to dive in. There will be many hours of fun awaiting you.

I normally play games a lot longer before reviewing them.  I'd normally do so for this game, but then then a woman lifted up her dress, dropped a phalic shaped crew served weapon larger than she is out of her skirt, yelled "This is my Valkyrie!" and proceded to blow my blouse off.  After I wiped the WTF look off my face, I decided it was ok to review this game.
So what is it?  Well...it's a game about anime girls with big gainax anime boobies beating the clothes off of each other for increasingly obscure reasons related to creating reasons for anime girls with big gainax anime boobies to beat the clothes off of each other...and friendship?
First, this sits in the overwhelmingly positive side of steam reviews and the reason for that is...it's an extremely well polished beat-em-up.  Forget about the gainax anime boobies, they were thrown on top of a well polished beat-em-up which combines a character action game, with a fighting game, and Dynasty Warriors.  It blends it together and produces the gameplay style for this game.  It likely also received the critical praise it has because there are few competitors in the beat-em-up genre on PC or Steam and few can match this quality.
As far as the gameplay there are about 20 characters each with their own fighting styles  (weapon reach, speed, status effects), move sets, close attacks, ranged attacks, and special attacks.  The characters are functionally unique and require differing playing styles to excel at, something any beat-em-up fan will celebrate.  The controller in the game is familiar to a beat-em-up player - weak attack, strong attack, jump, dash, block, special.  The game doesn't do too good of a job explaining the nuances of the game's system and I had to look up some help while I was doing the tutorial for things like air raids and frenzy mode.
Single player includes four story modes for each of the character groups in the game, each character also has a story mode of about five missions, missions can also be played on hard mode with tougher ai enemies or simply replayed, so there is no shortage of content to enjoy.  The flow of a mission is usually a mook wave followed by one or more bosses who may or may not be accompanied with mooks.  There are several different maps with different terrain, the other characters you fight all have their own unique fighting style and the situations will call you to treat the environment differently depending on who you are facing.
On top of that is a multiplayer mode (which I haven't delved too deep in) which includes 4 player deathmatch and 2v2 matches online.  Though, the multiplayer has few people on it, you'll likely have to run bot matches or bring friends if you want to play.
Next is the environment and story which can be described as all-together wierd.  There is a line between wierd, funny, and obscene and the game manages to skate right on the line without falling down and landing in a broken heap at the bottom of a pile of...dirty panties?  Anyway the game manages to avoid taking itself seriously and it doesn't try to be so silly you can't enjoy the game.  Titilation is carefully managed with either humor or as a means to keep the game from becoming too serious and it manages it all without becoming offensive (beyond being a game about anime girls with big gainax anime boobies beating the clothes off of each other).  It takes real talent to do that.  As far as the WTF moments I've posted above, they will hit you over the course of the game, sometimes when you're actually reading the dialogue or sometimes with you get blasted topless with the phalic HMG and it's hilarious when it does happen.
In short, if you are a beat-em-up fan this is a game that belongs in your library.

The gameplay itself is pretty fun - when you get to play it. The combat feels a bit like Budokai, but I definitely preferred Budokai 2. But it is still fun and worth playing if you're a fan of DBZ titles.
While the game does incorporate a lot of new elements, none of them feel fully flushed out. The Toki Toki hub world is just a huge pain to navigate, and why did they even give a jump button to you in that area? I like the student system, where you can learn skills from a chosen master, and gain items pertinent to that character.
The story is passable, and the voice acting is pretty much what you'd expect from a DBZ title, but the major disappointment is the Parallel Quest system. I think this could have been a great way to introduce battle scenarios, but it just feels like more of the same of the main questline. Yes, there are items you can go around and hunt, but it wouldn't feel like nearly as much of a chore if after every parallel quest it didn't start you back at the Toki Toki world entrance. That just makes me not want to do PQs.
But then comes the games absolute biggest flaw, and something that I feel is worthy of a refund: The constant disconnects from the game server. I understand that I can play single player without interruption by restarting Steam in Offline mode, but that is a major inconvenience when I can just choose any other title from my catalogue and play that instead. But what if I want to play with friends? Well, you just have to put up with being disconnected after just about every other quest. It is horrendously implemented, moreso than any other only mediocre-implementation of features.
All in all I would not recommend this game and I am quite disappointed in it for a variety of reasons.

Sure you can call me a salty vet, but the development of this game was so sad it almost made me cry.  When I found this game it was great, you would build a bot, level up, unlock new parts in a tech tree and win a decent amount of money in matches to buy new parts.  Now, rank means literally nothing, you randomly get "robits" from crates, ( which usually comes in an extremely small amount compared to what you used to be able to get from matches based on your score).  You can color bots, (but only four colors now), more op premium features were added, and building a decent bot became harder and much less rewarding.
Update after update Freejam continued to put out updates with more and more disapproval, and continued to lose more and more players.  The ironic thing is that I read Freejam's mission statement and they said that their goal was to, "develop a game closely with the players".  Unfortunately, at some point freejam either gave up or stopped caring what their players said and turned a unique game with one of the best premium feature systems I had ever seen, into just another shoot em up game.
This game went from being one of my favorite games of all time, to being a tragic loss in just a few years.  You may say I am not open minded to the new updates, but with the constant removal of all that was good in this game, there is no point.
For those of you who say vets need to just play the game again and get into it, I have.  I had a yearning for it on a roadtrip, came home and played it for almost a week.  Then I simply had just another wake up call that this game is SUCH a SHELL of its former self!
I then found out that Robocraft was going into full release tomorrow and felt now was the best time to finally leave a review.  I am looking forward to the day when someone finally completes running servers of the old version, but as of tomorrow when Freejam officially locks this awful version into existence, it will be dead to me.
Thank you very much for listening to us Freejam.  Literally everyone said no and you kept on going.  I would pay upwards of $30 to be able to play the old game, but you won't even do that.
Goodbye Robocraft, I'm so sorry you went down this road.
Update as of October 25 2017
As expected of myself, the yearning to play old Robocraft had grown since I had deleted it.  So I evenutally reinstalled it to check on Hallowfest one more time, as one of the best times I could remeber was Hallowfest 2015.
I could see that the decorations and music for Halloween had not changed, which brought me back and gave me an immense feeling of nostalgia.  I immeadiately dismantled all my bots to create one final bot to battle with.  I ended up making an almost completely light cube armored hover with 7 tier 10 plasmas on top, and electroplating everywhere.  Then when I got into battle and actually started playing, I realized something.  Even with my literally, Top of the Line, plasmas, I could barely put a dent in anything.
The multipliers or , " Balances", as Freejam calls it has literally changed the amount of damage I was able to output.  I had grinded forever to get all those plasmas, tier 10 hovers and electroplates, and I was torn apart by a mess of nothing but wheels, basic armor cubes and I believe tier 2 smgs.
I realized that even if you were to grind in this game, your weapons literally would not increase in efficiency or damage at all!! Making spending time saving up for new weapons, except for the pay to win ones (LOML, Grenade Launcher thing), aboslutely USELESS!!!
Its one thing to make it harder to play and to take out the fun of tiers and a tech tree, but to literally make it so basic smgs are practically as good as tier 10 ones that are hundred of times more expensive, literally ruins the game completely.
I am planning on trying to try to contact Freejam and beg them to add even a paid version that allows you to downgrade.  I use to think my negativity for the new version was based purely on nostalgia, but seriously, now it is just a bad game.

This game does have it's issues, but supposing you meet the minimum specifications it'll run fine. With some patience I'm sure this game will become something pretty incredible because the concept of gold mining is such a massive time sink. I bought the game a few days ago and sunk over ten hours into it in one day - Great fun, nice array of vehicles and fully deformable terrain puts this a cut above the others in my book. The expanse of detail into connections to generators, water pump hoses, filters. Car maintenence (Fuel filters, cogs etc). - Although I'm yet to experience a vehicle failure, no doubt an upcoming feature.  It's about as good of a gold digging simulator as you're likely to get and personally I think it's fantastic regardless of the minor bugs I've run into. (Hitboxes mostly on Arnolds Parcel). Considering this is a game that was released on the 13th of October, it's surprising how good it is and it's nice to see the developers taking feedback on board as they go along. Let's show some patience guys, they wanted a game out early to show you what it can do. For what it is it's pretty impressive and with a little time all the minor issues will no doubt be fixed. - Let's keep in mind it's barely been out a month.
Overall I seriously reccomend this game to anybody who has the ability to look past a couple technical glitches and just enjoy the great gameplay it provides in it's graphical greatness and sometimes amusing physics, attention to detail and operation of some complicated machinery.

As a former ARMA player, this game is a dream come true. I started out super skeptical because 'early access' but in honestly this is an amazing game provided you have the time(2+h) for one full game.
Pros :
Great community - I play on QFF/Mumblerines servers and the community on these are very good. It has been a blast playing with these guys and I haven't encountered many try-hards. There's a few jokers here and there but they do their bit and all's well and good.
Graphics - Graphics, textures and the likes are very well done and looks very very photorealistic in ultra or cinematic settings. A few artifacts and errors here and there but the overall aesthetic is very good.
Gameplay - This performs very well as a mil-sim and committing an action is definitely easier compared to the clunkier - ARMA 3. Controls are fluid for the most part(movement, aiming) while it might get a bit taxing sometimes(e. when you're a medic, it takes 2 button presses to choose the med bag) which isn't bad but it might get frustrating during an intense firefight.
VOIP - The VOIP system here is something else. When you're holed up in a building and someone from another squad shouts "Mortars" you know ♥♥♥♥♥ about to hit the fan. Plus, there's 3 types of communication available - squad, squad lead, proximity which all serve different purposes.
Building - Although I assume its not complete yet and could be easier to do/set-up control wise. The base-building system is very good at its current stage. You can set up sandbags, barbed wires, bomb shelters and a ton of other stuff whenever you want(there's requirements for each obviously and has to be commanded from the SL). But ain't nothing better than building a super-FOB.
Cons -
There's 2 main problems with the game at this point in time. Which are VERY fixable and I'm pretty sure fixes are coming for them in the next updates, but I'll leave it in here none the less FOR NOW.
Servers
There's a lack of AS/SEA servers at the moment. However I can guess this is because player counts in these regions are relatively lower. I play from SEA so most servers I have to play in are EU which more times than not leads to lag and clunky hit detection, but playable yes and you don't clip or have 'lagged movement'  preventing the enemy from hitting you.
Lack of weapon/class customization
There's a lack of weapon/class customisation. You don't really get you customise your class or weapon. In some cases, you might be forced to spawn as a rifleman which is fine, but in some factions, their default guns don't have optics thus making long-range firefights a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
But that's about it. If you love ARMA 3 or mil-sims in general, this is a great buy. I wouldn't recommend this for people who expect a Battlefield/COD experience because that is definitely not like that. Also, expect TO DIE A LOT without even knowing where you got shot from. It's a 1 - 2 shot kill most of the time.

As with my CLANNAD review, this is being written as a review of the story of Steins;Gate as I have seen the show 3 times and have only played 101 minutes of the VN as of writing this. This review will not talk about this VN's mechanics, art, or voice acting, but will include info on the OST as it shares one with the anime.
Okabe Rintorou is 21 year old who has devoted his free time to science. But not just any science, MAD SCIENCE! Except, not really. He just lives a neverending fantsy that he never seems to grow out of, despite LITERALLY EVRYONE CALLING HIM OUT ON IT. He, along with his childhood friend Mayuri (16) go to a time travel press conference directed by one Dr. Nakabachi. While waiting for the conference to start a loud boom comes from the roof, and Okabe leaves to see what caused it.

Why did I just write the entire prologue of the game? Because this story is so intricate that the only way to summarize it is to write as much as you can. So here's me talking loosely and generally, not about the plot or the story, but about its affect on ME. Ever wanted to build a time machine out of a microwave? No? Apparently you can, as long as you don't send organic matter into the past. Don't do that. Look, in my opinion, this is the definitive time travel story of all time. Although it isn't my favourite story in Visual Novels/Anime, in my opinion, it's the most perfect in terms of mechanics. I've watched it 3 times now, and any issues I've had with it were what I
to be plot holes, but they all actually do get resolved!
That's right, there isn't even
plot hole or paradox in this show about time travel. Furthermore, the cast of this story is some of the most diverse you will find, and it deals with very sensitive issues expertly. My one, ONE, complaint about the story is that the story is slow to start. Like, really slow. It's a very well made and interesting part to watch or read, and it eases you into the science of time travel that the writers masterfully created, but it may put newcomers off. Don't let it, for your sake.I honestly can't recomend this enough, no matter how you choose to experience it.
Don't even get me started. There isn't any complaints at all. It's 100% my
soundtrack in anything ever. Kanako Ito's unmistakeable voice graces evry vocal song in the sountrack, and evry instrumental is orchestra performed for the dramatic parts of the story and the electronic music is used for the
sciency bits. My favourite tracks have to be Skyclad Observer and Gate of Steiner, those are just... Incredible. Honestly, this show/VN would be worth watching/reading just for the soundtrack.
I love this story so incredibly much, it's simply fantastic Please, if you're considering buying this VN or watching the show, please do. Like, now.

So, I beat this game, and that took about 20 hours, and I usually roll my eyes when I see reviews that says they played the whole game but don't reccomend it, but there you go.
I'm a big fan of metroidvanias in general, as well as stat crunchy item games, and was excited when I first saw this game. I really enjoyed the premise and silliness of the game, and wanting to get to the end of the game was the largest driver of me continuing to play for the last 12 hours... also, I kept thinking "the ends gotta be soon, just a bit longer... ugh, just a bit longer."
As far as metroidvanias go, this game felt like it was missing something, namely in the finding-new-abilities-to-unlock-areas department. You get new abilities, but because it's stat-based build-a-character, they generally aren't required... except when they are, and you're mad because you didn't pick that magic path, and now this boss fight is going to be miserable and take 30 attempts. UGH. You unlock further areas by beating bosses and getting a key from them. Most of the boss fights were frustrating and repetetive. Despite leveling up and getting explicitly more powerful (in the "I can kill those early enemies I never have to fight really easily now" way) I never felt like any of my progression mattered, the only reason I couldn't beat the game earlier was because I had to jump through all of the boss-fight-get-key hoops.
