Interstellar Marines is a highly ambitious tactical FPS, promising a unique co-op experience with roleplaying and nonlinear gameplay. According to the developers, the game is heavily influenced by the likes of Half Life, System Shock 2 and Rainbow Six 3: Raven Shield and will have a heavy focus on realistic science fiction. Interstellar Marines has been in ongoing development for a very long time and the team have been subjected to quite a few complications. Zero Point Software has had to overcome some obstacles along the way, such as having to change game engine mid-development, filing for bankruptcy, as well as failing to reach their Kickstarter Campaign goal of $600,000.
At the time of the publication of this review, Interstellar Marines is in Steam Early Access and is expecting full release in late 2014. The game currently consists only of a multiplayer component, featuring the 'Team Domination' game mode, where the objective is to capture and hold areas within the map to gain points. All of the maps in the game feature a dynamic environment with changing lightning and weather conditions. This is for me the only real differentiator between Interstellar Marines and other FPS games at the moment. The dynamic environment force players to change their play style multiple times throughout the match. One moment, the map might be well lit and players will sprint to the objectives playing very offensively, until suddenly, the map goes completely dark and people will move slowly around using their flashlight sparsely to avoid detection. These sudden changes in player mentality really helps the game in terms of its tactical focus.
While Interstellar Marines' tactical aspect is quite impressive, it still has some fairly major shortcomings. Firstly, the game has yet to receive basic FPS functionality such as crouching and proper sprinting which is kind of odd, considering its long development. The shooting and overall gameplay is extremely barebones and not very satisfying. The assets of the game are fairly limited, and many of the maps are littered with big identical boxes at every corner. Lastly, the game has a very lackluster options menu, with barely any settings at all. Brightness and gamma sliders are not available at current time, which unfortunately for me means that under medium-low light situations my monitor looks absolutely horrible. This might just be a problem I am having, but settings like these should be fairly standard anyway.
All of this can of course be improved as time goes on, considering it's still in Early Access, but I do have my worries as the game is expected to release later this year. The game seems like it's been stuck in progress in the 1,5 years I've been following it, which honestly make me speculate if this game is vaporware.
ZP Software is currently promising a fully fletched story campaign with up to 4 player co-op, roleplaying elements, an open game world, and a customizable arsenal. As you might see, this is a lot of content, of which none exist as of yet. Taking into account that Zero Point Software are a very small development team, it is quite hard to figure out just exactly how they will manage to put out so much content in just under a year.
Whether my speculations are unfound, and the game will end up getting a successful release or not, is up to Zero Point Software. But as it stands, I do have my doubts and will therefore recommend waiting for the game to receive more content before buying into it.

I will preface this review first by admitting that I have not visited the game's forum board or its Discord server so if any of my concerns are addressed there, I will have missed them legitimately out of ignorance.  With that said, let's begin!
This game fulfils a niche within the game market that appeals to many interests.  Fans of the titular show, for one, will enjoy being able to fiddle with some tools of the trade that make their appearance within the realm of Gold Rush.  This experience can be both educational and enjoyable as it gives you the ability to experience something that would otherwise be limited to individuals with names like Yukon Cornelius. For others, this simulator provides some mind-numbingly repetitive task-grinding that yields minimal rewards for the effort put forth.  Don't get me wrong.  I fit into the second category here.  I have a vast arsenal of games that both simulate and challenge me to the limits of my mental and tactile abilities, but there is still beauty to be found in balance.  Sometimes I just want to see what happenings when I dig myself into a hole or if I can successfully flip my pickup truck after a long day of nugget searching. To each their own... nothing wrong with that, right?
Of course when you're not trying to break the game in spectacular fashion, you can always follow along on the handy Miner's Brochure that introduces players to a sort of tiered guideline that will give first-time-would-be-miners an idea of how to start and where to go after you hit serious pay-dirt. The premise behind having tiered progression in a simulator is a fantastic mechanic that is rarely executed properly.  This game is no exception. Within a day of setting up my first tier panning system, I found a nugget that all but voided the need for any of the other first tier equipment upgrades.  Sure, I could have continued to slowly pan for gold and lingered in the first tier for a little while longer, but why would I do that when I can suddenly afford vehicles for which I am disastrously under-qualified to drive.  Gold Rush rushes (heh) through the beginning and dumps you into a slow grind that can only be sped up through taking out a bank loan.  Without the loan, you will be looking at (a conservative estimate of) 12 hours of the same repetitive task in order to get into the tier 3 mining operation.  Personally, I hate bank loans, so I'm just gonna keep on grinding.
Aside from the game play mechanics, Gold Rush: The Game feels overall clunky and unfinished.  It lacks polish in some key areas of play, such as the sketchy character movement controls which feel as if they are stuck in the early 90's fps genre.  World objects are mostly just there for show as "clutter" and unfortunately do not benefit from any level of interaction with the exception of being something to crash my pickup truck into.  Load times between zones are unnecessarily long even when system specs are far above the recommended requirements.  I have to scratch my head a little at the 16Gb minimum RAM requirement too...  that just seems like sloppy code optimization to me.
Will I continue to play this game?  Absolutely.  Purely because I want to see what the devs will change and expand upon as time goes on. This simulator has a lot of potential, so I'm going to settle in and watch what comes next.

Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus is a port of a PS Vita musou-style beat 'em up featuring busty ninja girls, clothing damage, and copious amounts of jiggle physics. Despite its obviously explicit nature, it's a very fun and engaging brawler.
When it comes to graphics, they received a bit of polish in comparison to the original. The models for all the characters look good, and the costumes are detailed as well. Special effects and location design in general, while not anything special, are pretty good overall. The only thing I would criticize is that, due to the busty nature of the game, almost all girls share a similar body build. (Except for the two flat girls, Mirai and Ryoubi, as well as Daidouji being more muscular overall.)
In the sound department, my gosh the music is just awesome. It's either classical instruments, hard rock, an electronic synthesizer, or a combination of any. Each character gets their own theme which does a very good job at describing what kind of personality they have. Some of my favorite pieces include For Master Kurokage, Proof of Strength, Gessen Ninja Room, and Chaos in Bloom that was the main theme of one of the previous Senran Kagura games, Burst.
The sound effects themselves for beating stuff up, as well as the screams (or rather moans) of defeated ninja girls are just as satisfying as in most solid beat 'em ups.
Gameplay-wise, in single player every mission consists of you progressing through a stage, defeating all enemies across your path, and then facing the boss at the end. It's high-paced action, especially in the duels between you and the final opponents, with a lot of different moves and combos you can perform to be unpredictable. As both of you take damage, your clothes rip, revealing more and more skin for the player to admire, and you can even strip your opponent completely and leave them shamefully trying to cover themselves if you finish them off with a Ninja Art while they're down to their underwear.
You can also, from your base form (wearing the school uniform, corresponding to Flash on the Flower of Balance) you can either perform your Shinobi Transformation (which gives your character a specific costume as well as healing them and buffing their stats) corresponding to Yang, or activate Frantic Mode, corresponding to Yin, which strips your character down to their underwear, turning them into a glass cannon with fast, incredibly strong attacks but laughable defense. The latter two forms can also expend Ninja Art Gauge to perform different Ninja Arts which are super moves, including a Desperation Move that is unlocked later in the game, and requires you to be on low health and expend a LOT of your gauge, but is capable of turning the tide of the battle around.
By defeating enemies in each form, you level them up, unlocking more special abilities for each one of them, like health regen for Shinobi or extra exp and zeni for Flash. After each mission you're awarded experience and currency (zeni) that you can spend in the in-game shop to unlock costumes, gallery pieces, or play Lingerie Lottery. (This game has some weird stuff indeed...)
The game has 22 different playable characters, each with their own unique fighting style, five from each of the five schools, with two bonus characters that were DLC in the original Vita version,
There are two main mission types: Shinobi Battle Records, which is the main storyline, and Shinobi Girl's Heart, which is a special 5-stage makeshift arcade mode that covers a tiny extra story arc for each respective girl. You can also play through the former on Hard Mode, which beefs up the stats of enemies so your maxed out characters can have some worthy opponents. Outside of Hard Mode, the mission are relatively easy so there generally shouldn't be too many problems if you just wanna see some clothes rip and girls talk.
Outside of missions, you can browse through your gallery, buy more stuff from the shop, or dress up girls in the Dressing Room. There is an absolute
of costumes and accessories to choose from, some more lewd than others. (Not even talking about how you can... ekhem... "interact" with the girl in various ways.)
In multiplayer, the characters are differently balanced to what you have in single-player, and it's all either a 4-man free-for-all or 2v2 with different rules depending on the mode - either stripping as much clothing as possible, collecting panties (yes, panties) falling down from the sky, or just good ol' beating up. You can play online or with friends.
The story is a continuation of the previous Senran Kagura games, and while it might appear to be a bit carefree at the beginning, each girl actually has one or two dark details from their past, as well as having different reasons for becoming Shinobis, different moral codes etc. There is also some character development for each heroine, and a lot of them are related to each other in ways you wouldn't even expect. They're fun, interesting, and either cute or... uhm... attractive.
Overall I can reccommend this game (almost) guilt-free. It's a fun fast-paced brawler with an interesting storyline and characters, if you don't mind (or outright enjoy, you damn pervert...) all the fanservice within.

An immediate warning: This is not a game for people who suffer from seizures or have an aversion to sudden and constant brightness.
It's amazing how much pressure you can feel in a platforming game with a minimalistic color palette, pixelation, and constant movement both by the level and the enemies in that level. I have always enjoyed platformers, so I have to admit a bias with this type of game. And with the minimal graphics, then all attention must be paid toward the control since platformers are made or broken by poor controls.
ESJ, thankfully, does not suffer from poor controls. It's quite responsive and intuitive, which makes the learning curve easy. That said, the difficulty curve is quite an undulation between easy portions and hair-tearing difficulty. I've found often enough that the "simplicity" of the game makes it all the more frustrating at times because you start to push yourself and jump earlier than needed, only adding to the difficulty.
The music should also be mentioned. It, like the colorful brightness both adds to the feel and flavor of ESJ and can be distracting in its own right (which is a perfect blend for a platformer in this manner). It is a soundtrack worth the cost alone.
While I thoroughly recommend this game, I would add the caveat that you should look at this as a platforming game. I would also recommend only doing a few levels at a time. The colors can get to you after a while (though it does nicely change hues enough to not be too terrible) and some of the levels change in brightness enough to be a bit hard on the eyes.
All and all, a solid platformer with a great deal of fun to be had. And enough challenge to keep you playing without too much frustration.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets.
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest.
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates.
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

One of my top 5 favorite FPSs.
The Good: Almost everything. The gameplay is not fancy, but it is refined and the controls are responsive.
The story is surprisingly well crafted. The dialogue is all pretty believable. The voice acting is good.
The particle (and dismemberment) effects are excellent, as is the lighting and sound design.
The Bad: It's only an 8-hour Nazi-killing romp. You can never kill too many Nazis and I was left wanting more.
The pacing is sort of all over the place. It oscillates between frenetic and slow, with few good stopping points.
The annoying: Guns never seem to behave quite right in FPSs. Pistols are too accurate and high-damage, assault rifles are the opposite, shotguns work when they feel like it, and the signature weapon is crap until very nearly the end of the game, then it becomes useful in about 20% of situations.
The Ugly: The textures, literally. The textures are not good. Everything is fine beyond about 15 feet, but closer and some textures (tables and desk, especially) look like they were made in Microsoft Paint. It doesn't detract from the Nazi-killing, but it is odd given the next issue.
The. Game. Is. Massive. The game's file, that is. This is a 40+ GB game (which is sort of the norm, anymore), but you don't get much for the considerable file size. The graphics are OK, not great, and the game isn't that long, so I can only concluded that it's just uncompressed ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t filling up the 40 gigs. Not a deal-breaker, but if you're dealing with slow download speeds (like me), you're gonna have to wait a while.
Bottom line: Cathartic and viceral, it's Nazi-killing joy from start to finish, but you're gonna wait for the download.

BrotherZ is a mixture of modern FPS mechanics with Team Fortress 2 & ur favourite F2P shooters like Wolfteam but with transforming zombies instead of wolfs with World War theme on top of it.
Unlike the Team Fortress series where you have to choose one of the classes like Heavy or Engineer etc before you spawn, you have all of their weapons at your disposal. So that's something to look forward to.
While the core mechanic game works well & plays like a TF2 clone, there's alot of problems for this multiplayer only shooter to be worth your time.
Pros
There's lobby/server browser system
Can easily self host to play with your local friends
Well the network code works (Not great athough since I get 300ping from Russian servers)
Great artsyle for maps
Cons
The game looks abandoned from day 1 from the scope of things in the forums
Barely anyone is playing with a few empty servers
Poor jumping mechanic system. The game makes u wait a few seconds so you can double jump and there's many small platforms that makes you vulnerable to getting killed by others since you standing there waiting for the jump ability to recharge.
No spy abilities?
Gun sounds that sounds like they've been directly ripped from TF2/COD/CS
The heavy machine gun's animations looks & sounds incomplete.
No proper bots in game, just zombies that follow you.
Some UI elements are left in Russian
The Steam storefront trailer has Advanced Warfare OST that is mostly likely used without permission
Well from all of my points added up, it looks like a suspect of asset flipping in addition to f2p style rent shop & achievement grinding that makes very little sense since barely anyone is playing this game.
Too bad this game goes into the bin on my PC. Such a wasted potential, this could have been a decent TF2 clone if it wasn't from lack of people playing this game or real bots.
I actually like World War TF2 theme over it. Maybe making BrotherZ > F2P and having a real online community could save this game but for now it's not worth anyone's time.

So I just want to get out of the gate right now. I'm recommending this game. I love it. I'd go so far as to say that if I made such lists, I'd put it on my list of "games of the year"... If I did such things. That said. It isn't without its faults. So I'm gonna go ahead and be long winded and lengthy about everything I like, and am♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off about with this game. So shall we get into it?
Okay!
So starting with what I like about the game!
As we can all agree... It's a fighting game. No surprise there, it's a Dragon Ball title, and fighting is basically what they DO in Dragon Ball. But it isn't quite the traditional set up for a fighting game we're mainly used to, I.E. the 1v1 side view battle in a random and interesting looking arena venue. Cause... for starters, not many venues in DB are that interesting to see from that perspective. Instead, the game does things from a behind, third person view, which actually takes full advantage of being able to do the sort of superhuman feats you see in the series, and it does this while ensuring the game is nicely fast paced and frantic with its combat.
Speaking of the combat! That's something else I adored about the game, is how accessable it is to players. It's control system is simiilar to games such as Guilty Gear or Skull Girls in the sense that the control system is VERY simplistic and easy to figure out, but at the same time does enough with that simple control system that the game is deep enough to have varying levels of strategy to how the combat is done. Every character uses moves and abilities that make them opperate drastically differently from one another. Someone like Goku, depending on which incarnation of him your playing as, would be focused on using alot of rush down tactics, while still maintaining himself as a relevant threat with powerful ranged attacks, where as someone like Hercule is more about controling the field to his advantage by either going temporarily invincible (whcih I can only imagine is possible for him by letting his ego get in the way of what passes for reality in that game) or faking a stomach ache that stops his attacker dead in their tracks.
And since we're on the subject of the characters, lets talk about the thing that first grabbed my attention about Xenoverse: Character creation! That's right folks, you actually make your own, personalized fighter for this game from one of five races. This character is of course used in story mode, and is likely going to be the primarily played character for most people in the game that aren't interested in the main character roster. This character changes depending on what YOU want from them, and can be modified with a variety of cosmetic items (some of which give you stat bonuses and penalties depending on the item you use) and special techniques known in the Dragon Ball series, as well as a few that I'd wager are probably unique to the game itself.
All these things mashed together into a fighting game that also uses what could only be described as minor RPG elements for an actual leveling system to measure character growth, has made a game that I've just been adoring!
As I said though, it isn't without its flaws as well.
First and foremost being, and hopfully this won't be a factor any more by the time anyone in the future reads this review, is the server. Yes. The game itself, love it as I do, is its own flaw, based on its game server. I bought Xenoverse just a couple days after launch keep in mind. So at the time of my writting this, its game server is VERY unstable. Half the time, I can't even log in to the game to play it, and since the game doesn't have an offline option, I'm actually forced to set Steam itself into offline mode sometimes just to play the game without a connection inturruption! The fact the game doesn't HAVE an offline mode of its own was a bit disheartening to come to the realization of. I'd have liked it if I could keep Steam running online while not having to bother with Xenoverse's game server. But as I said, this is an issue that will hopfully be fixed in the future, and hopfully by the time anyone reads this, that issue will infact be fixed.
So lets move on to the next problem I have. Some of the battles in this game. The quests and story mode have a few encounters with characters that are just stupidly armored and never flich at anything you hit them with. As easy as the game is to pick up and play, I could see this turning some people off to the game after a while. Though personally I found it really satisfying when I could finally beat some of these tough enemies, such as Freiza in his fully powered, ultimate form, Cell, and of course, Beerus himself (and his attendant Whis, who is a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when you fight him). If you don't enjoy fighting enemies that are stupid hard to take down, or at the very least don't have the hell bent determination I do to overcome them when you meet them, you probably won't enjoy this game.
Then finally, it being a Dragon Ball game is probably going to turn some people off automatically. We all know how stupid and ridiculous the series on the whole can be, and it is ultimately an anquired taste.
All things considered though, I still urge people to get this one! At the very least give it a glancing thought on the days we know it'll eventually be on sale. All things considered, this one is deffinately worth the money!

Dragon Ball Xenoverse, what can I say. It's a Dragon Ball RPG. Though currently this week (Launch Week) it is plagued with disconnection issues. Putting that aside because I'm am sure in due time like any other game on launch server issues will be less of an issue. So on to the actual review.
The story is based around Future Trunks and Time Lines. You get to create a custom character that you build upon during gameplay. You can create up to eight characters (***SPOILER*** You will only be able to unlock them once you've beaten the game the first time). You can create Male/Female Majin's, Male/Female Saiyens, Male/female Humans, Namekians and Frieza Clan. There really isn't much to play with for customization (I mean it's not like this is Skyrim or anything) but there are plenty of choices to go around.
Without going nuts into detail you are summoned by Shenron after Future Trunks wishes for you. You are then appointed to work with him to correct corrupted timeline plots.
Combat is really solid and responsive with a controller. The graphics are fantastic, though some may beg to differ. The AI can be a tad noobish late game by stun locking you if you let them, but for the most part you can take control of any situation. That is from my own personal experience, it may differ for others.
And as a heads up to anyone who has or is planning on purchasing this game during the first week or so. Yes the servers are going to crash a lot, what game hasn't. If you put your Steam into Offline mode it will not connect to the servers making the game 100% playable without disconnection issues. Sure it may be counter intuitive but it works.
In closing. If you're a fan of the Dragon Ball universe I'm sure you'll enjoy this game. And if you're a hardcore DB fan it's a must have.

In short: It's good. Solid for the most part, exceptional here and there, little to complain about. Let's go through this bit by bit.
As far as the graphics go, it's RosePortal's standard fare which is in its own right top notch. The maps are varied and authentically constructed unlike the square-looking jazz many serve us nowadays. The characters' sprites are very detailed - three tiles in size as opposed to RPG Maker XP's standard two or the atrocious VX' one. This allows for much more detail and it shows. As for the portraits, the Whisper/Sweet Lily regular-sized avatars went byebye, replaced by full-size portraits akin to those of a visual novel. Sadly, their emotional expression suffered from the transition as the characters all seem to have the same expressions all the time and it's a damn shame, especially given the dialogue and overall story. It'd have a much bigger impact if the characters on-screen actually also showed their emotions via portraits. As for these portraits, they're indeed detailed and beautifully drawn (I'm looking at you, Stiletta, and I know where your eyes are, I'm just focused on something else... <3 ) and if various emotional variations of them were to be added, this could very well be the current standard in indie jRPGs. Another gripe I have is with the tilesets themselves as well as some monsters. They've been carried over from Whisper or Sweet L. with little to no modifications and there's simply not enough new items in. As for the monsters, the situation is nowhere near this serious - granted, there are many regulars coming back but there's enough newcomers to just forget about everything and scream: "MORE BLOOD!!!", then kill'em off.
The soundtrack is downright beautiful. Granted, a lot of tracks return from SLD or even WR but there's also plenty new melodies and they overall fit the purposefully exagerrated epic theme of the game. Keep up the good work.
As for the story... Well, if the humor is down your alley, you'll love it. Plenty references to classics both new and old (Game of Thrones and the Exorcist just to name a few), breaking the fourth wall (characters shrugging off the protagonist's question about the quest's purpose, saying that probably the developers came up with some reward), raunchy humor (a fairy talking from the inside of a female party member's body, guess how it got there!), parody of other well known indie jRPGs (Laxius and Aveyond chars make an appearance!)... there's enough to keep you laughing for days on end... unless of course you don't like that kind of jokes. This game is one big joke - in a good way. It's like one of those classic comedy movies where one funny scene is followed immediately by another with no boring mess inbetween.
And then there's.... the gameplay. Four levels in and I am yet to utilize the crafting system and the limit breaking will probably come so I can't really say a lot on this... yet. But what I do have to say is...
...it's certainly interesting. First off, aside from a single instance, so far monsters just don't respawn unless you use a special item called the Lure Candle. This definitely takes away the tediousness and repetitiveness of the battles which is an issue with many jRPGs out there. If you need to grind, you just need to ask for it but if you think you don't, then why bother? The battles won't be an issue or much of a challenge (unless you're on the highest difficulty level, like I am), so nothing will come in your way if you're just in for the story. Then again, if you do want to face the game's best, some preparations will be necessary and they will be rewarded. Each battle is rated in stars, you can score from 1 to 3. If you do get the top scores, rewards will come aplenty.
The battles are varied not only by the difference in skills the characters have but also by the new mechanics such as Overdrive and Limit Break attacks, allowing you to score MASSIVE DAMAGE in a single volley. These mechanics won't be a surprise if you played some high-budget jRPGs like Legend of Dragoon but seeing those in an indie production is a neat surprise.
An issue with how the game is constructed arises in level access, though. Similarly to Sweet Lily Dreams, you get to select the game worlds from a menu - but unlike in SLD, where it has a story-based explanation (a selection of dreamworlds from a portal in Rosaria works splendidly in SLD), in Epic Quest the stages are just dubbed "Level X: Level name" and are selectable from a very simple menu with no main overworld map of any kind joining them. I've rarely seen this in jRPGs and I must say it kinda breaks the suspension of disbelief. Epic Quest won't try to fool you it's not a game and IMO that's a problem that should be rectified.
All-in-all, this is a solid game. It was pretty good already on release and now it's even more polished and I'm happy for a chance to play it proper. 8.5/10

Masterpiece. One of the most complex, emotional  and well-fleshed-out time travel stories every written. In the 34 hours it took for me to get 4 out of 5 endings (one of which was the true ending,) I've experienced almost every humanly emotion possible: from happiness, to fear, to anxiety, to anger, to sorrow, to disgust, to bitterness, to despair, to hope, and even to love. Masterful writing, characterization, atmosphere, and soundtrack.
As someone who played the VN first and then watched the anime, I can surely say the VN is superior to the anime in almost every way. You get much more time to get really attached to the characters; you gain much deeper insight into Okabe's character and internal struggles, and you get much more detailed technical explanations of how time travel works.  I was actually blown away by how extensively the visual novel discussed actual quantum mechanics and metaphysics; the writer REALLY did his research.
But most important of all, there is no comparison between the emotional impact of the visual novel versus that of the anime. The visual novel's sublime soundtrack, voice acting, and pacing all combine to form one of the most turbulent emotional roller coasters I have ever had the luxury of experiencing.
There is just no way to describe it; the atmosphere of intrigue and raw emotions that ooze from just about every crevice of the game is something that is to be experienced, not described.
TLDR: If you havent seen the anime then this is the definitively best way to experience the story
But if you have seen the anime already buy it anyway because the masterful writing and soundtrack will still make cry like a ♥♥♥♥♥ even when already know the story

A fun and entertaining point and click adventure game - with a few minor issues, but easily forgivable.
Simple, but adequate graphics, moody music, and surprisingly good voice acting. The main character was actually the weakest in terms of voice acting, in my opinion, and a few of the voice clips for the main character cut out part way through or didn't play at all (the main issue I encountered).
The story was entertaining, partly predicable and yet partly surprising - and the predictable parts were enjoyable, with the developers realizing they were cliche and playing to that to make them fun.
The puzzles were generally logical and straightforward (even if a few were silly when you think about them), though there is a considerable amount of back and forth within the areas of each self-contained chapter, and I did get stuck and had to consult a guide twice.
I count the short length as an asset - the game tells its story and entertains without overstaying its welcome.
Overall, I recommend it for fans of story based point and click adventure games.

Disclaimer: I received a key from the developer because I backed another game by them on Kickstarter. I wrote this review for a promotion that included receiving a key for the Strategy Guide, but I was not obligated to leave a positive review in order to get that key.
This is a first impressions "review" based on my first about 1.5 hours with the game broken into good, bad, and neutral points.
Good:
- Much of the writing is humorous and the author isn't afraid to break the fourth wall on occasion. Probably not to everyone's taste, but I'm certianly enjoying it so far.
- Despite being an RPG Maker title, it's clear this had some serious effort put into it - it doesn't appear to use any of the stock assets and it has a nice custom battle system.
- I do like what they did with the battle system - I think the closest comparison is probably Final Fantasy X (it's fully turn-based, but turn order is based on the speed stat and shown on-screen, there's also a "limit break" style mechanic that can be activated once your bar for it is full). However it has a little twist in that the first time you fight each enemy (all are visible while walking) they have stars over their head and you're rated on your performance in the battle (specifically turns and damage taken) - performing well will net you some bonus items on the spot. At the end of the forest area, I was also given a rating for the area which appears to be based on performance in the ranked battles.
Bad:
- Some of the areas are a bit claustrophobic and it's not always obvious where you can/can't walk, although the minimap (all RPGs like this should have one IMHO...) does alleviate the issue to some degree.
- Unless I missed it, a run button would be nice. Ideally, I think that should be a requirement in all games like this to keep the pace moving. If I'm trying to grab everything in the area and retracing my steps a bit I'd like to do so as quickly as possible so I can finish up and proceed with the story.
Neutral:
- My opinion on the music and art style is fairly neutral - they do the job well but I can't really say I was blown away either.
- I haven't played long enough to make a call on this yet, but so far the difficulty (on the normal setting) seems to be very well balanced - the normal enemies have posed enough of a threat that just mashing attack seemed like a bad idea, but they never seemed overwhelming either and I seemed to get just enough experience by running through each encounter once to stay on par with them. Really, the only reason this is in the neutral category rather than good is because I don't know if this will change further in or if the game has horribly overpowered bosses (haven't encountered one yet).  If it does stay well balanced, this can be moved up to the positives section.
Overall, this is a pretty solid little RPG and definitely one of the better modern-indie-retro-rpg titles I've played based on my experience so far. I can't say anything about the length, but provided I'm not halfway through after about 1.5 hours (based on the area selection screen I saw after leaving the forest, I highly doubt it) I'd say it's probably worth the cash if this kind of game is up your alley, especially if you wait for the inevitable holiday/summer sale where it'll likely only cost a few bucks.

In Tales from the Borderlands, you play as Rhys and Fiona. Despite having completely different backgrounds, their fates become intertwined. The story begins in media res, as they are both captured by a masked individual, who then asks them about their stories in relation to a mysterious Gortys project. This results in an unreliable narration, with some hilarious and over the top incidents, as Rhys and Fiona sometimes describe the same event in a very different light.
The gameplay is very similar to recent Telltale Games such as The Walking Dead. It's a blend of a point and click, and an adventure game, with the main focus being on the story and how you shape it by the choices you make, instead of puzzles. The voice acting is top notch, which isn't surprising taking in account the veteran voice cast. Also, all known Borderlands characters have the same voice actors as in the main games. The soundtrack is on par with everything else, with the opening tracks for each episode being nothing short of amazing.
While not being a Borderlands fan nor an expert, which surely made me lose some references, I was still able to enjoy the story very much. It's well paced and filled with good and intelligent humor, but it also has some tense and sad moments. The ending was very satisfying and fulfilling, which is starting to become a rarity nowadays. Also as a bonus, the story is considered canon by Gearbox, so it will have an impact on future games.
For me, Tales from the Borderlands is one of Telltales' finest games to date and I hugely recommend it!

Disclaimer: I received a key from the developer because I backed one of their other Kickstarters. I wrote this review for a promotion that included receiving a key for the Strategy Guide, but I have judged this game by my own standards and was not obligated to leave a positive review.
The Epic Quest of the 4 Crystals is an RPGMaker game- but that's fine by me as I tend to like those kind of games.  Mechanically, the game looks and sounds great. I like that you can control it with either the mouse or the keyboard or a combination of both (controller seems to be supported, but I can't say much about it myself). The battles are standard turn-based from what I've experienced with the addition of an interesting 'rating' system where you can try and beat each encounter under a certain amount of time and party damage with the option to reset a battle if you want to give it another try. There also don't seem to be 'random' battles- except for one area so far, battles seem to be finite with them being visible well ahead of time on both the mini-map and well, right in front of you. The only real problem I've run into with the mechanics is that sometimes it's hard to tell what areas you can walk on/behind on the map and what areas are solid- leading to some keyboard-tapping to get myself out of a corner.
I haven't completed the game just yet, but the characters and plot aren't really jumping out at me much so far. They're not bad, per se, but just sort of shallow. The humor can be a bit hit or miss- I love meta-humor, so of course I'm loving all the references to other RPGs and when the characters sort of roll their eyes at RPG conventions. There's also some racy/lewd humor that I didn't expect and at times seems a little out of place, as they tend to make their jokes and then move on from it. Still, I'm interested enough to want to know where the plot is going and what other references will come up.
Overall, I think this game is worth giving a try if you already like the genre and are looking for something a little quirky and lighthearted.

Okay, let me just start out by saying that this is one of the best and most creative games I have played in a long time.
- They have no minions, puzzles or even platforming in order to get to the bosses. Generally, this would make them anticlimactic, but a combination of the vast and beautiful world you travel through to get between them and the fact that you don't have to finish one boss before moving on to the next (which means you will clear out all the ones you find easy first, and be left with the ones which seems like an impossible challange).
- You can figure out how to beat the bosses through a well balanced combination of logical deduction and trial & error.
- After playing for an hour I suddenly managed a boss on my third try, and it felt incredibly satisfying, as I felt like I had actually become better over the past few battles.
- No health bars means you don’t have to keep trying and trying to beat a boss even after you figured out how to hurt it (especially important in a game where you are supposed to die a few times). This put the focus on what the player want to do: figure out how to kill these gigant titans!
- No extensive backtracking (since it’s open world) and no filler rooms with no real purpose, means that every single time you explore a new area, it’s exiting!
- Different trace in the snow when you roll, rolling down stairs etc. (the devils in the details)
Reading through the negative reviews was what drove me to leave this one, because far too many of the claims are invalid.
- The few seconds it takes to get back into combat after respawning are strictly necessary to prevent the game to just feel like endlessly beating up the same guy. It is the very thing that make you feel the weight of having only one life. That you are fighting things that has a million different ways of killing you in a split second. In addition I would feel like I surrendered if I at any point spawned inside the boss room, but had to leave because I was tired of dying to the same titan. Now I just feel like I'm saving it for later!
- If the world was full of people and objects to interact with, it would lose all it's impact. Anyone who has played shadow of the colossus will know what I mean. The feeling that this world is unchanging, and have been like this since times unknown requires that you don't find belongings of others all around the place. And the effect the lonelyness has on the mood of the game speaks for itself.

Considering its on Early Access, consider this review to be null and void when the final productis released.
Now thats out of the way, but still bearing in mind that its unfinished and that its hard to review a product which is not yet completed, i'll base this review on the barebones of the game, which is TDM (team death match) and sandbox.
TDM is fairly standard, and not much has changed when compared to other games that have TDM as a game mode. Two teams are faced off against each other, and the end objective is to get as many kills as possible. What would help with the great atmosphere and graphics would be having a no respawn system, to make the games more tense.
Being dark and gloomy, it is hard to distinguish friend from foe, especially with the helmet off giving way to many cases of friendly fire. I feel that having friendly fire on, with no punishment system kind of makes no sense, i would like to remove friendly fire from the game unless there is some kind of punishment for the offending player
One of the interesting aspects of the game, is the dynamic environments which are constantly shifted to give more fun and versatile feel to the game. Dynamic in the way that the weather in game changes, so one moment it can be bright and shiny and the next very dark and raining. This helps alot in maintaining the tense atmosphere in the game.
For what the game has to offer thus far, I am very excited to see what the final product has to offer. But for 13,99€, and for what it currently has to offer, i would say wait and hope for more content. Because it is very barebones right now.

Squad is a Response as much as it is a Game. It's a response to the incredible need for a game that helps capture the brutality of war in a way that helps give an appreciation for what fighting in a war really means.
Granted, its very much a game, with health bars, revive mechanics. It is by no means a 'Realistic' depiction of war, but is instead an immersive depiction of it, allowing oneself to fully flow into the role of the unkown soldier, fighting alongside one's brothers.
You will run around in a gunfire with no idea where you're being shot from, while failing to understand what your squad leader is screaming over the sounds of mortar fire, while defending your last position from a full on assault. Hiding behind the mountain of sandbag barriers that you and your fellow squad teammates built, the laughs and cheery banter that you and your squadmates shared will fade into the distance, as the last remaining sandbags finally dissipate, and you are finally laid to rest. Only a moment later, the fighting fades and a list of players appears on your screen, where you discover that you held off the invasion just long enough to achieve victory.
This was one of my personal experiences, that having played a large number of first person shooters (mostly on console) I can absolutely say is completely unique to this game. It's not just about the mechanics and the graphics, its about the feel of the game, and every time I play this game I feel as if I'm bring thrown into another possible life that I could have lived, if only things went differently up until this point.
I seriously applaud the game developers for creating an innovate, incredible game that helps to capture such a serious subject in a beautiful way, instead of trivializing and exploiting it as almost all other first person shooters do.

A friend told me about this game, and I thought to myself... oh no not another fps game... what can they do differently that 100 other games haven't already done?
Well after trying it for a short 1 hr, I can say this game is a cut above the rest, already it demonstrates more common sense and playability than other fps's I have tried, and I just had to pop in and write something positive about this game and how (I would hope) it to go forward in the months and years to come.
I could start with the level design, realistic environments that really immerse you into the game, shadows of opposing players running through your screen makes your heart jump every single time, the terrain is almost flawless every detail is considered and implemented perfectly, and try to remember this is pre-release and they have done so much already, I cannot imagine how a finished level will look and feel to play in, but I do know it will be an awesome sight, and a terrible fright !! Each level design is made to have you gripped to your console, after playing a couple of levels I noticed a slight pain in my right arm, FROM GRIPPING THE MOUSE TOO HARD !!! These levels are intense, the design is breathtaking and although it's per-release I would still recommend you and a few friends playing multiplayer for a couple of hours and I bet 20,000 zorks you will be hooked.
Moving on to actual game play, it's about as real life as you can get (without getting shot ofc) in Pre-release we only have the smg, which is fine I would like to get a hand on a rifle or frag grenade but I'm sure it will come in good time, when it's ready and not before. Dealing with the smg is a lot different than every other fps I've seen (which isn't everyone, but a few)
So lets say you spot a shadow in the dark of night, and you pump a few rounds into it getting your first kill of the evening, you'll notice the guns aim doesn't reset to center, oh no it stays in the last place you fired it, until you aim somewhere else, I have to say I love this feature, it's about as close real as real gets, absolutely no easy aiming.
Everything must be done intentionally and with extreme malice, which will quickly sort out the pro's from the novices in no time. We have yet to see some kind of ranking system, to allow for the learning curb in this game, every at the moment gets mashed together and the best team wins. But I guess right now Zero Point Software is working on game play over ranking mechanics at the moment, but don't worry we already know this game is going to be amazing to play, casual, competitive or solo, so I don't think anyone cares about mechanics just yet. (but I'm sure it's on the list)
Stamina and exhaustion, keeping a good balance seems to be the key here, when your exhausted you can't really aim correctly or sprint... or jump very high, and recovery time can be an issue if you run into a building full of the enemy team, in the dark.... to afraid to turn on your flashlight in case you get spotted ! (would love to see some thermal imaging, though perhaps only heat signatures and not obstacles to allow some fairness also.)
So for right now I sprint for short bursts at a time, not allowing exhaustion to overcome me, (You don't really get feeling of moving fast when you sprint, perhaps some blurred edges and slightly increasing the speed of your sprint would help make it feel like your character is moving faster)
Weapons - SMG at the moment, and it acts and feels like a SMG should, good work on that, and I hope to see as much thought and detail in the rest of the weapons once they are released.
Solo content - Looking forward to it, and I hope it has as much diversity as ME3 when it comes to missions, non liner progression, pick-ups and power ups, and perhaps even a squad selection window even more immersion.
Overall it looks amazing, feels great, plays well and can still make your heart jump or skip a beat when it gets very intense, recommended to all players who love realism and high detail, and with upcoming releases and updates this game is going to be one game you just can't put down.

I got it because the premise seemed interesting, but wow was I caught off guard. The voice acting is stellar, the writing is fantastic, the story is well constructed and goes from light-hearted comedy to dark and tense moments effortlessly. One (optional) part of the game in particular has you watching a character's transition from comedy to relief to a sociopath because of what were noble intentions, and it's even saddening.
The characters are unique enough that I was invested in most all of them, although there is a tsundere type of character who's EXTREMELY cliche, to the point where it feels like parody.
Learning more about each character was a pleasure and I found myself jumping into the game without question, not even looking at the other games I bought around the same time frame.
The writing and story is strong enough that you'll blow through this game like you would a stellar show and when you complete it, you'll get that knot in your stomach like you do when you finish a book or show you were REALLY invested in.
When things escalate in the story, you feel as nervous and paranoid as the main protagonist. When banter is happening, you can't help but snicker at the insults the team throws at each other.
The game has a handy Codex mode that keeps descriptions of modern Japanese internet culture to explain and give context to some of the banter, and even documents real world historical internet / computer events referenced in dialogue, like Y2K and the John Titor posts.
The music is overall pretty good. One theme I found to be rather annoying, but when I watched the anime of this game immediately after beating it that same song popped up as a ringtone as a nod to the game, and I felt a wave of nostalgia. For a game I had JUST beaten. The main theme captures the idea of the game. Weird, sad, and scientific.
The main character is a Don Quixote type, but instead of believing himself to be a Knight of old, he considers himself to be a mad scientist bent on bringing the world to its knees. At first it comes off as strange, but it grows on you and the game uses it to portray his mental state. He often feigns the act when his friends notice that he's suddenly not spouting monologues to keep them thinking that he's okay, which was a little heart wrenching. And when you find out WHY he puts on an act at all, it pulls your heartstrings a bit.
You have a ditzy childhood friend, a nerdy, overweight hacker dude (who was a lot of the comedy relief surprisingly), a tsundere scientist, a girl who seems to know a lot and has been through tough times, a girl ...or guy? who works at a shrine, and a woman who communicates through text.
When things kick off, they REALLY kick off, and I found myself staying up extremely late to finish the story.
The twists are well done. Mostly unexpected.
There are six endings which are handily tracked by the game.
Man, this game makes you think and makes you feel. It starts off by shoving the Quixote persona down your throat and spouting science at you, but once you settle in you feel like you're part of a show.
And there is an anime based on this game!
I got more time out of this game than I did, say, I am Setsuna, and I even found all of the secret weapons in that, and I haven't even gotten all of the endings.
If you want a time kill and want to get invested, I highly recommend. There's nothing particularly engaging about the gameplay (most of it is done through the in game phone) as it is a visual novel, but it is a very good one. I can see myself revisiting just for the story.

I've beat this game only once on it's hardest difficult (you have the option between two different play throughs that have different effects on the game) and Compared to the similar bethesda game, DOOM (2016) it is not that difficult. Though the game throws a lot of enemies at you. Your job is to kill them all. The game is fun in the adrenaline pumping ultra violent way you'd expect from the ancestor of action shooters. The story is damn good and the characters, though they never do anything super note worthy, are perfectly written using the fewest words possible. The only gripe I have with the story I feel is that your main agenda seems to be misplaced. See you spend the entire game trying to kill one person, a general who helped create the tech that won the war for the nazis BUT your characters seem to want beat back the nazis and change the world back to pre-nazi rule. See the problem? Killing this general seems like nothing to major over the course of ending the nazi rule. So the whole time I feels like you're fighting the wrong people and the ending you feel like you didn't really accomplish the goal of fighting back the nazis which was the true goal from the start. Now as of 2017 the reason for this was that they wanted to gear up for a sequel but I feel that they shouldn't have made the over all goal to be fighting the nazis but instead make it about killing the general and getting revenge for what he did to you and your friends (and he did some♥♥♥♥♥♥alright)/ Gameplay is pretty good but some of the weapons feel very limited except in certain instances. You'll find yourself using mostly assault rifles almost exclusively due to how common their ammo is and some of their upgrades make them possible one of the most powerful weapons in the game. Ocassionally you'll use something with more damage on bosses or just really tanky enemies but other than those There feels like no reason for using most other weapons other than ammo. Not saying you don't use any of the other weapons, there are times but ammo forces you to use the assault rifles at least a solid 40% of the time which is a lot as the rest of the sixty percent is shared between like 4 other weapons not including pick up weapons. Over all though the great story writing and the fast paced action makes up for every down fall.

Unlike majority of RPGMaker games this one uses it's own graphics combined with parallax mapping to make really good looking maps and environment.
A well done side-view combat system. Not only can you attack, defend and use your skills but you can also unleash very powerful overdrive moves and limitbreaks.
There are supportive skills and skills that will give negative status effects to enemies such as blinding them. So you wont just spam your strongest skills every battle.
After each battle your performance will be ranked at the victory screen. The best rank you can get is 3 stars.You'll get 1 star for winning the battle, 1 star for winning the battle under certain amount of turns and 1 star is related to how much damage you take during the battle (there's a heart chain that will keep disappearing when you take damage, healing your characters recovers it. If you manage to win the battle without losing the heart chain you get the star).
If you don't get the 3 stars or if you think you could have done better there's an option during victory screen to restart the battle and try again.
There's a mini-map in the top left corner of the screen. It lets you see where chests and enemies are. Really useful and helps you navigate through levels.
You can craft various potions with the stuff you get by defeating enemies.
Something every RPG should have but most of them don't have.
While you can solve certain quests in multiple ways, different choices they wont have impact on the story. They will impact rewards though.
Considering the game is made in RPGMaker I'm sure this isn't surprise for anyone familiar with the limitations of the engine. Disclaimer: Wrote this review as part of a promotion where doing so entitled the reviewer to the Strategy Guide and 2 additional keys. With that said, this will not impact my opinion of the game.
Before I go into what I like/don't like about Epic Quest of the 4 Crystals, I'd like to preface by saying that I do not normally play RPGMaker games. The few RPGMaker games that have piqued my interest have generally put in that extra effort to look and feel unique. I am giving this game no special treatment because it is an RPGMaker game.
What I like about EQot4C:
- The game is visually appealing, with well made environments and nicely drawn character artwork.
- The battles are fast-paced and come with a 3-star rating system based on damage taken and turns taken to beat the enemies. This provides a fun challenge, and failing to meet the criteria for the battle allows you to Retry immediately, which is great.
- The music for this game is pleasing. The battle themes are energetic and intense, and the dungeon themes capture the environments well. It is also worth mentioning that a fine-tuned ear might catch homages to other games, such as Final Fantasy, Breath of Fire, and Ocarina of Time.
- There are a number of collectibles and treasures to be found, for the completionist. Luckily, there are icons on the minimap to indicate the treasures, which is a great boon.
What I don't like about EQot4C:
- The story (up to the point I've played so far, after a few dungeons) has been pretty weak. It is very generic, and heavily inspired by tropes from other games. I understand that the game is a parody of other popular JRPGs, but I don't see that as an excuse to shy away from making a deep and engaging story.
- The dialogue is pretty terrible, unless you're a fan of sex jokes and sarcasm. The characters have rarely had anything useful to contribute to the plot or their own backstories, usually amounting to fluff.
- The UI can be confusing. While graphically nice, there's a bit of a learning curve to understanding how to access the various elements of the UI. Equipment and Accessories are found under "Misc", for instance.
- The balance and the design of the game is a little haphazard, and you'll often find that you'll miss 3-star criteria because of an unlucky miss against the enemy, or the enemy scoring an unlucky crit against you. For instance, Stiletta's "Fury" Overlimit is notoriously bad due to its randomness, oftentimes doing 0 damage or healing the enemy, and doing rather pathetic damage when not. There's a boss battle at the end of the Water Dungeon that can either go very well, or very badly, reliant more heavily on luck than player choices. Equipment in the game is uninspired and boring, with hardly any reason to equip new pieces of gear that you're finding along the way.
- The game is badly optimized. This may be attributed more to this being an RPGMaker game than anything within the developer's power, but I'm playing on a machine that can easily run Shadow of Mordor on High/Ultra settings... I shouldn't be having jitters in my gameplay here. Also, if you hold the "A" button on the controller (old habit in trying to make characters dash), it causes the framerate to drop while doing so - while no one is forced to hold the button down, it's a little unusual to have that behavior.
Overall, the game looks and feels like a solid game, but ultimately boils down to an average experience. If you're generally a fan of RPGMaker games, then this will likely be a nice addition to your library. If you're not, you'll likely wish to give this one a pass.

Wolfenstein 3D was the game that jump started the first person shooter genre. Often mistaken as the first game to utilize the concept of a shooter game in first person perspective for gameplay as oppose to third person perspective. However the first first person shooter games were the 1974 "Maze War" & "Spasim". Anyways Wolfenstein 3D is the third game in the Wolfenstein franchise, the first two were the 1981 "Castle Wolfenstein" & the 1984 "Beyond Castle Wolfenstein". For this game it dropped the word "castle" and added "3-D" at the end. Making games in a 3-D perspective was still a primative attempt for game developers back then, something that is common to see in games today, but back then gamers were amazed to play through levels that felt like going through actual rooms. The plot is very basic, you assumed the role of an American Polish WW2 soldier named  William "B.J." Blazkowicz who must escape a castle conterted into a prison called Castle Wolfenstein that's heavily occupied by SS officiers. B.J. must kill various enemies in order to escape the castle alive. The release of this game has inspired various future first person shooter games and even provided inspiration for various war genre games. Wolfenstein is an important piece of gaming history that all gamers should experience. It's a fun and rewarding experience with various weapons and treasure to collect in various floors of Nazi occupied headquarters.

TLDR: Not P2W at all. Heed the warnings in the negative reviews but for god's sake the game's free, try it out for yourself and see if you enjoy it. Very customisable and if you have the patience you can make some great designs and have great games
In all seriousness, this game is in early access. There are going to be drastic changes to the game and presumably the majority of the vets had top tier stuff and that was all removed. Which is still far from fair in my opinion and freejam could have at least eased into that, or at least kept some of the progression system.
However, the progression system was never something i liked when i started the game. It was daunting and i couldn't really make any designs i wanted, and I have other vets who even agree with me. With all weapons and blocks available now I am free to create and have fun, so I do.
Honestly, the main reason why I play this game. It bring out the tiny desk engineer inside me to make designs, and improve them. Honestly, the customisation in this game is endless, you can make (in terms of movement):
- Jet bots
- Hover bots
- Heli bots
- Rover bots
- Tank bots
Each having their  own disadvantages and advantages and couplings with the weapons. on top of this you can customise these bots with any design you want (almost) due to the freedom and space they give you with the blocks. You can build your own designs from scratch, use shells or even share bots with the "workshop" in game. I enjoy making the odd themed bot from games like Halo.
On top of this, there are several different weapon types which each have their own playstyle, however unfortunately some weapon types are slightly unbalanced. I hope this will be fixed soon enough, but in the mean time the game is fairly balanced if you have a solid and mixed team.
There are 2 main game modes (which you can also play in custom games):
- Deathmatch
- Battle arena
Deathmatch is what you'd expect, alot of death. I don't really enjoy this gamemode as it is usually just filled with snipers. I generally just test the killing power of my bots in it
Battle arena however is really interesting, both casually and competetively. It consists of a typical capture-point type base (like tf2's for example) but expands upon it and makes it a hell of alot more interesting. It's made in a way so that no matter who's winning, the tide of the game can turn either way, with protonium cores catching you to the enemy time if you're far behind, or stealing energy if you've capped all the points. It's a constant tug of war and it creates a good change of pace compared to most other shooters of this type
This game uses it's own friend system independent from steam, which, while i dislike in most games, seems to work for the most part. However, this games excels at being one you can play with your friends. You can have full parties for quickplay and comp, and fully private custom games to test your mettle against your friends.
Ontop of that there's a clan system so if you find a good clan you can find players who enjoy the game as much as you do.
Unfortunately this game suffers from the odd connection issue and the ocassionaly impassable screen. This problem can be bigger for others but over time has become less of a problem and hopefully the devs are working on it. This game can be tempermental but patience is a virtue!!
Customisation: 8/10
Graphics: 7/10
Game modes and gameplay: 9/10
Would i recommend this? Definitely. Give it a shot and allow your creativity to run free!

I like the gameplay.... however, that game is full of unacceptable bugs right now.
The most annoying one is how the world terrain is loaded. It's not done in a separate thread but all in the same thread then the gameplay and display. Which means that when you are moving to the town the screen will always freeze because it's loading. It's not something acceptable in a game with a kind of open worldness to it these days. This needs to be seamless.
Sometime that loading even fails to detect it needs to load part of the terrain in time, so you'll come accross a white non loaded terrain. Usually, in games when this happens, there's something that makes sure you can't jump into it. But in this case there's nothing. So what happens is that you fall in the void dans the game crash.

A more appropriate name for this game would have been: 'CrackWorld'.
As you might have guessed, this game is very addictive and engaging. Most famously, based on the comments, is the fact that this game creates stories for your characters as you manage them. Everyone who plays will have a different story. Since most of the comments are focusing on player stories, I figured I'd write about the game itself instead.
What is this game? Think about The Sims combined with Stronghold, Banished, and Minecraft. Like Banished, you start off as a group (or one person) survivor dropped into a barren map where you have to start building farms, buildings, and products to survive. Winters are brutal and random events can occur which can throw your colony into chaos. Researching lets you build more advanced technology to help yourself survive.
Like in Minecraft, you're free to design your base however you want, mine for vital resources, and are given the ability to just go hog-wild with development mode ('creative mode' in minecraft) and turn it into a true sandbox experience.
Like in Stronghold, building defenses is very important depending on the difficulty. Depending on your 'Storyteller' (random event generator/Dungeon Master), raids against your base can be common and the threats can range from petty to disastrous depending on how well prepared your are. So, building your 'Castle' and its defenses is essential. Further, you'll need to have well-armed fighters ready. When raids arrive, you enlist your colonists for semi-direct control. This opens a whole tactical layer to explore.
And, finally, like The Sims, your colonists are their own people. They've got their own DnD-like stat sheet along with various traits that affect how they do things and how they interact with others. They'll build relationships with the other colonists over time. This can lead to friendship, marriage, or rivalries.  They all have moods and needs that have to be managed.
Unlike in The Sims, that really unhappy colonist might have a psychotic break, one-hit KO a fellow colonist and start lighting him and everything else on fire (happened to me). You're also able to capture prisoners and attempt to recruit them… or commit crimes against humanity (literally). This game gives you a pretty long leash to do things how you see fit.
TL;DR: If you like The Sims, Stronghold, Banished, Minecraft, or Prison Architect, you'll probably like this game.

‘’ I am the insane mad scientist, Hououin Kyouma!’’ This is one of the most common things you will hear in STEINS GATE. Steins is a game developed by MAGES. INC. and is essentially a visual novel. The game was released in 2009 but it just appeared in 2016 on Steam.  Before this VN, I have never heard of STEINS GATE before which made it quite a surprise to review it thanks to its nature and the fact it is a
sci -fi game.
From the very beginning, the game starts without any introduction. On the other hand, if you leave your game for about two minutes at the main menu, you will have a mesmerizing trailer that presents the main characters involved in the game. The trailer itself has amazing music, great imagery and gets you excited to play the VN.
One of the unique features STEINS GATE has is the cellphone. Through the game, the player will receive many messages from different people either informing him of specific details or random banter. During some of those moments, the player can click and reply back to the characters and usually get more details on his friends. The cellphone is also a catalyst later in-game which will weave the path leading you to different endings depending on some choices.
The main character of the game is Rintaro Okabe who likes to call himself ‘’Hououin Kyouma’’, the mad scientist. I personally disliked the protagonist for a big part of the game due to his eccentric act and his inability to be serious in many situations. There were times when ‘’oh my god’’ moments happen due to the oblivious state in which Okabe put himself. On the other hand, we find out later in the story why he acts that way and we start to care for him a lot more than before.
All the characters in this visual novel have unique personalities and secrets. Each of them holds a burden which explains why they act in a particular way which in turn makes you love them all. There were moments when I hated specific characters for actions they were performing which annoyed me greatly, but the story is so good that despite my dislike for some of their actions I still persevered. Some of those characters are Kurisu Makise, aka Christina, the genius girl that never believes in time travel, Mayuri the airhead girl that loves to sign tutturu every time she has the occasion, Itaru the expert hacker of the team that loves to talk about his passion for games and 2d wives as well as many others.
The story of the game revolves around time travel and spin out of control when the group manages to find secret information about SERN, a research company that attempts to take control over the world through time travel. STEINS GATE is one of the wackiest visual novel you will read in your life in terms of sheer detail. The game itself focuses partially on sci-fi fiction but also uses many scientific theories related to physics and neuroscience. The beginning is also extremely slow which will require determination from some players which are not as interested or hardcore in terms of sci-fi fiction. I personally was not one of those players but despite that, I loved the story created by MAGES. INC. They managed to create a unique universe and tell a beautiful and detailed fantasy. The game starts very light early on, has a couple of dark moments during some chapters while switching back to light feeling before going dark completely. At some point in the game, the main character was on the verge of losing his mind due to the inability to help his friends and always being stuck time traveling to the same moment.
In terms of bugs, I personally did experience an issue when the game got released. I personally kept having my screen bugging at the beginning every time Mayuri’s face displayed which made it impossible to continue further. Luckily, the developer offered a solution and after downloading a specific DirectX from 2009, I was able to play. No other bugs were encountered during my play through.
Overall, despite not being hardcore in terms of sci-fiction, STEINS GATE was one of the best VNs I have ever played. At its current price, I believe it is worth every dollar and it is a must have for anyone that loves visual novels as well as the sci-fiction fans. The game deserves a 10/10.

The gameplay is fun and extreamly fluid, I've been playing for the past 10 hours straight and this is my take on the game.
The Pros:
The Super Moves are great, some may need rebalancing but that can be fixed with a patch if the devs want.
The Saiyan transformations are diverse, you have 4 transformations for Super Saiyans; 2 for melee and 2 for blasts; however the max level for Super Saiyans is 2.
Character Creation, not as extensive as say a Skyrim character creator but it does the job and I love the options that it does have.
Races play differently, each race has its own special abilities and strengths as well as weaknesses making picking a race about playstyle as well as about desire.
Opponent Dialogue, it changes depending on which race you are.
The Cons:
Only Saiyans have transformations, even though I do play a Saiyan character myself it would have been cool to have transformations for other races besides Kaioken.
Lip Sync, a nitpick but the sync is off for some of the cutscenes obviously this is because its been dubbed in English instead of made for English so this isn't really an issue.
Subtitles, another nitpick but a lot of the subtitles aren't what the character actually says; the subtitles look like they were translated directly from japanese and not written and synced with who said what in English, this could easily be fixed with a patch but I just wanted to throw it out there.
Characters Missing, not really a big thing for me since I'm always playing as my custom but for some its a big deal so I'll throw it out there; some characters like Majiin Vegeta and Frieza Transformations 2 & 3 are missing.
Online Connectivity (March 4, 2015), to connect online is a HUGE pain in the butt; for me it just doesn't connect at all, I get stuck on the connecting screen; Play offline until they fix the online functions.
Some people hate the game for its repetative combat system but its combat is similar to other fighting games. On a 360 controller your X is light attacks, your Y is heavy and your B is blasts. You have a combo list for the button sequences and you have super moves and ultimates. It could be repetative if your just mashing one button but if you try to pull off combos then its not AS repetative; still is a little but not as much. But what fighting game doesn't have repetative controls?
All in all its a good game, its up there with Budokai 3 and Budokai Tenkaichi 3 for me. I'm not going to say which is my favorite because that will just spark the usual tireing debate. But the game is; for me; one of the best Dragon Ball games out there to date. If you love DBZ then you'll; if not; love you'll at least like this game. The controls are a little strange but simple once you get used to it. Certain things like what I listed in my cons list may throw you off but once you jump into the game then you will be having a blast.
If you get this game the I'll see you on the other side!
