The great-grandad of the FPS genre.
Yeah, it's alright. I didn't like it too much.
I know, I'm a horrid person, aren't I?
So far, I've only played a couple of id games, and unfortunately this is the first one I didn't really enjoy. DOOM was like a blast of cocaine, and Return to Castle Wolfenstein was like a slightly less better version than Half-Life that I still appreciated. But this? Well... it's just kind of nothing.
In Wolfenstein 3D, you follow a similar pattern of old-school gaming platforms that loosely tie a story together as you go and kill more and more enemies (which in this game's case is Nazis). So, most of the issues I have instantly fall towards gameplay. I will say this though, this game has NOT aged well, especially for its controls. I spent a while reconfiguring them for mouse input, but at that point, I could move around by moving the mouse. And the A and D made you look- not strafe- right and left, which was really irritating at certain points.
The levels are pretty simple- find the key, kill the Nazis- but their structure definitely isn't. These maze-like dungeous kept me stuck for nearly 20 minutes, just trying to find my way out of one corridor, because all the hallways in this game look the same. Yes, there are deviations of color, but in those specific areas, everything looks the same! It's incredibly easy to start losing your head as you run in constant circles around the same places again and again and again...
DOOM aged much easier, since it allowed actually understandable controls and gameplay that anyone could adapt to, with some relatively posh level design. Does that make Wolfenstein 3D a good foundation? Certainly. But does that make it a good game? Frankly no.

Epic Quest of the 4 Crystals is a turn-based RPG made by developer RosePortal games. Having completed some of their other games (Sweet Lily Dreams and Whisper of a Rose) I immediately noticed that this game does not occur on the same universe; the plot is much zanier, and the dialogue is filled with jokes and references to RPG clichés and other games. There is an option in the Options menu to censor the jokes should you find them inappropriate.
While the gameplay is similar to the developer's other games (the player wanders around beautifully-made towns and dungeons that make use of hand-made sprites and assets while listening to pleasant or sometimes downright epic music, talking to NPCs and fighting turn-based battles while advancing the plot), I have to say that this game is most technically polished of theirs to date. There is a handy minimap on the top left-corner of the screen, an option to turn off enemy encounters (a godsend when it comes to back-tracking) in the Options menu, and battles are more complex than in their other games, featuring an Overdrive bar that lets the characters perform special attacks when filled and a star system that rewards the player for ending battles effectively.
All in all, the game plays well and does not fail to entertain; while I personally liked the plot from their other games better, it is clear that the developers have given their best effort to polish the game and take player convenience into account.

Even though I only got to scratch the surface of this game so far, I must say that I’m really enjoying it. I honestly never thought I’d come to love an rpg maker game, but Rose Portal Games gave me a new experience and new outlook on these type of games. I must say that the game’s humor and jokes are definitely its strongest segment, but I will get to that later.
Detailed review followed bellow:
I’m not sure what to say about graphics. It’s the standard pixel, rpg maker graphics. However RosePortalGames made the best of it, so they game truly looks and feels beautiful. The sceneries are done amazingly. I love how the whole town has this colorful and cheerful look, and most of the houses are designed beautifully as well (like the pink house of one of the characters). But from what I’ve seen, the game will get a bit darker at some point, so if you are afraid the game will be all sugary and sweet all the time, don’t worry. The tone of the game changes according to the story progression.
The developers of the game also did a very good job on the artwork in this game, that is the character models (when they talk to you). I presume they are hand drawn and look beautiful.
I must say that I am loving the story so far. Like I mentioned above, this looks like a more cheerful game that focuses on the comedy effects. However this is not over the top, and not at all times during the game. As the story progresses things will get a bit darker and have a slightly more serious tone. I love that there are many different stories interviewing, and so many side quests to do. But most of all, and I do believe this is the strongest aspect of this game, at least it is what made me love it) is the dialogue. The lines said by characters are quirky, funny and filled with humor that even too explicit at times. The game is also filled with various references, for example Game of Thrones references, both through dialogue and the names of some characters (and me being a GoT fan, I especially enjoyed these jokes). Now, some might find this type of humor a bit over the top and might not like it, so if you don’t there is an option in game to turn off “jokes”. Do this especially if you are letting younger kids play this game as it has some strong adult language at times.
Now I must say even though I said I love the story, that I am not truly involved with the characters yet. It might be because they are not showing any particular traits and characteristics that might define them, and thus make them likeable or make the player care about them. Even the main character is a bit one-dimensional.
I hope the more I play the more complex the characters will get, and I will be able to change this segment of the review. I will let you know of my opinion later on.
I must admit that this is the first time I have played an rpg maker game (though I have played rpg games at times before). I was not really familiar with the combat system, but it was simple enough to learn, and wasn’t incredibly hard for me to defeat opponents at the start (I am sure the difficulty raises with progression into the game)
The inventory is also very simple to use. For example when using potions, it tells you how much health it restores, and how much health the character has, so you can double check whether you want to use it or not. I am yet to try the crafting system.
Now I must say that the game is truly vast with so much area to explore.  Now to me honestly, I was at times getting a nit annoyed by having to walk from one side of the town to the other doing quests, but I'm sure this is a part of many rpgs and a feature many people like. Who doesn’t like questing right? However, I’m still getting used to this kind of a thing. Though it is a bit more noticeable here as it is at time quite difficult to walk since the character can get stuck due to tight spaces (through forest for example) or blocked parts of the scene (where the town ends for example). So I suggest using mouse for walking and determining where to go instead of keyboard keys. I also noticed that even though the game has an fullscreen option it does not look good at all in fullscreen, but this might be due to the rpg maker engine used to create the game. I still hope it can be fixed in the future.
One more thing I must say I loved was what I consider a small bonus, collecting coins from time to time as you go about your way and exploring. I really like that.
This game probably has some of the most beautiful medieval music I’ve heard play in game. I found myself turning the volume up quite often. I could probably listen to it for hours.
All in all I am very intrigued and invested in this game right now and can’t wait to play more of it and see how the story progresses. I love it so far, especially all these quirky jokes and the art style and will keep on playing it.
This review will be updated as I play more or when I finish the game.

When I saw that this game was released on Steam, I was extremely excited, because I thought Borderlands was the PERFECT game that Telltale could do a series on. The harsh world of Pandora is one of the best worlds ever crafted in video game history, even rivaling
Rapture,
Kanto Region, and
from their respective games. After patiently waiting for episode 5 to come out so I can finally play this game, I finally gave it a run. After finishing it fairly quickly, I only have one word for this game:
Call me crazy like the psychos that inhabit Pandora, but this game might just be the best game of 2015 so far.* I knew this game would be good.
Sticking with Telltale's trademark comic graphics and mixing it with the identical Borderlands-style visuals makes environments look absolutely gorgeous. Compared to their other games, I think this one might just take the cake as the most visually appealing Telltale game so far. Not much else to say, but I did notice a few graphical issues, mainly with Fiona. However, these weren't too frequent.
Finally! THIS is what I should see in something like The Walking Dead. You switch between two characters named Rhys and Fiona, and each of them have a special attribute to them. Rhys has an ECHO eye, which can scan and hack various things around you. Fiona, on the other hand, has a special pistol that gets upgraded as time goes on, but I won't spoil those upgrades. There are less frustrating QTEs, a big pro in my books. I didn't see too many puzzles, but I'll let this one slide as TftB isn't the game for those. The items you get throughout your journey will actually affect you in the final episode, and TRUST me on that one. I need to save room for the next big part of the review, but trust me. This is Telltale gameplay done right.
The story is near flawless. People who followed my reviews know I'm a HUGE fan of the first The Walking Dead season. Well, this game just John Cena'd it to the ground and stomped on it. I know, that's saying something, because
was one of the most well crafted moments in video game storytelling. However, even with this game's fairly light-heartedness, this story is absolutely amazing. It had a few moments where I thought, "Heeey, how did they get here?" or, "I can't choose otherwise?" But that is all ignored by the extremely clever and hilarious writing that is miles better than the ones in the original games, plus the fact that the characters are ALL enjoyable in their own right. Of course, this game has its moments of sadness, and I won't spoil too much, but one major character from the whole series is killed off. When combined with the plot twists this game offers, you have an outstanding, nigh perfect plot. I should also mention that the finale is by FAR the best finale of all the Telltale games, even crushing TWD S1's finale. The choices can be absurd, difficult, random, but worthwhile, you can trust me on that. The ending to the game could've used a bit more context, but ended on a very interesting note as well. In the end, TftB's story is just flat out AWESOME.
Another high point to this game, the music choices are excellent. I won't get too in-depth, but I will say one thing: just LISTEN to the end credits song. You won't regret it. The voice actors are all excellent with their roles, my favorites of the bunch being Rhys, Gortys, and Vaughn. Again, not too much info here, but this is also very well done.
Compared to other Telltale games, this one is actually far more open and is much better for replayability. The finale, especially, will have you wanting to go back and play differently. Again, without spoiling too much, watch your money and decisions, as it will all be extremely important. I could see myself playing this a lot more often compared to the other games and still enjoy it as much as the first time I played it.
In the end, Tales from the Borderlands proves to be my favorite game of the year so far because of, well, everything. Even if Telltale has been doing some questionable and unlikable decisions lately, TftB was definitely not one of those. I HIGHLY recommend this game. And trust me, with how polished this game was, I will definitely remember that. Definitely buy it, whether you played any of the Borderlands games or not.

OK I keep seeing people saying this is pay to win. Thats just not true. If you play this game and you enjoy it, all you have to do is grind a little bit to make good parts, or just buy and sell and buy good parts. I havent spent a dime on this game and I have an extremely powerful rig, and I have a great time playing PVP.
Now that ive gotten that out of the way, I want to say this is a GOOD game. Its F2P which is usually a turn off for me but they work it out very well. Compared to other building combat games like robocraft or galactic junk league, Crossout is a lot more balanced and doesnt force you use sepcific weapons. All the weapons are very balanced. Even if youre just starting out you can buy a generator, load your rig up with basic machine guns and rip people apart. If youre skilled its not hard to go toe to toe with stronger players. This is because there are limits to what you can add to your rig. So if you use a ridiculously poweful weapon, its going to take up most of your power, and you will be limited. More powerful versions of any weapon cost more power. You might think youre a badass when you equip multiple powerful cannons to your rig...Until you run out of ammo and become useless in battle.
The physics are also better comparatively to other similar games, and with the cabin of your rig being the core, it adds a bit of strategy, and there is no healing which in my opinion is nice. So when you go up against someone with more powerful weapons you can aim for their weapons, destroy them, and they wont get them back until the next round, this way your opponents cant just run and hide and recover and come back to destroy you (like robocraft, ♥♥♥♥ that game).
My one problem with this game is when you get to a higher level and you start doing harder raids, there is almost always one incompetant player that ruins it for eveyone. This has lead to me giving up on daily missions and sticking stricly to pvp. The Borderlands universe allows for more variety in storytelling, tone, and fun mechanics than most of Telltale's cinematic adventures, but it still feels like a mismatch, pairing the fun, colorful, comic atmosphere with a game system fundamentally about making big choices and dealing with their consequences. The overpowering bleakness of Walking Dead and The Wolf Among Us really feel more at home in the Telltale model.
But while that mismatch means it can't really compare to the other Telltale adventures as a total package, it's still a fun enough little romp to be worth your time. It's especially cool how some choices radiate through the season to create some very unexpected outcomes all the way to the end.

Rimworld is a kind of game that can make you addicted to it, just like ya-yo does the colonists in the game.  But that's not enough to make you buy it, or is it?
It has simple mechanics that you will get used to it even in five minutes. But learning how to play the game takes a lot more than. You can simply play the tutorial first, then you can create a new game and start again. You can continue if you want, it's up to you. But my advice is starting again.
I said that it takes some time to learn the game, for me it was about 30-35 hours.During that time I tried to improve my colony, build some staff and discover the game. Then I realized that I need to start focusing on beating the game.
The game has 6 different difficulty levels, Intense is the one suggested by the developers. That's a hard one, you had better played like 30-40 hours before to play it.
I can finally talk about the game. The game has three scenarios but I will talk about the popular one, which is Crashlanded. You have three colonists, an optimal start for resources and there will be ship chunks that gives components you will need the most by deconstructing them. Be warry of fire, the biggest enemy of yours. At the start, you will have to construct everything from wood, but beware of it for later. Fire can be cringy for your first play. It can destroy everything in a few minutes that you tried so hard to get, but you will be able to save yourself from it by constructing fire foam later, but you will need to research it first. There are technologies that your colonists can learn by researching them. There are also works like hunting, growing, smithing, crafting, cooking, hunting etc. You can make them hunt every animal, and can eat all of them. You can even make your colonists eat humans but it makes colonists feel cannibal and that decreases their mood.  The point is build a ship and leave that rimworld with colonists by launching it. When you do that, you will beat the game. But there will be raiders, mad animals and even ancient mechanoids that will try to prevent you. But you won't be alone, there will be turrets and traps you will construct.
The game is not just this less, it is large enough to make me feel like I don't even know a thing.

It's not a bad game, it has some good aspects but I don't feel it captures the essence of the TV show it's based on.
The whole place is a ghost town, there's nobody around at all! I would have thought the towns would be populated to give the world some life. The invisible barriers are annoying and you'll randomly get caught up on things for no real reason. I've also had the game crash on me a few times - SAVE OFTEN.
The controls... they aren't great. Using the default bindings, my left hand (right hand on mouse) is having to move all over the keyboard to perform tasks like switching between shovel, hand, and torch.
I have the game installed on a SSD, I have 16GB RAM, a GTX 1080, and a i7 6700k. As I'm driving around it'll pause the whole game to load the next area - what is this, 2001? It's possible this will improve in the future, but right now it's quite annoying driving along and as you're rounding a corner, it pauses to load. Quite easy to lose control.
I want to like this game, I think I will if the bugs are worked out and more life is brought to the world. Right now, I cannot recommend it to anyone but the most diehard Gold Rush fans.

This game is packed with content; tons of missions, an Underwear Lottery, Online matchmaking, and a damned good story. The game does have some flaws though. For one thing, there is never anyone online, dispite this being a really fun feature. Shinovi Versus can be very repetative in it's missions, typically in the form of kill a ton of weak enemies then fight a character at the end. The game does try to mix things up by making the levels big and having the player travel through it for a while fighting a couple waves in each area, but they all become samey after a while. The in game store is kinda♥♥♥♥♥♥ there are tons of cool outfits, but you unlock them very infrequently but in mass ammounts. After each chapter the game dumps a handful of new items for you to buy, but with each chapter taking around half anhour to an hour each, getting that perfect look takes a long time.
The game does have a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of really cool things in it that counter it's flaws. To start, Shinovi Versus has really good graphics, they stand out in just how well done they are. you can play through a handful of missions as each character outside of the mian story to level them up and make beating the story mode a lot easier, this takes time, but is well worth it if you want to play every mission on hard mode. As with a lot of Anime games, the soundtrack is amazing. Shinovi Versus intro/menu theme is really good. You do have to use in-game money to buy the songs, a minor drawback,  but after pplayeing a ton of chapters, this isn't really tthat bad. The story itself is pretty good, it's a little slow and can be confusing if you play as a different school half way through another's story. After beating the game, (Or through cheats) you can unlock Homura's Crimson Squad as a playable School. It'll take a while to get that far, but it's a nice reward if you stick with it that long.
Overall, Shinovi Versus is a pretty good game. When compared to other Anime games, it certaintly is one of the best, as Senran Kagura games have always been. It's a title well worth getting at full price, and a staple for any Otaku's collection.

In it's current state, I DO NOT reccommend this game. However, based on what the devolpers have planned and how frequently the updates are coming along I think it will be a good game in the long run. Let's get to the Pro's and Con's of the game so far. {I PLAN TO UPDATE IT}
===PRO===
1. The game looks great and runs great, even on some of the lowest settings. The enviroment changes really do add to the combat experience.

Not gonna rant on how there's no melee or crouching yet in the game, because, once more, it's EARLY ALPHA!
In short, Interstellar Marines in it's current state isn't great, but hopefully in a few months it will be well worth the $15.

A pretty solid port concidering this port was done by one person. The game plays just as well as it did ont he vita minus a few differences. If you ever wanted to play Shinovi Verses and never had the chance to due to not owning a vita (tv), or if you just want to play the game in it's 60FPS glory, the steam version on Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus is the best version out there for you to play.

Interstellar Marines is hard for me to recommend in its current condition. While it's visually spectacular and deserves some slack for the fact that it's still not complete, it does not have any partically unique nor remarkable gameplay aspects. They've said it themselves: it is an overly ambitious, wannabe sci-fi experience that is trying to fit in with the quality of popular shooters such as Half-Life and Doom. The problem is, however, instead of offering any new or simple themes to the gameplay, this game clones the gameplay of your average online shooter. For an indie game to become successful (like Minecraft, Fez or Amnesia) it has to introduce new gameplay features that dramatically change the experience in its genre. Interstellar Marines tries to do this but only manages to create minor enhancements to the gameplay such as 'lifting up your helmet' or 'not being able to figure out who is and isn't your teammate after you've been shot too much'. One feature, however, that I really enjoyed on a few of the maps is the variation of brightness or conditions (such as weather and fog) on the maps. On some of the maps this can be quite annoying, but on others this really helps create a genuine atmosphere and truly immerses you in the gameplay.
The best I can say is that you're guaranteed some fun playing some of the brilliantly designed maps and immersing yourself in the impressive graphics and typical FPS mechanics. I'm also looking forward to seeing how they eventually execute the single player gameplay.
Unfortunately though, if this game is trying to rival other Sci-Fi shooters, it has a long way to go. Simple aspects that are essential for creating immersive and strategic gameplay such as crouching, meleeing or throwing grenades still haven't been added to the experience, and this must be included in the SOONEST UPDATE POSSIBLE. Furthermore, in the eventual finished product, I would expect to see some real, brand new ways to play the game that we've never seen before, especially considering the goals it is trying to achieve. IF YOU'RE TRYING TO MAKE THE BEST GAME POSSIBLE, DO SOMETHING ORIGINAL OTHERWISE THERE'S NO POINT.
Hopefully we'll eventually see this game in a much better quality than it is at the moment, but for now I simply can't recommend it to anyone until there's a large increase in overall content.

I'll start off by saying I've played this for a couple hours and I have played one of the previous DBZ fighting game installments for the playstation 3, which is Dragon Ball: Burst limit.
This is an okay game in terms of sheer content and story with vast diversity in terms of what you can do, it mostly pans out to act out in the same ways (fight against x & y or just x with one condition). It  does offers a new take on the old story and anyone who has seen the anime will find bits they know of and it is fun and interesting in that way.
However I feel it is lacking when it comes to the combat's gameplay and not even coming close to achieving the same epic feeling I would get when I was playing Burst limit on the playstation, the game play simply does not feel as responsive & intuitive as it was then. This is even more evident when playing the game for a little while as you'll notice you cannot use your kamehameha on an opponent you just struck down to the ground (you'll be lucky to get even one hit in without very careful timing to actually wait for the opponent to rise to their feet before any damage will be sustained) This ruins the immersitivity for me as I really want to pound cell with some good ol' DBZ tricks while he's out cold. Also the lock-on is incredibly static and does not allow for chaning of target inside a combo (I understand this from a gameplay perspective but there's no reason to not allow a simple camera change to a new target while continuing the aforementioned combo on the first target.)
I realize this is a bit of a minor thing but there are several issues like these that make this  a difficult game for me to play as it "just doesn't feel right" when I am playing it. Searching online for a room seems to take anywhere from 30-60 seconds to find a match to do "Parallel Quests" or simply co-op missions which gets tedious as you'll have to repeat that same process every time you try to join a room that seems to have a problem with being either full or seemingly connection issues (there's a msg that tells you 4 different causes but not which one actually was the problem)-
I cannot recommend this game as it is now mostly because of the combat mechanics in place at the moment, I simply do not feel this is a game worthy of 40$ as it still feels like it is in a very late beta stage.

I used to really enjoy this game, a bullet hell brawler with punishing difficulty but not too long ago I loaded up my lvl 150 pyro to find they've changed the game so much that I don't find it fun anymore.
It used to be that loot dropped and you would have to either wait until the end of the wave(s) to decide whether to equip it or do it during battle.  Instinct told you whether an item was better and you would quickly press A or B to decide.  Now you pick up equipment, it's placed into storage and have to go through a tedious process of deciding whether to equip or sell it.  In theory this would work well except that the loot screen doesn't tell you the full stats for the item, some attributes are missing rendering the whole thing moot.  Also money in the game only has use in the shop so selling items is pretty much pointless since you get enough of it during the waves.
The change to have an energy bar has destroyed your talents.  Instead of being on a cooldown timer they now have an energy cost and all draw from the same pool.  I can see that they are trying to go for "carefully pick which one to use at the right time" but in reality it means that you only try and use your strongest attack the other 3 are useless.  For a pyro this means you get 2 hydras and then have to wait ages to get another as the energy bar slowly refills.  Enemies will sometimes drop energy pills that refill the bar a little but there is so much flak on screen it's difficult to get to them.
You can still get insta-killed by acid spitters and other ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t one hits which is the reason why I stopped playing the game in the first place.
Everything seems to be a lot easier as well, even with limited hydras I can still trigger all waves and get through with no hassle.
The problem is that this seems to be change for the sake of it but it's still buggy and not well balanced.  There are still times when I wonder what killed me.  The relics still aren't explained.  Keys still drop far too infrequently.  Bosses are still way too easy (I haven't checked if you can still farm them by save scumming).  The energy system is a needless addition that prevents you from having "oh♥♥♥♥♥♥oh♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; moments that spamming buttons gets you out of, it has also made useless 3 of your talents. The new loot mechanics are buggy, needless and add little.  You still can't have local multiple player on multiple monitors (so you can push each other off the screen).  Potions are still a hit and miss affair.  You still get killed by the environment more than enemies and the core game I originally enjoyed has gone.
And wtf is a wormhole???  The game could explain these things a LOT better.

Perfect example is Tekken games on Playstation - Can choose characters, COM difficulty, Timer or no timer, Health depletes or not, Ki Depletes or not, COM positions - Guarding/ not guarding, COM move selection - melee attacks, super attacks, ultimate attacks or normal COM play. 1P vs 2 COM or 3 COM etc etc.

TL;DR - If you're up for a new take on the JRPG experience, give this a try.
Disclaimer: I was given a Steam key for this game so that I could try it ahead of time and write a review on the release date, but I did so because I support this developer, not for the promise of future keys.
This is a pretty good game, but it has its flaws.  Before getting into the gameplay, it took a little while just to get comfortable with the controls.  They're not complicated, and there was a (very) brief explanation at the beginning, but I was expecting to just start playing this like other JRPGs I've played, and that didn't work.  There are other things that confused me at the beginning as well, like how the coins that I was collecting weren't accumulating in my gold pouch (they turned out to be "points", not "gold"), and how I couldn't walk through shady parts of the grass (though I think this is fixed now).  This game is interesting in that it is both very similar to other JRPGs yet at the same time very different.
The combat includes features present in many other games, but has one defining feature that makes it play in a completely new way.  Each battle will award one to three stars for winning.  This is a game without random encounters, just enemies that you can see and choose to fight, so that means that there are a specific number of stars obtainable in the game.  Monsters can be refought for XP and gold, but stars are only awarded during the first battle.  One star is awarded just for winning the battle, one is for winning without taking too much damage, and one is for winning in a set number of turns.  These limits are set per battle, so boss battles are more gracious with the turns and lost health allowed.  With these restrictions in place, you are no longer just fighting a battle to win, but you are fighting a battle to win it quickly while taking few hits.  At first, this might sound like it would be really annoying, but luckily this feature comes with a second: you may restart a battle at any time without consequence, even a boss battle.  So if you're fighting and you miss and have to take an extra turn, or the enemy crits and does too much damage, you're not automatically out a star, you just have to restart the battle.  Restarting also helps for being able to try out new skills and test out new enemies/bosses.  This game changes combat from grinding to efficiency optimization.
As I said earlier, the controls take some getting used to.  I should point out that I've only tried using a keyboard (and a mouse a little bit) so far.  Everything works well enough, but it's not super intuitive.  For example, to equip weapons or accessories, you have to go to the Miscellaneous submenu.  To cancel or go back, you have to either press Escape, which isn't reachable without moving your hand, or right-click.  There is no diagonal movement, and if multiple directions are pressed at once, the vertical direction wins.  (This may be a problem with the engine itself.)  There are actually two main menus that are opened by two separate keys.  It all works, it's just not normal.
That's the thing about this game: it's not normal.  If you want a normal JRPG, look elsewhere.  This game has all of the features of a JRPG, but it's very light.  There are weapons, but you'll rarely actually have to make a choice as to which one to use.  There are optional sidequests; well, one or two, at least.  (I've only played through the first two stages so far.)  There is hidden treasure to find, though all treasure
are marked out on your minimap.  There is combat, but it doesn't feel very complex.  As I explained above, the complexity to the battles is a meta-complexity rather than mentally calculating numbers or massive item use.  This is a fun game, but you have to be willing to explore something new.
I've mostly talked about what's awkward so far, but now let's cover the simple stuff.  I like the art style, personally.  You can see for yourself from the screenshots what it's like.  This is a very light-hearted game, and the art styled matches that feeling well.  The music is pleasant, but nothing spectacular.  The broad storyline seems pretty commonplace, from the little I've seen, but the details to the storyline keep it interesting.  The humour is very enjoyable, though it probably wouldn't be for everyone.  There is an option in the settings to eliminate suggestive humour, but that seems to be about all there is.  ;)  The main character is pretty mundane, as most main characters tend to be, but the other party characters are all pretty creative and interesting.
I'm glad I started playing this and will continue to the end.  In an age where so many video games are made to fit a mold, it is refreshing to watch this developer try out new things - some that work in really cool ways, and some that should probably be scrapped.  What I love about how this developer implements ideas is that he always keeps things easy for the user.  If you want to explore a new take on JRPGs, give this game a try.

In a nutshell, this was an utterly fantastic experience.

The Silent Age is an atmospheric and stylish narrative driven point and click adventure.
No spoilers.
TL;DR at the bottom.
The main mechanic, (being time travel) is executed well and fits into the plot neatly - it was refreshing to experience a piece of fiction that looks at the actual practicalities of time travel rather than just leaving it up to your usual Sci-Fi type reasoning as to why and how it was created/introduced.
The art style is fantastic - a great take on retro 60s/70s illustration type graphics. The script, as well as the voice acting were for the most part top notch and there are some great moments of subtle humour to relieve the tension and atmosphere of dread that the game does such a good job of driving through to the player. Excellent soundtrack - woud love it if it was possible for us to buy/listen to outside of the game.
In terms of story, I thought the pacing was well defined early on - there was never a moment in the game that I felt dragged on a little too long. The ending was satisfying and comes to a good climax, with just enough ambiguity to keep the player thinking long after completing The Silent Age.
It took me about 2.5/3 hours to finish The Silent Age - which is probably my only slight gripe with this title. There isn't really much in terms of replayability here, and whilst I'm pretty sure that it would be a great title to come back and replay in a few years - it is up to you whether you can justify the price tag for 2.5 hours of gameplay. (Excellent gameplay, for what it is worth.)

I like this game, but it has issues
Pros:
- Setting: Think Mad Max meets Twisted Metal
- Graphics: Uses realistic graphics rather than Minecraft pixels
- Low Queue Times: I rarely waited more than 10 seconds for a match
- Being able to customize your car like a Lego-set is awesome
Cons:
- The game is far less about skill and strategy, and more about your character progression and/or how much money you've spent to unlock parts and weapons early.
- The ONLY alternative to spending money is grinding, and after a few levels you don't play against bots anymore, and you'll get crushed, which is frustrating because YOU HAVE TO WIN THE MATCH TO GET THE LOOT YOU'RE GRINDING FOR.
- The result of this system is that you'll lose far more games than you win, and there is nothing you can do to stop the vicious cycle other than spend real money so you have a chance to enjoy the game
- Vehicle customization has very little impact. Creativity isn't rewarded. Your vehicle might look unique, but it will play about the same as it would have if you didn't bother with anything fancy.
Advice for the developers to improve the game:
- Allow players to play against bots to grind loot. Playing against high-level players and losing over and over again sucks.
- More weapon types: If you're going to copy Twisted Metal, copy the variety of weapons. Every vehicle in Twisted Metal had personality, while all the weapons in Crossout are basically the same.
- Reward creativity: Add options like wings, springs, or things like that for players to make crazy cars and reward them for doing so.
- Cut out the P2W model: When people realize they have to pay you money to get anywhere they are just going to quit and play something else. Your greed WILL kill this game.

Also the talings won't play big role as currently t2 refineries don't produced them at all and t3 tailings are not building fast enough to be a real issue. With T3 refineries low framerate is problem for many.
If you love machines and remain happy just with getting to move dirt around (which will be fun for a while), you will probably like this game even at this stage. If you love fully finished experience, would consider waiting few months and seeing how things are then. Currently there are still alot of bugs which may get to your nerves after initial shine of the game wears off.
----------------------
The biggest downsides of this game are the ones listed below;
- There are still loads of bugs and unreleased/unfinished things.
- Gameplay around mining itself is really shallow and some features like current worker system is plain joke as a feature.
- Some paydirt related things are still somewhat buggy or unbalanced.
- Also moving or pushing paydirt may change it's gold content (some gold gets wiped).
- There is no (and there will not be) multiplayer mode.
- Tailings don't play big enough role in the game.
- Roadmap to next stage of the game is there, but wouldn't count that it sticks.
- No open alpha/beta program;  patches tend to generate new bugs or balance issues frequently.
- Entire community is forced to play product in alpha/beta stage.
- Developers are clearly not very experienced.
- Devs are planning to release DLC on the current state of the base game?
Dim lights in the end of the tunnel;
- Developers are releasing SOMETHING.
- There are some communications and announcements in the forums. (However forum moderators are what they are and overall planning/communications in this game get rating of 1/10 from me) .
- The game has lots of potential if done right (in long term).
- Discovery is backing the game (one of the reason why it was pushed out too early also).
----------------------
In current (unfinished) state I will give this game 5/10. This game has potential to become 10/10, but to archieve that - following stuff has to happen:
- Most currently reported bugs get fixed, paydirt starts to feel consistant no matter how you move it and gameworld gets smoother loading transitions  and optimization = +1 point
- All currently pending features get finished = +1 point
- Tailings start to play bigger role in game = +1 point
- Additional content around the actual mining and refining gets to be more meaningful = +1 point
- Multiplayer = +1 point (will not happen as devs have clearly stated).
Multiplayer is buggy and the game got boring quick. It'll be one of those games you buy and play for a day, maybe a week, then never again.

For anyone coming from Borderlands 2 wanting to see where it all started here are a few pros and cons in comparison with BL2:
Pros:
- Much better loot system. Anyone who has clocked in enough time in Borderlands 2 will know that finding anything better than Green is fairly uncommon, but in this you will be find 10 times better and more varied loot and twice as often.
- Fairer Scaling. The scaling in this game is Linear instead of Borderlands 2's Exponential, meaning that when you find a powerful weapon, it will be useful for much longer before having to replace it with a more powerful weapon.
- Easier to run. Granted this is just due to it being older but even still, it's something I guess.
- Cheaper. Again this is just due to it's age, but still, the GOTY is cheaper than the bsae game of Borderlands 2.
- Backstory to Borderlands 2.
- Able to play as Brick, Roland, Lilith and Mordecai. Awesome NPCs, Awesomer Playable characters.
-
Personal Opinion:
- Different feel. This game has a more dark and serious feel than the second Borderlands game. Some people may like it, some may not.
- All the Areas have the same look to them. Every area is either a desert-like area, run-down buildings or Atlas buildings, with the Zombie DLC and the final area being the only exceptions. Again this can be a matter of opinion.
Cons:
- Skill Trees. The characters skill trees aren't as fleshed out as in Borderlands 2, with the major gamechanger 1 point skills not being there. While i'm not in any way saying the skill trees are bad, they're just lacking something that Borderlands 2 has.
- Voice acting. The voice acting in this game can feel very hit or miss at times, with some characters sounding cool, while others feel very flat and last-minute.
- Animations. Same as above, some animations are good, while others feel robotic and basic.
Overall
Worth getting if you want to see where it all started, although as a first purchase in the Borderlands franchise, it's better going with number 2. Get if on sale and definitely get the GOTY.

This is one of those rare shooters that defies all expectations when approached with an open mind. Having grown up playing the "old-school" Wolf games on my brother's PC it was extremely refreshing to see some of the game tropes of yester-year (Armor, Picking Up Ammo, etc.) being imbibed with The New Order's (TNO) play style. To anyone on the fence with this game, PLEASE, take the 12 to 14 hours necessary to play this game through to completion and be prepared to enjoy yourself! Recommendation: Play on Uber difficulty and take your time with the fire fights, they are very visceral and this difficulty level, while intimidating, is not that difficult in the long run. Save for a few exceptions in the late game where difficulty spikes can occur there is nothing you will not be able to usurp eventually via brute force and sheer ingenuity!
This game is a breath of fresh air and I cannot wait to dive into The New Colossus this holiday season!

It's like Mario kart, but more or less everything is done really well... which is exactly unlike Mario Kart.
There's no idiotic bias for weapons based on your position, and it is a largely skill based ordeal.
The AI can be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥on harder difficulties, so if you get upset easily, but want to be a completionist (or at least unlock everything)  you might want to be wary. For 20€ it's more or less a steal, and anything below that it's a no brainer, which is something i don't say lightly.
It also isn't just simply racing. There's some twists thrown in at times in the fashion of challenge maps of drifting, flying and time attack (solo) variety.
The only gripe i have with the game is mild randomness in jumping physics in certain maps, especially in boats. If you just get bad waves off something, you can't consistently do flips/drifting to keep up your speed, which probably lost me a couple of races, but it's a small thing to moan about.

I was looking forward to this, based on generally glowing reviews, but any anticipation was wasted, as I found out immediately when I had to exit the game all the way through the deeply nested console menus just to find out which button was "accelerate".
The closest this game has to an explanation for anything is the loading screen hints which advise the player which console buttons they should press in order to play the game. Even the config doesn't give any indication of how these buttons relate to the buttons which you might have on your keyboard - this level of buffoonery is as inadequate for a PC game this year as it would have been twenty years ago, when SEGA was making games that were at least adequate for console.
The fact that nothing from game modes to mechanics to items or abilities is explained at all makes the game a gruelling campaign of trial and error and strongly detracts from the pacing that a game in this genre should deliver.
A lot of the characters are bland and explicitly made up for the game, loosely based on other SEGA IPs. There are a lot of big names missing and lo and behold, Ryo Hazuki joins the cast as DLC! Unfortunately, SEGA leads the industry in this kind of pitiful customer disservice.
The little difference that there is between characters can be anulled with kart stat modifiers won through the campaign.
I mentioned the ridiculous console menu, but I'll bring it up again to point out that it's slightly buggy, with yes/no buttons sometimes getting confused among themselves and sending you up and down through the tower of menus or entering you in a race when you were hoping to quit the game.
These gripes aside, the races are responsive and not too floaty. The music isn't SEGA's best but it's not bad either. The voice acting is extremely annoying, but it pales before certain other Sonic games. The maps are mediocrely designed. The items manage to be both unintuitive and unimaginative at the same time, but at least they aren't heavily skewed toward catch up mechanics.
I can see why people are sick to death of where Mario Kart is going and relieved for anything but that, but to anyone who remembers the classic Mario Kart games from SNES to N64 and GCN, it's abundantly clear that this is at best a B game, following the legacy of Diddy Kong Racing, but lacking some of the polish and imagination of that cult classic.
I can't recommend this. I hope SEGA wakes up to themselves one day and cleans up their act.

Finally! A Dragon Ball game for PC and a good one too! But is it as good as Budokai Tenkaichi 3 and Raging Blast 2? What is all this MMO stuff? And is it a proper PC Port? There are many things the first and only Dragon Ball game on PC has to do right to please the fans. For fans of the show the purchase is definitly an easy decision to make, but for people who dont know anything about Dragon Ball I recommend waiting for a sale.
First you start with creating a character. The character creator is not the most complex creator, but it gives enough options to make it feel not unnecessary. Still, your own character is what makes this game motivating to play, at least its singleplayer, because of the rewarding progression system. Boost attributes, equip new costumes, learn new KI Blast, Super Attacks and Ultime Attacks. You can buy stuff at traders, but you can get them earlier by doing side quests where you get them as rare drops (the good Skills like Super Saiyan for example). Also progressing through the main story will unlock new characters, some of them can be your masters and teach you their skills, for example Vegeta teaches you his Gallick Gun skill and so on. Choosing a master is cool and all, but I dont know if its just me, but it takes forever until my master has a new training session for me, which is a little frustrating, but I guess it makes sense cause youll get their most powerful abilities at the end.
But all of that doesnt matter if the combat system doesnt work, so lets talk about that. Budokai Tenkaichi already had a fantastic combat system and Raging Blast 2 did it even better in my opinion. Xenoverse´s combat system is like those 2 games, however it feels a little simpler, BUT maybe it just feels that way because until now I only played against AI. Cant test multiplayer because servers are♥♥♥♥♥♥currently and I have no one to play local with (in 1 week I will have someone).
I like the new control scheme (well I changed it to Type C, then it was fine to me). I like that you have 2 Ultimates now and 1 Evasive skill and I like that you have a seperate Stamina bar. There are a lot of small changes like that which make sense, but there are some small things which feel like they are the way they are only because the game has 2v2 and 3v3. Like some things are balanced a way that 2v2 and 3v3 dont get too crazy, but that makes 1v1 a little bit more dull, just a little bit though.
They changed the "Sprint"-Attacks or whatever they were called in previous games. Now when you do one of those skills you dont get a cutscenes, but the fight just goes on and your character does the move, and I like that. In previous games those cutscenes mid-fight were annoying and made the fights less dynamic and other players now dont have to wait for you cutscene (I guess this is another change due to 2v2 and 3v3).
Overall I dont want to give my final judgement for the combat system yet, since I still have to play vs real players, but so far I like it but sometimes its A LITTLE dull.
The character creator is fine as I explained, but it is at the cost of DBZ lore. You can make pink namekians, but afaik there are only green namekians, also you have male and female Buu which doesnt make sense, since Buu was a demon without a gender or anything like that and having so many powerful characters in the world makes the main series characters less important which is not something I like that much. Thankfully they still have their special moments in the story mode and side quests, and in boss fights against Cell or Frieza or even Goku in Super Saiyan form they still feel really powerful because your hits do not stun them.
What I like the most about Xenoverse´s  story is that the devs knew they need a story like this to make a good game for Dragon Ball, because with this story you first of all can re-experience the main DBZ show, but with a new twist (which is your own character) and at the same time you can fight in many different scenarios, for example fight along side Frieza against Goku or something like that.
The story itself though is surprisingly good, its not really well written, the voice actors are terrible, and the 2 new villains are boring and uninteresting, but its fun and interesting to follow. At least the cutscenes are well made. Its motivating and gives your fights some context, especially because every character has some sentences mid-fight depending on team-mates and enemies.
And there are some really cool moments, my favorite was when SPOILER ALERT Ginyu changed his Body with you instead of Goku. SPOILER END
I only wish there were more anime scenes.

Squad is a FPS Mil-Sim which heavily focuses on communication, tactics and teamplay. As a military shooter it has large maps that goes from desert, to cities to forest with different game modes with two teams battling against eachother. Since Squad is more of a simulator than an arcade shooter, it is a bit more harder on damage, recoil, aim-down-sights, stamina and spawn times and locations.
You will join a team then join a squad and then pick one of several roles in that squad. Each team starts with an amount of tickets and in Conquest mode (there are several modes) the team who reaches 0 tickets loses.
So here is the thing, if you don't plan on using your mic then don't play Squad. Even if it is possible to neglect voice communication, you will miss out on a big part of the game that comes from working together, communicating and relaying information. Also if you don't enjoy talking to other people or listen to instructions you won't enjoy Squad or get along with people who do.
As I mentioned each team has squads in it. It is players who create them and the creator is the Squad Leader. This role is the backbone of this game and is therefore increadibly important. Squad Leaders coordinates with the others SL's in the team and plan overall strategies and provide orders during the match to the squad. They also place different things to build on the map that other members construct as well as placing a limited spawn location (rally point). They can also put markers on the map, for example where enemies are, based on the information you give them.
Players make or break a match.
As a FPS competitive player I really enjoy Squad. Gunplay feels good overall, it takes 1-3 hits for a kill depending on where you hit. As long as the squad communicate and your Squad Leader does the job, you are in for a game that feels rewarding when you put effort into it.
Squad is still in Alpha at the time of writing but has periodic updates and fixes. Although it has been for a few years now.
So what downsides do I experience with this game?
You won't benefit from playing on higher settings in this game. A high resolution is good with max draw distance but you want to have low on everything else. Otherwise you will see grass and bushes when the enemy who has low settings only see you and a default ground texture. You want to see as much as possible. Also your fps may not be very high anyway unless you have a high-end PC but it is getting better.
Not everyone wants to lead or knows how to do it well. That is just how it is. Although you will find that people will create squads only to leave them so that people will join in and someone else gets to lead. You will get good SL's and you will get bad ones. It is up to everyone to make things work but if no one leads the game is basically over.
Vehicles aren't broken but they are indeed buggy. They will get stuck or they will flip or they won't reload at times. At the same time, when used properly they win you games.
I personally feel that the core game has a good foundation to stand on and it is fun to play. When communication and teamwork is on point it feels really rewarding the work you do. Now we just need more and bigger updates in performance and content. Seems like we are getting it slowly but surely.
If you want to play casually you can. If you want to be competitive you can. It is all about teamwork.

Your only focus is to complete a track as fast as possible... or in some cases just simply complete the track (believe me when I say this is NOT an easy thing to do all the time, particularly in the player created tracks).
The premium "Forever Star Edition" version takes that free base content and then multiplies it tenfold, adding new racing vehicles with their own unique handling / track types / speed, and further expands upon the track creator also available in the free version.
It's a free game, with a completely optional full version available on the side, and a track editor, what's not to recommend? Give it a shot.

Pros:
- Interesting, captivating story with surprising twists and turns and intelligent, funny dialogue.
- Beautiful graphics, and beautiful music and spoken dialogue.
- Pretty straight-forward point-and-click interface with some minor issues (see below).
Cons:
- Most of the dialogue isn't spoken, so you have to read it, which isn't really a problem for me, but in this game:
- The location of the text dialogue on top of the screen feels a bit weird and out of place. Bottom or centered would have made much more sense IMVAO.
- 10€ is quite expensive for such a short game. I'm an adventure game enthusiast and try to combine everything with everything, and I finished the game in about 6 hours (6.5 including the 4 achievements I missed the first time). I bought this on a 75% sale and it is definitely worth that much!
- Minor issue: There's a weird delay regarding dialogue that sometimes confused me. When trying to skip a line i was sometimes unsure if it had worked and whether the next line belonged to the skipped action or my next action. Not really a problem though, except when coupled with the next point.
- Minor issue: It is possible to accidently skip some (more or less) important "scene entry" dialogue lines by acting too fast. This happened to me a couple of times, and I found it quite annoying. A scene starts, nothing happens for a few seconds, so I try to play by interacting with something. While my character moves to that location, the delayed scripted dialogue of the scene starts and is immediately skipped when my character reaches the location he is interacting with. Meh.
- Minor issue: There is no introduction into the finer points of the interface. For example, there is quick running (double LMB?) which sometimes works and sometimes doesn't. I don't know why.
- Minor issue: There is no drag-and-drop, only "click an item, release LMB, point to location, click again". A bit counter-intuitive after 1995.

Actual review:
STEINS;GATE is, in my opinion, the single greatest visual novel in existance. The story and writing are both outstanding, the art is beautiful, and the music is absolutely glorious. In the game, you make choices via the phone trigger system, in which you get an email or call from one of the characters and you have to chose what to reply with, if to reply at all, and whether or not to answer a call. This system made the game feel really immersive and added a lot to the overall experiance. STEINS;GATE has one of the best stories I've ever come across in my life. It's very funny in some parts, but makes me cry my eyes out in others. The game did something that not many others can do. It made me care about the characters. Whenever something bad happened to one of them, it made me feel like it happened to a real person that I knew. I'm not going to spoil anything, but there were many parts that I felt that I had to keep playing the game or it would be disrespectful to one of the characters somehow. This game gave me the feels on so many levels and so many times. It's probably more feels than most people feel in a lifetime. The art in the game is absolutely beautiful and fits perfectly with the games story and atmosphere. If the art style were any different, the game would be nowhere as good as it is. The music, openings, endings, and background music alike, was some of the greatest music I've ever heard. The opening for the game sets the tone of mystery and suffering for the rest of the game and fits perfectly with the game as a whole. The music for all of the endings besides the main one was also amazing. It inspired a feeling of sadness yet hope. The music for the main ending was simply outstanding. It tied the whole thing together and sprinkled some feels on top. The background music always fit with the mood of what was currently happening in the game, making it much more immersive and dramatic. It changed just at the right times, and never felt awkward. It always added to whatever was happening, instead of taking away from it. Overall, STEINS;GATE was an amazing game to play and I will play it again soon.

I went into Epic Quest of the 4 Crystals not really knowing much about it besides it being an RPG and supposedly funny. I left Epic Quest of the 4 Crystals 3 hours later not knowing much more. You might say 3 hours is not a lot to judge whether an RPG is good or not. And to you I’ll say, if you can’t get past the 3 hours, then it’s at the very least certainly not for you.
This was my experience with Epic Quest of the 4 Crystals. I have nothing against parodies and comedy and even some sex and/or explicit jokes, but I found the whole thing on this game to be too over the top. It’s a pity, because I really went in expecting to like it, but I ended up not enjoying my play through so much.
So let me get to the point with this one.
The Good:
Although it’s an RPG Maker style game, the sprites seem to be hand made, the fact that they’re not the usual super chibi size helps make it a bit different. The art is not stock, and while it’s not a masterpiece, it’s not awful either. You can tell effort was put in this.
The music is beautiful, it does get a little repetitive from time to time, but it’s certainly one of the strong points of the game.
What little I got to see of the crafting system seems interesting. The battle allows you to ‘retry’ it if you want to get a better ranking. The system used for traversing maps is different from most RPGs. I also liked the option to ditch one of the first quests you get, that bit -was- funny.
The story (if you don’t look at the villains) seems sorta decent in a parody kind of sense. At least as far as I played through, it’s a typical boy-becomes-hero and then has to fetch items to defeat evil. I don’t know if it changes later on.
The Bad:
The jokes were over the top and not funny at all. Even the ones that weren’t over the top were not really funny (and no, I don’t care that we have an option to censor jokes, if you have to censor your game to make it “good” then maybe those jokes weren’t needed to begin with). The references to pop culture were also not overly interesting. Some of the maps seemed a bit labyrinthic.
I found myself annoyed at not being able to walk through certain plants that I should have been able to and instead having to go all the way around, when there really was no reason for it. Call it a pet peeve if you will.
There weren’t too many chances to interact with the environment; my favorite thing about RPG maker games is being able to walk up to a random item in a house and getting interesting story bits or comments when interacting. There was hardly any of that here
The Villains. Enough said.
All in all, for an rpg maker type of game it’s not really the worse you could get, but it just wasn’t a type of humor that resonated with me. Even if I didn’t overall hate the game,  and I might give it another chance at a later date, I can’t say I enjoyed it at all, either.
Recommended: Not unless you really love RPG Maker games and in-your-face type of jokes. I think you will only find the game good if you can get past the jokes and the not so good dialogue.

Senran Kagura as a franchise is about the fanservice first. But there are plenty more layers to it and so much to enjoy.
If you are looking for a game full of actually strong female protagonists, each with their own dreams and motivations, then you really should give Shinovi Versus a try.

So just pick it up and allow yourself to be pleasantly surprised by just how much a "fanservice" game can offer.

Two years ago, RosePortal Games first released the game
. Now, the game is available on Steam advertised as a new-and-improved version. With two years to work on it, it makes you wonder how much work they spent improving the game.
The game is advertised as one in the style of 16-bit RPGs like
and
, and the graphics show it. Areas like a mushroom valley show both creativity in the art design and the level of detail in them. This level of detail doesn't just stop at the backgrounds. The monsters, especially the bosses, as well as the magic spells show that a lot of care went into the look of the game.
While the graphics are very good, the story is another matter entirely. That part makes the game feel as if a bunch of teenagers designed it. In many cases, the focus is on sex. With scenes where the villain wants to collect people's testicles and questioning the gender of a dwarf, it feels like it wanted to imitate the
style, but without success. Add to it the constant fourth-wall references makes it sound as if the game acknowledges that the story is one big joke.
Exploration is what you would expect for an RPG. You got your standard forests, caves, swamps, mountains, and so on. What make the areas feel odd is that they sectioned off each one as a platformer game would do. Once you complete one area, you go to a menu screen to pick the next area or return to a previous one. In other genres, this would make sense. However, RPGs are supposed to be one continuous world. Additionally, except for the starting town, it does not feel like there are any real places to visit except for more fighting. This makes exploring feels like it is an alien planet without any civilization. Without some safe place to visit or anything logical to connect them, the exploration feels lifeless.
As for combat, the game does not offer many differences from most RPGs. Battles occur with traditional weapons, spells, and the occasional special move. The one thing about it that really stands out is the retry feature. After a battle, it will rank the outcome and rewards accordingly. If the player did not get the best rating, it will offer the option to retry the battle. Doing so will put them back in at pre-battle conditions with all stats and items restored. This makes that many will use this as a crutch in order to get that perfect battle with minimal cost. Offering it if all characters die is one thing. However, by making it a standard option, it encourages people on breaking the system.
The one bright spot about the gameplay is the crafting system. As your inventory grows, instead of leaving the items as is, the player can combine them to have new effects. A couple of examples an ether that increases your magic stats and a potion that gives immunity to blindness. This is an interesting concept, but it is underdeveloped. Since this only works with items and not equipment, it feels more like an afterthought. It just makes you wonder why more ideas like it weren't used throughout the rest of the game.
As much as I wanted it to like the game, I just cannot recommend this for others to play. This is supposed to be an improved version of the original game. While it might be improved, it is not enough to justify playing. If you want a good 16-bit RPG, get the recently re-released
instead.
Note:  This game was provided by the developer with compensation for beta testing and review.

I don't like fanservice. I don't like beat-em-ups. And yet I absolutely freakin' love this fanservice-filled beat-em-up, as my many friends whom I have not shut up about this around can attest to.
I was among the many that was turned off by the sexual themes in this, but the thing that isn't really clear until you start actually playing is that it is very much not played straight. It's extremely over-the-top for humor's sake, and if you go into it expecting that, it's an extremely enjoyable experience that goes above and beyond the element most pushed in marketing. (Don't get me wrong, it's still omnipresent; there's just a lot more to it than that.)
The story has more mood whiplash than... well, I suppose "emotional roller coaster" is the term here, but it's more like "emotional crazy bus driver going the wrong way on the interstate". It wildly, violently swings between slice-of-life comedy (the tone it sticks with the most throughout the game), badass life-or-death battles, heartwrenching backstories, and horrific fatalities. The last bit, as well as the most disturbing part of the Senran Kagura titles on 3DS, is kept purely to text and never actually shown onscreen. There's four stories to play through, serving a classic beat-em-up format of "go here, fight enemies, go here, boss battle". The boss battles are the real core of the gameplay, as you're fighting other playable characters, and you can also take the game online to battle more if you exhaust these. In the main story modes, as well as the 22 side stories (one per playable character), the boss battles end up being an accidental cakewalk if you simply save all of your powers for one enormous limit break at the end, turning it into a total curbstomp. This doesn't make it without challenge, though. I can safely put it next to Skyrim in the "I was doing so good and then there were bears" category.
The art design and the soundtrack are fantastic, and the characters are... well, let's just say after a few other series like this, I didn't have much faith in games like these to have the characters be much more than aimless fetish fuel based on tired archetypes. I was extremely wrong in this case. I've come to love pretty much the entire cast, and every single School's story left me with a new favorite character or two. I only actively dislike two of the 22 playable characters, and they're still fun to play as, even. They're well-written, well-designed, and well-translated. The main stories contradicting each other did irk me a bit, but if you know ahead of time that they all go in different directions with the same basic concept, I don't think it'll be as irksome.
This is not a perfect port. You can tell they genuinely put in a lot of love and effort, and it shows; you're saving an absolute ton over the Playstation versions just by virtue of having the DLC built-in here, for one! However, I have suffered from some really terrible texture issues in story cutscenes (and only in story cutscenes; the graphics for any bared skin were replaced with random glitched visuals from the Steam overlay, which never occurs in actual gameplay), and two crashes in 24 hours of play total. The levels are short enough that this isn't a big loss of progress (some battles can, with a lucky combination of abilities, take only
), but the looming concern that it may crash before I can save on major battles does provide concern.
However, the devs here are absolutely listening. Patch notes have been noted by the fans to be almost directly quoting the Steam forums in addressing exact concerns, and some great improvements have been made. Notably, you can elect to skip, via individual menu options, the transformation sequences, clothing damage cutscenes, and super-move cutscenes. This is not an option in any other version of the game. The frame-rates are mostly smooth, with only occasional slowdown with effects-intensive scenes, especially prominent if the camera is pushed into a corner.
In short, I bought this on a lark and ended up very, very impressed. I highly recommend giving it a go at the least, and showing that this kind of effort is extremely appreciated!

Not good...not good at all.
The concept is interesting:  you build and protect a tower while defeating the enemy's tower or hero, and use a variety of cards from your deck as spells or minions to do so.
The problem is, it's far too overly simplistic, which creates an incredibly boring experience.
You GAIN cards either from winning a match or from buying it in store with in-game currency that you win.  Your deck continues to grow, and grow, and grow. Which, as any CCG/TCG player knows, is a HORRIBLE thing because it saturates the deck with low end cards, prevents synergy, prevents specific tactics.
Eventually, your deck will have 100+ different cards, and you'll rarely see the good ones as a result.
Given that, there really isn't any strategy here at all. There are no real special cards that do something unique. The more powerful cards just do more of the same (higher damage, give more resources, etc.).
This summarizes the available options:
* increase your wall (which acts as a shield)
* increase your tower height (which wins the game)
* do dmg to the enemy (wall or height)
* increase level of resource building (generates more resources per turn)
* increase x amt of resources
There is NOTHING else in the game play. Cards either do more or less of the above, or they may combine one or more of the above. That's the extent of the creativity and variation here.
There is no synergy between cards, there is no way to edit the deck to be "more tower dmg" focused or more "wall defensive" focused. You just get random cards put into your hands, and go with it. You'll be doing a little bit of everything, which means there is no actual strategy.
Devs are non-existent, as is the community. At the time of this review, there are 3 threads, 2 posters (myself included), and zero dev responses. You'd think the devs would care enough about their game's launch to at least introduce themselves, see how things are going, answer questions of prospective or new customers. But...they don't.
If the devs don't even care about their own game...why should consumers?
Stay away. Even though it's $5, it's a waste of time...and your time is probably more valuable than the $5.  There are plenty of F2P card games with substantially more depth and creativity, which will provide a fulfilling, enjoyable experience. Unfortunately, this low cost game...just can't compete.

Such a beautifully told story! Even though the game is a bit simplistic in terms of play mechanics and feels more like a short story you occasionally solve some puzzles to move forward, it never gets boring or repetitive. Our main character, Joe, is a simple man, but still manages to surprise. It's very interesting to see the events take place from his point of view. I totally loved the character.
It's a relatively short game, but every moment is very enjoyable. The puzzles are pretty easy but fun to solve. Time travel is not an easy concept to manage but they did it well.
I also liked how they handled internal monologues. Instead of talking out loud, you just see the thoughts in writing. At first that actually made me think that there would be no voice acting, but there is. And it's pretty good.
The game certainly has a pretty dark tone, but it also manages to use some funny elements to balance it.
This could be a great introduction to point and click adventure games for anyone. But a fan of the genre will certainly enjoy it too.

If you haven't heard about Steins;Gate before this, I think the less you know is the better since I went into it knowing almost nothing. I've played this before it was on Steam, and from what I experienced I think this is the best version available at the moment due to some differences I noticed.
I feel this is 100% worth playing even if you have seen the anime, while the anime is good the VN is definitely longer and more detailed, and allows you to go along multiple routes not covered in the anime.
The VN has gorgeous, stylized art that the anime honestly failed to capture. On the version I played before this, the game only supported 720p. This version has full 1080p support, with the art looking still perfectly normal.
The VN has a pretty unique choice system, you use the protagonists cellphone to make choices. You'll receive text messages and phone calls, and you choose whether to respond to these or not. When replying to a text message, you can specify a specific subject to talk about in your reply. You however do not know what the reply will specifically say, which was somewhat annoying because once you chose what to talk about you were locked into the reply and could not back out of sending it. This version allows you to back out of replies before they are sent, meaning you don't have to save and load likely multiple times every time you want to reply to a text message.
If you haven't seen the anime, this VN has some really, really good characters and development. The protagonist is really fun especially, compared to the usual faceless male you see in quite a few other visual novels. I'm being a bit sprase in details because again, I think the less known makes it better. The translation seems to be pretty high quality, seeming to be exactly the same translation I saw when I played the VN earlier.
I'm not sure if any of the changes I mentioned are present in any other version of the VN, so every improvement I mentioned here could be totally present in another version. I'm not aware of any personally, though.
So yeah this is one of my favorite visual novels, except with some definite improvements. I really recommend it.

Senran Kagura is a 3d hack and slash franchise that has been slowly gaining a fanbase over the past few years for the fact that its full of over the top♥♥♥♥♥♥and♥♥♥♥♥but still manages to be a good game. Well, decent enough, in my opinion.
Senran's combat is nice. Controls are responsive and intuitive, Attacks feel visceral and satisfying, and jumping and air dashing have a wonderfully floaty and ethereal feeling that gives the movement and proceeding aerial beat downs a uniquely graceful flavor. The combat immediately impressed me and had me itching for more from the first flash of the blade.
What frustrates me to no end about Senran's combat, however, is that while they got the "engine" right, they put absolutely no effort into the "environment". Beyond the fact that most "stages" are just a few linked wide open arenas with waves of enemies to kill (who needs level design?), the games lack of challenge is crippling. After 5+ hours of effortlessly combo murdering hordes of faceless ninja and dumb npc's that never seem to be able to raise a finger in retaliation, I gave up on hoping anything was going to improve and started to feel the WARP/burn out overtaking me.
The game attempts to make up for this with a lot of content, many missions (which all boil down to the above), and many characters (who mostly play the same outside of a few gimmicky ones, differentiated solely by slightly faster/slower attack speeds and ranges), but as a longtime hardcore action gamer, this can't replace a well designed campaign.
Senran also tends to get a lot of praise for its story from fans, citing that, beyond the fanservice, it actually gives its cast proper development and attempts to make you connect to them emotionally as full fledged characters. However, unlike the numerous breasts in this game, Senran Kagura does not succeed in grabbing me. I can see that there was genuine effort put into creating characters with distinct personalities, motivations, and character arcs, as well as a plot that attempts to run deeper than "fight the evil", but for me, numerous little story telling and writing nitpicks add up and prevent me from really connecting to the game's world or characters. If you enjoy flavor of the month shounen anime, you might be impressed by the attempt to translate an 'alright' fighty ninja story into a game that otherwise runs on pure♥♥♥♥♥♥and♥♥♥♥♥ but I'm not.
Also, when I effortlessly over-kill a boss on my first try without taking any damage, and the following cutscene tells me my character was severely injured while the boss has barely been scratched and is now gloating about it...I swear, that is the most hilariously immersion breaking thing I've seen in a long time. Oh, and this happens more than 4 times. Damn.
So...why is this a positive recommendation? Well, the dashing combos and floaty air combat were just barely interesting and engaging enough to convince me not to ask for a refund. Senran can be fun to pick up once and a while, but you should know what you're getting into: This is no Bayonetta. this is an animu masher for animu fans. Those seeking depth will need to tolerate the games lack of it in order to enjoy its better aspects.
