Okay so I'm probably going to finish this game anyways since I hate unfinished games, but please, if you're looking for a good medtroidvania that's not too much of a hassle to complete, and with good references to older games and geek culture without forced cheap jokes, please go play
, it's free and Unepic definitely isn't worth 13 bucks, at the very least if you hate retro pixel graphics, wait for
's release.
I remember being really interested in this game's theme of some D&D player being sent into a castle for adventures, there's a lot of time between when I first heard of Unepic, the moment I got the game, and when I installed it on an old computer on Lubuntu (at least it works on most OS, that's a plus). What I didn't expect was how boring and how cheap the references to geek culture are.
First of all, the gameplay. A good Metroidvania is supposed to be based on quick thinking, and/or on puzzles during levels to proceed further. As far as I've been in this game, Unepic does not have any of these. The battles are slow and usually mindless button mashing and mediocre "infiltration" (more like "running behind the guy while he's not looking"), they're mostly bad because they're easy to figure out, but one simple mistake can get you a game over. I mean it's not even a "git gud" difficulty level because most of the enemies are really easy to fight, it's simply that you usually have to go back to the save point and redo the level aaaall the way, which makes it quickly boring. And don't get me started on the bosses, they have easy to counter but anarchic patterns, which can make them either way too easy or way too hard (with no inbetweens) regardless of the boss. And that's not how a boss is supposed to work.
The graphics are okay, I mean it's not something you'll remember, but it's not fugly either, the music is mostly okay, but sometimes it tends to be actually annoying, especially if it's used to highlight crude dudebro jokes.
That's where I'm getting at: the writing and most of all, the jokes. Most the geek references are actually forced unfunny jokes that are used to cover up the lack of creativity from the dev. Like one of the characters is literally Yoda, you can earn a special type of cash from challenges that can be used to buy stuff from well known franchises. Heck, even the joke when you kill your first enemy is an overused MGS joke that feels way out of place... It's like watching a bad episode of The Big Bang Theory.
And it wouldn't be such a problem if it weren't so unfitting, I mean I saw merchants with linux distribs as names, one of them, called "Ubuntu", told me that he didn't give away free stuff and only sold it (I spare you the racist misspelling, because of course the character being black, he obviously can't speak correctly; as racist as Tintin in the Congo).
On top of that, besides the "geek jokes", the protagonist acts like a virgin preteen who tries to hit on every female character in the game (not like there are a lot of them). Best way to make half the players (if not more) stop relating to the main character imo. Not only did I have to read his dull lines about wanting to bang one merchant, but there's literally one side quest that consists of killing one mob then have sex with a couple of female goblins - it's not even elliptic, you have to move your character to the goblins' rooms and awkwardly watch the bed moving behind curtains while cheesy music is playing. That's forced heteronormativity at its finest.
One good point I did notice: not a single bug in sight. Maybe that's because I haven't played enough, but the game seems pretty well wrapped up in this regard.
TL;DR: the jokes aren't funny, the game is pretty boring, you won't miss anything by playing another game instead.

Me and this man survived together. We were in this hamlet, defending against the Americans as the BTR that was our lifeline was blown to bits by an incoming mortar round. The squad leader shouts something about incoming as I prepare for a fight. I go downstairs, and Mortar rounds begin to fall all around us, sending schrapnel into any crevis it can find. Our medic was killed in the first volley of fire. I look and I see Cheese, as he says "Hold me".
Mortar rounds continue to explode all around us, my monitor shakes and my headphones are busted by the sheer power of the PTSD simulator that is being stuck in a mortar barrage with only 3 of your comrades in SQUAD. I hear rapid gunfire as I turn around and see my squad leader fall to the ground. The shelling stops. In a split second my MLG instinct took over, as the American soldier walked through the door I let a long burst rain upon him in fury. He sloops over, dead.
I turn around not realizing what is going on as I hear a 50. BMG going off, and panic ensues. We are surrounded. I fire at another soldier who takes cover. I pull out my RPG.... Step out the doorway in which Cheese lies dead, aim it in an instant. And fire at the Humvee's gunner. Fire and smoke fills the air as a immense feeling of satisfaction overwhelms me. I did it. In that moment, I see a Machine gunner turn around, firing his weapon. I am filled with bullets. This is how my story ends.

It's nostalgia bait, but it's executed in the very best way. Being able to put your own custom made character into the Dragon Ball story is the cherry on top.
The combat, while fairly simple, is actually fun, fast, and very responsive.  The ability to have 3 on 3 fights in a large arena where you can fly around in is awesome.  The character customization also allows for you to equip moves and ultimate abilities from other Z fighters at any time outside of combat.
Keyboard controls are awkward, but it works great if you have an Xbox (or similar) controller.
There is also a small element of exploration in which you can search for items in the arenas, these can be used for crafting in your hub world.  While not necessary, since you can just buy said items, it helps to do that to save money for the large variety of clothing and accessories available for your character.  Most of which change your stats in some way.
Overall this game has a lot of content for the player to unlock.  And a lot of bang for your buck.
Before I go into the bad, the only other thing that I can say that makes this game purchase sort of iffy is the difficulty wall.  It's easy enough up until you beat Freiza, but then after that there's definitely a skill wall that you need to climb up.
The bad thing about this game is the awkward interface and hub world.  For example, it's really awkward to have a 2 player offline fight.  You need to sign in, and then pick your character, then run through the hub world to the npc that'll allow you to do this.  There's no way to pick it from a menu at the title screen.
The other  bad thing I can say about this game is that, at the time of writing, the online mode is completely broken. Often getting disconnected even while playing in single player.

Note: This review was written within the first week of release.
Dragon Ball Xenoverse is a single-player + multi-player Dragonball game. It sports both an Offline and Online play modes: these play modes are a PvE-style story line and a PvP mode like your classic fighting games. Characters can be customized in both appearance and skill, so you can really create the character you want. Alternatively, you are not forced to use your character during the Parallel Quests (they are a repeatable mission you do for items and XP) and can use any unlocked story character instead. The use of the player character is required for the main story line. You start with one customizable character, but once you do a complete playthrough, more character slots are unlocked. Other features include:
- Ability to create teams in game.
- World Tournament for PvP events.
- Voice chat.
- Collectable dragon balls which can be used to unlock new characters, lots of cash, items, combat moves, skill point resets and character visual do-overs.
- Most, if not all, of the original english VOs from the series, plus it covers characters from the start of Z to GT series, plus the latest movie.
- Easy to learn, difficult to master gameplay.
- Customizable characaters in both skill and appearance.
- Does not require online connection to play.
- Fun, intense combat.
- Items are shared between characters, no need to re-farm items or cash.
- Netcode seems to be spotty. Desync and lag issues.
- Camera is a bit finicky at times.
- Crash-prone if steam overlay is enabled.
- Servers are frequently down, but fortunately you can still play the game.... but requires steam to be in offline mode first.
- Can be grindy. RNGesus does exist in this game which can make getting items frustrating.
[h2]Conclusion[/h2]
This game is a must for anyone who is into all things Dragonball. If you are patient and can deal with the fact that the online servers may go down without notice, then you should have a good time in game, especially if you have friends to play with. Hopefully the developers/publishers add more resources into supporting the game to buff out some of the release-week issues.

If you want to go back to the roots of a popular game genre and have a lot of fun doing so, Wolfenstein 3D is certainly the game for you.

You would need to have a tremendous dislike for Borderlands as a franchise to avoid stating Tales from the Borderlands might easily be the best game Telltale ever made.  And I'm saying that as someone who's not really much of a Borderlands fan AND who has consistently had a bone to pick with Telltale's approach to game design.
Game follows standard Telltale interactive adventure formula with a twist of having two main characters to control this time around, even if they are both on the snarky side to begin with, and benefits from the addition of largely tangential elements like Fiona's wallet or Ryhs' cybernetic eye which really only come up in rare few situations where they were actually used in some meaningful way. They were still good additions though, and precisely what these games need to involve you further on some mechanical level even if it is just inteacting with couple of windows and additional button presses. It should be noted this is by far the most light-hearted game as befitting its native franchise and this comes through in general  atmosphere, characters themselves and writting overall resulting in incredibly zany situations and even crazier directions story goes towards. I would also say a much-complained-about-wait for the final episode was well worth it having finally played it considering it pulls off some decent story resolutions as well as new last-minute system additions I did not see coming while still keeping the doors open for a potential season two.
In the end, Telltale really outdid themselves with this one and is probably their new benchmark as of right now.

RimWorld is a bit of an interesting game. To begin with, it is fun. I thoroughly enjoy it. That said,t here are things I must cover.
First off, this game is very indicative of Prison Architect, from the art style to the mechanics. The games are, fundamentally, quite similar; Your primary job is to design and administrate a community. On one hand, they're prisoners. On the other, colonists.
That said, RimWorld does many things to make itself feel unique. There are many survival and gathering/scavenging mechanics, alongside many traits which really add to the experience. All colonists are unique. Sometimes that's good, sometimes that's bad.
There's quite a learning curve to overcome. The first two to three hours of the game was met with failed colony after failed colony. The Bills system, the jobs, the assignments -- they all are complex, and require a lot of trial and error to grapple. (Or a few hours of YouTube tutorial videos.) Once (or if) you can overcome the learning curve, the game opens up to be a challenging, yet fun, simulation of colonizing another world. Random world generation means no two situations are the same, and there are several biomes to choose from, all with their own unique challenges.
Overall, I would definitely recommend this game. It's fun, but has a steep learning curve, and feels a bit indicative. I will say that some things feel lacking; In some areas, it feels as if there should be more things to be able to craft, more things you should be able to make your colonists do. The game provides for a very good baseline, but after so many hours in Colony X, I've found that the only way to restore the fun is to move on to Colony Y. This game is still far from complete, however, so I expect the longevity to grow as the game does.

Even thought the game claims that it is a finished product.. its not. The stage of the game's  development is incorrectly titled.
So much work has to go into the physics of the machines and the dirt. Now i understand you cant have a fully real life simulation of using the machines, nor would you  ( as the player ) want to learn to how properly operate these machines correctly, but it does simulate it somewhat.
As for the machines and the dirt, what the games does do correct is function like a idle game. The worker hire function is  "broken" inregards to making money. Once you have merely bought the tools to do what ever stage of mining youd wish to do, you can simply just hire a worker to use the equipment, without the equipment even being rigged up properly. hence you can just buy the equipment leave it on your claim and tell them to work it. This will then net you a passive gold income ( in ounces ) while youre meant to work away and make the gold the " proper way ". So basically you dnt even have to mine anything to make decent money. Now given you cant get the "huge nugget events" through workers, you can get more money for less work than actualy running about operating all the machinery and cleaning everything.
So if you like to own a over priced idle game then buy this game.
If you want an under developed game to what they try and sell it as, then buy this game.
If you want to get frustraded as the machinery physics and get your 8 tonne dozer stuck between 2, 1 ft high blobs of dirt and potentially pop a blood vessle in your brain, then buy this game.
BUT! the feeling of making gold does feel nice. The feeling of progression is pretty good. Once youve reached those highs... the game will become boring as you then just get stuck in your dozer or slide all over the road in your truck while towing potentially 2 tonnes of sludge to be processed.
Verdict... dnt buy as the game does not sell what its claiming to sell. Not a finished product by any account.

This is not the sort of game action packed junkies will enjoy, if you like to play games such as Construction Simulator, Farm Simulator, etc... then, this is most certainly up your street.
Gameplay consists of extracting gold from one of several locations which you can rent or buy, then ranging from manual labour to full machine automation you strike it rich, whilst upgrading your equipment and machines in the process.
I personal love the setting up aspects within "gold rush" especially enjoy setting up the cables and pipes to my personal taste. Some of the controls could have been slightly better, but are fit for purpose and a few tweaks in the controls can yield decent enough results.
It ultimaly boils down to how much you will enjoy driving JCB around and digging dirt in the end that is the primary stay of this game, so if that doesnt sound like your bag i would really avoid it at all costs.
It's basically a replica of a working lifestyle...
Whilst at the beginning my rig is capable of running Ultra Graphics @ 1920x1080 (average 30+ fps) I dont meet the minumin requirements of 16GB ram, and this may be a direct result of the lag spikes during loading sections. In addition to that, i have noticed that when i start to increase the amount of cables, pipes, machinery those graphics settings have to come right down to low in a lot of cases.
It also has to be said that there are a lot of issues in this game, from collision detection issues, through optimization problems, right through to a few borderline game breaking bugs.
The lack of ram, and a weaker system is probably going to kill my experience as time goes by, but i really do enjoy playing the game, setting up my world, and playing with the vechiles. so its getting a thumbs up.
Hopefully the developers will sort out some of these issues, and my experience will get better. but on that note, this should have been released as early access, and it amazes me these days how developers just simply get away with releasing games on the store, that are in worse shape than some on the early access sections, but whatever right ?

As it was a NaNoRenO VN contest entry, developers had exactly one month to make it - regardless of that, they chose a multi-route, expansive formula that just couldn't work out well within such strict time constrains. The game shows a lot of interesting ideas and both the overarching storyline and the character design were really solid IMO. Unfortunatly, the final product simply lacks the polish and production values necessary to truly make it work - or at least work as well as it could if given a bit more time and care.
Obviously, as a free game AIRIS is still in many ways remarkable and something worth experiencing if you like otome, or even romance VNs in general (after all, it has yuri and female/non-binary routes). Its mystery elements, the creative and often ambiguous endings, and the variation in romance options created a basis for a really great product. Sadly, because of sloppy writing, occasional pacing issues and underwhelming visual assets many parts of it simply fall flat, without ever reaching the emotional impact the authors were aiming for.
All that being said, I give it a cautious recommendation - if you can see past its faults, it still offers a very interesting and fairly deep story, mixing romance, mystery and adventure in creative and distinct ways. It simply lacks the finishing touch that was necessary to make it truly special.

Before you buy this game, you must first realise that this is an alpha and is missing many of the features which they are working on for the final game. There is ONLY multiplayer and the 7 maps which you can look around/play in multiplayer.
Having said that, this game is surprisingly polished for an alpha.. there is so much immersion, firing a weapon takes time to master and adds a good level of depth to the game. The weather changes on the maps, sometimes it goes pitch black or foggy which completely changes the tactics you use. Currently the game is also very balanced (due to there only being 1 weapon) so it feels satisfying to get good at the game knowing no one has an advantage.
Some issues you need to be aware of: currently there is only 1 gun in the game and couple of game modes (team domination being the most used and the best), there are some issues with hit detection and lag *make sure you pick a server with low ping however even then you'll need to learn to lead the target a bit more etc* (also make sure you turn off smoothing in the options to help with this). They are fixing this but for now it's there. Also there is no crouching in the game, no leaning or anything like that.. I believe they want to add in these features.
In conclusion, this is definatly an early alpha with many features missing... however I believe that the current strengths of the game (immersion, satisfying shooting and balanced multiplayer) make this 100% worth the asking price which will also help them continue development. Have a look at some more recent videos and make your judgement, it's changed a lot over the past month (december).

Me and this man survived together. We were in this hamlet, defending against the Americans as the BTR that was our lifeline was blown to bits by an incoming mortar round. The squad leader shouts something about incoming as I prepare for a fight. I go downstairs, and Mortar rounds begin to fall all around us, sending schrapnel into any crevis it can find. In a split second my MLG instinct took over, as the American soldier walked through the door I let a long burst rain upon him in fury. He sloops over, dead.
I turn around not realizing what is going on as I hear a 50. BMG going off, and panic ensues. We are surrounded. I fire at another soldier who takes cover. I pull out my RPG.... Step out the doorway in which Cheese lies dead, aim it in an instant. And fire at the Humvee's gunner. Fire and smoke fills the air as a immense feeling of satisfaction overwhelms me. I did it. A quick note for my play time, I actually completed this game 100% off itch.io before it released on Steam.
There's a lot of things I love about this game, but the highlights to me are:
+ The Story
I love that it takes place where the characters are dungeon crawling and going on quests and whatnot, but still doing it while exploring who the characters all are, their relationships to each other, and what's really going on with the world. The nerd in me was exceptionally pleased.
+ The Characters
The characters aren't perfect. They're flawed, and for that they're so much more real. I especially appriciated Aliya being a much stronger willed MC than so many other VNs, especially of the Japanese variety. She's was a fresh breath for me. That and she just does things that left me laughing sometimes.
+ The Endings
There is no 100% happy ending, and this I really love. It really makes you feel like your choices mattered because there's no way everything is ever going to be perfect, and you really get to see how it changes in the endings. You get to decide for yourself which ending you prefer, and I've seen different people prefer different endings so that's fantastic.
Overall with the writing I can really see how much care was taken into a game, which is more than I've seen in some VNs that were made in way over than just a month.
There are other things that I really enjoyed. The backgrounds, the sprite art, the CGs. I'm always up for finding a VN that retains lovely art without looking like the basic anime style that's so popular. I appriciate the diversity in including Lyall, a non-binary character, without using it as a tokan identity character. They're there, no need to talk specifically about that sort of take on it.

An ancient classic re-imagined for the modern age, Wolfenstein: The New Order shouldn't fool you into thinking it's just another mindless FPS. While there's more than your fair share of guns-a-blazing action, BJ Blazcowitz's quest to topple over the regieme of a world where the Nazis won world war 2 is as story rich as it is action packed. End-level cutsceens seem satisfying, and the hundreds of secrets laden throughout the game are often satisfying to find and can fufill that sense of nostalgia to those who've played the original. While FPS isn't everyone's cup of tea, Wolfenstein: The New Order has no multiplayer to distract the developers from the very talented original writing and level design. Wolfenstein: The New Order is an excellent title and worth every penny (although nowadays you'd be ridiculas to purchase it at full price)

They don't apprea there (not being able to customize my controls doesn't bother me, but let me know them). I accessed the options menu from the main menu randomly because after the game crashed a few times when I tabbed out for google searching I though maybe it was in there and I just missed it. I then found you can change the controls (and see them) from the options menu, but only if you go from the main menu,so ok fine F is talk to NPCs thats not a game breaker or anything, but getting information on things in thie game is like pulling teeth.
The next UI thing is that I cannot find a way to see your inventory unless you go back to town and talk to an NPC. This is a massive problem because you auto equip anything you pick up. I do love racing games (I played the originals  Top Gear in SNES , and beated them . Played Mario Kart in SNES and N64 and I beated those 2 in all dificulties) , but Sonic All-stars racing transformed is by far the most dificult race game out of there.
Im not a person of reviews but i really needed to review this one.
** Personal Progress **
I have 45 stars in 8hrs.. im not that bad. I have unlock Danica Patrick and Shadow. I won a lot of A-Class races but they are so very dificult.
**Installation and OS**
The game worked at first shot , steam installed it with no problem. I have Windows 8.1 and XBOX 360 Controller , with an Asus R9 270X , and the game runs very fine. Be aware if you dont have a powerfull PC , the game can run under 30-40fps , and it really needs to run at least over 50fps.. because the AI is so brutal that it doesnt admit mistakes.
** Game **
My overall impression is that the game has a very high learning curve, and it really can make you feel that you suck at racing games. But is not you , is the Brutal and broken AI .
** Racers **
The game has like 27 racer roaster.. everyone has diferent stats , and handles diferently , they can be level up with playing any type of races. Some of them can be unlocked in the game , what is really nice and extends the game a lot.
** Tracks **
The tracks are very fine , and has is own themes (Sega Games), tracks are beautiful , some are a candy to the eye , you wont be dissapointed in that aspect. The water is very nice and tracks effects are great.
** Shortcuts **
Tracks do have shorcuts but , some of them are very dificult to get, and it doenst make you to get a huge gap or advantage. Because the AI is so brutal that they take the shorcuts too (better than you).
** Race mechanics **
Run fast Run far... you get the usuals , power-ups and offensive and defensive items. The All-Star item is like the mario Star. It makes you invincible. Yeah , AI get those too it can and make you cry.. Some race mechanics are important to point it out:
1. You always start in 10th place.
2. Some levels desing are very simple , and make chases to the first places very dificult. because the AI is so good and doesnt make mistakes that are very dificult to chase.
3. Tracks really do need a lot of practice and knowledge, you can play it for over 10-20 times and never get the firsts places..
** AI **
I have never seen so brutal AI in a Game. Some time if feels like 9 vs 1 battle.
1. Remember that boost that you can do starting the race? , The AI does it better than you most of the time.
2. The AI is so brutal , that they gonna hunt you down if you are in the 3rd firsts places.
3. The AI Takes the mini-shortcuts better than you.
4. They do drift boosts very well... very well
5. AI do stunts. A lot of them.
6. They will shot you a lot. Some times is very frustrating.
7. The guy in the first place never makes a mistake , unless you shot him in the back.
It makes the AI feel like you were racing against a better version of you... always. Since the first track..
****But the real problem is this.****
In A-Class:
1. If You do any mistake , you'll need to restart the race.
2. They run faster than you. I have notice even if you got boost (Items and Lines) and the didnt.. AI runs at the same speed like you.
3. They are bullet proof. I shoot one of them with 3 Ice balls and later with a tornado in the same race segment , and it hadnt any problem to keep with me in the race.
3.1 If you hit any of them , they will keep you in race with no problem , .
4. Tornado doesnt affect them , if you get hit by one of those , say hello to restart button.
4.1 Ice ball doesnt affect them. I noticed they had better acceleration than you. Thats a big problem.
4.2 Now im thinking that the only thing that can surpass them in A-Class is the all star item. And they got it a lot more  times than you.
5. They do level 2 or 3 boost with no problem , even for you is dificult (with a practice maybe not).
6. They shoot you at sight. And they are really good at shooting.
7. If you are in the first place , run fast run far , they gonna hunt you , if you get hit by anything say bye bye to first place , by any reason they are always behing you no matter you do , ive seen some video were people exploit some parts of the maps , but those are things that you can make with +50hrs in the game.
The problem is making an almost invencible AI to play with. Makes this game certainly dificult and frustrating, some people will say that you are newbie or bad, but now mix all the items explained above and you got a nightmare racing game.
Im not recommend this game for casuals , Hardcore racing gamers will have a wreck festival.

Which is an important detail about the characters since it explains why it was such a big deal when the trains all shut down- Mayushii was completely trapped inside a city trying to kill her. Spoiler alert I guess?
If I'd known that when watching the anime for the first time, I would have been able to focus on the fact that the series was climaxing and my two favorite characters were trapped in a nightmarish Groundhogs Day-esque situation instead of wondering "sooo why don't Okarin and Mayushii just go back to one of their apartments and bunker up for the night?"
2. Another thing the game does better is the humor. The game's very self aware, which leads to a lot of meta humor. For instance, after finishing the "prologue", the game cuts to a conversation between Okarin and Daru about the nature of their reality and whether they actually exist, or are in fact, just characters in a video game.
The difference in mediums also means that the humor can be TOLD differently, my favorite example being when you meet Luka for the first time. I won't explain what happens because of spoilers, but I was rolling on the floor laughing during his introduction.
The music is amazing, voice talent is top notch, and the art style is distinct.
~~~~~~~~~
Negatives:
1. THE PORT SUCKS♥♥♥♥♥HOLY COW THIS HAS GOT TO BE ONE OF THE WORST STEAM PORTS I'VE EVER EXPERIENCED. The controls are confusing, buttons are located in weird places, and nothing is intuititave.
2. Another thing I dislike is that when you're at a crossroads of choices, it's confusing to know what each choice actually means. Choices are presented to you via a text message conversation (or email or whatever) on your phone. There are some highlighted words that you can click on to move the conversation in that direction. If it sounds confusing, that's because it is. But it's not a terrible downside since most of the decisions you make are fairly inconsequential.
3. The game's also a bit pricey for an old visual novel. Although the fact that it's around 20 hours long means you'll only be paying for $1.50ish per hour, which isn't too bad
t;ldr
Play the game if you liked the anime, it's a much more complete version of the story
Play the game if you didn't like the anime, it's a much more complete version of the story
Play the game if you've never even heard of Steins;Gate (also get out from under your rock more), it's an brilliant, heartfelt story about time travel, sorrow, and the unintended consequences of one's actions that will completely suck you in

I can't go in-depth with my analysis on this game as I've only played 100 minutes of it, but I can at least describe what caused me to refund the game. I skipped every cutscene in order to get as far into the game as I could before Steam's refund window passed me by, thinking I could always go back and watch them later. Another game I would have liked to refund stripped much of my time away with cutscenes, and now it sits permanently in my library, a harsh reminder of money wasted.
Fine-movement and precision in this game are impossible, making the controls feel very loose. Your character will move frantically about regardless of the type of input you provide. While this itself isn't terrible, it does necessitate the inclusion of much "assisted targetting" wherein your character is homed into an enemy whenever you attack. This makes combos essentially create themselves, solely requiring button mashing to make a perfect combo.
For attacking, you're given a strong and light attack with which you build combos through preset trees each character has. Now, I only unlocked about 3 tree expansions for roughly 7 characters each, but they did nothing to change up combos. Whether or not you make use of the heavy attack options or op for mashing light to finish a string, the same amount of damage will be done, the same followup opportunity will be activated, the hitboxes remain roughly identical, changes in combo safety are minimal, but mashing light will often give you a higher combo count.
"Missions" consist of either hacking through a small group of lower level enemies before fighting a playable character or simply fighting the playable straight away. Missions lasted anywhere between a minimum of 20 seconds and a maximum of 1min10sec with the average resting at around 1 min for mobs (very very small mobs) and 30 seconds for bosses. I'm a neophyte, and bosses are torn down in roughly 30 seconds. The difficulty can be increased, making the bosses absorb more damage, but the combat is so shallow that I bore withing even 30 seconds. These missions are, of course, bookended by loading screens, each of which takes roughly 10-15 seconds. They're short, for load screens, but you'll be spending a lot of time in them relative to the gameplay. Besides that, while fighting bosses cutscenes will constantly be activated by their transformations, their special attacks, when their clothing gets ripped, etc. and it is a jarring and frequent wrench in the pace of combat. All of these cutscenes can be skipped, but they are so frequent that even their startup time before you skip them amounts to an obnoxious amount of time, collectively.
The game has a clothes-breaking "mechanic" wherin cutscenes are triggered when clothing is ripped. I put "mechanic" in quotes as this has no effect on gameplay other than to cut away from it for a prebaked animation that I've seen more than 30 times in just 1.7 hours. Breaking of clothing will happen when the boss takes a predetermined amount of damage, whether you try and aim for it or not. It's a hollow experience.
This game, as is likely clear, has a lot of emphasis on female nudity. I thought, at first, that this would be something that would be handled well. Something lighthearted and stimulating; something that would be played for laughs as a sort of mockery of the trope while also being a player of that same game. The way the T&A is actually handeled, however, is very unironic. The tone is always "ooh, come here, big boy. Look how SEXY I am. Oh yeah. Let me press my boobies together. *giggle*" and it feels like it's genuinely expecting me to swoon. As a result, what could've been both a satirical, as well as sexy, facet of the game only provides a very icky-feeling and awkward experience.
All in all, this game is not terrible in its execution, but it's completely useless. What I mean is that, for everything this game does, other games have done it better. It feels like a game of this quality has no place in the context of modern games as it provides significantly less than both its peers and predecessors. I bought this on sale at $26.99, but I would hesitate to pay even $10 for it. For what it provides, I might think $8 would be fair. It's a rough critique, I know, but I'm trying to be as honest as possible. At the very least, skip through the cutscenes if you're willing to try this game out so that you can get a real feel for what the game is before you decide to keep it.

Titan Souls is a wonderful jaunt into a world of frustration and adventure.
You do nothing but fight bosses, a lot.
However all of these bosses are extremely well designed and enjoyable to fight.
Some you will be able to beat in a matter of seconds as you understand how they work and execute it properly,
and others will take you an hour or so to beat by infuriatingly throwing yourself against a wall.
Before I go into pro's and con's, I'd like to address some common complaints I saw in many other steam reviews:
One complaint was that it took forever to get back to a boss that you continuously throw yourself against.
I saw varying times throughout, but as long as you touch the next respawn point in an area it should only take you about fifteen seconds to get back to the boss.
It is a bit long I admit, but in my opinion, it just kept inspiring me to not die, and to walk out of the door than back into it next time.
It certainly took no longer to walk back than an average Dark Souls boss, which I've heard this game compared to a few times.
The second complaint was that it is difficult to find the bosses.
While I admit it can be a bit frustrating to find the next area, it's always easy to find the bosses in the area.
There is a "glyph" at the center of every area, that functions as a respawn point if you touch it.
It gives you a general direction to every boss in the area, by having grayed out parts on it pointing the way.
Now that we have that out of the way, let's address the pros and cons.
Pros:
1. Frustrating, but the feeling of success every time you kill a boss is worth it.
2. The soundtrack is absolutely gorgeous.
3. The visuals are amazing.
4. The gameplay is very unique.
5. The designs for every boss is different and creative, making every fight feel vibrant and new.
Cons:
1. It is a bit short for the $15 price tag.
2. The game can feel more luck based than skill based sometimes.
3. It is easy to lose yourself between areas,
4. If you're quick to anger it may be best to skip this one or take frequent breaks.

The game also have a decent amount of maps that can change as the match progresses mostly by lighting, the atmosphere is very impressive and one of the best in MP FPS games. The game now has COOP with several modes in the game. The Terrorist Hunt-like mode Elimination, the Objective-based Survival, and Nucleus-exclusive Escape. There's also two Campaign maps (The Neurogen Incident and Assault on Starcrown Aerospace) including a tutorial for the game.
The bad: The game has only has two weapons, the framerate isn't that great unless you have a good processor, and content is bare bones.
If you expect a lot of stuff in this early version, you'll be disappointed. However, the game is decent enough to sink a lot of hours into it, and the community is remarkable. I would recommend buying it now, mainly for that and for future content.

Theoretically, this game would be a lot of fun. With the recent patches the dev have attempted to bring more depth into the game (improved inventory system, mana based ability system, dedicated multiplayer servers). There are a bunch of opponents of the mana system, personally I think the recent changes were all good.
BUT.
This game is bugged as hell. I can't recall ever playing a game that was as bugged as this. And this game is supposed to be finished since more than a year. In its current state I would call it an alpha at best.
Now it is obvious that if you introduce new features that there are some bugs, but many bugs have been in this game forever (i.e. jumping out of map boundaries with certain classes) and there doesn't seem action of the devs in these regards. More serious bugs include your whole inventory disappearing, or even worse, the whole character being overwritten with a new level 1 character for no reason whatsoever. Truth be told, the programmer(s) don't seem very competent, each new patch seems to introduce more bugs with things that have worked fine. I.e. since the last 4 patches the game always starts in windowed mode even though it is set to fullscreen. This is something that should be easy to fix, you'd think. I'm not even going to start talking about issues when playing with others on multiplayer.
Aside from the major system changes to the game that I mentioned, most changes seem to be nothing but number changes (i.e. damage values changed back and forth with no apparent afterthought).
Also, there are obvious balance issues and I'm not talking balancing between the player classes. You will probably never die to any of the bosses in this game, most of the deaths come from some maggot worms that kill you in one shot, even if you have good equipment. That feels just cheap and makes you wonder whether the devs even test their own changes.
This game also has severe FPS issues. My laptop (which has proper components for games) can handle games like Battlefield easily but this game runs at 20-30 FPS most of the time and is barely any fun on there. I was thinking that this is a casual game that should be playable on the go, even with less powerful devices.
TLDR; If the game was bug-free (or at least almost) and would run smooth on all devices (which it should, as it is merely a 2D game with no fancy physics or anything) this would be fun. In its current state it is just frustrating and I'm not sure whether you can expect it to get better.

is a visual novel where you take on the role of Aliya, one of the warriors in Airis' guild of vassals.  Aliya comes from the world of Airis (hence, the name) where she must defend it from the constant dangers of rampaging creatures that can unleash magic and hurt or even kill the citizens.  Airis is a fantasy world where magic reigns supreme.  When the game starts, we find that Aliya has been suffering from blackouts.  She will wake up in the middle of nowhere, not remembering how she ended up where she was.  Thus, she tries to find the answers for her condition.  Along the way, Aliya may end up discovering more than she had bargained for and the knowledge she gains may end up being beneficial or harmful.
That is the basic gist of the story.  As for the game itself, there are a total of 3 romance options for Aliya to choose from: Everea (a fellow warrior from the guild), Kylan (a mysterious stranger who learns about Aliya's condition and offers to help her even though Aliya doesn't know much about him), and Lyall (Aliya's best friend who is a mage in the guild).  Each romance option has 4 different endings-3 of which are known while 1 is hidden.  There are also CGs (including chibi art) and extras like the all endings list and the developers' notes.
Now as to my thoughts on the game.  I liked it a lot.  The concept was very interesting and although I'm highly tempted to reveal exactly what interested me, that will probably end up being a spoiler so I'll keep quiet on that.  I liked Aliya as a character and the story was written well although there were some grammatical errors here and there.  However, this game was made in a month (more or less) so it is very impressive.  As for the paths, I did like some more than others.  (Oh and if you're interested in what paths to play in order, I'd recommend playing from Everea's to Kylan's to Lyall's, for spoiler purposes.)  My least favorite was Everea's because I felt that her paths would get repetitive and long at times.  My favorite would definitely be Kylan's because I do like his character.  He would have good intentions, try to fix his mistakes.  Even though he wouldn't get it right immediately, he wouldn't give up and I suppose I like that kind of determination.  On Lyall, I have mixed feelings regarding them.  (Lyall is the non-binary character, which I think means that they could be either male or female, so the game calls Lyall "they.")  If I didn't play on Lyall's paths, Lyall would seem absolutely insufferable.  I would dislike their character.  However, when I did play their paths, they do explain why they behaved the way that they did and that did end up making them more likeable or, at least, more tolerable.  The art was good as well even though the chibi art could have been polished more (again, this game was made in a month so we should keep that in mind).  Also, the music was pretty and there was lots of replayability, which is always a plus for me when it comes to VNs.
Overall, I enjoyed
and it's a free game.  It's definitely worth checking out, especially if you're a fan of VNs.  Also, even though all of the achievements and whatnot can be earned quickly by skipping text, I'd recommend not doing so.  The story is quite enjoyable and I liked taking my time to immerse myself with it and the world of Airis (thus, accounting for my long playtime here).  So if you're looking for a good VN with pretty art and music and a well-written (not the best but certainly good) story, then check out AIRIS for yourself.  ^^

So with me just having beaten the main story, here is a run down;
The good
+Solid fighting mechanics
+Great fun with friends
+Custom character creation is solid
+Wide variety of moves to choose from
+Like Smash Bros it is easy to pull moves off, the hard part is using them at the right time. AKA Easy to pick up, harder to
master.
+Decent story (Though it is basically fanfiction of a self-insersion Deviantart OC, ha)
+Seems to be a decent amount of post story content to do, namely PvE content in both solo and co-op.
The bad
-Silly hub world that could just as easily have been a menu, very slow to walk through and key NPCs I want to speak to spawn at random, often not appearing at all, only shuffle about when I do a mission and get back.
-RNG drop rates of certain skills, equipment and z-souls is total bullcrap. A mentor asks me to get a specific soul from a mission I could do as early as lv10, I've now beaten the main story hours later and despite over 20 attempts I have yet to get the z-soul I want.
To summarise; in each mission you have X drop, to get X drop Y event must occur, Y event has Z requirement during the mission. Such as beating all enemies in under 5 minutes which spawns an additional enemy that MIGHT drop the item you want. But here's the kicker; that event only has a CHANCE of occuring in itself when the requirements are met. This does not belong in a fighting game.
-Servers are crapping themselves right now, BanCo is aware of it however so this may be fixed eventually.
-Sadly, the game has NO anti-cheating measure. There are already trainers and ini tweaks around which are easily used and make your character absurdly powerful, beyond what is actually possible. This also works in PvP.
-Speaking of PvP; like all DBZ games, if someone picks an extremely powerful character from the show, you may as well give up on the spot. SSJ4 Vegeta for example, who was a pre-order bonus only of all things, is frequently picked because he simply has an absurd amount of health, damage and so on compared to about 90% of the roster. If you're expecting balanced PvP, look elsewhere, unless you're okay with choosing powerful characters all the time.
-PC specific bugs, Examples;
-Teleporting doesn't work properly, instead of moving you behind the target you just 'blink' on the spot. This works fine on the console versions.
-If you use an ulti ability, pause, alt-tab, tab back in and unpause, your character will perform the ultimate move AGAIN without costing ki or stamina. This does not work in multiplay as it requires a pause but it makes a lot of PvE very easy if abused.
-Some people are reporting the ki blast effects are not displaying correctly
-AI cheats a bit, having infinite ki and stamina (Not visible to the player, but when an AI spams ulti's something is up).
-Some PvE fights are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ without absurd amounts of healing items, many of these can only be done solo, no friendly AI or co-op.
So, would I recommend it? Yes. If you are a fan of DBZ, this is a very good release. Non-DBZ fans however may find little to like as the whole thing is basically just fabservice. If you're on the fence, wait and see if some of these issues are cleaned up in the coming weeks or months. The combat isn't as finely tuned as Tenkaichi nor is the roster as big but it's perfectly good as is.

I really wish Steam offered an in between option: "Yes, No, Maybe"
The reason being, having spent such a huge amount of time for a game like this, I'm still on the fence on whether or not I'd recommend this. But I don't feel it does enough, and the nostalgia quickly wore off within the first few hours.
There's a boatload of consoles to play through, each with  a set of 8 levels, going from the early ZX81, through the Atari, Apple, Commodore 64, NES, and SNES phases, while including some other lesser known computers as well. Some are locked until you hit certain achievements.
Having gone through an entire set of 8 consoles (a total of 64 levels), plus a few extra levels on some of the various other computer stages, it was time to call it quits. I may revisit some of the other stages later on, but the biggest gripe I have is that it focuses too much on the graphics and audio of each passing console world, but hardly any of the mechanics that separated them from each other.

I have this both on ps4 and on steam (it was free on psn one month). I've beaten the game probably two dozen times now and am slowly working through the achievements. I absolutely love the game and here's why. Although you "need" a controller to play the controls are great. The mechanics in the game are simple and responsive. The bosses are interesting and different from one another. If I die I never feel like it was because of a flaw in the game. Do not look up guides on how to beat the bosses at least for your first play through. The discovery of finding out how to beat each boss is part of the fun. Yes, I think having to walk all the way back from the checkpoint to the boss room after you die is a bit annoying but I also think that adds to your desire to beat the boss. *Reading the other reviews I think some people are missing the checkpoints in each area. After dieing it should usually take you 5-10 seconds to get back to the boss* The game can get very frustrating and is quite challenging so if you don't have any patience then I wouldn't suggest it. oh and just FYI, you and the bosses die in one hit.
+Good mechanics

+Visually appealing graphics
+Awesome music
+Good replayability if you're into achievements
+Challenging
-Walking back to the boss after dieing could be tedious for some people

My fiancée and I have had so much fun with the vanilla Borderlands games that I didn't think
could outdo them.  I was wrong.
Telltale Games has really gone above and beyond in creating a story and characters that are dynamic, likable (yes, even Jack), and that I actually care about.  It is one thing to replicate the hilariousness of the
games--Telltale does that quite well--but to actually inject some depth beneath those humorous layers is what really impresses me about Telltale's take on the series.
I enjoyed Telltale's
, but in many ways I found myself not caring about the eventual outcomes of my decisions.  In
, I did find myself regretting decisions, wishing I could go back and set things right.  The fact that a game set in the
universe can conjure up a feeling like regret tells you that Telltale did an impressive job in adding depth to an otherwise comic book set of games.
Even if you don't like the story-heavy/gameplay-light genre of games,
is definitely worth checking out.  Although you might have a hard time going to play the vanilla

It's about time to write a review for this game, especially considering it has mixed reviews.
In this game, to put it simply, you create your own cars and put them into battle vs other player's created cars. The customization in this game is where it's its best. You can make some really insane stuff, there's hardly any limitations to building your car. I've seen people stack a bunch of s**t in the air and place a machine gun on top, hell, if you wanted to you could give your car one wheel and screw yourself over. So yes, customization is the best part of this game, and it's VERY fun.
How about some of the gripes people have with this game?
First gripe: Pay to win. It's a free to play game, it's no surprise it's pay to win. In this game you can buy currency with real money to purchase things on the community market, or in the shop. Is it unplayably pay to win? No. If you want currency or something nice on the shop, it takes a bit of grinding, but you're not limited to paying only money. NEVER, EVER use scrap to craft weapons. You can take the scrap needed to craft a weapon and sell it on the community market, and you'll have enough currency to buy 100 of those guns. What I'm saying is, sell your scrap in 100 or 1000 bulks, which gives you a good amount of currency. (You get 10-20 scrap per game, in some modes you get up to 100)
Second gripe: Matchmaking. The only thing I can call the matchmaking is "okay". It's nothing great, I usually get paired up with people around 500 combat points higher or lower than me. Which can make a huge difference. Does that make it unplayable? No. It's more of a challenge than a frustration. (Then again, I'm only lv. 7 and from what I've heard it gets worse at lv. 10)
The game is fun, free, and will give you many hours of enjoyment. It has great modes, great customization, and it feels very rewarding. Although the game has poor matchmaking, is a complete grind and can be pay to win, it's worth giving a try to see if you like it.

UnEpic is a non-linear RPG platformer. UnEpic begins with the game’s hero, an average guy called Daniel, playing an RPG fantasy board game with his friends. When Daniel heads to the bathroom, the lights go out and Daniel finds himself transported to a castle. Daniel shrugs this off as a hallucination and plays along with the cast of weird and wonderful characters he meets on his journey as fantasy. Daniel learns that his ultimate goal is progress through the castle and to slay its master – Harnakon.
UnEpic’s levels look like an 8-bit adventure game, littered with enemies, traps and rewards for the intrepid adventurer. The standard RPG components are in this game like: earning XP, upgrade abilities with points, making potions, learning spells, trading and encounter many different (funny) types of side quests.
The game tries its best to poke fun at itself, making jokes about the genre that it’s paying homage to, with nods to the classics weaved into the dialogue between Daniel and Anokra Bash.
UnEpic would be an excellent addition to any RPG fans library. UnEpic could ultimately be compared to 8-bit Marmite; if you love RPGs you’ll enjoy it – hate them and it’ll leave a bitter taste in your mouth and hunger for something different.

I'm hesitant to say this game is Bad... but it did disappoint me...
I'll give it points for excellent presentation (seriously, the graphics and music would fit perfectly for the levels they're representing), but that can only get you so far...
The controls work for the most part, but for some reason you stay positioned over moving platforms when jumping which can make some leaps harder to pull off (also NO FIXED JUMPS IN MEAT-BOY CLONES... PLEASE...) And there's not much innovation as the levels go on (and what little abilities DO Get introduced are rarely used throughout the game) which makes the gameplay stale after a while...
Perhaps my biggest complaint is how punishing it is when you die. If you spent like 2-Minutes going around collecting Diamond things and get killed (and there are A LOT of insta-kill obstacles, as if only having 2 HP and only One Health Pick-Up IN THE ENTIRE GAME wasn't bad enough...) Anyway, if you die, you have to start ALL THE WAY BACK at the beginning of the level as all of the collectibles mandatory for finishing the Level Respawn. If Pac-Man respawned all of the Pellets you have to collect after Dying JUST ONE TIME, I'm pretty sure that game wouldn't be fun for too long either...
My recommendation for fixing this error would be the ability to continue your progress in a level. Say for example: Give a player 3-5 Lives, and if they lose all of them before completing the level, THEN Respawn all of the Diamonds and Stuffs!
Honestly, I'd like to see a possible sequel to this game, as there is SOME level of talent and competence in the people who made it and there's a lot of potential with this kind of material (despite my frustration with this game, I'd still be interested in seeing levels for the Neo Geo, Turbografx-16/PC Engine, Game Boy Advance, Possibly even 5th Generation Consoles, or... Dare I say it... Retro-Like Indie Games from the 2000s and the 2010s!)
But unless they fix up the issue with Collectible Progress (preferably by taking the suggestion I made eariler) and maybe fix a few Glitches I noticed while playing through this, I wouldn't recommend the game unless you're REEEEAAAALLLY interested in the concept...

A solid point and click puzzler. Story is interesting and captivating, voice acting is believable, and the puzzles are creative. The music is a bit dull, but given the atmosphere and thrilling overtones of the game I think it fits rather well. I was assuming to see a lot of the typical "surprises" that have become cliche in this kind of story, but encountered absolutely none of them. You are, quite literally, an average Joe. You're also the very last person anyone wants around to help them, and they tell you this several times. It's a nice change from the "Chosen One" scenery the market is saturated with.
There are only a couple downsides to this. It's really short. Actual play time was probably ~2-3 hours, most of that spent getting stuck because I forgot that I could time-travel. The ending was a little lacluster, though not at all disappointing. It just seemed a bit dull compared to the rest of the game, but you are an average Joe, so it makes more sense that way.
Overall, this game was definitely worth it, at least for a once-through. I give it an 8/10. It'd be an easy 9, if not for it being so short.

I really enjoyed The Silent Age!
The mechanics are single mouse button play, and logic puzzles. The plot moves along smoothly, and it rewards players who, like me, click on everything twenty times to see what changes in the dialog. It's got enough 70's funk to make it campy fun, too, and the main character is adorably stupid about what he falls headlong into. The puzzles aren't too hard, though I got stuck for stupid reasons a few times, which is standard procedure on most point and clicks, but the story more than makes up for the quick pace. The voice acting is good, as well, which can be a deal breaker for me, and I was satisfied with it even though it is kind of sporadic. I really recommend it, but the fact that I bought it on sale does make a difference because it its a pretty short game for the regular ten dollar price tag.

For me, I didn't receive the nostalgia effect as I expected. It just feels like another modern 8-bit platformer where each level has a different theme. The player mechanics never seemed to change on each machine, breaking the illusion you're actually playing on a different platform, if that makes sense.
So in the end it just felt like I was playing a bog-standard platformer with uninteresting level design and a box-shaped character.
If you do like pixel art platformers, and don't really care for the nostalgia aspect, then you might still enjoy this. If you're expecting to feel like you're playing on the machine the theme is telling you it is, then you will probably be disappointed like myself.
Overall, Life of Pixel does have an appealing design, and I liked the menu layout where you can pick the platform and level. My USB snes controller (Buffalo) was picked up automatically which was a huge plus, too.

Life of Pixel is a very nice homage to the retro games of the 80s and 90s in terms of graphics styles based on the Levels you play in certain Console Eras. It's a simple game of collecting items in order to get to the exit of the level. If you manage to beat each Console Era levels, you'll get access to even more consoles like Genesis and Sega Master System and SNES for starters. Some sequences can be tricky in the levels as you progress of course but not really annoying to do.
For its price, it might be worth getting if you like classic style platformers. I got it on sale before though so It's up to you if you want to spend full price. I can still recommend playing it regardless for nostalgia reasons.
Graphics: For trying to copy the style of the Console Graphics, I'll give it 9.0 out of 10.0
Sound and Music: Music tries to fit certain consoles eras. I'll give it 8.5 out of 10.0 for the nostalgia in style.
Replayablity: Well, once you beat the first set of consoles available of the start (8 Consoles), you'll be able to play more 16 bit Style Levels of different Consoles. I'm still on the SNES levels. After beating the whole thing, can't say if It's good to replay again. Only if you want to replay the levels for fastest time to complete a level. Pretty sure it has leaderboards for it. I personally don't care to try to beat for best time. 8.0 out of 10.0
Gameplay: It does its purpose of Collecting items to complete level. There are secrets in nearly every other level so talk to the Blue Pixel Dude who gives hints to find these secrets in order to collect Candy/Snacks for being able to access more consoles so have a look out for hidden spots or places. You also get to use jetpacks, Cars, and more to keep it slightly more interesting. 7.5 out of 10.0
I'll rate this game a B or slightly a B+.

Warning: Disliking this game is an inadvisable course of action. The Organization has eyes everywhere. They are always watching. And if you make yourself known to them by such a negative opinion, then you may very well never be seen again...
...At least, that's what Okabe would have you believe. What a crazy deluded conspiracy nutter. Or is he? o_o
Anyway, this will actually be my 4th playthrough of this game since I have owned the JAST version of this game on PC for the past 2 years. And yet I was more than willing to buy this game again anyway even though not only is there nothing wrong with my JAST version, it's still installed on this PC. That should pretty much tell you how much I like this game.
The game starts off fairly slow as the characters/world are introduced and fleshed out, but soon leads to serious plot events that only intensify over time. Both the story this game tells and it's characters are of the highest quality. And while that might not be immediately apparent in the prologue chapter, it will become inescapable the further you play through the game. By the time you finish it, I can say with confidence that, aside from the rarest of cases, you will have enjoyed this very much. :D
For those out there who have seen the anime adaptation of this game, you can consider this game to be, in essence, the "full version" of that story. The adaptation did a damn fine job, but not everything could make its way into the anime, of course. Plotlines that might have seemed a bit short are expanded here (Luka and especially Faris get more screentime), and... perhaps some new things lurk to surprise you as well! But that is for me to know and you to learn for yourself. :)
If there is one negative I have to say, however, it's that the port job for this is... bleh. Which I completely do not understand. The JAST version, despite the distaste that comes from buying from a site that basically sells eroges and nothing else, is perfectly functional and easy to play on PC. The bits of this I have played so far... just hasn't been as good. I don't know why they decided to mess with this Steam release when there was already a perfectly functional version of this game on PC that didn't feel like a crappy console port. All they had to do was keep the interface that JAST had, and nobody would be complaining that this was a "bad port". *sigh* Why do game devs/publishers keep screwing up easy things that taint otherwise superb games? Maybe I'm just irritated because this is too soon since Mankind Divided, but still...
But, ultimately, none of that messes up the fact that this game is amazing. At least since it's a VN you won't actually be forced to mess around too much with the lame porting. Just sit back and enjoy the game. :D
If you have an interest in visual novels, excellent characters, and a story that may stay with you long after you finish the game itself... then this is what you are seeking. I cannot recommend this game enough. Steins;Gate stands among the best VN's you could ever play.

Starts off great, but gets rapidly more and more and more annoying. The controls are good, the idea is good...the game is quite pleasant. And, perhaps that's the problem. The graphics change as you advance through the consoles, but the gameplay remains pretty much exactly the same. There's very little variance...and the experience isn't a great one. They've given us all the bad parts of the old games, with very little of the good stuff. Yes, games used to be incredibly frustrating, but why go to the trouble of deliberately making a modern game like that for the sake of authenticity? What's next? Paddle controllers?

This game took an amazing concept and did nothing with it.
Imagine, bite sized chunks of game consoles in the 80s and early 90s. Experience what it was like to play an Amiga or ZX Spectrum game, but with original content. Hear the (seemingly?) authentic music, see the (mostly) accurate visuals. Watch as video games grow and evolve from simple dots and lines to gorgeous, expansive worlds.
Except instead of that, we basically play variations of the exact same level over and over. Collect the dots, find hidden secrets, try not to die as you reach the exit. Sorry, try not to get -hit-, especially if it's near the start. You may as well just leap into the nearest waist deep pool and start over. Or, since there's an awful lot of leaps of faith and retracting spikes, be preparred to do that anyways. A lot.
Let me say this up front, the game looks and sounds amazing. I loved stepping into each console and getting a brief blurb about it followed by playing a level or two. At least I did up until a point, but the initial excitement before going into that first level of a console is still there.
What hurts the game and is pretty much the entire problem is that the level designs are horrible. Perhaps some of that is meant to emulate an authentically frustrating experience, but there were actually a lot of well designed games they could've taken some better inspirations from. Which is interesting, since they name drop a lot of titles that were, in fact, generally better laid out than the levels they're based on.
Also, many platformers, even on the NES and especially the SNES, had checkpoints. That's kind of a must once you start reaching longer and harder levels. Not -every- game relied on jumps you couldn't see properly or hidden spikes. And believe it or not, games don't normally make you wait a minute for a bat to move away from a damned platform. Basically what I'm saying is only the graphics and music evolve. The gameplay never changes, only gets more and more absurd.
Let me give you the example that finally made me through up my hands. I'm playing the second SNES level, I've already done absolutely everything else from the previous consoles, even the hardcore stuff. The SNES seems to introduce out of sync retracting spikes of varying speeds. A little ways into the second level there are blocks with spikes coming out above, below and sideways. Now, you're supposed to be able to time these jumps when one set of spikes isn't there, but because of the timing being broken there's never a moment when they're not. I sat there for a minute waiting to see if they'd fix themselves but an opening never presented itself.
I believe the trick with these situations is to reload the level and hope for better, but after everything else I'd already endured I really didn't feel like gambling even more of my sanity with the RNG gods.
Ultimately, whether you'll like this game boils down to how much crap you're willing to accept. I'm particularly bitter cause I really had high hopes for this game given the concept. I mean, I lived through those eras, I guess I just expected something better than what we got.

"Hey, bro, I brought out my Wii U." "Great! I don't feel like Smash Bros. Let's play some Mario Kart 8!"
*2 minutes later*
"What the hell??? Drifting does almost NOTHING. AND I just got hit by a red shell, and knocked off a cliff."
*2 minutes later*
"Oh, come on. I can't even tell how the CPUs are making those turns. And I was NOT getting useful items. This...this game is NOT as good as I remember. I honestly think Sonic Transformed was more fun."
An excellent addition for anyone looking for a good party racer, Sonic and the Long Name is like Mario Kart, but with much less focus on picking out a random racer to punish, and more of a focus on racing well. The game's various items tend not to mess players up as much, and are more focused on increasing your speed. The few offense-focused items  either require skill on the part of the user, or can be negated through skillful awareness of their target. (For instance, the Blue Shell is replaced with a "hornet swarm" that all players will need to avoid, and can be dodged by a good driver) They even have more interesting boosting mechanics than Mario Kart - doing one or more tricks in a jump, performing a drift for several seconds, going off a boost pad, or even barrel-rolling away from an obstacle, all grant a bonus boost effect.
Local co-op support is on-par, making this a good Big Picture game.

A satisfying game clearly inspired by Shadow of the Colossus and Dark Souls.  Like Shadow of the Colossus, you will find the world barren except for boss fights (don't expect any climbing mechanics, though).  Like Dark Souls, these boss fights will be difficult but very possible to master once you get to know your opponent.
The most interesting aspect of Titan Souls is the design constraints followed by the developers.  Your character has three abilities: dodgeroll, shoot an arrow, and call the arrow back to you.  You are killed in one hit but--and this is the interesting part--so are the bosses.  Most boss fights manage to feel unique by exploiting a game mechanic or having novel movements or attacks.
Titan Souls does not reach the heights of either of its influences, but it works as an homage.  The game took me a few hours to beat on my first playthrough, but an experienced player could theoretically finish it much more quickly.

First off: this is from the perspective of a person who got the game on sale and played it with a controller.
The opening of this game gives you the impress that it might be easy with its two simple game mechanics. A button to shoot an arrow and a roll button.
This game is hard. It's still hard whether you play it with a controller or a keyboard. You can shoot your arrow in any direction with a controller but with a keyboard your aim is limited to a 45 degree angle. It's comparatively unfair but aiming is part of the challenge.
It's a beautiful open world to explore with no other enemies except for the 19 bosses, each one being unique with its own set of attack patterns and ways of defeating it. You'll die a lot in the game but the respawn point is never too far away from the area's set of bosses.
The wall art and ruined/overgrown structures in some environments tells you bits of a story and there's a cryptic message from one of the titans that gives you an idea of who the character is. It's open enough so you can toss around ideas in your head and let your imagination run wild.
A fun yet challenging little game with a suprising amount fo depth.

From Ebullience Games comes AIRIS, a science fiction fantasy otome novel. Released in 2017, AIRIS is voted mostly positive on the Steam Store and, after playing it, I can easily say it is for good reason.
In AIRIS, you play as Aliya, a warrior dedicated to protecting her plague ridden country, AIRIS. Ever since you joined Airis’ Vassals, she has trained constantly, hoping to one day become the best warrior in the land. However, recently, Aliya has been suffering from blackouts with absolutely no idea what has caused them. Determined to get to the bottom of her problem, Aliya works furiously to find some kind of cure – but she finds something else instead. Things about her friends, her country and the cause of the plague that ruined her country in the first place.
I went into this without knowing anything about it, which is how I like to play games. Don’t give yourself a high standard, don’t give yourself a low standing – go in with an open mind and discover what it’s like for yourself. I knew that Ebullience Games also released Red String of Fate, another romance, fantasy otome novel that I highly enjoyed – so I did have quite a few high hopes for this.
And the high hopes paid off.
I have never been more moved by an otome novel than I was by AIRIS. The routes are all absolutely spectacular and it took me some time to completely finish this off, I was so moved. This is the first game I have come across that has taken the time to do a route for both a male and a female – and a gender neutral character. Lyall was a total surprise for me and the first time I saw them referred to as “they”, I honestly teared up. It was an absolutely wonderful surprise and if you’re a non binary gamer like myself, this might be just the game you want to play.
The story lines in this were absolutely wonderful. I fully enjoyed every single route I played, and had my breath taken away so many times. Each route, although similar in endings, was wonderfully written, with such plot twists and romance scenes that I actually found myself crying at some of them. It did get quite boring sometimes, following the same route two or three times for different achievements, but luckily, there’s a save feature.
The character designs are also something that I really enjoyed about this. They may be quite simple but they were really well done, and I almost felt like I could walk down the street and bump into the main four characters. I honestly fell in love with the character designs and their personalities went so well for them. It all really joined together perfectly, and it was so well done.
Considering this was done in a single month, I’m honestly speechless. Ebullience Games did amazingly with this, and I cannot wait for their next game release – hopefully, it should be The Masquerade Killer.
I would definitely recommend this to check out, and Ebullience Games are definitely a company you should keep an eye on.

I play a lot of visual novels and I'll be the first to say that I'm fairly picky, and this isn't among my favorite. That being said, it's still a well-done game with enough things to keep me interested until I complete it. The most admirable element of it is the premise and writing quality. While I don't follow the character development and intimate dialogue tension as much as in other games, I do feel involved in the world it's written in, like the premise wasn't just an afterthought for creating some sort of romance. That's a feature that I can appreciate. It's a bit longer of a game, but there's enough choices that it doesn't feel like I'm just reading the story and the text does seem to actually correspond to the choices, unlike lesser games I've played.
If you're looking for a nice fantasy adventure experience with a handful of interesting characters and gender diversity, this is a good pick well worth your time for its wallet-busting price of absolutely free with more work than you would expect behind such a product.

Without a doubt development done right.
The game itself is amazing, does it rely on everyone on the battle field to win, yep. Does it rely on communication, you bet. Does it get your heart racing, sure does. Does it implement a real combat feel, hell yeah.
But hands down... the most important aspect of this game is the development team. Development directly involves those who play the game, all input is taken into consideration and furthermore, development is being done right.
You want new content, more vehicles, more physics? It will come, but it will be developed correcty. Time and time again new content is released, and the next couple months after that is fixing bugs found with the new released content. The development team doesn't give you more content until the previous is IMHO flawless. This is how development should work, add content, let players test it, take feedback, make bug fixes, iron out the kinks and move on. Not, add content, fix major bugs, add more content, fix those bugs.... etc.
Developemnt done right, and it shows. The game is off the charts awesome, every game will provide an immersive environment like never before. The learning curve can be steap, but 99% of people who play, are willing to help you out. So buy the game, get out on the battlefield, and FSU!

My day 3 of Squad:
Hop into a game on the side of US forces, join squad Bravo and pick medic. Immediately squad arguing about who (has to) lead the squad. After a good while a young american man with 100 hours gets to take the lead. SL tells us not to spawn so he and one of other squad member can quickly get into position with a single car and lay down a rally point. good enough. so... rest of the squad watches as our two heroes TRY to make it to the objective, Radio tower. They crash douzens of times, argue who gets to drive and take wrong turns. We're just laughing our asses off and one squadmate remarks that he doesnt think we're gonna win this one.
After a really, really good while, our two heroes crash into the middle of a farm field and rest of us get to spawn. Radio tower is most certainly already inhabitated by the enemy but we manage to sneak right next to their sandbags. After 5 minutes of screaming, cursing and laughing our asses off we cap Radio tower and it becomes our job to defend it with Squad Alpha.
We try and get some sandbags on the ground together out in the open.  But then... a faint whistling sound is to be heard in the air. "MOORTAAARS, INCOMIIING" explodes our local radio with as everyone starts sprinting for the fear of their lives. Few of my teammates and half of squad Alpha become ashes before my own eyes. The air is filled with the sound of russian regards and we can't even hear our own thoughts. We stare at the bodies of our friends getting bombarded relentlessly who yell "MAMAAA" in to the local radio. Then. Silence. I'm almost certain more is coming but I risk to save the lives of my mates. While reviving my 2nd mate I start to hear a fear inducing sound again. I press B and calmly say "it was nice knowing you guys". A second later I am no more and my squad bursts into laughter.
After that we hear that the other squads have secured another FOB and we are free to continue our journey across wheat fields. Every now and then I could swear I heard whistling in the air but no, it was just my imagination. During the last 15 minutes we make a last push and are met with victory screen. Im left staring at the screen.

Very rarely does a game that seeks to be "retro" pull it off. Life of Pixel should be one of the gold standards to anyone looking to do a proper "new retro" game. The designers have done a brilliant job creating levels in the same spirit and theme of original hardware of bygone eras, even so much as replicating the color bleed of the ZX Spectrum. There are also quite a few nuanced things they got right as well such as color palettes and sound emulation. When so many developers get "new retro" wrong, it really makes games such as this one stand out in a good way.
You'll have as much fun playing Life of Pixel as you will in identifying all the cameos and homages to old hardware and games.
