This is a masterpiece. The finest game Telltale has produced. Whilst the Walking Dead is (though very good) kinda bleak and very sad this game just wants you to have fun with it. Practically every line of dialogue is guaranteed to have something that will make you laugh, smirk, half-smirk or at least smile inwardly. There's a couple of jokes that fell flat in the first episode but that's such a small percentage considering everything is funny.
It does some very funny and clever things, for example, the story is being told to another character by the two protagonists Rhys and Fiona as they've been captured. They will lie and argue with eachother over how things went down and you'll sometimes see the same scene twice, once with a highly unrealistic version of what happened and then again with what really happened. Also the first time you die, your captor will raise an eyebrow (okay maybe, he's wearing a mask- (his/her identity is a major plot point) and Rhys will say "Okay, maybe I didn't die, but I could have!"
It really captures the Borderlands feel, from the way it introduces the characters with their name coming up and a little subtitle, to the intros. The musical intros are perfect- in true Borderlands spirit. The first one in particular makes you feel so cool, the second one is sleek as well. The third (my favourite) one feels like a road trip movie, the fourth is just playing with the by now established characters, and the fifth one is more melancholy. They are all awesome
Leading me to my next point. It is consistently funny, but it'll play with your whole emotional range. There's some cute, incredibly awkward romance, a little bit of tension, some sadness (it made me sniffle once) and some ridiculous over the top silliness. You'll come out feeling very fond of this cast of brilliant, funny characters and I can imagine many people will have different favourites- mine's Sasha, or maybe the robots.
Your choices- well, they don't effect the main storyline thaaaat much- (but when do they ever in these kinds of games? I've made my peace with that) although there are some scenes that you'll miss out on depending on your choices. There is a bit of replay value then, because as I've hopefully made clear, everything in this game is funny. If you were to replay it you could pick all different dialogue options and get different witty retorts and rejoinders from the characters. Whereas in the other telltale games it's a little disappointing when your dialogue options don't make a massive difference, it's okay here because really you're just picking the option you think will lead to the funniest punchline.
I only wish this was getting the attention it so readily deserves. My personal GOTY
Also if people could stop buying the game thinking it's a borderlands sequel and then down-voting it THAT'D BE GREAT

Titan Souls is a game that is all about fighting bosses. The game has about 20 bosses and most of them can be defeated in just a single hit. Now that sounds like the game would be really easy but the baddies are pretty good at guarding their weakspot. For most bosses it took me multiple tries to understand what i had to do and then a bunch more tries to actually execute my strategy to defeat them, however when you finally get a kill it is very satisfying. The controls are simple and good but your character is deliberately poorly prepared for fighting, he only brought a single arrow to defeat a bunch of huge titans.
The game is short, it took me about 5 hours to get the "real ending" but after you beat the game once you can replay the game on hard mode, no roll mode or 1 life only mode, none of these are too exciting but at least it offers some replayability.
Things i disliked:
While the fighting system is good for the most part, the 1 hit kill system sometimes allows you to kill a boss by accident without even understanding the mechanics of the bossfight. After you have defeated a boss he is gone that means if you want to fight the boss again you have to make another savefile and beat the tutorial again to get another try at that boss.
The game has a superficial overworld and the game forces you to walk 5-10 seconds after each death instead of respawning you directly in front of a boss fight, about an hour of my 5 hours of playtime was just walking back to fights.
Summary:
All in all i enjoyed titan souls, i often found myself "just trying one more time" until i eventually beat the game. If you are looking for a short but well designed experience this is the game for you.

Senran Kagura: Shinovi Versus
Score: 7.5/10
TLDR: Senran Kagura is the by product of a game developer who figured out you could play Dynasty Warriors one handed, so modded it with Ikki Tousen skins so he could jerk it with the other hand.
Overview: Senran Kagura is a fast, action packed beat em up where schools of Ninja Girls beat the pants off of eachother. Literally beat the pants off of eachother. As a character takes damage, their clothes blast apart like they were made of toilet paper. What could have been a fun concept in a good game actually ends up bogging down the battles. It's relatively short, taking only 45 minutes to beat it, and about 12 hours to finishthe game.
Gameplay: The game is a simple beat em up with light and heavy attacks, high combo strings and 3-4 specials per character. Its extremely fast and very fluid, especially in 60 FPS. Even thought he combo lists are limited, it still feels fun even if it does get a little competitive. Theres a big list of characters, and 2-4 player battles can be made of different squads allowing for some diversity between matches. Another plus is that the hard mode is actually really challenging.
Visuals: The game runs standard Chibi renders of characters that are fitting of the handheld games they came from. It looks good and plays out smoothly, but it's obvious where the money in this game went. Jiggle Physics. Seriously, the bouncing boobs were given more attention than basic walking animations, to the point where they act more like paper bags floating on a draft than actual breasts.
Audio: The soundtrack to this game is about what you would expect. Japanese sounding wood blocks and flutes, pretty much any song that didn't make it into Naruto: Ultimate Ninja Storm. On the bright side, the soundtrack has a few upbeat songs that let you know when a cut scene just isn't important, allowing you to skip it immediately (which will be explained momentarily). Despite the overall generic music, there were a few tracks during the final battles that genuinely hyped me up, and the voice acting was overall well done.
Story: So the plot to this games is about as generic as it can get. One ninja school gets challenged to battle by another ninja school, and for whatever Anime♥♥♥♥♥reason, the losing school gets their Dojo burned down. This eventually becomes a battle of Good and Evil; a life and death for all of humanity because, well, ANIME. Half the plot you can skip because it's just more generic anime tropes and the music tells you when the scene is just going to be boob talk or some awkward lesbian innuendo. In the final scene one of the characters, after a life and death battle is legitimately: “let's go take a bath. Even you, my enemies should join!” I shouldn't even have to explain why that's groan city. However seeing the characters trying to argue about good, evil and honor while little chibi faces cover their gazunkas is pretty amusing.
-That being said the overall themes of good and evil, fighting for equality are campy that they actually come off as endearing, cheesy as they may be. And as much as I hate to admit it there is decent character growth and development through the short playtime.
My biggest gripe with this game is the insane amount of fanservice. While I understand that its a theme (i guess?) of the game, I don’t enjoy being stopped mid combo to see tig ol bitties popping out of a shirt as often as they do. Maybe 1 or 2 times in a fight would be fine but the amount currently in the game is exhausting. You break your enemies clothes two times during a fight, they transform, and then there are two more layers to break through, not to mention transformation and layer breaks on the player character. So that's 10 combos interrupted within the short span of a 2 minute fight. If you could disable the special animations the game would be much more fluid and enjoyable.
Other:
-The main reason to continue playing after the story is hard mode, which is surprisingly challenging. Other than that, each character has their own set of side quests to power through or you can rack up money to buy new clothes and hair for the characters. Not my thing but it's a reason to keep playing.
Overall if you like beating the ever living crap out of enemies, lighting fast boss battles and 3000+ combos, then this game may be right up your alley. Provided you can look past the the jigglies, you have a fun campy beat Em up that's worth picking up on a sale.

Note: I haven't finished the game yet, and I'm not even close; but I thought I'd review this game anyway, because I plan on finishing it and it'd take a lot to change my current opinions about this game.
First off I love this game, its humor down to its exploration to how everything is delivered, I'd say this game is a definite buy if you like references, funny dialogue and or metroidvania games.
TLDR; A lovely metroidvania game with nice personality, characters, and dialogue. Always makes you want more, with very few downsides. Its worth the purchase on or off sale, I've had a lot of fun with this so far. P.S Thanks Mike!
Positives:
- Dialogue: Its nicely put together and makes you want to see the next lines. The interactions between the characters are amazing.
- Humor: full of references across the board for "nerds" I guess, but you're bound to understand at least one of     them in this day and age (I'm not really.. up to date on anything, and I got a lot of the references and laughs)
- Simple, but challenging:Nothing really complex, enemy patterns, to weapon types being effective or not so effective on specific enemies.
- Enemy variety: Okay variety of enemies, all with different ranges, weaknesses and strengths.
- Secrets: Lots of nice secrets that you can find(May be a positive or a negative, Not sure, depends on the person but I love it)
- Characters: Man, these characters are hilarious, this kind of goes hand and hand with the dialogue. Just love these characters, can't help to like the character I'm playing too. Hes pretty funny as well.
- Combat system: Although a bit of a double edged sword here, at times this combat system seems nice, but at others it seems pretty gimmicky. I personally like it, but it feels like you have to change play styles on the fly a lot.
Negatives:
- The soundtrack: To me, didn't feel memorable at all. I can't really remember much, even after recently just playing it.
- Combat system: I feel it is a bit gimmicky, but its not all bad. I think just some status effects are pretty brutal, but besides those its still pretty good.
- Jumping system: This just feels hard to use, and a bit awkward at times. Its not terrible but most games usually grant you the option to redirect your jump. Its okay, I think its just more realistic if anything.
Conclusion
A great game that teaches you to remember your surroundings and punishes you if you aren't cautious. It has hardly any negatives to it besides a few nitpicky things about it. I think the only real draw back to this game is it isn't accompanied by a great sound track. Besides that, this is a fantastic game with lots of personality and I love it. I got this as a gift, and I enjoyed it immensely, I think its worth a buy during or even without a sale.
P.S Thanks again Mike! I really appreciate reviewing something great like this.

I really wish I could recommend this, but there's just too much bad mixed in with the awesome.
-You can make your own character. Let's be real, this is the main selling point and it's ♥♥♥♥ing awesome.
-CaC has 5 different races with unique racials and quite a few different costumes to play dress up in. There's a small variety of body types and pieces, so for the most part you'll end up with something that looks close to that OC you made when you were 7.
-It plays like the Budokai Tenkaichi series; it really captures the feeling of Dragon Ball battles. Movement feels great and there are a lot of different movement options available to you.
-3v3 (or more when playing against the AI) is really chaotic and fun, even if it's not perfectly balanced.
-The master system adds some amusing lines from many different characters. Cell would hug you if that's something he did.
-They tried to mix up the story with revisions in history. I always enjoyed the What If story modes in previous Dragon Ball games; in this installment What If
the main story.
-There are so many different supers and ultimates in this game, and quite a few have utility beyond dealing huge damage.
-The servers are absolutely awful. It's unlikely you'll get into the multiplayer lobby on your first 5 tries, and even if you do there's no guarantee you won't be booted back to the title screen after one mission. I cannot stress this enough, you can't even play single player if the servers are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ themselves, which they often are. There's no excuse for this; I should not have to struggle this much to play offline single player even.
-While the CaC is awesome in concept, there are few physical customization options. You will see many characters that look almost identical to your own. This extends to the clothing options. While there are many to choose from, you soon realize how little outfits there really are, especially since many of the lower parts, for instance, are identical except for color changes.
-Combat is very fast paced but also very simplistic. Your combo list is comprised of when you start pressing Y instead of B. Due to the lack of balance, you can breeze through most fights by maxing your Ki Blast Supers parameter and just spamming supers and ultimates. Any depth really comes from loadouts and movement.
-The game seems to lack polish. For instance, when your character turns Super Saiyan your hair doesn't change models, it just turns gold. That was quite a let down. Another example is the dialogue found in story mode. There are numerous typos and scripting errors, and the lip sync simply doesn't exist. Sometimes it's funny (Yamcha will declare that he defeated Cell), but regardless it shows a lack of care.
-The hub world seems very lifeless and flat. The only way to traverse it is by walking or jumping, which does nothing of value. You can't fly or run. While you can pose your character with a handful of emotes, you can't really interact with anybody in the hub world. Chat is restricted to premade phrases, and characters will pop in and out of existance before your very eyes. There's also no guarantee you'll end up in the same instance as your friends, so trying to team up with them can be a little frustrating, especially when paired with the server problems.
-The look of the game is very bright, neon, and harsh in my opinion. It is overwhelmingly bright and full of bloom.
-There seems to be many DLC character packs in the works for this game. While DLC isn't necessarily a bad thing, I doubt the pricing will be fair, especially when they're offering a season pass.
-I praised the game's story mode earlier, but I have to say that as far as What If stories go, this game's story lacks depth. Most revisions of history happen in the prologue of each saga--that is to say you don't actually experience any of these revisions. Mostly what you experience are the same fights that happened in the series, except your enemy will revive 3 or 4 times. They could have done a lot more with this and it's disappointing that the main selling point aside from the CaC is so shallow.
-The grind is real in this game. Due to some messed up RNG, the secondary phase of each quest isn't guaranteed to take place even if you satisfy the requirements. Even if it does happen, you're not guaranteed to get a drop, much less the drop you want that's specific to that mission. This leads to a lot of frustrating repeats of the same mission over and over while you pray that the skill you want finally drops. God help you if you're going for a full outfit. God can't help you if the servers are having a tough day.
Despite the descrepency of pros listed compared to cons listed I really want to recommend this game, but I just can't. I'm glad a Dragon Ball game has been released on PC, and I'm glad they finally implemented a character creation system in a Dragon Ball setting. I have fun when I play this game, but I recognize that the fun I have stems almost entirely from watching my character in action, and it's despite many glaring flaws. That fun is also combined with a large helping of frustration. My hope for this game is that it's the Budokai 1 or Budokai Tenkaichi 1 of the series; those two games were enjoyable but objectively flawed games that led the way to spectacular and inovative second and third installments. A Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 or 3 that followed that pattern would be absolutely astounding.
Finally, if you are a diehard Dragon Ball fan, you will enjoy this game. If that's you then go ahead and get it. You probably won't regret it.

Alright, I've played this game like crazy over the past weekend of launch, and I have to say, it has to be one of the best games within the Dragon Ball series. There are many reasons for my love of the game, however I have a few slight issues at the same time, which I will explain below (long review ahead, I really wanted to put effort into this):
The graphics of this game are easily the most touched up and crispy visuals I've ever seen from the series of games, yet alone most games in general. Beautiful colors, appealing constructions, realistic grounds, buildings, skies, the list goes on. As soon as I saw my first Kamehameha in the game, I realized instantly that the developers of the game heavily made sure there were no dull, unappealing textures or visuals to turn your eyes away, and that a good amount of time went into making it look flashy without overdoing it. Seriously, take a look at some screenshots, those in-game graphics are very smooth and luscious. Graphics options in a game are also a great thing to have as well, right? Well, you've come to right place. Xenoverse has many options to accomodate to many computers, even if you may not have the best PC known out there. Such options include... V-Sync, Frame Rate, Antialiasing, Resolution Size, Motion Blur, Voice Language (English, Japanese), etc. Even if you may possibly worry about how intensive the game may be with its eye-inducing graphics, the options in the game are very flexible to give the gamer his/her best preferred look and feel of gaming. Honestly, the graphics alone made me want to buy the game, but of course, I had to research more into the game before carelessly buying such an expensive title.
Not much to say in this section. Character roster is solid, includes many characters that played major roles within the series, however some may feel disappointed with others being taken out from previous games. Everyone in the game has their own way of having an advantage over others with their movesets and abilities, and can actually stand up to stronger characters, such as Transformation and Fusion characters, which posed as a serious problem in the past games. Stages are easily manuverable and can be explored to your heart's content. Small barriers prevent you from going out of bounds, but mostly the whole battlefield can become your playground for exploring and destruction. Excellent designs and visuals for the stages as well, no problems there.
The gameplay for Xenoverse relies on a previous title, known as Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Z. Personally, I did not like Battle of Z for the new style of fighting it introduced as a whole, and should've been revised before officially being released. However, this game rebuilds the fighting mechanics of its predecessor and greatly improves on the combo system, combo canceling, follow-ups on combos, everything you would expect from a good fighting game. Xenoverse emerges you into a setting where you can feel comfortable trying to string together long, powerful combos to ensure your upper edge on the opponent. Xenoverse also includes a format of fighting that allows you to team up with other players to fight against several forces, bypassing the usual restriction of having to deal with a quest that possibly may be too difficult for just one person. Unlike Battle of Z, the teammates' AI actually attempts to help you by reviving you or other downed allies in battle, even going so far as to following up from a combo that you've done to your opponent! This doesn't mean that you are able to just mash buttons and possibly try to loop your opponent and cause infinites on them. Xenoverse limits this possibility with Ki and Stamina bars, each going up to a certain amount, depending on the characters chosen. You'll have to play smart in order to play effectively with these bars in mind! Overall, I believe the gameplay is very solid and can be picked up easily with only an hour or two of practice.
Mostly every Dragon Ball game out there has a story mode that just shows you a boring timeline and you reenacting the events from the anime. Lame, right? Well, in Xenoverse, you're able to actually able to play through the story that we all know and love, while also having its own twists and turns with a completely new element of story replayability, which shows the events of the anime rewritten to the point where the complete opposite, or even something absolutely different happens! For example, when Goku and Piccolo fight Raditz as the first threat to Earth in Dragon Ball Z, usually Raditz and Goku die from a Special Beam Cannon. The twist of this event includes Raditz escaping Goku and being able to kill both him and Piccolo. This alone brought my attention to the story more than ever, I sat at the edge of my seat waiting to see the other distortions that could occur. You'll have to play the story for yourself to see exactly what could happen with other events, but I would easily recommend knowing the original story before trying to learn the distorted story. I also recommend the story for anyone who would like to experience a detailed, thrilling storyline that makes you wonder what could happen next.
Now, with the story's way of execution explained, character creation is the next subject to get into. Normally, playing with the fabled hero of the specific event you go through in Dragon Ball Z has always been a recurring event that may never get old for some. Xenoverse allows for you to create a character to go through the actual events in a different perspective! With 5 classes to choose from (Saiyan, Namekian, Earthling, Frieza Clansmen, and Majin), the possibilies are quite endless. Though there are only female classes for everything (except the Namekian and Frieza Clansmen), that alone does not bar the imagination someone could have for them. Leveling up is also another bonus the game includes, which gives the character opportunities to become stronger in the areas that are wanted, such as Health, Ki, Stamina, Basic Attacks, Strike Supers, and Ki Blast Supers. Playing through the game at your own pace allows for diversity between how you want to distribute your bonuses to your character to your preference. You're even able to give your custom character special clothing, accessories, and even Z-Souls (given for special advanages, many to find, all are different) to make them stand out more than usual. Very good execution of the system into the game, while overall adding a new experience for new and old fans of Dragon Ball Z.
There's never a game out there that has no problems with it, including an amazing title as this. Personally, I do not feel as though there are many issues with the game, but I do have a few that I would like to point out.
Again, not much, but still deserved to be mentioned.
All in all, I love the way Xenoverse presented itself as a whole to Dragon Ball fans. Excellent music, character roster, stages, character diversity, leveling up, going on quests, having masters from the series, fantastic graphics, suspenseful story, and the ability to play together with your friends. As a player of many previous games in the series, I recommend this game for any fan of it.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a good game, and I recommend it.  I've heard quite a bit about it and the prequel and I think I expected more of The New Order, due to getting a variety of information.
But at the same time, I really like Wolfenstein: The New Order for the most part.  My real problems come from expectation and a few issues with difficulty.  The fact is I found the game to be harder than most players seem to, I started on Uber, and went down to medium, before the halfway point, and finally on the final boss I dropped it to the easiest mode just to get through it (more because I was sick of the repetition).
That's actually a big of a the problem of this game.  You really only fight about 3-4 enemies and they just keep coming.  It's not that the level design is bad, or the game is bad, but the enemies that you fight stay generic from beginning to end.  You fight nazis, robots, and dogs, and more of each of the three of them.  There's some cool fights, there's a couple boss fights, but ultimately they fit in those three categories, and that's a bit of a shame.  There's also no real mention of Hitler (which does get mentioned in the sequel that just came out) but I have to admit I'm curious about the Furher, even if it was to know he's alive and that means I might have a chance to kill him in another game.
The other issue with this game is that while I REALLY liked the characters in the game, and the life bred into them, the story feels almost like it's lacking something.  There's two real problems with it.  First the story seems to be building to a big twist.  You black out at times, you switch from a sex scene to action relatively quickly, you clearly form these emotional relationships with people we don't seen.  If they told me "You never had any friends" I'd believe it.
Problem is, there's no really big twist in the game, the building and the awkwardness of some scenes are just awkwardness.  The love story doesn't really pay off, and I've heard people saying the sex is appropriate in this game... sorry no, it's just sex for sex sake.
The other problem is the story seems to be written by someone who didn't really see the action until after they finished writing.  BJ Blazkowicz, the man character is a rough and tough bad♥♥♥♥♥ and in the cutscenes they try to make it sound like he's a gentle man, there's even points that show him in the first chapter chastising someone else "Another dead because of you." or something.  Again, these things are never paid off. We play him as a total badass from beginning to end, and that's the game.
The world is interesting, if not really explained.  The game starts in 1946, Nazis ultimately win world war 2, the world is run by the Nazis, and everyone stops fighting... There should be good stories here...
And the thing is I LIKE Blazkowicz, I like the female character, I like almost every character in the game.  I felt horrified by one character in the game.  Oh god she kind of scared me and that's a good thing.  So I like the characters, I like the setting a lot, it's a great alternate history, but the narrative itself was lacking.  Well that and the fact that the end boss is ... not who it should have been.  It makes sense who the final fight is against but there's another villain that the game has built up, why not use the villain you developed verses the villain who only appeared once and only had a little development?
But ultimately I liked the game.  Killing Nazis is fun, there is good level design like I mentioned, and the mixture of action to stealth was good, and even the stealth felt right most of the time.  Sometimes a level started and I wasn't sure if I could stealth it, but most of the time the answer was "no, go kill Nazis."  And so I did.
There's a fantastic perk system, where you complete little feats and get little perks, maybe an addition 10 bullets in a magazine, maybe less damage from X, and so on.  None of these are game breaking, but they're a lot of fun to earn, to the point I farmed a number of them on the first stage.
The collectibles were done well, the only real issue I had is some levels had a "commander" that if you kill stealthily you get to see where collectibles are.  A great perk (earned on the first stage farming) but some levels don't have any commanders, so you're eventually going to need a guide for those levels.  Why? Why is the system that's developed to help the obsessive people only available on 90 percent of the game.   The collectibles themselves are great.  Nazi gold, enigma tapes that unlock bonuses, and letters and records.  All good additions to the game and mythos.
There's good action, good amount of violence, nazi killing (which should always be acceptable), good characters, so all in all I like the game.  The gameplay is a mixed bag that worked well.  My trouble came from the fact that the cover shooting isn't my favorite thing.
Well the game surprised me.  After playing doom I love run and gun and wanted it back.  Wolfenstein looked in it's bag and with the first enigma code I got from the collectibles, I got what was called the 999 mode.
You see when you die, you normally revive at a checkpoint, in 999 mode, you revive at the last checkpoint but you get 999 health that will slowly fall back to your max).  Oh and infinite ammo, but the gameplay is on the hardest difficulty (Uber).  THIS right here is a game changer in every meaning of the word.
No longer is cover "mandatory".  No longer is the enemies as dangerous, with 999 life, you can just run and gun the game, and just have fun killing everything you want and ignoring those who you don't care about.  The game changes from a cover based shooter that people are used to, to just a pure action game and the results are glorious.  It's the perfect way to do a second playthrough and I love it.
So without 999 I would still recommend this game because it's good, and while the story tries to be a lot more than it is, it's still a very good game, but with 999 mode, I absolutely adore this game, because they found a way to make it more fun.
And yet you kill Nazis, and if you are a person who dresses up in Hugo Boss uniforms with Swastikas on your shoulders and talk about the master race and how other people are undesirable, and do nazi salutes, and threaten to kill "unworthy people"... yeah you're probably going to be offended by the game (even if it is about a world which has Nazi's winning world war 2).  If however you've been called a nazi, but don't believe in any of the actual Nazi German crap, I'm sorry but this game isn't insulting you.  The German Nazis that this game are about, are a specific group and the game is about killing them.
And you know what?  It's damn enjoyable no matter how many times you do it.
PS. The game is kind of an unoptimized mess, I was still playing with my settings in the final stage when I gave up and set it to low graphics (which still looked good), but still, while voice and audio got desynced during cutscenes and every so often i got a slow mode (that was more to my advantage than anything).  It didn't affect my enjoyment at all.   However it's sad to see the game in a state where I knew for a fact the game was causing more issues than it should have.

First thing's first: it's free.
You're a medieval fantasy warrior in this otome visual novel. It's actually more than that but in the interest of spoilers that's all I'm going to say. You're here to "date" one of your three guildmates. A dude, a dudette, and a "they" because that's cool I guess if you're into that sort of thing, as you unravel the secrets of the world around.
I chose the girl every time, so I can't really say how everyone else's routes were, but for the most part it was worth my time.
The story is good, or at least novel enough for me to overlook a few gaping plot holes. The fact that there's a decent overarching plot progression with ups and downs makes it not get in the way, as long as you don't think about it too hard. Pacing is good. Actions scenes are quick and impactful, and more peaceful situations take the necessary amount of time for you to listen to what the characters have to say. Positive.
The dialogue's a little spotty in places, probably because of the decision to stick with contemporary vernacular in the interest of accessibility. It doesn't sound like it's trying too hard, but the tone is inconsistent at times, and the pages of dialogue doesn't convey as much personality of characters as I'd have liked.
Characters were pretty good, or at least the two I care about. Aliya is a competent yet flawed protagonist whose external influences causes internal struggles, and she goes through a developement arc that we get to see, all very good things. Everea is a strong character as well, somehow acting both as a plot device and an independent entity that reacts properly to the player's choices. She also experience a general shift in tone when communicating with Aliya as their relationships grew. A+
The game system were also adequate, for a visual novel of course. There's a hefty amount of choices here and I'm happy to say that they're represented well enough in the number of endings (12 in total and 4 for each love interest). Naturally I only unlocked 4 so I can only speak for those, but what I've seen has been very well done. The choices all make sense, and their consequences are fairly well justified in-universe.
The art was somewhat all over the place, even in character's expression sometimes. It's the sort of faux-anime style that goes on a lot of artist's blog ever since the plague has taken over, but it's serviceable at the very least. If cuteness is your thing you can excuse most of it.
The music is rather uninspired, though that's about what I expect. There's no glaring issues with the placement or timing, so even if it's a little boring at times that's not a deal breaker. This game is about reading after all.
Overall if you're here for gay you can do a whole lot worse than 90 minutes of free entertainment.

THE SHORT VERSION:

Pros:

Meh issues that are being worked on but aren't quiet cons:
-Theres several bugs that of the time of this writing haven't been totally fixed, such as resetting equipment when you have several items sometimes leads to stuff getting LAUNCHED in the air. Once I got launched without even hitting reset, Just was wrapping around a hill driving my truck with a trailer and it launced both into the WAY up in the air, smashed the hood off my truck, sent my trailer back to the reset area (on it's own) and i never did find 1/2 the contents of my trailer
-Another issue is the crashes, (again at the time of this review) just yesterday i lost about 3 hours progress because i tend (like alot of people) to forget to save regularly
-The bank system needs alot of work, You sale bars of gold at the bank, however after you sale them your money total doesn't update until you back out of the banking system then go back in.
- More banking issue: I found (and most i read have the same issue but NOT ALL); If you take a loan out it automatically takes the balance out daily (which is fine) HOWEVER if you hit it big and can afford to pay the loan off... you can't... The balance drops but doesn't completely pay off, so if you take out a 60 day loan, and 5 days in you strike it rich, you can't pay that loan off and thus wont be able to get another until the day limit expires
-The map can't load all at once- basically everytime you go from town to your claim, or your claim to town about 1/2 way through the game stutters for a good few seconds (it's the game loading the map- a pc built by MIT with no budget won't help you).... if theirs a world where loading takes longer or the game requires better system to avoid it i'd prefer that option
My MAJOR ISSUES (cons):
-No dump trucks..... you're expected to use an excavator ONE SCOOP AT A TIME to load your 1st large washplant.... the excavator drives 5mph, and when you go up hill (which you must to get to your plant) runs LITERALLY 1mph or less on the steep parts.................. My guess is they're forced to do this to prolong the game, but it makes it very very very SLOW grinding...... frankly i'd rather get 1/2 as much gold per yard and have the ability to speed up my mines yards per hour.... this 4 scoops an hour excavator run is TORTURE............my hope is that this game does well enough to warrant an addon pack that includes dump trucks to speed this issue up AND more maps to keep the game interesting and prolong a then shortened timeframe before you're out of stuff to do.......
-Lifeless map.... all this potential, a HUUUUUUGE map, multiple minable claims which you have to rent or buy from multiple different owners, a town, a bank, a store, a gas station, a heavy equipment dealer and NOOOOOOO npcs.... NO store clerk, NO loan officer, NO buisness mean, NOTHING... I'm not at all a game designer but when your game is solely about mining and said equipment there's not ALOT you need to do to fix this issue.... a guy at the store asking you hows the mining.... a guy at the gas station complaining about his trucks being late..... the used cars saleman who decided his new gig would be opening a large equipment dealership..... the greedy fat old banker trying to make 1 more dollar off you..... and as if NO people isn't horrible enough- there's not even any story lines... you walk into these empty buisnesses and just grab what you're looking for and check yourself out..... even if the devs couldnt/wouldnt add npcs for WHATEVER reason i don't for the life of me understand why they couldn't add chat dialogue when you're making these game changing purchases.... like at the store, what if there was a dialogue for ANY large item you bought reminding you to pickup the accessory that goes with it (buy a new water pump? dont forget to grab hose and filter!.... buy a new generator? dont forget to pick up an extension cord and maybe an extender....etc etc)
Conclusion:
This game will never be a sims, or world of warcraft, or league of legends where you play it day in and day out till you're dreaming about it- BUT with an addon, or just outright additions of a few very minor things (compared to what they've already accomplished) this COULD be one of those games you play a cpl times a week, and randomly bring up to your friends, or binge play for 8 hours after watching a real good episode of gold rush, and while i've owned the game less than a week, i would ABSOLUTELY pay twice what it cost to have those few items added- and i hope that message and these critiques make it to someone who has enough pull to make it a topic of discussion in their office

Life of Pixel is a fun, well constructed, lighthearted love letter for a lengthy history of gaming, demonstrating the evolution of graphics and mechanics for a basic one dimensional platformer. The game spans 13 consoles, beginning with the ZX81 and Atari 2600, and ending with the NES, SNES, Sega Master System, and Sega Genesis.
You are a square with a face named Pixel who has befriended an elderly, bespectacled, mustachioed, professorial pixel with a face who often shows up to give hints. Your friendship is based on your interest in the evolution of game systems over time and his knowledge of each, conveniently and informatively passed on to the player when selecting a stage from the appropriate system. Each system has 8 stages, and to progress to the next stage a number of collectables have to be collected, and the exit reached. Additionally gems and special food items can be collected on many stages, which unlock additional systems.
The main joy of the game is getting to play a game with 13 different graphical styles, 13 different bit appropriate musical selections, and some numerous design decisions/flaws/necessities of the past, experiencing the evolution of the artform and the graphical changes in Pixel, the environment and the various enemies in the game. The lower end systems serve as a simple gameplay introduction, being easy, more abstract graphically with low quality music, but this is part of the experience, and each new system seems refreshing for its recognizable advancements and differences. In addition there are a slew of referneces to classic games from the past, as well as some winks and nods to the platforming genre and classic game design, delivered with the classically dry English charm.
The controls are fluid and simple, with a clean double jump and a button for basic item gathering and use. There are also a handful of vehicles ranging from bubbles to skateboards that are used for a number of levels. At no point did I experience any frustration with the controls or jumps. The difficulty scaling is gradual, and the game overall is not designed to be challenging, nor is it ever significantly challenging with most stages completed after a few attempts. Though each stage is small, there are over 100 total stages, meaning that this game has a significant amount of content that can easily satisfy for long enough to justify its price. The stage designs themselves are often rather inspired, and finding secrets is of an appropriate difficulty to neither be frustrating nor overly trivial.
All in all, the game is a delightful experience to play, that is elegantly and thoughtfully presented with evolving audio, visuals, and game design coinciding with the actual development of the systems represented.

Alrite, so Sonic in a racing game. The first thing on your mind is, Sonic R, and yes that was terrible. The next on your mind may be that "its ripping off mario kart" and thats unfair cause there are many kart racers out there.
Anyways, long story short this is different.
Story: There isn't really any to be honest. You play as Sonic, his friends, and some other mascot characters from Sega in a no holds barred racing tournament. Pretty simple in Sega's storytelling record. 7 / 10
Graphics: Pretty good for a racing sequel. The cars look nice, the characters look great, and the many worlds you race in look especially good too. My favorite track has got to be Samba De Amigo's Track, or the Distant Future Track. The transformations from car to boat or plane are decent as well. 8/10
Gameplay: Oh boy.. Now this game isn't bad in fact the controls function like they should...with a few kinks. The cars have a very slippery feel to them so taking wide turns causes swerving if you havent mastered drifting. Drifting is very useful in this game as it really boosts you ahead a great deal. However it cant be utilized everywhere, and certain tracks literally scream "its a BAD idea!" The boat handles a bit clumsily, and often times waves will send you flying off course. When you crash it stops you in your tracks, or sometimes bumps you back. Turning is awful so you really REALLY dont wanna crash using the boat. Now the plane isnt too bad. No inverse controls though, unless changed in options. Crashing is rare, and handling is decent. Thing to keep in mind is that its not as "free" as mario Kart. It feels very "on rails" and you'll find some tracks more linear than others. 6.5/10
Multiplayer: Great fun to play with friends! However , your connection better be smooth. Unless you enjoy glitching through walls, blinking in and out of existence, or other racers teleporting back and forth. 5/10
Extras: Unlocking characters is great fun, though once you get Metal Sonic your almost god like. Upgrading your racer is definitely a must to get through later levels such as the Monkey Ball track. Theres many missions aside from the story mode, so replay is a plus.  The difficulty curve of some racers kinda rocket up so yeah, expect to be frustrated at some later races. Soundtrack is great too! Also if you can get your controller to work it feels alot better control wise.
Overall Score: 6/10  If your looking for an intense racer with crazy perks, then this isnt for you. But if your looking for a casual racer, that can get a lil competitive from time to time then I say this fits.

Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed is the Mario Kart version for the PC. Or better yet, the old Diddy Kong Racing.
Run in a different environments and with different vehicles (car, plane and boat) is very fun and every course and characters brings that old and good feeling to revive the golden hits of the Sega company. It's just to much fun to bring Alex Kidd in the Golden Axe course and the Get Set Radio challenging you for the first place.
The race controls are pretty good, it's very similar to other games with this kart style, but in here you must learn how to drift to keep it up to the competition and earn some boost to make your way to the first place or to beat the time.
The game modes are very nice, you can play only some races, go for tournaments or go on career mode to earn starts and then unlock more courses and characters.
The power ups works the same way we are used to know in this style of game, and they add a good fun element. Some of them you can choose to throw ahead or leave to hit someone behind you.
The sound design is great. Every music and sound effect make all the experience in the race unique and brings the memories of those games.
The level design is awesome! It gives you the feel of movement and speed that is the heart of a race game and it is always changing! In some courses you will see all the landscape and the road being attacked and as the race goes you will change to other paths or even change completely your vehicle to a plane or boat to continue the race. And this is absolutely fantastic!
If you are an orphan of Mario Kart or Diddy Kong Racing (which is better, sorry to say that...) you MUST try this one. It's a great and extremely fun race game.
There may not be a lot of stuff yet, but is is going in the right direction, and i can imagine its better in the futer than every other fps to date.

Forget about this. Nothing the trailer or description promises is actually in the game. I get that this is early access, thus an alpha, but alpha state means the basics are basically implemented albeit in an unpolished and buggy state.
You can't promise a "4 player co-op tactical FPS" inspired by Rainbow Six, when all you get is 8 servers with random team deathmatch, featuring gameplay that would be archaic even by the standards we had 10 years ago.
If you buy this now, this is what you get:
A space marine with sluggish controls (you walk very slow, sprint barely changes speed) ONE weapon and useless features like being able to open your helmet. Multiplayer consists of very basic team deathmatch (good luck finding a non-full server though, there's only 8 of them) that feels very uncomfortable due to the aforementioned controls, which are so archaic, especially for a supposedly "tactical FPS", that it feels like a joke. Quake did control better than this. Seriously, after multiple updates you are now able to jump (meaning, you press space and then akwardly hop a little bit, after a short delay). What's more, you can't lean to the left/right to peek around corners and you're unable to crouch. In a tactical FPS. It's ridiculous.
And don't talk to me about "it's early access, bla, bla", we're talking about basic, most fundamental things missing that really undermines my trust i have in the developer.
Other critics meantioned the fair and balanced maps and online gameplay. Seriously? I just joined a server in which i killed ONE dude and then subsequently got killed as soon as i spawned. The top player in my team? 43 kills. The top players of the enemy team? 389 and 346 kills respectively.
Don't buy it, it's not worth 5 bucks (it's on sale right now) and i'm very doubtful now that this will ever be something akin to a finished game (another critic mentioned that this game is in development since 2009).

Ttain Souls is a 2D isometric game entirely about fighting bosses.
Visually the game is nice to look at and has a nice art style, though it's nothing special or anything we haven't seen before, however, the soundtrack is really quite good, it fits the game very well and gives the game a nice atmosphere, though it's nothing memorable.
Unfortunately when you get to the gameplay, that's when the problems start to show up. Like I mentioned before it's an isometric game in which you fight bosses, there's an overworld that serves no other purpose than to get to the boss fights which feels like something they put in to pad the length of the game since there's no point in exploring it and there barely seems to be any background storytelling of any kind, so it just becomes a matter of getting from the checkpoint to the boss, and that becomes really problematic when you keep dying to a boss and have to walk all the way back to it. There's no reason you couldn't just respawn at the enterance to the boss arena. The overworld is also kind of tricky to navigate, in a bad way though. I was just wandering around trying to find the next boss and all of a sudden I ended up in a completely different area, which made navigation even more confusing afterwards.
The pointlessness of the overworld aside, the combat system in the game is very basic, you have a dodge roll without any invisibilty frames, and you can shoot an arrow, the interesting part is that you have only one arrow which you need to retrieve after shooting. Now the problem arises from the fact that you die in just one hit, so do the bosses, but the bosses have a weak spot usually protected by other stuff, you just flat out die from anything, which is especially problematic because this game has a lot of trial and error involved. You could just walk into a boss room and die quickly by an attack you had no way of predicting and you won't even have the chance to realize what just happend. It'd be nice to have a health bar or at the very least three hits that you can take before dying. The bosses themselves are alright, some have more interesting designs than others and all of which require you to figure out how to kill, which is almost always having to shoot the weak spot, though due to the trial and error nature of it, you'll probably end up dying quite a bit just trying to figure out how to beat the bosses, or you could just walk in and kill them immidietly because the difficulty curve in this game is all over the place, it's difficult for the most part (though it's mainly because of all the wrong reasons), but occasionally really easy.
It's not a bad game by any means, but it has far too many issues for me to recommend it to anyone. If you can deal with the frustration of it and you find the idea of the game interesting enough to try it out, go for it, but only when it's really cheap because the game is also incredibley short, I beat it in less than an hour and a half. Yeah.

Wolfenstein 3D. A first-person action game developed by id Software in 1994. This game is often known as one of the pioneers for the First Person Shooter genre, pushing it towards what it has become today. It drew inspiration from the old 1980’s Castle Wolfenstein games. Wolfenstein 3D put players in the first person perspective and let you run around several levels, shooting Nazis.
Wolfenstein 3D was originally developed for Dos PCs. Back in the day it used the common shareware marketing model that let people play the first episode for free. It has since been re-released and ported to several gaming systems and mobile platforms.
-Story
As with alot of action games at the time, Wolfenstein 3D had a very simple story. You play as William Blazkowicz as you try to take down the Nazi regime. The original game was split up into 3 episodes, having the player work their way through a series of levels, wandering through buildings and caves as you shoot at Nazis, Dogs and Zombies. You had simple goals like escaping a prison, foiling the Regime's plans, and coming to a final confrontation with the Fuhrer himself.
Later releases included the three episode prequel, the Nocturnal Missions, that dealt with German plans for chemical warfare. A Standalone Expansion, The Spear of Destiny, was also a prequel that tasked the player with reclaiming the Spear of Destiny from the Nazis.
-Design:
As a First Person Action Shooter that was developed in the early 90’s, the graphics may be primitive by today's standards, but back in the day compared to other 3D games of the time, the 3d walls and sprites combined with the faster movement blew minds away. Castle and cave walls made up most of the environment that were littered with sprites of furniture, water puddles and enemies. While there is a lot of Nazi imagery in the game, later versions had some alterations such as removing swastikas due to controversy.
The game is divided up into episodes consisting of 9 levels each, as well as a secret level to find. Level design was quite extravagant with several branching paths. It was often like a maze as you tried to find the exit door, coming across some doors that required special keys you needed to find. There are also several secrets hidden throughout, usually behind pushwalls,  with goodies such as gold, ammo, health and sometimes a new weapon. Spear of destiny broke from the episode format by just having a series of 18 levels split into four sections, each ending with a boss.
Gameplay wise, it was a good advancement from other first person titles at the time. For several players tho, the controls may be hard to get used to, with the key configuration being a little awkward. If you want a better experience, I suggest installing a 3rd party engine such as ECWolf, which will allow modern key configuration and higher resolutions. If you prefer to use a controller, the XBLA and PSN versions will work as you expect.
-Verdict:
Wolfenstein 3D is a nice piece of gaming history that put the FPS genre in the direction that it ended up in today. If you can look past the primitive graphics and like to get to know where shooters came from, it is a great buy for $5 on Steam, XBLA and PSN. Or if you need a nice diversion while you're out, $2 on the iTunes app store.

This second free to play otome visual novel from Ebullience Games feature a female protagonist Aliya, a vassal of the magical kingdom of Airis and a warrior member of a guild which accept various fetch, escort and clear dungeon quests. Aliya suffers from periodic blackouts where she would fall asleep and wake up in a different location with no memory of what happened. After being woken up from a blackout by her animal companion Teddy, Aliya decides to investigate the reasons for her blackout experiences through her fellow vassals and guildmates Lyall and Everea as well as Kylan who claims to be a retired vassal and an experimenter who might be able to make a potion to treat Aliya of her blackouts. After returning from a dungeon quest to obtain ingredients for Kylan, the town is suddenly attacked by a horde of creatures where Aliya is separated from the main characters and Aliya(and the player) has to decide on which main character route to take.
Each route will take approximately 1-2 hours. It would be nice to have more save slots in the game as there are many choices in the game and many of the choices affect the ending where each route has 3 possible endings and 1 hidden ending. There is one published community guide to help players to unlock all endings for the ending gallery and get all achievements at the time of this review. Soundtracks, CGs and overall game presentation are good after factoring in appropriate background music for the romance and mystery themes in the story, the use of chibis and CGs showing small movements in the protagonist and a main character. Recommended as a free to play visual novel for those who like a visual novel with romance, mystery and humour in the story or for those who like a short game to finish and get all achievements in less than 10 hours.

I am a huge fan of Point&Click Adventures but this game didn't click with me.
It starts with the animations for me. The characters seem so stale in this game. Character barely move while talking or idling and the main character has such a limited variation of poses. When you go through doors, your character just stays there and the screen fades out. Even Monkey Island showed Guybrushs back and that game is ages old. There is voice-acting but only partially. It was absolutely necessary to have it, though because otherwise you would have no idea how people felt. No facial expressions, no gestures, nothing.
The artstyle could be okay but coupled with the lack of animations it seems more like an alpha version of the game. It needed some polish before it got shipped. Right now, there a lack of athmosphere. The places don't seem interesting to me. I wish I could put my finger on the exact problem because in screenshots the game looks great.
I did a full playthrough anyways just so I could see if it was any good apart from the poor animations and bland artstyle. Finishing the game takes only about 2 hours and the puzzles are really, really simple so that wasn't too hard. And sadly I can't say it was worth it. The plot in itself is quite interesting but the presentation and the writing are lacking. Dialogues feel really clunky and the few characters you meet in this game are shallow, uninteresting and unconvincing in my opinion. There is no real tension because the build-up is done poorly.
The gameplay is nothing special as well and consist largely of walking through rooms, clicking on things and a lot of backtracking. You have a maximum of three things at once in your inventory, every item just has one purpose and breaks immediately after its use. There are a few clever puzzles but most of them are pretty straightforward and just seem to waste your time executing them. You click on everything until you finally find something you can pick up and then you have to do some trial-and-error where you can use that item on. Sometimes you just have to click your way through because you have no idea. You get items like a hammer and there is just one thing you can use the hammer on. But you have no clue what you want to achieve with that hammer and the solution is arbitrary. It is just a key-lock thing. Often they don't even bother to disguise it, you just get a key and have to find the fitting lock. Literally.

Truly an exceptional FPS.
It's not perfect and it's got some flaws in the core combat & stealth. Sometimes it leans a tad heavily on cutscenes to tell story over in-game action & narration. That's basically all the flaws I have.
The story is pretty damn unique in its execution and tone. The game keeps a perfect balance between serious reality and levity. The weapons all feel great to shoot- especially the standard assault rifle that'll carry you through most of the game. The combination of high-speed sliding, quick melee takedowns, destructible cover, dual-wielding & a flexible peek-from-cover system means that the game always feels dynamic even when you're pinned down behind a wall getting shot at from six different angles. Levels are thematically & visually varied, at least to an extent, and although enemy types are limited the arena layouts mean W:TNO simply doesn't NEED the strong enemy variety of Half Life or Doom.
My biggest endorsement of all, however, goes to the game's narrative and characterisation. There's plenty of good shooters, there's plenty of good WWII games. TNO, however, is a nazi-slaying dieselpunk adventure that manages to somehow make the crazy moments seem crazy (like fighting giant robots with a laser minigun) and the serious dramatic moments feel serious and dramatic (like staging a breakout at a concentration camp).
Wolfenstein: The New Order isn't perfect, but was well worth the price of admission at launch and is definitely worth it now. If you've seen the sequel and aren't 100% on dropping about $90 AUD on it, consider picking this one up first.

TL;DR At first I thought, this was going to be another "Simulator" trash game, but I feel like the devs really want to make a good game. They do have a solid base, which is far from trash. And if they do as they say they want to, fix the issues that have become apparent after launch, and then add content, my hopes is that Gold Rush is going to be a pretty good game worth buying.
You get exactly what they tell you. You do "work hard" (spend time playing) to earn money as a gold miner. Contrary to popular belief, it's not as simple as hacking on a resource node using a pickaxe. Digging dirt with a shovel, excavator, or front-loader can be repetitive, and you might not enjoy operating machinery for hours. I do.
Unfortunately, the game launched in a rather sorry state with many small and big problems, that really need to be addressed and fixed. But it has also been treated unfairly by claiming, it doesn't tell you what to do, or display the (rebindable) control scheme. The developer apparently had to implement message boxes for the blind, who didn't find the "journal" giving you directions, the in-game video showcases (Dig-Tube), and the "press Z to show controls for your current vehicle/your character" in the bottom left of the screen.
But even with all those little problems yet (e.g. getting stuck walking on uneven dirt, at the edge of sidewalks even, bulldozer also getting stuck in tiny dirt spikes, sound stuttering, dozer and front-loader handling), the game really shines with its details that steadily become apparent, and are fun to play with. I'd proably spoil the game if I listed them all here (e.g. drive to gas/petrol station, get out of car, open fuel door/tank cap, take nozzle from pump, put in tank, choose amount to refuel VS just "press E to refuel").
Luckily I haven't had any game crashes, corrupt save games, or exploding pickup trucks due to crazy physics. Although my excavator wanted to fly off sometimes when jamming the bucket in the dirt, but the game was like "that seems wrong" and reset it immediately. And the sound stuttering made me take a break and wait for updates, because that's just horrible to listen to. I really hope it was only released because they needed the launch money to survive and stick to developing the game, which was a Kickstarter project.

The parts offered in it's sandbox setting are very limited and sparse, making cusomization difficult. Just how "armor" works in this game is unclear, along with how much damage weapons even do. *FYI, machine guns rule this game right now. Everything else is irrelevant* It includes a sort of crafting interface, which requires "rent" on it. Basically, the closest thing to a centeral currency in this game is required in quite vast quantities to just craft items.
In all, this game falls victim to the same problem that all other sandbox "shooters" do: Your designs will suck. It doesn't matter. You could directly copy another persons vehicle, and you will still lose. I actually found the Match Maker to be somewhat okay, but it will seem that it's unbalanced due to your creativity, I guess.

My advice: try it, but don't commit much money into it right now. I would wait until at least the full launch. (In case you didn't already know, it's in Open Beta, supposedly). If you like it, great. Tamsoft knows how to make satisfying combat systems, usually focusing on half naked ladies (Oneechanbara: Bikini Samurai Squad is their creation for example) Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus benefits from all their expertise with prior ecchi-action games. Even though there is a lot of cheesecake the combat is not compromised and is really well done.
There are lots of characters to play as and plenty of costumes, music and artwork to unlock. It uses the Visual Novel technique for story-telling, and the story is stupid of course but still enough to keep you moving with objectives and character motivation. There are three schools, each with thier own story and perspective. On top of that each character has thier own side story you can play though to see a more personal story outside of the overarching theme of the competition.
While I don't find any of the characters as interesting as Neptune from HDN, they are some solid choices for Waifu material, in fact I see no lack of options. I think all the character archetypes are present, so something for everyone. Or if you are like me, you pick your favorite based on thier outfit, and there are some cool, silly and sexy designs to be found here.
and make watching the transformations and clothing destruction sequences entertaining. Amazing what a bit of anime butt giggle can do for your brain.
As I said earlier, this is better than HDN Action Unleashed and Oneechanbara.  While I own several HDN games, and a couple of Oneechanbara games, this is my first Senran gaming experience. So if there was any bias, it should have been for the other titles. However,
Compared to HDN Action Unleased, the combat in Senran is more exciting and less repeative. Instead of fighting 200 boring mobs and falling asleep you tend to fight smaller assortments of enemies, often in duels and the fights can end very fast keeping you alert.
Compared to Oneechanbara ZII Chaos, Senran has an overall better story presentation and IMHO better character shapes and special attacks. I enjoyed Oneechan, but after I beat it I felt no need to go back and unlock more costumes, skills or anything. Thats because Oneechan is a visual mess when you play it. Senran obviously has a totally different art direction, and leverages the anime styling and presentation to show off their shape, personalities and costumes regularly. This is noticeable in the story scenes and during gameplay.  If your main selling point is smexy action, I want to see it clearly.
Also the enemies in Senran are better looking than most of the enemies in Oneechan and HDN.

My friends and I have been playing the original AOE II since 1999.  I HAVE NEVER BEEN BEATEN BY ANYONE ON ANY LEVEL.  I'm not bragging simply stating a fact.  I consider the original to be one of the best games ever made.  That being said, I'm very disappointed in the HD version's AI.  Medium seems too easy & hard clearly allows the computer opponent to cheat.  By cheat, I mean the AI is able to advance through the ages & produce units at a rate that does not reflect the number of resources & villagers the opponent possesses.  This becomes a problem when playing multiplayer with friends who aren't as experienced.  I don't use cheats or mods & feel they would defeat the purpose of playing the game.  On a positive note, it is nice to see new civilizations & I do appreciate everyone's efforts to bring back a classic game I love so much.  This however does not out weigh the problems currently with this remake.  My recommendation at this time would be to buy the original & keep an old 32 bit PC around or play the HD version on original AI.  I truly hope at some point the bugs are worked out so I can write a new review & begin recommending to friends.  I have edited this review due to comments from people who appear to either be illiterate or want to nitpick my review.  I don't need comments from people who want to argue with my opinions because they are just that, my opinions.  I'm not interested in childish responses from people who have no life other than playing video games all day & commenting on reviews.  I wrote this review in hopes that developers would have feedback to make changes that would allow them the opportunity to target new players.  I apologize for the novel this review has become but apparently that is what it takes to avoid idiotic comments.  Irregardless I will continue to play & kick a** every time I do.  My thanks to Skybox Labs, Hidden Path Entertainment, Ensemble Studios, Microsoft Studios, & Steam.

One of the earliest FPS games ever made, Wolfenstein 3D has a lot of historical importance, and with a lot people playing it and having fond memories with it, its still considered a great game. Do I think its good well...
Yes and no.
First things first this port is crap. Its just a DOSbox shell which would be fine, but the configuration is absolute garbage. You have to do a lot of DOSBOX config changes before the game is even playable.
After that you are left with a game that is fun, but only in short bursts. That isn't really a knock against the game as a whole because it was one of the earlist FPS games ever made, but rather a warning to you if you choose to buy it.
Wolfenstein 3D has a lot of flaws in 2015 that weren't really apparent back in 1992. The levels are repetetive mazes that are easy to get lost in and theres no map which worsens the issue. The controls by default are clunky and hard to use (though this is fixable but not on this release alone, a source port will fix this) the game is unfairly difficult, the list goes on.
But its still a really FUN game.
The shooting is very fun and the 3 guns that you get in the game are all fun to use. Especially the chaingun with its loud sounds and sheer power. Killing things is really fun in this game thanks to great sound effects, good hit detection and good animation. The game is fun, but it hasn't exactly aged well, but if you can tolerate its problems Wolfenstein 3D is still a fun game. If anything you should buy for its historical importance.
The visuals are basic, no surprise there, but they don't look bad. The sprites are very detailed and the textures look good. The textures do tend to repeat and the levels are complex in design but basic in look. There are no multileveled floors, the levels are flat and static, but again this game was released in 1992 so its okay.
The music is really good, I love that twangy Sound Blaster\Adlib sound that many DOS games had at the time and this is no exception. The sound effects are also good.
Overall I recommend this game only if you know if you are getting into. You have to know how to tweak the DOSbox config file before starting (unless you get a source port) and this game does have a lot of flaws by todays standards, but its historically important and for that reason alone you should give Wolfenstein 3D a try,

For anyone who has, like me, always wanted to make a character to join the cast of the Dragonball Universe, this game is a dream come true and I sure hope they keep things coming for it.
Now for some details:
The Good:
- Combat is fast-paced and fluid. There's lots of opportunities to adjust things to your playstyle, particularly when you make and level up your own character.
- The Story is hilarious. Getting to take part in the iconic Dragonball Saga's as your own character in a (for the Universe) believable way is excellent.
- Character creation and customization is already pretty good. Guessing there will be more cosmetics added down the road, too.
- Playing with friends is a lot of fun. Particularly over voice.
The Bad:
- Online Multiplayer is...laggy and unreliable. I find that I am having trouble even logging into the multiplayer lobby these days. This may be launch issues, but it still is a bit annoying.
- PvP. People who pre-ordered and use one of the overpowered characters will wipe the floor with you. Happily, the Co-Op is more fun anyway.
- Local Multiplayer same issue with inequality in characters.
I don't know of any truly ugly things at the moment.
All in all, it's an excellent time-waster and I am having tons of fun leveling up my little Saiyan girl and looking forward to do it with a couple more characters down the line. If they keep the content coming, I have no trouble seeing myself playing this for a long time to come.
Recommended for:
- People looking for a fun brawler with a bit of lighthearted story and co-op fighting.
Not recommended for:
- Fighting game purists who value a balanced approach and PvP.

TL;DR - If you like Dragon Ball Z, arena fight games, or RPG style fighters, this is for you.  The animations are great, the graphics are colorful and appealing, and the controls are so damn smooth.  The online coop and pvp is fantastic, and there are plenty of special moves and combos to master with your own custom-made character.
You do need to be familiar with the Dragon Ball universe or you will be confused by the storyline.
**********************************************
No Spoilers
**********************************************
Dragon Ball Xenoverse is the game DBZ fans have been waiting for since the 90s.  Forget about Budokai, Sagas, and Final Bout.  This is THE Dragon Ball Z game.  DBX hits all the right marks and doesn't skimp on the awesome; Dimps and Bandai/Namco have truly outdone themselves with this title.
Those of you who enjoyed the Funimation dubbing will be pleased because the English version of the game has all the hallmarks of a Funimation dub: lines of dialogue are slightly altered, stilted/cheesy acting, and unsightly lipsyncing.  A lot of the voice acting is done by the original voice actors, and they use some audio clips from the original episodes.  It's par for the course and completely nostalgic.  I wouldn't change a thing about the sound design/voice acting.  The music is great too, classic DBZ music mixed with 90s power-metal and the original opening theme("Cha-La Head-Cha-La") has received a nice remix treatment.
The game includes a new plot thread to the DBZ universe, which allows the game to occur as it does, and so you get to create your own character to fight alongside the rest of the Z Fighters.  This means you HAVE to be familiar with the Dragon Ball universe to understand anything that is going on, otherwise you will be completely confused.  The plot deals with time travel, allowing you to use your custom character, or an existing DBZ character to play through all the most iconic fights from the series.  Plus, after beating a certain fight/stage you have the ability to replay it for perfect scores and exp, or you can play through them with your Steam friends.  Playing fresh scenarios also opens iconic alternate costumes for the default characters (more than 30 characters from Dragon Ball Z) which also change the special power loadout for that character.
The combat itself is some of the best around.  The controls(with a controller) are so smooth and responsive that this hardly feels like a port at all.  The camera changes, pace of the gameplay, and sound design lend themselves perfectly to creating an atmospheric fighting scenario.  The combat is very engaging, it's not too easy(even for veterans of fighting games) but the challenge increases perfectly with your gameplay progression.  You'll find yourself slamming through fight after fight, honing your edge, and begging for more combat.  It is simply stellar.
Character customization is a little weak, the only features you can choose for your character are the same ones used to create the DBZ NPCs, so your character will likely end up looking like a main character with slightly different hair or eyes.  The simplicity of the customization is alleviated a bit with costumes, accessories, and other kinds of gear that is either beneficial to your stats, or just aesthetic.  Another thing adding to character variety is the good amount of character races, such as Namekian, Earthling, Saiyan, Majin, and even the Frieza Clan.
The coop and pvp is nicely executed and very addictive.  You get the chance to play with Steam friends or perfect strangers as you team up to take down Frieza or Cell or whatever other baddy you want.  You can set up custom teams with your friends to make mission to mission binges that much easier.  The pvp are custom battles, allowing you to test your skill with your custom character or other DBZ characters against the thousands of would-be heroes online.  **Initially there have been some connection issues with the servers because of overloading and such, but it hasn't been a real issue, and apparently Bandai is working to fix whatever issues there may be.
All in all this is a fantastic game, it feels like you are actually playing the scenes/episodes from Dragon Ball Z.  It's incredibly immersive.  The port is amazing and Bandai/Namco must be commended for it.  The nostalgia factor is high and the fact that they used a lot of the original voice actors just makes it all the better.  If you are a fan of the series then this is the DBZ game to end all DBZ games, and if they make more games(which they will) I sincerely hope Xenoverse is the yardstick by which these games are measured from now on.
