Well, this is an interesting little thing, I'll give it that much. What we've got here is a simple retro-themed jumpy game with the gimmick of going through different "eras" of video game consoles and home computers. Credit has to be given to the selection here; rather than just a simple Nintendo-centric view of old video games like a lot of this genre boils down to, they have a wide variety of consoles on display here, each with their own quirks. Consoles like Atari 2600 and Sega Master System are here, as well as 80's computers like the Commodore 64 or ZX Spectrum. The aesthetic for each platform is represented well enough, and there's plenty of variety; although there's only one track for each console's set of 8 levels. You'll be hearing that one track a lot.
This game's tough, and not an entirely fair tough. It's a masocore-esque jump game with lots of instant death hazards, and surprise spikes are in abundance here. If that kind of thing puts you off, this isn't for you. Hell, I like my games hard and it still soured me because there are also no checkpoints. Fine and dandy when you have single screen affairs, but the issues compound when the consoles get more advanced. By the time you hit the NES and SNES eras, the levels have become two to three-minute long sprawling stages where one missed jump or failure to know a trap was ahead in advance leaves you to redo the whole thing over. Some might call that being faithful to old video games and their high difficulty level, but I disagree; even the hardest NES games had
, for goodness's sakes. The shorter levels end up being tolerable, but those longer ones really drove me up the wall with this.
Though the graphics and sound evolve over time as you advance console generations, the gameplay almost never changes. What few new wrinkles they add in are either minor gimmicks or rarely used. There are some powerups, but they're so few and far between and minor that they only alter things for a handful of stages. The majority of the game is just you and a double jump against enemies that walk back and forth, flying enemies guarding jumps that annoy more than challenge, and a bunch of instant death. If nothing else, the control is almost without fault; the only issue being the awkward momentum when jumping from moving platforms.
All in all, it's mediocre. I paid 2 bucks for it and got 5 hours out of it. It's worth that, I guess, and I'm giving it a "recommended" since I don't outright despise it. It's not terribly offensive or anything. It's just kind of there. An admirable attempt at emulating a variety of old console aesthetics, but the actual game part isn't really all that hot, I'm afraid. If you see it on sale and you like old video games and don't mind the "new" retro style of instant kill spikes everywhere, you'll probably dig it. Otherwise, it might not be your thing.

This game is the love child of Arma 3 and Insurgency with a side-affair of Battlefield 2. It has the realism of Arma 3 with smaller maps, the combat freshness of Insurgency and the remnants of fun found on Battlefield 2 (which later had a mod called Project Reality who are the developers of Squad). I've been struggling to find a game to play that makes me feel the way I do playing Squad. The thing that makes Squad such an amazing experience is the fact that it brings you into a world and environment that feels authentic. When playing together with a squad who's leader genuinely understands and commits to their desicions, there's a sense of comfort in their organization skills. When stuck with a less desirable squad leader, there can be a sense of discomfort. These are the aspects of reality that are very rarely found in other games where your ability to peform is directly related to your skill. In Squad, your performance is only partly in relation to your ability, but mostly from the experience and trust you have invested into your squad leader. I love that this game's community is helpful, friendly, and understanding, it makes role playing in this game feel so much more fun and again, authentic. I absolutely love this game and I'm more than happy I bought this, it has been one of the best purchases I've made in a long time and I hope to see this game rival some of the best game titles out there! I think it has the potential and I believe the developers will continue improving this game as time progresses.

Squad is a game about tactics, communication and team work. The game core mechanics practically force you to operate with a 9 player squad and make it very enjoyable to work together... and a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥if ou go all alone fighting your own war.
Simply put: if you dont communicate and coordinate with a squad leader and your squad mates, you will die. And wait 60 seconds to respawn a mile away from the combat. No matter how skilled or smart you are. If the squad leader doesn't communicate and coordinate with other squad leader your whole squad will get killed. Or just be a nuisance, at best.
This game is extremely rewarding for team players who feel better at making the team play well rather than beeing the star of a losing game. There are roles for skilled shooters, building and healing supporters, smart armor-killer ambushers, and clever commanders... as long as everybody work together. On the other hand, the game is extremely punishing for lone-wolves.
In the end, wheater you should or should not buy this game comes down to one question: do you like fps that value skill or team work? If you think CS:GO is tactical enough for you, don't buy it. If you think ARMA 3 is not hardcore enough, go ahead and get it.

Do you like insanely hard platformers? Do you like kick♥♥♥♥♥electronic music? Do you have an odd sense of humor that involves evil Groove Wizards stealing butts? If so, then this game is for you!
In Electronic Super Joy, you play as a nameless protagonist who's a serious badass. Even though you lost an arm in the Disco Wars of 1515, the War of Rock 'n Roll claimed your eye, and defeating DJ Deadly Skillz cost you both legs, you jump and smash your way through 4 rediculously difficult worlds on a fantastic adventure to recover your most prized possession: your own♥♥♥♥♥ If that's not enough, there's a kick♥♥♥♥♥soundtrack that's not just there for background music, it's the driving force that keeps you going throughout this pixelated, adrealine-rushed, rave-fueled (and sometimes seizure-inducing) adventure.
When I said this game was hard, I'm not kidding. Just when you think you've mastered everything about this game, it throws a wrench into the gears and slaps you in the face with some new mechanic that'll force you to adapt and change your playing pattern. The difficulty seems to pay homage to many difficult platformers from the past, such as Contra and the NES version of Ninja Gaiden.
The graphics, although not important to the overall game, cast all the characters and landscape in shadow, while the background is alive and animated. Sometimes I seem to get lost in its beauty.
The controls, gamepad or keyboard, are perfect and well-responsive. When you ♥♥♥♥ up in this game, it's usually your fault, and you know that.
Another large part of the game is its humor. Checkpoints emit sexual moans and groans that will likely catch players off guard at first, but after a while, they'll seem fitting in this world full of bright colors and awesome music. Foul-mouthed characters adorn the landscape, such as the insanity-stricken Pope who threatens to shoot you down in his flying Popemobile.
The only downside I can find with this game is that the smashing attack is a little too accurate. Often times I find myself dying from missiles I clearly smashed beforehand, and this lead to many frustrating moments.
All in all, Electronic Super Joy is an original, artistic platformer that'll keep you entertained for hours. Now go and get your booty back from an Evil Groove Wizard!

Atmospheric and psychological point-and-click adventure game, which has a great sci-fi storyline with unexpected twists and interesting riddles. The action takes place in two time frames – 1972, which is relevant, and 2012, which is future. There is a minimalistic visual design, however it is well-thought out in details, bright & stylish. The view of each location in real time and in the future is different, in general, they have various colors and style. There were also added some interesting natural elements such as rain, or shining dust particles in the air within the ray of light. The music and sound effects fit perfectly the atmosphere of the game. Various sounds, such as the whisper of the wind, or the tender noise of the rain are completely unobtrusive and don’t distract from the walking through the quest. There also should be mentioned a very pertinent humor in the right places, the game won’t let you get bored. Everything was made of good taste and nice quality. It's the game that is deep through its story, not for the superficial individuals. Immerse into the atmosphere, and you won't regret, I definitely recommend it.

Yeah, the game has lots of RPG elements and references to movies and other video games. There are also funny and enjoyable voice dialogs.
The graphics and sound aren't something special, but they are not bad at all either.
The gameplay is easy to learn and there are a lot of things to customize. Key shortcuts or notes on mini-map are very convenient. There's also a variety of cool weapons, lots of abilities, spells, scrolls, pets and artifacts, unique weapons and specials that can be bought with rare UN points from challenges. The enemies have strengths and weaknesses accordingly.
The difficulty is normal to high, but eventually you can move on. Many areas require good reflexes and there are moments that test your patience and they may get you angry. You will die a lot or you'll have to try over and over again to pass them.
Generally, all the castle areas have the same main quests and goals. Good thing is that there are some mini-quests and secrets in each one, which add a little bit of variety.
Note that there is a limited save system and a punishing anti-cheat mechanism. I suggest you backup your save files often. They will come in handy later near the end (eg. the different endings or in my game, when I had a pure fighter class and I had to kill distant Wyverns with a healer elf supporting them and I didn't have strong projectiles to harm them fast enough).
However the minor issues, the game is very addictive, with cool RPG, platform and action elements and enjoyable dialogs.

Tries to be a fast-paced music-centric platform game, but just falls short.  The controls are not tight enough for how fiddly the jumps are, the sound effects seem distracting and mildly out of place.  The music is pretty decent, I'd go so far as to call it good -- but I don't think it's good enough to carry the game.  The visuals are flashy and visually distracting in a way that makes it occasionally difficult to tell what's going on, which makes it very hard to build up the kind of rhythm that's necessary to make trial-and-error platformers fun.  Similarly, dying animations are too long and slow for how often you'll see them.  It makes dying repeatedly punishing (emphasis on the fact you died), rather than rewarding (emphasis on how far you got before it happened).
The controls just feel bad to me, in a way that makes me wonder if it was designed for use with a console controller.  Maybe that would make a difference.
All in all, I've played much worse games, but I've also played better.  I will probably not revisit the game.

A rare mixture of clunky movement/attack controls with fun intellectual gameplay.  What I mean by this is I really don't like the "feel" of your character... like jumping and attacking.   But it's a very immersive system that really takes a lot more into consideration than most side scroll games.  Inventory feels clunky at first also, but the more you see the engine can do, the more you grow to appriciate why it needs to be that way, and how being a little clunky really helps compliment the overall point of the game.  I've never considered a side scroll game to be like a paper and pencil role playing game, but this one does it (I don't mean the obvious humor thematic tie-in, but rather the mechanics, but they both compliment each other).  The game is imensly meta, which I'm not normally a fan of.  But my personal tastes aside, they do pull it off well.  If you are looking for something different, and enjoy learning different systems and differnt types of puzzles, then this is a very good game to check out.  But for sure this is a game for people who want something different.  I'm very happy with what the game gave me through my playthrough.

I have been played about 100 hours via native client, so I have something to say.
This game is funny and enjoyable for first 10-20 hours, but after that you will inevitably face the true content of this game.
The main problems is typical for any B-class projects:
- Pay2Win. If you don't pay, you will struggle dozens of hours to farm some good gear and play on an equal footing with others.
- Pay2Lose. Even if you pay, you still need to grind a lot to build really powerful cars.
- No balance. Do you like machineguns? Well, you will suffer. Do you like cannons? Ok, you will PWN regardless of your skills.
- Noobkillers. You will constantly get oneshots from guys with epic/legendary gear. And you won't be able to get such gear without heavy grinding or paying real money.
- No variability in building. Craft meta-trash or just die.
- Totally failed end-game. In fact, it's consequence of the preceding paragraph.
- Serious economics problems. There is a free market, but it suffers of inflation/deflation and developers doing weird things to struggle those processes. In result, insiders always gain money on the market and you always lose money.
Summing up, I can recommend this game only for 1-2 evenings, but not for playing for long. And never pay to those guys.

I would give  this a mixed grade, with a slightly positive tip on the scale.
The fights are great and suspenseful, but nevertheless easy to understand. You have one arrow that you can pull back with your telekinetic powers to fire it again (or drive it into an enemy from behind). Each titan is unique and has a different way to defeat it.This way is communicated fairly well without being too easy to pull off.
That's everything on the good side, 'cause this game consists of nothing but boss fights.
The bad thing is everything else in between. You die a lot, which is not a problem because it is expected, but there is always this delay of 4-6 seconds before the black screen fades and you respawn. Same goes for entering a boss area, 2-4 seconds delay before the room appears and you can start fighting. Then there is the walk to the boss area, which is 10-15 seconds long from your spawn point (at least for the first 4 bosses).
It doesn't sound like a lot, but because there are many deaths to be had, the seconds turn into minutes very fast and it gets really annoying. You often die 5 seconds into the fight, but you need almost half a minute to reach it again.
If it wasn't for this extremely tedious design choices, I would totally recommend it to everyone who likes hard fights with a handicap, because fighting and defeating the titans is very rewarding.
8/10 for the fights, 5/10 for the mindbending tediousness of the overall framework.

I have mixed feelings about this game, but have to lean on the negative. I've personally beaten every boss except the final boss (The Soul).
Starting off, the biggest problem with the PC version is no mouse support. This is already a hard game, and with keyboard only, you can only shoot in 8 directions (I still got to where I did though).
Certain bosses are fun and creative, and it is very rewarding to figure out how to beat them, and executing the technique. But some bosses are no fun at all as their weak spot appears too randomly, so your beating them is based largely on luck. Most bosses are passable in this aspect, but the worst offender is the final boss, which has an erratic weakspot that randomly spawns and despawns. Even if I can survive that boss fight for 10 minutes straight, there was no way I could hit the weak spot unless I was extremely lucky for it to spawn in one of the 8 directions and I had my arrow on.
Another problem is that some of the bosses feel cheap. Their AI is not well done because their attacks aren't natural. For example, the Golem with fists will home on you perfectly, even if you quickly change directions. It just makes it feel weird as a huge golem's fist shouldn't be able to predict precisely where you're moving. When you see how well each attack homes onto you, it starts to feel unnatural, and makes the bosses feel one note.
For a game that is ONLY bosses, the AI of each boss needs to not just be perfect, but FEEL perfect. They can be extremely difficult and frustrating, but it needs to FEEL that the AI attacks are natural. Because of these facts, I can't recommend this game, which is a shame as its art is gorgeous and its premise is great, and a lot of the bosses are actually very well designed.

Dragon Ball Xenoverse comes with a positive recommendation, but also some precautions...
For the Dragon Ball Fans:
Positive points:
Dragon Ball Z fans will love this game, as it is probably one of the best Dragon Ball games to date, including hyper dimensions for the SNES. Why? It contains an original story with fantastic voice acting and interesting new characters. This has not been done well (in my opinion) since Dragon Ball Z: Super Butōden 2. It is not a mere re-telling of the Dragon Ball story. Fans will also like the parallel storylines and, for the first time in a DBZ game, we are given a plausible story-driven excuse for why Super Saiyan Vegeta might square off against his younger self.
The fight mechanics are fresh and easy to master, and all characters function virtually the same. While many in the fighter game community might see this as a drawback, DBZ fans might enjoy the fact that they don't have to select one character to master to get the most out of the game. Most of the characters people love are here, including a custom character which can be mentored by various heroes and villains... that's right... villains.
The ability to create a custom character is not new to the series, but what is new and refreshing is that there are a lot more options this time around, and I would bet money that the mod community will work tirelessly to add more. The ability to create a female saiyan will draw many to this game on this basis alone. Also, the race of your character will be remarked upon during battles by friends and foes, giving a more 'personalized' touch.
Negative points:
Fans will be disappointed for a few small but negligible reasons. They do not have all of Freiza's transformations, which many people enjoyed about the Tenkaichi Budokai series. While their character roster is very impressive, fans of the series who loved seeing more obscure characters do battle, such as Taopaipai, Pilaf, Kiwi, Zarbon, Dodoria, Bibidi, and so on will be disappointed to see they're not here. However, many fans will doubtlessly overlook these omissions and it is possible that future DLC may add more to the roster. Also, to my knowledge, you cannot play as an Oozaru (great ape) as you could in prior games.
For non-Dragon Ball Z Fans:
Positive Points:
The story and voice acting in this entry are some of the strongest in the series so far, and leagues ahead of other fighting games. While Soul Calibur's voice acting and story are, in many cases, embarrassingly bad, you will not feel like skipping cut scenes to avoid ridiculous dialogue in this entry. I found it quite entertaining, as time travel is one of my favorite storytelling devices. Non-Dragon Ball fans will also enjoy the variety, as you can create a custom character from the various races that populate the mythos, each with strengths and weaknesses, and a custom skillset.
Non-fans will also enjoy the RPG-inspired level up system. Training feels actually effective as you begin to crush enemies with greater ease the higher level you go, giving a satisfying feeling of actual progression. There is a great amount of satisfaction in one-hit KOing a once-difficult opponent.
The number of optional missions also keep the game fairly fresh and interesting, when one tires of doing the story missions, many of them increasing the replayability of the game as they come with hidden objectives that you can discover through multiple playthroughs.
Negative Points:
There is very little handholding in this entry as far as storytelling goes, as it presumes you know the main story of DBZ. This will probably confuse people who only have a passing knowledge of the story. However, this is negligible as it does well enough to explain the stakes of the battles and you know when you're fighting a bad guy or, conversely, a good guy without it being ham fistedly pointed out to you like you're an imbecile.
The story mode does have a few bugs as well, since it presumes the custom character is male by default, leading to more than a few awkward conversations where my female saiyan is referred to as "he" and "his." This is one glaring error which can take you out of the experience.
Another problem, alluded to earlier, is that every character will feel the same. While DBZ fans will ignore this or even see it as a benefit, everyone else will likely feel like it is a bit cheap and stale. However, with a character roster such as this, it was probably inevitable. Mortal Kombat 9 got away with it, but let's be honest here, fun as it is, Xenoverse is no Mortal Kombat 9. People will probably also be confused by the stat system, as it doesn't really explain what each stat does very well. While I understood what 'health' means intuitively, "Ki Strikes" is a term I had to look up more than once on the forums to understand it properly as an aspect of one of my stats.
The BIGGEST and most glaring problem with the game is the online connectivity. Since launch, it has been fairly difficult to maintain a connection to the Xenoverse servers. While steam is set to 'online', it will constantly drop you from your singleplayer game to tell you that you've been disconnected, to say nothing of the multiplayer component. While this may be fixed at a future date, for now it remains a fairly prominent black mark against an otherwise good game, and many who paid launch-day prices will be bitterly disappointed. The way to solve this, for the singleplayer, is to set your steam account to offline. This will at least enable you to play the singleplayer game without issue.
Conclusion:
Dragon Ball Xenoverse is an incredibly fun game, but lack some critical depth that other fighting game genres seem to provide, and unless you're a fan, I'd recommend waiting until this title goes on sale. It is not worth the 60 dollar price tag. If you ARE a fan, though, this is a game you should purchase at full price to help promote future DLC and games along this line. This is a must-have for any fan.
EDIT: As of 5/5/2015 this game works fine offline and on. Ultimate spamming is a problem in online multiplayer with super saiyans, but its not a lost cause. The right strategy can be made to work around it if you're willing to put in the time.

My friends and I have been playing the original AOE II since 1999.  I HAVE NEVER BEEN BEATEN BY ANYONE ON ANY LEVEL.  I'm not bragging simply stating a fact.  I consider the original to be one of the best games ever made.  That being said, I'm very disappointed in the HD version's AI.  Medium seems too easy & hard clearly allows the computer opponent to cheat.  By cheat, I mean the AI is able to advance through the ages & produce units at a rate that does not reflect the number of resources & villagers the opponent possesses.  This becomes a problem when playing multiplayer with friends who aren't as experienced.  I don't use cheats or mods & feel they would defeat the purpose of playing the game.  On a positive note, it is nice to see new civilizations & I do appreciate everyone's efforts to bring back a classic game I love so much.  This however does not out weigh the problems currently with this remake.  My recommendation at this time would be to buy the original & keep an old 32 bit PC around or play the HD version on original AI.  I truly hope at some point the bugs are worked out so I can write a new review & begin recommending to friends. I wrote this review in hopes that developers would have feedback to make changes that would allow them the opportunity to target new players.  I apologize for the novel this review has become but apparently that is what it takes to avoid idiotic comments.  Irregardless I will continue to play & kick a** every time I do. Truly an exceptional FPS.
It's not perfect and it's got some flaws in the core combat & stealth. Sometimes it leans a tad heavily on cutscenes to tell story over in-game action & narration. That's basically all the flaws I have.
The story is pretty damn unique in its execution and tone. The game keeps a perfect balance between serious reality and levity. The weapons all feel great to shoot- especially the standard assault rifle that'll carry you through most of the game. The combination of high-speed sliding, quick melee takedowns, destructible cover, dual-wielding & a flexible peek-from-cover system means that the game always feels dynamic even when you're pinned down behind a wall getting shot at from six different angles. Levels are thematically & visually varied, at least to an extent, and although enemy types are limited the arena layouts mean W:TNO simply doesn't NEED the strong enemy variety of Half Life or Doom.
My biggest endorsement of all, however, goes to the game's narrative and characterisation. There's plenty of good shooters, there's plenty of good WWII games. TNO, however, is a nazi-slaying dieselpunk adventure that manages to somehow make the crazy moments seem crazy (like fighting giant robots with a laser minigun) and the serious dramatic moments feel serious and dramatic (like staging a breakout at a concentration camp).
Wolfenstein: The New Order isn't perfect, but was well worth the price of admission at launch and is definitely worth it now. If you've seen the sequel and aren't 100% on dropping about $90 AUD on it, consider picking this one up first.

This game is the love child of Arma 3 and Insurgency with a side-affair of Battlefield 2. It has the realism of Arma 3 with smaller maps, the combat freshness of Insurgency and the remnants of fun found on Battlefield 2 (which later had a mod called Project Reality who are the developers of Squad). I've been struggling to find a game to play that makes me feel the way I do playing Squad. The thing that makes Squad such an amazing experience is the fact that it brings you into a world and environment that feels authentic. When playing together with a squad who's leader genuinely understands and commits to their desicions, there's a sense of comfort in their organization skills. When stuck with a less desirable squad leader, there can be a sense of discomfort. These are the aspects of reality that are very rarely found in other games where your ability to peform is directly related to your skill. In Squad, your performance is only partly in relation to your ability, but mostly from the experience and trust you have invested into your squad leader. I love that this game's community is helpful, friendly, and understanding, it makes role playing in this game feel so much more fun and again, authentic. I absolutely love this game and I'm more than happy I bought this, it has been one of the best purchases I've made in a long time and I hope to see this game rival some of the best game titles out there! I think it has the potential and I believe the developers will continue improving this game as time progresses.

Finished Unepic. "Finished". Will come to that later.
Premise is simple but well executed with plenty self-aware humor and nods to many cliches and franchises. During a D&D game-night with friends you get sucked into a real dungeon or rather castle. And boy is it a castle indeed. It's huge. Separated into several areas with unique themes and enemies. You slowly get to explore the castle, open up new areas in your journey to meet the master of the castle Harnakon. Each area has a boss fight which drops a key opening a previously locked area. Besides the main quest each area also harbors a Pure Spirit with a quest. These are particularly interesting since the loot is a whole new character skill which opens the path for various spells and skills. On top of these there are also more menial side quests abound which net you either gold, a companion pet or a special weapon. All in all, there is always something to do once you go exploring a new area. These quests sadly are almost always very similar in that you need to collect certain elements in the near vicinity and thus can get repetitive. The rewards make them still worthwhile.
The way you beat the plethora of enemies in the castle depends on you though. From classic melee weaponry to staves, potions to spells, the options at hand are enormous. You will need to decide early on which playstyle to choose since enemies become more powerful as you explore further and the necessary stats to wield apt weapon, spells and armor increases as well. Thankfully there was a side quest that netted me a one-time item to respec. I got stumped at a certain boss for good after having neglected Bow stats. This aspect, the stats and immense amount of spells, swords, maces, axes, hammers, bows, robes, armor, potions, staves, wands and their each respective stats you can level up surprised me by sheer depth. It was fun to change pace from melee combat to magic based combat. Weirdly enough Shields are a total no-show. A shame since melee combat ends up mindless button mostly.
The boss fights were usually the highlight of each area. They are all very unique not only visually but in their regular and special attacks which makes for a fun and fair challenge even while dying many times. For the most part. And this is where the grand finale comes up again. It's a blunder. A dud. A total wreck. Everything you learned up to this point gets thrown out the window. Suddenly you find yourself under time pressure. Not only fighting a boss but going through a whole area filled with enemies. But that's not even the worst part. You also get suddenly control over a second character where you have to fend of enemy waves with some light strategy/tower-defense elements. This especially does not work well with the game. Having two dozen characters have an all-out war is not meant for this viewpoint. You don't see what is happening, who is friend or foe, even where your own character is. Most importantly it is not fun. The best moments in the game are boss encounters where you have to time attacks, run at the right time and repeat. These fights give you control, clarity and the time needed for the right tactic. The final fight is a rushed catastrophe compared to that. You never feel certain what is happening with all the character switching, strategic NPC placement and time pressure.  And when you die, you start the whole area from start.
No thanks. If it's not fun, I'm not game. So I still call this a finished game since I got to the end. All in all, Unepic is a fun and surprisingly deep and big game with passable combat mechanics. This won't be a good time for many I assume. Movement, combat they all feel not overtly satisfying but it's definitely a case of greater than the sum of its parts. Give it a try. You might like it like I did and get close to 30 hours of a good time out of it.

Ok... for an alpha stage game it is just amazing.
Great mechanics. If you have half a brain you will be afraid of peeking out of a door and getting killed. If you have half a brain you will value your life just enough for not rushing against a fortified position. If you have half a brain you will value your life just enough for not driving an armored vehicle right into an enemy ambush. Because man, does it punish you for beeing a no brainer.
Squad is a game about tactics, communication and team work. The game core mechanics practically force you to operate with a 9 player squad and make it very enjoyable to work together... and a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥if ou go all alone fighting your own war.
Simply put: if you dont communicate and coordinate with a squad leader and your squad mates, you will die. And wait 60 seconds to respawn a mile away from the combat. No matter how skilled or smart you are. If the squad leader doesn't communicate and coordinate with other squad leader your whole squad will get killed. Or just be a nuisance, at best.
This game is extremely rewarding for team players who feel better at making the team play well rather than beeing the star of a losing game. There are roles for skilled shooters, building and healing supporters, smart armor-killer ambushers, and clever commanders... as long as everybody work together. On the other hand, the game is extremely punishing for lone-wolves.
In the end, wheater you should or should not buy this game comes down to one question: do you like fps that value skill or team work? If you think CS:GO is tactical enough for you, don't buy it. If you think ARMA 3 is not hardcore enough, go ahead and get it.

Like seriously people, this game might as well be called "Comunicate in a war simulator" because you won't get far if you and your squad does not talk to each other constantly. This however is quite a good thing according to me, as it forces you to socialize with your team mates, and makes good friendships.
The shooting mechanics are quite basic. just point and shoot, no advanced moevement like games like ARMA and such. just walk, run crouch and prone while firing your weapon.
The tactical element however comes in form of your objective and how to accomplish it. Set up a FOB for your entire team? Gotta find a good spot that the enemy doesn't find easily. Push unto the point of interest? Better pray your bullets hit something while under heavy fire.
I could go further with a more in depth review, but i'll just leave here while saying.
Squad is a wonderful Multiplayer FPS experience if you want a slightly slower paced gameplay with lots of chatter in between.

UnEpic is a Metroidvania style game in a D&D setting with weapons, magic spells, and enemies from the fantasy genre.  The graphics and interface are excellent, however the controls sometimes get in the way of the difficult battles and platforming required to navigate the huge castle.  Although everything about this game is charming and detailed, I found myself getting frustrated by constant deaths and getting lost.  However I still recommend the game especially if on sale.
PROS
+ Unique RPG/D&D take on Metroidvania genre
+ Attractive graphics, good sound/music, and decent voice work helps immersion
+ Multiple ways to level up character improves replay value
+ Tons of weapons, items, spells, and recipes to find
+ Large inventory and great menus leads to a supportive, useful interface
+ Raunchy humor kept me entertained
+ Level Editor and Workshop support means potentially endless replayability
CONS
- Imperfect controls leads to frustrating situations (controller is a must)
- Easy to get lost (ability to make text notes on map helps a little)
- Navigating huge map can cause irritation (expensive teleportation items help)
- Constantly respawning enemies, while great for grinding, get annoying
- Found myself Rage Quitting more than I thought I would
- Game crashed to desktop on multiple occassions

I don't know what they were going for with this game but I don't think they hit it, unless they just wanted to frustrate people a lot.
You spend way too much time walking back to one-shot or be one-shotted again. Even when it's only a few seconds it becomes incredibly tedious.
The whole one-shot-everything mechanic also takes a lot of the sense of accomplishment out of beating the bosses. They, as far as I saw, universally had a red thing to shoot with your crappy magic arrow, so if you catch on to their patterns quick you're looking at 2-4 second boss fights on a success. When it's your first or second attempt against them it feels like a completely empty victory, however, if it took a lot longer considering you one-shot them, it would feel like the game was wasting your time even more than it already is with the walks back.
The bosses largely feel hijacked from a dozen SNES games of years past, the visuals are a mix of incredibly bland and vaguely neat and the audio is nothing to write home about. How this game became so universally acclaimed is beyond me.
For what it's worth I was already iffy about the game and didn't like the developer's behavior towards people so I paid a whopping dollar expressly for this in the humble bundle, and I gave it all to chairty. Your game sucks and you didn't get anything from me.

Tales from the Borderlands was a nice surprise for me. I figured that Telltale had peaked with Walking Dead and Wolf Among Us (in terms of writing) and was worried that TftB would be filled with the same gameplay on the same engine. Well, at first I was a little disappointed by the gameplay, as it was unrefreshingly identical to some of their older titles. In this game though, the characters and writing drive the experience and pull you in the entire time. The cast is brilliant, the writing is laugh out loud funny (at times) and the atmosphere was spot on for the franchise. After all was said and done, I felt like I had experienced a more "borderlands" style story than each of the last two entries into the actual series. That alone says something about the quality approach Telltale takes when being handed an already storied license. I look forward to more Telltale games, and I can only hope that they can evolve their engine/mechanics in the near future, as it is starting to noticably lack some polish in certain areas.

**NO SPOILERS**
Fast-paced action, mediocre difficulty.
Wolfenstein: The New Order is a historical fiction game based on Nazis winning WWII. You play as a soldier named William Joseph Blazkowicz who survived the war due to falling into the sea after jumping off a building to avoid an explosion. Shrapnel from the explosion leaves you with a damaged brain which leads to a mental healthcare institute in Nazi territory. The main objective of the game is to find and kill “DeathsHead” a sadistic Nazi war General responsible for the death of your squad mate and most of the inhumane human experimentation done on war prisoners that give the Nazis the upper edge with mutated humans. This game was an adaptation of an older game “Castle Wolfenstein” and keeps relatively the same elements from the older game.
Gameplay – 6/10
Even though the shoot em up game play of unleashing hell upon hordes of Nazi soldiers with dual machine guns seems like anyone’s ideal game, I really found the game to fall short in difficulty. There was a lot of variety in weapons like pistols, shotguns and the Laser Kraftwerk (my favourite). It also wasn’t just wave by wave basis of progressing through rooms and areas too, there was some stealth aspects where you can save your ammo even though you really don’t need to. Which brings me to my next point in how Ammo is distributed. Even on the hardest difficulty(Uber) I found there to be way too much ammo for all my weapons. Enemies where difficult and I found myself in a pickle a few times since there is a wide range of enemy types (Infantry, Tank though I don’t remember a sniper) but I could always just wait for my health to regenerate(Regeneration seems to round up so if your health is 90% it will regen to 100% and 45% it will regen to 50%).The Armor system can also be quite ridiculous at times, Having full Armor allows you to take many hits kill some enemies and then loot there corpse to give you Armor. Perhaps I am too used to old school shooters where you had to collect health, however for the casual gamer having an indefinite amount of ammo and health/resistance keeps the game interesting and reduces annoying repetitive levels where you just die and die. But for an FPS veteran like me, I was sincerely hoping for a greater challenge like the original game.
There is a perks system which branches off into 4 different categories – Stealth, Tactual, Assault and demolition. They work by rewarding you for completing tasks such as killing 3 people while sprint sliding or performing stealth kills with knives. Though they give you minor upgrades such as an increased knife capacity or increased ammo loot. To be honest none of them really appealed to me, boring stat bonuses weren’t enough to keep me from accomplishing these tasks so I ignored them half the time. However, in a way this is good, giving powerful weapons for achieving difficult feats can be unfair and limit enjoyment from the game. I suppose since they are minor upgrades it makes it so if you cannot complete any of these perks that it won’t really affect your gameplay however can tempt you to making your life easier. So, I can see why the developers put such an underwhelming perk system.
Story – 6/10
I didn’t expect much from the story, there is some basic romance and a feeling of vengeance for your fallen comrades however, and I see this a lot, the world in which the story is based on is more interesting than the story itself. I would have loved to see how the Nazis treated their test subjects or how they created with hybrid animal-machine and human-machine creations and advanced technology. However, that would most likely take away from the overall style of the game so you can see why they did not go in-depth with cut scenes, journals and books however where enough for those such as myself interested in the makings of these monstrosities. Most of the story is told in Blazkowicz’s internal monologue was is very interesting to give an insight of the character’s personal feelings the thoughts on the situation being the mentally scarred killing machine he is.
Graphics - 5/10
The graphics of this game where quite detailed, you can see all the age wrinkles in Deathshead’s forehead (that was tricky to read). Especially if you own a 1080p or 1440p monitor you can see a high amount of texture detail and shadow detail in some clothes and weapons, however some faces really needed to have a lot more work done as quality was really reduced for some characters and even environmental details like paper can be blurred on the highest graphical setting which is annoying to see to say at the least. I really disliked the post processing effects and how you could not completely disable them without going through the console or installing 3rd party software. Which means I had to play most the game with a vignette and the cursed film grain and poor depth of field implementations. There wasn’t really a major perceivable difference between ultra and low pre-sets either which means low-end PC’s will most likely have a really bad time in tweaking this game to run without lowering the resolution. Also there is a very annoying feature that occurred with me in the game, once I played long enough in steam offline mode (not everyone wants to be online all the time) the game triggered visual artifacts to the whole gameplay screen (not the main menu or other menus) it was so cluttered that it is impossible to play the game without connecting back online with steam. An annoyance implemented to stop illegal copies of the game being played, however it just ruins the gameplay experience for people like me.
Music/SFX - 7/10
I found this to be a major positive in the game, from the heavy metal distorted guitar played at the main menu, to the creepy piano I am no expert in soundtracks however Wolfenstein: The New Orders soundtrack was marvellous to me, It really set the tone of the world with the ringing of acoustic guitars being finger-picked echoing in some levels and the finger clicking that may or may not have led to some toe-tapping. It really hyped me up before boss fights or during stealth missions with siren-like synthetic effects. There were hardly any vocals in most of the tracks which really put a focus on the feeling of the music rather than the meaning of it. The sound effects of the games guns and stealth kills where quite short in my opinion and weren’t the disgusting sounds of bone breaking and blood splattering that you would see in titles such as DOOM 2016 however they weren’t bad just disappointing at times besides from cut scenes where you could tell most of the work was put into.
Overall - 24/40
A great world with some beautiful soundtracks however it really lacks that special polish which turns “games” into masterpieces. The game seemed to be developed with console in mind since the PC port was lacklustre in the settings department. However, It was a fun game however I do regret purchasing it.The 20$ price for the game is quite unfair in my opinion since it gave me only 12 hours of gameplay I would recommend purchasing this game on sale for $10 to at least get your money’s worth. It barely gets my reccomendation with its lack of content.

Everyone seems to prefer "Race" mode, which is racing with battle items allowed. I prefer "Lucky Dip," which randomly alternates between racing with and without battle items, capture the chao (basically capture the flag), and arena battles (killing people with battle items). Public Lucky Dip rooms are pretty much non-existant; I suspect people mostly play with their friends in private rooms.
The art and soundtrack are charming, bright, and colorful. Single player racing gets a little boring, but it's good practice for map familiarity, character unlocking, and unlocking character builds/stats.
Something that I haven't seen mentioned in other reviews are bugs, which may be rare, but I do encounter them regularly. The first is that the audio for the game automatically reduces in sound level, even when I do not have any other voice chat programs that may mute the game running. Volume simply drops the moment I run it. Whenever I exit the game, it lags for a second and the true volume at which the game should be blasts my ears.
If you like time travel stories, then i recommend this.

Okay I should just explain what this game is. Life of Pixel is game where a Pixel gets tired of being one in millions of pixels on a TV screen so he takes a trip to a museum where he travels through levels of older computing systems and consoles from the late 70s to the early 90s. Sounds cute. So each level is aesthetically designed to look like their appropriate console and computer which is kind of nice, the chiptune music is good as well, the gameboy one in particualr is my favourite. Each level you have to collect every diamond or gem or whatever to open the door to the next stage? Sounds simple enough. But no some levels are just bad. They take forever to finish with no checkpoints. There is a lot of trial and error in these levels as you will accidently land on one hit kill spikes and get hit by enemies. The enemies themselves are annoying. In particuar they are the flying ones and the ones that just move left to right on a platform. The reason they're crap is that they have no sense of direction or pattern. They might just hover on top of a vital spot you need to go to or maybe you're behind them just shifting along trying to get that one little diamond they seem to cover but then all of a sudden at complete random they might turn around without any notice. They did not reach the end of their platform, they just turned around. It get's really frustrating. On another note if you're one to hate bats or one hit kill spikes then STAY AWAY FROM THIS GAME. This game is the king of spikes. I will update this if I am ever to find a leginimate game with more spikes than Life of Pixel. Maybe this game is supposed to be unfair considering one of the levels is literally called "Leaps of Faith" for crying out loud!

The idea is cute but the level design is crap, it offers either loads of one hit kill spikes, a tonne on bad enemy placements or just dozens of goddanm diamonds to collect. If you're still interested in it go ahead. Maybe there is something that I cannot see that you find appealing but I didn't like it. I'd say try and get Pix'n Love Rush instead on PSP if you can. It's also on Android and iOS but I didn't like the controls.
Life of Pixel gets a 4/10 It looks nice but the level design can be horrid with lots of one hit kills and long slogging platforming along with horrid enemy placement, leaps of faith and first time traps. Oh and spikes. Never ever ever forget about the spikes...

I'm giving this a thumbs up because it's so close to being awesome. I want to encourage the developers to keep working on it, and I want to cautiously recommend it ONLY to people who have an interest in the subject matter and who also derive pleasure from figuring things out on their own.
There's a good game here, but ironically, it's buried beneath a bunch of dirty issues and you have to dig for it. I've got probably 3 to 5 hours in this game (playing offline) and it's clear the game isn't finished. Still, I've had a good time with it so far, despite the glitches, performance issues, and an isolated crash I've experienced.

The game is stylish, atmospheric and funny, and the soundtrack is amazing. "Story Rich" tag does not lie, and the plot literally thickens as you move through the chapters. The levels in each machine are just long enough to get you to feel accomplished once you've finished them but also make you look forward to the next set of levels.
The actual platforming aspect of the game also works very well, the only reasons I would miss a block, fall off and die is because of my older controller. But otherwise it is a very fair game with bits that are just a little bit evil. Mostly in the beginning stages where the levels dont scroll with the player but screen after screen, those can be tricky. One more thing to mention about gameplay is the secrets, there are some and they are quite easy to find. Actually I believe I haven't missed any in my playthrough so far, but I wouldn't know if I did anyway. I could only tell by not getting the final achievemnt for collected fruit.
If there was one thing I fault this game for, it is that the gameplay doesn't change throughout the levels only their design does. Although wether this bothers me that much I don't know.
Is it worth £5?
Well if you saw this game and got a warm feeling inside imagining the gameplay through the levels then yes, yes it is worth your money. Get it right now on 50% off for a great deal on a great platformer.

9.25/10
Here is why.
Pros:
1. Amazing combat system, flows very well especially once you get into the game. A great mix of a fighter with a 3D world RPG aspect.
2. Parallel quests (or like side quests) have great replay value as sometimes the very same quest will be slightly different (IE: you fight Goku and Krillin and finish, then you do the same quest, kill Goku and Krillin then Gohan appears.)
3. Also with the parallel quests there is gear, skills, and items that can be earned (IE: you do one mission and get a healing capsule, do the same again, get a peice of gear, a new skill, and a Ki capsule)
4. Allmost to many playable characters. Also character customization is put together very well.
5. A good leveling system that lets you boost the stats you want, also armor is usefull and boosts your stats in different ways where most will take away stats in other areas.
6. Did not launch with day one DLC and its 10$ under the normal price for games that come out.
7. Super Saiyan is an ability AND NOT A SKIN OR COSTUME! It actually boosts stats and does something. Not cosmetic like the previous few games. (Note: you have to have made a Saiyan race character in order to go super saiyan, if not the closest you can get is Kioken.
8. No difficulty slider, and Its hard. You start off easy and will destroy everything but very soon things start to seem allmost impossible (IE: theres a side quest that you fight Freeza and i tryed twice and did not even get one punch in before i died.)
9: You can actually grind to get the 7 dragon balls and summon Shenron and actually make a wish ( like money, more characters, exp, gear) and theres no limit to how many times you can farm the dragon balls and make wishes.
Cons:
1: The area you walk around in when you are not on a mission is just a walk and talk. you can talk to other players (sorta) and do emotes, but i feel there could of been more done
2: Balance issues between weaker playable characters (if i pick Full power Freeza and you pick a Saibamen chances are i will destroy you with no issues)
3: PROBABLY TEMPORARY: Server issues are very bad, in some cases i will disconnect from the server after every mission and be placed back at the title screen. (luckly you do not lose any progress and still get everything you worked for, also it will not kick you in the middle of a mission if you disconnect, just right after, still you will lose nothing.)
4: A few audio discrepencys. (IE: Freeza might say "i will destroy you immediately!" but the caption subtitles will say "i will destroy you very soon!")
5: Main quest line skips a few importaint parts, i will not spoil any of those issues. But kinda sorta has a reason for doing so.
Thanks for reading. I do, and have, recomended this game to everyone i know. It is well worth the money as is in my opinion. There has been alot of work put into this game (or so it seems at the moment) and will probably end up buying any DLCs happily as they come out.

After playing Titan Souls and reading several reviews I have mixed feelings. Lets start off that I do reccomend this game on sale. I bought this on HumbleBundle, which is currently bundled with two other games for $1.  So roughly 33 cents. More than worth it. Full price I'd be rather hesitant to recommend .
We'll start with the good. The pixel art is lovely, absolute eye candy. The gameplay seems to take a number from Shadow of the Colossus, an amazing game. A large world filled with Titans to destroy and absorb. No specific order of what needs to be done. Various atmospheres. The music does nothing outstanding but it fits the world just fine..Relaxing while exploring and starting to pick up the pace. The gameplay mechanic was something that surprised me...with the main actions being dodge rolling and a single arrow, which you have to either go pick up or call back to you. This was something I really enjoyed.
Now my main problem with the game. Irronically I've read a lot of people complain that this game is too hard because of the difficulty. I feel the exact opposite. Essentially it is one shot one kill both ways...The only difference is you have to find out how to kill each titan. The bad part is most titans take little effort to figure out and kill. I've literally went into a boss room, had a boss charge at me, as soon as he hit the wall and landed I struck his weakness and boom fight was already over. And thats how I've found most fights. There have been a few that took a little thinking, but nothing has been challenging so far and thats a shame. I get that fights can't be overly complicated seeing as you are very easily killed, but bosses shouldn't be as easy as you.
Overall, if you want something unique and its on sale, jump on it. Otherwise I'd say just wait.

As I wrote somewhere else, if there's a game you shouldn't judge by its cover, that's Senran Kagura. I just did the test over and over, and the result was always the same. "Haha Fanservice - The Game" "Wow this game must have some great plot" and such. If you're trying to get into this game, and at least, understand what happened before, I'd suggest you to play Senran Kagura Burst or watch the anime first, as it explains the conflict between Hanzo and Hebijo schools, but hey, we're talking about a spinoff, so don't bother about it too much, as most characters' backstories are already explained there, and that's where SK gets good. Aside the monster-sized boobs, the characters are well developed, each one with its reason of why they became a shinobi, and how they relate between each other makes the game quite interesting. I swear, I was kinda disappointed by the plot in this game, as the 3DS titles (Senran Kagura Burst and Senran Kagura 2 Deep Crimson) had a much more interesting plot (and longevity), but I actually liked the gameplay here, kinda repetitive as you just have to smack a lot of foes and other shinobis mixed with ecchi stuff and boobs, but I really enjoyed the side-stories of each character, as some were really funny, and the online side, which let me check out how other players play, and actually improve myself through practice. Although my PC doesn't meet the reccomended requirements (got a GTX560 there) the game runs smoothly even at 1080p HD, while my old laptop (integrated graphic card) runs it at full speed ONLY if the game is on the lowest resolution, otherwise it'll just have costant framedrops. If you're planning to get this game I'd highly suggest to play the first game (Senran Kagura Burst, although the framerate might not be that good) or watch the anime (although it doesn't have the Hebijo's story side, and it has tons of fanservice) as it lets you understand what happened before SV.

The game suffers from various problems such as unresponsive controlls, Hitbox errors and complety luck based boss fights.
In other actual difficult games such as Momodora and to an certain extend Shovel Knight it's all about experience, skill and observation/reaction.
In this game however it seems to be complety based on luck and inhuman speed (if the controller responds in the first place) which in my book, is just artificial difficulty.
The gimmicks most bosses bring are interesting and the fact that you fight each boss with the exact same base as you started brings some nice moments, however like I said most bosses just seem to be straight out luck bases and rarely even give you a chance to observe their moveset before filling the whole area with whatever instant-kill effect. Not to mention that you need a milisecond of perfect timing to hit most of the bosses. And if that's failed it usually means game over. It's a very unforgiving game, but it's the bad kind of unforgiving. Atleast you dont have to play the whole level again.
Another problem I noticed after messing around what that the issue with hitboxes seems to come due the fact that the game uses a 3D/2D mix, though I'm just assuming things.
anyway, if there's something the game did right, it's clearly the OST and scenery.

I have played this game for over a month so far (including playtime from pre-Steam launcher) and, honestly speaking, I am pretty impressed although this game has its flaws. So lets jump in straight away into reviewing it.
1) Some players will say this game is p2w, but I strongly disagree, they are just impatient. You can craft anything you want without paying even 1 real life cent, but it takes time and some serious grind, but it is worth your time, trust me. I really love the feeling when you finally craft your 1st epic or legendary item, it's really satisfying. I started with the basic car with powerscore around 800, but after 1 month I am currently running a 6k powerscore vehicle.
2) Speaking of grinding, there is one thing I hate though - it's the limit of recources u can get per week. It's really annoying.
3) There is some variety of maps both in PvP and PvE, so it doesn't get boring playing the game, maybe only if u are seriously grinding then it can start to get old. One feature this game is missing - you cannot chose the map before PvP missions, because I would like to chose the right car for the right map - open fields benefit vehicles with long range guns, but maps with lots of buildings in it and tight corners require quick and fast cars with close range weapons.
4) I got into clan pretty fast (in my 2nd week of playing) and it only adds some extra fun playing with people you know.
Conclusion: The game is pretty good and solid overall and it's free, so why don't you give it a try, it won't bite you, right?

First of all, I have to confess I don't do puzzle games, in fact, I use to hate them. I not as patient as I would like to be but sometimes I like to play puzzle games and try to get over that lack of patience.
This is an "enjoyable" isometric game, but if you like this kind of games I'm sure you'll love it.
Abrix the Robot game is really tricky game. Here you are a tiny robot, wich reminded me as Rosie from the Jetsons, you have to make de clean up! All rooms are full of boxes and you have to move them to pass and get to the exit. But those boxes will get into a maze once you start to pass the levels. And if you think the beginners are difficult, just check the hard ones!
First, the controls are simple but as being an isometric game maybe you'll suffer a little at the beginning about how to move the robot, but you'll get it fast.
This game is organized by five levels of difficulty. Most are full of lava, laser beams and things you'll suffer a lot. I promise. I couldn't reach those levels but I love to watch Abrix the Robot  teaser trailer  and dream about playing the hardest ones.
As I said before, you use the robot moving the boxes and containers to reach the exit. The problem is not all of them are the same and think well how you would use the boxes, maybe you can pass destroying them but maybe you'll gonna need some of them to reach other boxes and then the exit. I had to restart the level several times because I destroyed the items.  Take your time but not a lot, there's a clock and you have  a countdown against you. So, be quick!
Some of the exit gates are closed, and there is a key to open them so get the key first ad then go to the exit.
Also, there are extra items you can collect when you are playing a level and use them , like bonus time, going backwards,  floppy disks that save the room status, and other interesting ones.
Not all containers could be moved so if you get a laser beam, use it! It's a consumable item, don't forget that.
Dynamite is an extra item too, and you'll remember the famous Bomberman. Just try not to get so close to the explosion or you will be exterminated.
Do yu like to have workshop items? Well, here you have the chance of creating your own levels! There's a level editor that allows you to create the most complicated levels and share with the Abrix the Robot community. It's quite simple to use and you gonna love it.
Of course, I cannot forget the music! The game has a great music with some "retro" style. And about graphics, you know isometric style. You gonna like it.
All levels are difficult from my "lack of patience" viewpoint but just get some time and you'll pass them. It's a good game to gain mind agility, or that's my excuse to play these games after all. I really recommend it, I'm sure you will enjoy this great game!

Did you know I hate the spikes?

I don't like puzzles much, and i chose to give this game a try because i wanted to see if someone like me can have fun with it.
The result? You sure can!
Also, for those that aren't familiar with my reviews, i am mostly reviewing the technical aspects of a game, as i believe that pretty much everything else is subjective.
The levels in the game are organized by difficulty (Five categories of difficulties), and you want to know the best part?
The Workshop integration is very important as the game will never get boring this way.
I tested the level editor myself a bit, and i played with it for 20-30 minutes. My verdict? It is damn easy to use and everything is just point and click!
So, you kept hearing and kept hearing about the basic idea, now it's time to get more into it!
The containers you have to move to finish the level are of multiple types, you can destroy two of them of the same type by pushing them, you can already imagine how this can be tricky.
Sometimes you get to use some nice lasers to aid you into destroying containers that you can't really move.
Sometimes to clear up the arena a bit you have to use either a beautiful six pack of dynamite either a fireball, both are fun to use! (Dynamite bringing more joy, while the fireball is more useful as it can destroy multiple containers)
It can be painful, it can be easy, and the most important, it can be
, due to the Level Editor mentioned before.
The controls might seem just a bit weird, but it's not the controls themselves but the isometric style of the game can make them seem so.
In my opinion, the game being isometric is what makes it a good puzzle game, but i will leave everyone else have their own opinion on this since personal taste can be easily applied in this case.
Another thing i liked is that you 'move' the arena itself on the screen, and maybe i am a bit too fastidious but i would like if you could also rotate/zoom it.
As someone that isn't much of a puzzler, i can safely say i had fun in this game and probably you'll have some too!

I've been playing for a while now but recently switched to Steam (yay! No double verification and it auto-loaded all my achivements). I love the game. It's crazy fun. You can custom build a junkyard brawler, jump in a game, and shoot parts off the enemy until they blow up. Aim at thier guns to blow 'em off and disarm them. Fun bits:
Vehicle Builder - SUPER customizable. People make some CRAZY rigs, from hard core battlefield brawlers to fidget spinners. Yea, no kidding. Missions and Raids - Go PVP or PVE and earn gear and raw materials for crafting. Do the dailies for even more goodies.
Market - Player driven market with crafted goods. For good or ill, players set the prices. I am running nearly all blue gear and it's working great for me, and it was affordable.

I feel this game is only about 75% of what it is trying to be. It really needs a bit more attention to detail to nail the feeling of the old systems that are being imitated. My biggest complaint is the "analoguey", smooth movements and animations, particularly of the player. Making the graphics blocky with limited palettes is only going to get you so far, as the illusion is totally shattered when you can move in fractions of what is supposed to be a pixel. The weird particle effects are even moreso out of place.
It ends up just looking and feeling like a modern 2d platformer with a "retro" skin than a true retro experience. Which would be fine if retro wasn't obviously what the game was trying to go for.
More thought should also have been given to the music. Apparently to the developer(s), "chiptune" is enough description to qualify for a retro game. The tunes match neither the levels nor the system. The sound limitations were often just as interesting and characteristic of a system as the graphics, and to truly replicate the experience of a particular system the sounds are just as important as the visuals.
Then there's the gameplay. It's not bad, but very uninspired and basic. Elegant simplicity is one thing, but this is just meh.
TL;DR:
This game seems like it was made to look retro just for screenshots.
If you want a real retro experience that truly replicates the hardware limitations of a system, try "You Have To Win The Game" or "Super Win The Game".

You start as Abrix who is a robot who seems to get himself trapped an awful lot, and you must escape each room using your own wits and sometimes a few bonus power-ups to help you.
The game starts rather easy, each room has an exit that you must navigate to but you'll find various things blocking you along the way. The main thing Abrix will encounter are boxes of various colours and these can be pushed around and destroyed by pushing them into another box of the same colour which sounds pretty simple right? Well it's not, trust me. Each level must be completed within a time limit as Abrix will fall to pieces if you fail.
Boxes aren't your only challenge in Abrix the Robot, you'll also encounter crates and barrels which can only be moved around or destroyed using a laser, fireball, bomb or dynamite. Running out of time isn't the only danger you'll find, some levels also have Lava which will destroy Abrix if he steps into it (but also any boxes, barrels or crates) and water which can only be crossed using a bridge (bridges will collapse if used too many times). There are various power-ups to help you through certain levels including an undo which will reverse your last move, a save which saves the state of the current room and you may revert to it once, a fireball which destroys everything in its path (even the exit so be careful), dynamite which will destroy a single crate/box barrel and a few more. These not only add an extra difficulty to some levels but they make you think a lot more than you would; sometimes a power-up will seem useful only to find out you actually need it for something else.
The levels are split into difficulty rooms and each difficulty room contains around 10 levels. Once a level is completed you'll be given a score based on the time it took you, how many steps you took, how many power-ups you collected and used, the amount of blocks destroyed and coins you collected. You can revisit a level at any time once you've completed it to try and better your score and doing so will give you more EXP. EXP is spent unlocking new levels so it's better to try and get as much EXP on the lower levels as you can to allow you to skip the harder ones if you're truly stuck.
There is also the editor which will allow you to create your own level that you can share with others via Steam Workshop. The editor is easy to use and I created my own little easy chamber in ten minutes which was fun and it was my first ever upload to the Steam Workshop. It wasn't long before I found myself thinking up another level and creating it thought this one was a little harder and took maybe 20 minutes, but once again the editor was very easy to use.(
). Being able to create and download new levels is a huge plus and adds tons of re-playability even though the game already has loads of content already that I haven't even completed. It also allows you to play some easier custom levels when you get stuck so you don't feel like you constantly have to repeat hard levels you aren't understanding.
Abrix isn't for the easily annoyed though, as the levels are very challenging and do require thought and planning ahead. There is no undo button besides the power-ups that are found rarely and some mistakes will require you to start over. Though this frustrated me at first I very quickly realised I needed to take a moment and actually analyse each level before just rushing into what seemed obvious. Since levels are locked one by one using EXP you don't have to worry because if you really are stuck you should have enough EXP after a few levels to skip one and come back at a later date.
The only thing I find a little off-putting about Abrix is the isometric design of the game but this is 100% personal taste. With puzzle games that require accuracy I find an isometric layout makes me misclick a lot more than I'd want and due to the fact that one misclick can make you restart and entire stage I found myself restarting a few times when I started playing. There are also some hidden walls which are much much harder to see because of this, but once I got used to it it wasn't much of a problem. I has a small issue with the explosion animation killing me after it looked like it was over but after a post asking the devs about this they explained the last frame is almost invisible but they are changing it in the next updated (within a week) which is fantastic and shows dedication to the game from the developer.

A Rimworld Tale...
Our escape pods crash landed on a tropical Rimworld. Just Doc, Miss Farmer and Chef on a strange world.
We gathered what resources we could from the wreckage and slept the night rough on the floor of a cave.
The next day we started building a lavish stronghold before planting a few crops.
Before we knew it the rations we scavenged were gone, (should have planted crops first). So we were forced to hunt the local wildlife for food.
A cry for help came over the radio. It was Doc's sister, Princess, she'd also survived planet fall and was being chased by raiders!
We set out in force and rescue her and bring her back to the fortress. We celebrate with a hearty meal of our first crop.
It turns out that Chef is a nudist. In a bid to make her more comfortable we let her spend her days o'natural.
Everyone is fine with it.
Our home of Fort Haven is finally finished and we start researching upgrades.
Chef makes a statue of her self striding around in the nude and we use it to decorate the guest room.
Another escape pod crashes down. We rescue the occupant, some guy called Aiki. He's a junkie with violent tendencies.
We patch up his wounds, give him a hot meal and send him on his way.
Both Doc and Princess catch plague! I bet it was that space junkie. They're instantly confined to bed.
It take some doing but Doc treats Princess and Princess treats him.
Raiders attack with half our crew bedridden with disease. We push them back but Chef is badly injured.
Miss Farmer carries her back to Fort Haven and heals her wounds.
Through sibling compassion, and their medical know how, Doc and Princess survive the plague and Chef is also restored to full health.
Realising how vulnerable we are we start building defensive gun turrets. We need more metal so everyone heads off to mine.
Princess doesn't like mining and, for some reason, she snaps. She runs around setting fires all over the place.
Doc and Farmer knock her out and put her to bed, but not before the fires spread taking out a huge section of forest to the North.
A huge army of raiders attack. Perhaps they saw the fires? The attack our walls and devastating most of our crops. The new gun turrets come online and we mow them down.
With our crops in a bad way and our food supplies low Chef recommends eating the would be raiders...
A fun game. Would crash onto a Rimworld and eat man flesh again...

Abrix the robot is an isometric, very clever implementation of sokoban with match 2, along with many puzzle mechanics!
Your objective is to reach the exit door in a maze of obstacles, most can be cleared, by getting 2 of the same type and pushing them together or blasting them, while others must be either avoided or moved out of the way. But be careful, you may destroy the exit in the process!
The good:
-Given that the game seems quite simple on first view, I was happily surprised by, even, the easy levels, each adding something new, be it a mechanic or obstacle.
-It is a lot harder than it seems. I had to restart quite many levels because of a miscalculation that I would not need a certain block. It put my brain to work a lot more times than I expected, given that I have played a fair share of puzzle games.
-It has a great difficulty increase curve! I 've played all easy and most of the medium puzzles but for the sake of this review I had try hard ones and I was not disappointed! And there is also extreme difficulty!
-Easygoing and hardcore! By this I mean that you can play a puzzle now and another in two days or whenever, the mechanics are fairly simple and can be easily be remembered by the time you get into the level. Hardcore because each level has a time limit and score points. By finishing a level you earn Exp depending of your performance, there are certain bonuses here, like 'no undo' or 'more than 50% of initial time left', Exp are used to unlock other levels. I had to replay a level quite many times to improve my performance and get some bonuses so I could at least gain more Exp than the levels unlock cost!
-It supports steam workshop! And while at the moment the game is relatively new, there are already some jewels made by users!
The bad:
-For me this game has only 1 issue. The explosion animations feel wrong. When you explode something the boom happens (normally:p) and then you have to wait for the smoke to clear in order to move in the cleared spot. However the last frame of the explosion feels misleading and given the timed nature of the game, I died quite many times while I thought it was safe to proceed.
The ugly:
(By ugly I mention stuff that are either weird, don't directly affect gameplay or can be get used to)
-If you play on windowed mode, any resolution besides the native, will result in main menu buttons going partially off screen.
-The isometric grid may confuse people, each grid title is a box that you can move into, essentially it is the space a box covers, but each of these grids, has an unneeded smaller grid in it. It is the 'art' used for the floor and can get your movement messed up.
-No controller support. Given its simple controls, it would benefit greatly by adding this feature.

While I would certainly give this game a 10/10 on concept, the execution of this concept leaves a lot to be desired. I got about 1/3 through the game before I realized that there wasn't really any significant progression other than the graphical presentation. It would have been nice if your character actually developed as the graphics had, but just being a pixel really exacerbated the lack of development.
The concept basically masks that the game isn't progressing in any meaningful way as you play. Most of the enemies don't really do anything other than walk back and forth, even if they have completely different appearances. The game is over-reliant on spikes/pits/water in that they make up 99% of the challenge.
I think this would make a really good game if a little more thought went into elements besides the concept, or at least incorporated that concept into the game itself. Maybe a story about bumbling fool protagonist in a town whose citizens get turned into blocks? With everyone looking like blocks the main character is mistaken for the town's hero and they send him out to save the town. The player has to visit the towns of Atariville, NESburg, who have met similar fates and free them. As the player goes through the game he begins to look more like his former self, before reaching the end where he battles the town's "hero" who was the villain. He returns to town looking just as he did at the start, and they learn that they have underestimated him.
